body.translated_text:
(1)
Section on the Types of Heroes (<s>Nāyaka-bheda-prakaraṇam</s>)

children.translated_text: He who attracts the knowers of <s>rasa</s> by His very name, who by His nature kindles eternal bliss,
who bestows the festival of His own beauty, the eternal Lord — may He be victorious! // RUnm_1.1 //
Among the primary <s>rasas</s>, he who was previously described in brief due to its secret nature,

children.text: pṛthag eva bhakti-rasa-rāṭ sa vistareṇocyate madhuraḥ // RUnm_1.2 //
children.translated_text: that king of devotional <s>rasas</s>, the <s>madhura</s> (sweet), is now described at length separately. // RUnm_1.2 //
The sweet <s>rati</s> (love), when relished through the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and other [elements] to be described,

children.text: nītā bhakti-rasaḥ prokto madhurākhyo manīṣibhiḥ // RUnm_1.3 //
children.translated_text: is called by the wise the devotional <s>rasa</s> known as <s>madhura</s> (conjugal love). // RUnm_1.3 //

children.text: asminn ālambanāḥ proktāḥ kṛṣṇas tasya ca vallabhāḥ // RUnm_1.4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>ālambanās</s> (supports) herein are declared to be <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and His beloved consorts. // RUnm_1.4 //
He whose foot-radiance vanquishes the beauty that is the summit of <s>Kāmadeva</s>'s splendor,
whose sidelong glances — skilled dancing-girls of amorous arts — are enchanting to the mind,
whose form gleams like a fresh raincloud, who is a treasury of supremely divine pastimes —
may He, the fulfillment of the fortune of the young women of the three worlds, bring delight! // RUnm_1.5 //
This [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] is exceedingly charming, sweet, endowed with all auspicious marks,
the most excellent, in the bloom of fresh youth, eloquent, and sweet-spoken. // RUnm_1.6 //

children.text: sudhīḥ sa-pratibho dhīro vidagdhaś caturaḥ sukhī |
children.translated_text: He is wise, witty, steadfast, sophisticated, clever, and blissful;
grateful, courteous, subject to love, and an ocean of profundity. // RUnm_1.7 //
He is the most excellent, renowned, enchanter of women, ever-fresh,
marked by incomparable amorous play, beauty, and the dear sound of His flute. // RUnm_1.8 //

children.text: ity ādayo'sya śṛṅgāre guṇāḥ kṛṣṇasya kīrtitāḥ |
children.translated_text: These and other qualities of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the context of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love) have been celebrated;

children.text: udāhṛtir amīṣāṃ tu pūrvam eva pradarśitā // RUnm_1.9 //
children.translated_text: their illustrations have already been shown earlier. // RUnm_1.9 //
Of Him, who has the previously stated four divisions — <s>dhīrodātta</s> (calm and exalted) and the like —

children.text: patiś copapatiś ceti prabhedāv iha viśrutau // RUnm_1.10 //
children.translated_text: two subdivisions are well known here: <s>pati</s> (wedded lord) and <s>upapati</s> (paramour). // RUnm_1.10 //

children.text: uktaḥ patiḥ sa kanyāyā yaḥ pāṇigrāhako bhavet // RUnm_1.11 //
children.translated_text: He is called the <s>pati</s> who would be the one who takes the hand of a maiden [in marriage]. // RUnm_1.11 //
Having defeated <s>Rukmin</s> in battle and bringing <s>Rukmiṇī</s>
to <s>Dvārakā</s>, the valiant one,
while the citizens' assembly overflowed with festivity,
the lotus-eyed Lord took her hand. // RUnm_1.12 //
Having attained the state of couplehood with the daughter of <s>Vidarbha</s>,
consecrated in the sacrificial ground, giving gifts as <s>dakṣiṇā</s>,
<s>Hari</s> sports joyously, presented by <s>Satyā</s>,

children.text: kvacid alam alasāṅgaḥ puṇyake nāradāya // RUnm_1.13 //
children.translated_text: sometimes with languid limbs, in the festival, to <s>Nārada</s>. // RUnm_1.13 //
O <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, O great <s>Māyā</s>,
O great <s>Yoginī</s>, O supreme sovereign,
O <s>Devī</s>, make the son of <s>Nanda Gopa</s>

children.text: patiṃ me kuru te namaḥ // RUnm_1.14 //
children.translated_text: my husband — obeisance to you! // RUnm_1.14 //
Those maidens of <s>Gokula</s> who performed this vow,

children.text: tāsv eva kiyatīnāṃ tu pati-bhāvo harāv abhūt // RUnm_1.15 //
children.translated_text: among them, for some, the state of <s>Hari</s> being their husband came to be. // RUnm_1.15 //
For in the <s>Māhātmya</s> (glorification) of the original <s>Mādhava</s>, it is thus heard
that the wedding festival of those [<s>gopīs</s>] [took place] even before the wedding of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>. // RUnm_1.16 //
Now the <s>upapati</s> (paramour) —
He who transgresses <s>dharma</s> through passion, who seeks the strength of love from another's woman,
the abode of her <s>prema</s> — he is known by the wise as the <s>upapati</s> (paramour). // RUnm_1.17 //
While the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> makes the calls of the <s>kokila</s> and other [birds] into a signal,
while repeatedly hearing the jingling of conch-shell bangles at the eagerly-opening door,
his heart wounded by the bold old woman's words 'Who is this? Who is this?',
the night passed in the hollow of the <s>koli</s> tree at the corner of <s>Rādhā</s>'s courtyard. // RUnm_1.18 //

body.translated_text: It is precisely in this [paramour love] that the supreme excellence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic <s>rasa</s>) is established. // RUnm_1.19 //

children.text: bahu vāryate khalu yatra pracchanna-kāmukatvaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Where much is forbidden, and where there is concealed desire,

children.text: yā ca mitho durlabhatā sā manmathasya paramā ratiḥ // RUnm_1.20 //
children.translated_text: and where there is mutual difficulty of attainment — that is the supreme delight of <s>Kāma</s>. // RUnm_1.20 //

children.text: laghutvam atra yat proktaṃ tat tu prākṛta-nāyake |
children.translated_text: The censure (<s>laghutva</s>) that is stated here applies to an ordinary hero;
not to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who descended [as an <s>avatāra</s>] for the sake of tasting the essence of <s>rasa</s>. // RUnm_1.21 //
The very essence of <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s>, adorned with a peacock feather,
who has assumed a human-like form — I take refuge in Him, the shelter of the universe. // RUnm_1.22 //
The <s>anukūla</s> (favorable), <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (courteous), <s>śaṭha</s> (deceitful), and <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (bold) — of both [<s>pati</s> and <s>upapati</s>], now are stated

children.text: pratyekaṃ catvāro bhedā yuktibhir amī vṛttyā // RUnm_1.23 //
children.translated_text: four divisions each, systematically, by their conduct. // RUnm_1.23 //
Deceit (<s>śāṭhya</s>) and boldness (<s>dhārṣṭya</s>) are stated in dramaturgy as belonging to the <s>upapati</s> alone;

children.text: kṛṣṇe tu sarvaṃ nāyuktaṃ tat-tad-bhāvasya sambhavāt // RUnm_1.24 //
children.translated_text: but in the case of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, everything is appropriate, since all such dispositions are possible in Him. // RUnm_1.24 //
Of these, the <s>anukūla</s> (favorable) —
He who, due to extreme attachment to one woman, has abandoned all desire for other women,

children.text: sītāyāṃ rāmavat so'yam anukūlaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // RUnm_1.25 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Rāma</s> toward <s>Sītā</s> — he is celebrated as the <s>anukūla</s> (favorable). // RUnm_1.25 //
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s well-known favorable disposition is toward <s>Rādhā</s> alone;

children.text: tad-āloke kadāpy asya nānyā-saṅgaḥ smṛtiṃ vrajet // RUnm_1.26 //
children.translated_text: whenever He gazes upon her, the association with any other woman never enters His memory. // RUnm_1.26 //
Whose intellect is kissed by clusters of cleverness, who are brilliant with the essence of beauty —

children.text: kāminyaḥ kati nādya vallava-pater dīvyanti goṣṭhāntare |
children.translated_text: how many such charming women sport today in the pasture-grounds of the Lord of cowherds!

children.text: rādhe puṇyavatī-śikhā-maṇir asi kṣāmodari tvāṃ vinā
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhe</s>, you are the crest-jewel among the fortunate, O slender-waisted one — without you,

children.text: preṅkhantī na parāsu yan madhuripor dṛṣṭātra dṛṣṭir mayā // RUnm_1.27 //
children.translated_text: the glance of <s>Madhuripa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) has not been seen by me to sway toward any other woman. // RUnm_1.27 //
Toward the lotus-eyed women standing at the rendezvous, who with the artistry of sidelong glances
weave the overture of the dancing-girl of <s>Kāma</s>'s arts,
not even a slightest trace of slackening in His vow — [His vow of devotion] that brings about
the occasion of <s>Rādhā</s>'s sport — is possible for the enemy of <s>Agha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). // RUnm_1.28 //
Deeply in love, relieved of the burdens of worldly duties
by His parents,
<s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), sporting with <s>Rādhā</s>,
adorned the forests along the banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>. // RUnm_1.29 //

children.text: kṣmā-devasya kathaṃ guṇo'py agharipau drāg adya saṃcakrame
children.translated_text: how did even virtue so swiftly take hold in the enemy of <s>Agha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), O earthly deity?
Behold — His intellect is endowed with the skill of discrimination, His glance exudes forbearance,

children.text: vāg etasya mṛgākṣi rūḍha-vinayā mūrtiś ca dhīrojjvalā // RUnm_1.30 //
children.translated_text: His speech, O doe-eyed one, is steeped in humility, and His form is resplendent with composure.' // RUnm_1.30 //

body.translated_text: 'When He entered your dwelling out of the fullness of affection during the worship of the sun,

children.text: satyaṃ me parihṛtya tāvaka-sakhīṃ premāvadātaṃ mano
children.translated_text: 'In truth, having set aside your friend, my mind, purified by <s>prema</s>,

children.text: nānyasmin pramadājane kṣaṇam api svapne'pi saṅkalpate |
children.translated_text: does not imagine even for a moment, even in a dream, any other young woman.',
'O <s>Gaurī</s>, who grasps the essence, who is weighty with good qualities, who has abandoned all pretense,

children.text: mudrāṃ kiṃ nu mayi vyanakṣi lalite gūḍhābhyasūyā-mayīm // RUnm_1.31 //
children.translated_text: why do you, O <s>Lalitā</s>, stamp upon me a seal imbued with hidden jealousy?' // RUnm_1.31 //
Now the <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (courteous) —

children.text: yo gauravaṃ bhayaṃ prema dākṣiṇyaṃ pūrva-yoṣiti |
children.translated_text: He who, even while his mind is attached to another, does not abandon respect, deference, love,

children.text: na muñcaty anya-citto'pi jñeyo'sau khalu dakṣinaḥ // RUnm_1.32 //
children.translated_text: and courtesy toward the former woman — he is surely to be known as the <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (courteous). // RUnm_1.32 //

children.text: tathyaṃ candrāvali kathayasi prekṣyate na vyalīkaṃ
children.translated_text: 'What you say is true, O <s>Candrāvalī</s> — not even a trace of falsehood is seen
even in a dream in the <s>prema</s> of the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> toward you, whose heart is pure.',
'Having heard the talk of malicious-minded friends that contradicts this,

children.text: yuktaḥ kartuṃ sakhi savinaye nātra viśrambhabhaṅgaḥ // RUnm_1.33 //
children.translated_text: it is proper, O friend, to act with humility — there is no breach of trust here.' // RUnm_1.33 //

children.text: nāyikāsv apy anekāsu tulyo dakṣiṇa ucyate // RUnm_1.34 //
children.translated_text: He who is equal toward multiple <s>nāyikās</s> (heroines) is also called <s>dakṣiṇa</s>. // RUnm_1.34 //
'The daughter of the lord of <s>Kuntala</s> has bathed; tonight has been won at dice by the sister of the king of <s>Varoṅga</s>;

children.text: dyūte rātrir iyaṃ jitā kamalayā devī prasādyādya ca |
children.translated_text: and the queen <s>Kamalā</s> must also be propitiated today,'

children.text: ity antaḥ-pura-sundarīḥ prati mayā vijñāya vijñāpite
children.translated_text: — when thus informed by me regarding the beautiful women of the inner apartments,
the lord, his mind bewildered by indecision, remained still for two or three <s>nāḍikās</s>. // RUnm_1.35 //

children.text: padmā dṛg-bhaṅgir alaṃ kalayati kamalā jṛmbhate sāṅga-bhaṅgaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Padmā</s> casts a sidelong glance; <s>Kamalā</s> stretches with a languid body-movement;

children.text: tārā dor-mūlam alpaṃ prathayati kurute karṇa-kaṇḍūṃ sukeśī |
children.translated_text: <s>Tārā</s> slightly extends her arm-pit; <s>Sukeśī</s> scratches her ear;

children.text: śaivyā nīvyāṃ vidhatte karam iti yugapan mādhavaḥ preyasībhir
children.translated_text: <s>Śaivyā</s> places her hand upon her girdle-knot — thus, simultaneously invited

children.text: bhāvenāhūyamāno bahu-śikhara-manāḥ paśya kuṇṭho'yam āste // RUnm_1.36 //
children.translated_text: by his beloved consorts through gestures, <s>Mādhava</s>, his mind pulled in many directions, sits bewildered — behold! // RUnm_1.36 //
The <s>śaṭha</s> (deceitful) —

children.text: priyaṃ vyakti puro'nyatra vipriyaṃ kurute bhṛśam |
children.translated_text: He who displays love openly [to one] but elsewhere causes great distress,

children.text: nigūḍham aparādhaṃ ca śaṭho'yaṃ kathito budhaiḥ // RUnm_1.37 //
children.translated_text: while concealing his transgressions — he is called the <s>śaṭha</s> (deceitful) by the wise. // RUnm_1.37 //
Having overheard the word '<s>Pālī</s>' spoken deceitfully by <s>Vanamālī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) in His sleep,
her face turning pale,
<s>Śyāmā</s>, sighing deeply, endured that spring night
as though it were a thousand <s>yāmas</s> long. // RUnm_1.38 //
'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by the garment of golden luster
that was spread out today in the bower's hollow,
your innocence has been pondered —
abandon this veneer of sweet words!' // RUnm_1.39 //
Now the <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (bold) —
He who, even when the marks of enjoyment with another young woman are manifest, is fearless,

children.text: mithyā-vacana-dakṣaś ca dhṛṣṭo'yaṃ khalu kathyate // RUnm_1.40 //
children.translated_text: and is skilled in false speech — he is surely called the <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (bold). // RUnm_1.40 //
'These are not nail-marks, O <s>Śyāmā</s> — this is a line of thick saffron paste;

children.text: na lākṣāntaḥ-krure paricinu girer gairikam idam |
children.translated_text: this inside [your lip] is not lac, O cruel one — examine it, this is mountain ochre;

children.text: dhiyaṃ dhatse citraṃ vata mṛga-made'py añjanatayā
children.translated_text: how strange that you perceive even musk as collyrium!

children.text: taruṇyās te dṛṣṭiḥ kim iva viparīta-sthitir abhūt // RUnm_1.41 //
children.translated_text: What has happened to your vision, O young woman — has it become inverted?' // RUnm_1.41 //
With the four divisions beginning with <s>udātta</s> (exalted), and the three [grades] beginning with <s>pūrṇatama</s> (most complete),
twenty-four types [of the hero arise] from the pairing of <s>pati</s> and the like. // RUnm_1.42 //
The <s>nāyaka</s>, with [the divisions] <s>anukūla</s> and the like, has been stated to be of ninety-six types;

children.text: nokto dhūrtādi-bhedas tu muneḥ sammaty-abhāvataḥ // RUnm_1.43 //
children.translated_text: the divisions of <s>dhūrta</s> (rogue) and the like are not stated, due to the absence of the sage's approval. // RUnm_1.43 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the types of heroes in the illustrious <s>Ujjvala Nīlamaṇi</s>.
Now the section on the types of the hero's companions (<s>Nāyaka-sahāya-bheda-prakaraṇam</s>).

children.text: athaitasya sahāyāḥ syuḥ pañcadhā ceṭako viṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, his companions are of five kinds: <s>ceṭaka</s> (attendant), <s>viṭa</s> (libertine),
<s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester), <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (confidant), and <s>priyanarmasakha</s> (intimate friend). // RUnm_2.1 //
Skill in arranging humor, constant deep devotion,
knowledge of time and place, dexterity, ability to appease an offended <s>gopī</s>,
secrecy in counsel — these and the like are declared to be the qualities of the companions. // RUnm_2.2 //
The <s>ceṭa</s> (attendant) is clever in arranging meetings, engaged in secret tasks, bold in intellect;

children.text: sa tu bhaṅgurabhṛṅgārādikaḥ prokto'tra gokule // RUnm_2.3 //
children.translated_text: he is declared to be [exemplified by] <s>Bhaṅgura</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgāra</s>, and the like here in <s>Gokula</s>. // RUnm_2.3 //
'O <s>Devī</s>, this has never been seen anywhere before —
that this <s>mādhavī</s> creeper has blossomed out of season in autumn!'
Thus was the maiden of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> [i.e. <s>Rādhā</s>] lured
to the bower-lane on the pretext [devised] by the young prince of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). // RUnm_2.4 //
Now the <s>viṭa</s> (libertine) —
Skilled in the customs of courtship, roguish, adept in social gatherings,
versed in the arts and strategies of love — he is called the <s>viṭa</s>.
<s>Kaḍāra</s>, <s>Bhāratīvandhu</s>, and others are declared as the <s>viṭas</s>. // RUnm_2.5 //
'In <s>Vraja</s>, I am a companion whose word is never transgressed by the throngs of doe-eyed women;
with sweet words I repeatedly beseech [you] on behalf of that friend [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]:
He whose flute's playful melody arrests the youthfulness of the entire world —

children.text: stvayā yuktaḥ śyāme na khalu parihartuṃ sakhi hariḥ // RUnm_2.6 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Śyāmā</s>, surely <s>Hari</s>, united with you, O friend, is not to be abandoned!' // RUnm_2.6 //
Now the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester) —
Named <s>Vasanta</s> and the like, fickle, fond of eating, quarrelsome,
causing laughter with deformed body, speech, and attire — this is the <s>vidūṣaka</s>.
In [the play] <s>Vidagdha-Mādhava</s>, he is celebrated as <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>. // RUnm_2.7 //
'Being pleased, may a shower of smile-blossoms now be released by you!
The eager lord of <s>Gokula</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) has ascended the incomparable aerial chariot [of imagination] —
O <s>Devī</s>, though thus fervently entreated with a wish,

children.text: yatte mānini nādharaḥ prayatate tannādbhutaṃ rāgiṣu // RUnm_2.8 //
children.translated_text: that your lip does not yield, O proud one — this is not surprising among lovers.' // RUnm_2.8 //
'My beloved deity (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) Himself brings to me with longing
a fresh, brilliant lotus — [His own offering] of obeisance;

children.text: mayā tu tadavajñayā bhuvi nirasyate ruṣyatā
children.translated_text: but I, being angry, contemptuously cast it to the ground!

children.text: na mānayasi madvacastadapi mānini tvaṃ kutaḥ // RUnm_2.9 //
children.translated_text: You don't honor even my words — so why, O proud one, would you [honor His]?' // RUnm_2.9 //
Now the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (confidant) —
He who is equal to the hero in qualities and follows him with love

children.text: pīṭhamardaḥ sa kathitaḥ śrīdāmā syādyathā hareḥ // RUnm_2.10 //
children.translated_text: is called the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>; as <s>Śrīdāmā</s> is to <s>Hari</s>, for example. // RUnm_2.10 //
On the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), the deeds of <s>Mukunda</s> that astonish the universe —

children.text: draṣṭuṃ gacchati goṣṭhameva nikhilaṃ naikātra candrāvalī |
children.translated_text: goes to the cowshed itself to see everything — <s>Candrāvalī</s> is not one [of those] here.

children.text: brūmastasya suhṛttamāḥ svayamamī pathyañca tathyañca te
children.translated_text: We, his dearest friends, say to you what is truly beneficial and true:

children.text: mā govardhanamalla ghaṭṭaya mudhā govardhanoddhāriṇam // RUnm_2.11 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Govardhan</s>-wrestler, do not uselessly provoke the lifter of <s>Govardhana</s>! // RUnm_2.11 //

children.text: taveyaṃ śrīdāman bhaṇitir iha viśrambhayati māṃ
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrīdāman</s>, this speech of yours gives me confidence here.

children.text: prasādo rudrāṇyāḥ kim iva capalāsu prasaratu |
children.translated_text: What [would happen] if the grace of <s>Rudrāṇī</s> (<s>Durgā</s>) were to spread among the fickle [women]?
Seeing a young wife going to the forest, her hands marked with saffron and garlands from <s>Durgā</s> worship,

children.text: vadhūṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅke prathayati kalaṅkaṃ khala-janaḥ // RUnm_2.12 //
children.translated_text: I suspect malicious people will spread scandal. // RUnm_2.12 //
Now, the <s>priya-narma-sakha</s> (intimate jesting friend) —
He who knows the most confidential secrets, who has assumed the disposition of a female friend (<s>sakhī-bhāva</s>),
among all loving associates, the <s>priya-narma-sakha</s> is the best.

children.text: sa gokule tu subalas tathā syād arjunādayaḥ // RUnm_2.13 //
children.translated_text: In <s>Gokula</s>, he is <s>Subala</s>, and likewise <s>Arjuna</s> and others. // RUnm_2.13 //
For example:
He pacifies and brings back a beloved girl who has departed in a lovers' quarrel (<s>kali</s>);
he prepares the bed suitable for the love-play of the destroyer of <s>Agha</s> in the bower-house;

body.text: svinnaṃ bījayati priyā-hṛdi parisrastāṅgam uccair amuṃ

children.text: kva śrīmān adhikāritāṃ na subalaḥ sevā-vidhau vindati // RUnm_2.14 //
children.translated_text: where does the glorious <s>Subala</s> not find authority in the service? // RUnm_2.14 //

body.translated_text: he fans Him when perspiring, His limbs loosened and sprawled upon the bosom of His beloved —

children.translated_text: By those [<s>gopīs</s>] whose sidelong glances playfully caress the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
whose pair of arms press their breasts against His chest in free embrace,
whose lip-nectar He relishes with unbridled delight —

children.text: kiṃ jānāsi sakhe vyadhāyi kataradgopībhirābhistapaḥ // RUnm_2.15 //
children.translated_text: do you know, O friend, what austerity was performed by those <s>gopīs</s>? // RUnm_2.15 //
The friends are of four kinds; here the <s>ceṭa</s> (servant-companion) is called '<s>kiṅkara</s>' (attendant).
The <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (confidant) also renders assistance in heroic exploits and the like. // RUnm_2.16 //
The female messengers (<s>dūtikāḥ</s>) who will be described in the section on <s>Hari</s>'s beloveds —

children.text: atrāpi tā yathāyogyaṃ vijñeyā rasavedibhiḥ // RUnm_2.17 //
children.translated_text: they should be understood here too, as appropriate, by the knowers of <s>rasa</s>. // RUnm_2.17 //
O friend, the messenger-artistry of <s>Mādhava</s>'s glances
is wonderfully skilled in enchantment (<s>kārmaṇa</s>);
even you, who are pure in your integrity (<s>upadhāśuddhā</s>),
are captured by it as if painted [still]. // RUnm_2.18 //

body.translated_text: Among them, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] Himself [acts as messenger], as in:

children.translated_text: Seizing modesty from the homes,
she who skillfully draws <s>Rādhā</s> to the forest —
she triumphs, the messenger entrusted with [full] authority,
the sweet cuckoo-call born of the noble flute (<s>vaṃśa</s>)! // RUnm_2.19 //

body.translated_text: The flute [as messenger], as in the <s>Śrī Lalita Mādhava</s> (1.24 — <s>Gārgī</s>'s speech):

children.translated_text: The trusted messenger (<s>āptadūtī</s>) —
<s>Vīrā</s>, <s>Vṛndā</s>, and others are also celebrated as trusted messengers of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
<s>Vīrā</s> is bold in speech, and <s>Vṛndā</s> is skilled in flattering words. // RUnm_2.20 //
Do not turn away, O proud one!
My mountain is not without protection when upheld by the mountain[-lifter].
O foolish girl, [approach] with passion
<s>Mādhava</s>, who has attained the fullness of youth! // RUnm_2.21 //

children.text: vṛndā sundari vandanaṃ vidadhatī yat pṛcchati tvāmasau
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, <s>Vṛndā</s>, offering salutations, asks you —
O you whose eyes are [like] the fluttering lovely <s>khañjarīṭa</s> (wagtail) bird — express your answer there:
What is this exceedingly crooked serpentine brow of yours, by whose fear

children.text: klāntaḥ kāliyamardano.api kurute nādya praveśaṃ vraje // RUnm_2.22 //
children.translated_text: even the subduer of <s>Kāliya</s>, exhausted, does not enter <s>Vraja</s> today? // RUnm_2.22 //
The exclusive messengers of <s>Hari</s>, such as <s>Vīrā</s> and others, have been described;

children.text: liṅginyantāstu vakṣyante yāstāḥ sādhāraṇā dvayoḥ // RUnm_2.23 //
children.translated_text: those ending in the feminine suffix [-<s>iṅginī</s>] who will be described [later] — they are common to both [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the <s>gopīs</s>]. // RUnm_2.23 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the section on the varieties of the hero's companions in the glorious <s>Ujjvala Nīlamaṇi</s>. ||2||
Now the section on the beloveds of <s>Śrī Hari</s>.

children.translated_text: Those who possess the general qualities of <s>Hari</s> and are His beloveds,
the foremost repositories of vast love and the treasure of supreme sweetness — // RUnm_3.1 //
I bow to those who are endowed with supreme sweetness,
the crest-jewels among the beautiful women of accumulated merit,
who, having mastered the guru of approaching youth,
declare the expertise in the love-sport of <s>Hari</s>. // RUnm_3.2 //

body.text: svakīyāḥ parakīyāś ca dvidhā tāḥ parikīrtitāḥ // RUnm_3.3 //
body.translated_text: They are proclaimed to be of two kinds: <s>svakīyā</s> (one's own [wedded wives]) and <s>parakīyā</s> (belonging to another). // RUnm_3.3 //

children.translated_text: Among them, the <s>svakīyā</s> —
Those who have undergone the rite of hand-grasping (marriage), who are devoted to their husband's commands,

children.text: pātivratyād avicalāḥ svakīyāḥ kathitā iha // RUnm_3.4 //
children.translated_text: unwavering in their conjugal fidelity (<s>pātivratya</s>) — they are called <s>svakīyā</s> here. // RUnm_3.4 //
On the well-made path of <s>dharma</s>, well-known among the wives of their lord,

children.text: mudā baddha-śraddhā giri ca guru-vargasya paritaḥ |
children.translated_text: with joyful faith established firmly in the circle of elders,

children.text: gṛhe yāḥ sevante priyam aparatantrāḥ pratidinaṃ
children.translated_text: those who serve their beloved at home daily, free from dependence on others —

children.text: mahiṣyas tāḥ śaures tava mudam udagrāṃ vidadhatu // RUnm_3.5 //
children.translated_text: may those queens (<s>mahiṣīs</s>) of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) bestow upon you exalted joy! // RUnm_3.5 //
I do not see among my housewives one so devoted as you,
O proud one, who at the time of your own wedding,

children.text: prāptān nṛpān na vigaṇayya raho-haro me
children.translated_text: disregarding the assembled kings, secretly sent to Me
a Brahmin, having heard of My excellent virtues. // RUnm_3.6 //
Of these, the famous [queens] of the hero of the <s>Yadu</s> [dynasty] number sixteen thousand,
one hundred and eight in the leading group, at <s>Dvāravatī</s> (<s>Dvārakā</s>). // RUnm_3.7 //

children.text: āsāṃ sakhyaś ca dāsyaś ca pratyekaṃ syuḥ sahasraśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Each of them has thousands of female companions (<s>sakhīs</s>) and maidservants (<s>dāsīs</s>);

children.text: tulya-rūpa-guṇāḥ sakhyaḥ kiñcin nyūnās tu dāsikāḥ // RUnm_3.8 //
children.translated_text: the companions are equal in beauty and qualities; the maidservants are slightly inferior. // RUnm_3.8 //
Among them, <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>), <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, the daughter of the Sun (<s>Kālindī</s>),

children.text: śaivyā bhadrā ca kauśalyā mādrīty aṣṭau gaṇāgrimāḥ // RUnm_3.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śaivyā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Kauśalyā</s>, and <s>Mādrī</s> — these eight are the leaders of the groups. // RUnm_3.9 //
Among them, <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyā</s> are proclaimed as the most excellent;

children.text: aiśvaryād rukmiṇī tatra satyā saubhāgyato varā // RUnm_3.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s> is superior therein through majesty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), and <s>Satyā</s> is superior through good fortune (<s>saubhāgya</s>). // RUnm_3.10 //
Thus in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>:
<s>Rukmiṇī</s>, the daughter of <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>, was the mistress of the household;
<s>Satyabhāmā</s> was the foremost among women in good fortune. // RUnm_3.11 //

children.text: pādme (6.88.28) ca kārttika-māhātmye tāṃ prati śrī-kṛṣṇa-vākyaṃ
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> (6.88.28), in the <s>Kārttika Māhātmya</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s words to her:

children.text: na me tvattaḥ priyatamā kācid anyā nitambinī |
children.translated_text: There is no woman dearer to Me than you, O beautiful-hipped one;

children.text: ṣoḍaśa-strī-sahasrāṇāṃ priye prāṇa-samā hy asi // RUnm_3.12 //
children.translated_text: among the sixteen thousand women, O beloved, you are equal to My very life. // RUnm_3.12 //

children.text: anayoḥ sakalotkṛṣṭāḥ sakhyo dāsyaś ca lakṣaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The companions and maidservants of these two [<s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyā</s>] are superior to all, numbering in the hundreds of thousands.
All are imbued with the disposition of being <s>svakīyā</s> (married wives). // RUnm_3.13 //
And those among the maidens of <s>Gokula</s> who are devoted to <s>Hari</s> with the sentiment of wifehood —

children.text: tāsāṃ tad-vṛtti-niṣṭhitvān na svīyātvam asāmpratam // RUnm_3.14 //
children.translated_text: since they are firmly established in that mode of conduct, their <s>svakīyā</s> status is not inappropriate. // RUnm_3.14 //

children.text: āryā ced ativatsalā mayi muhur goṣṭheśvarī kiṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Even if my noble mother-in-law (<s>āryā</s>) is very affectionate to me, if the mistress of the cowherds — so what?

children.text: prāṇebhyaḥ praṇayāspadaṃ priya-sakhī-vṛndaṃ kim etena me |
children.translated_text: Even if the circle of dear friends is dearer than life — what is that to me?
Even if <s>Vṛndāvana</s> conquers the groves of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — what of that?

children.text: dīvyaty atra na ced umā-vrata-phalaṃ piñcāvataṃsī patiḥ // RUnm_3.15 //
children.translated_text: None of this matters if the fruit of the <s>Umā</s>-vow — a husband with a peacock-feather crest — is not playing here! // RUnm_3.15 //
Through acceptance by the <s>Gāndharva</s> rite (love-marriage), the <s>svakīyā</s> status exists in reality here;
because the marriage is not manifest, the concealment of the desire is perfect. // RUnm_3.16 //
Now, the <s>parakīyā</s> (those belonging to another) —
Those who have offered themselves through a love (<s>rāga</s>) that disregards both worlds,

children.text: dharmeṇāsvīkṛtā yās tu parakīyā bhavanti tāḥ // RUnm_3.17 //
children.translated_text: who have not been accepted through [ordinary] <s>dharma</s> (marital rite) — they are <s>parakīyā</s>. // RUnm_3.17 //
Though their conduct transgresses the path of propriety through the exuberance of passion,
their deeds are worshipped by the community of chaste wives headed by <s>Arundhatī</s>, who are captivated by [their] extraordinary faith;
though they dwell in the forest, their glory draws even <s>Lakṣmī</s> by the fragrance of their sweetness —

children.text: tās trailokya-vilakṣaṇā dadatu vaḥ kṛṣṇasya sakhyaḥ sukham // RUnm_3.18 //
children.translated_text: may those companions of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, unparalleled in the three worlds, bestow happiness upon you! // RUnm_3.18 //

children.text: kanyakāś ca paroḍhāś ca parakīyā dvidhā matāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>parakīyā</s> are considered to be of two kinds: unmarried maidens (<s>kanyakā</s>) and married women (<s>paroḍhā</s>).

children.text: pracchanna-kāmatā hy atra gokuendrasya saukhyatā // RUnm_3.19 //
children.translated_text: The concealment of desire here is the source of happiness for the lord of <s>Gokula</s>. // RUnm_3.19 //
Thus <s>Rudra</s> [says] (in the <s>Śṛṅgāra Tilaka</s> 2.30):

children.text: vāmatā durlabhatvaṃ ca strīṇāṃ yā ca nivāraṇā |
children.translated_text: The coyness, the unattainability, and the prohibition regarding women —

children.text: tad eva pañca-bāṇasya manye paramam āyudham // RUnm_3.20 //
children.translated_text: that itself, I consider, is the supreme weapon of the five-arrowed one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>). // RUnm_3.20 //
And in the <s>Viṣṇugupta Saṃhitā</s>:

children.text: yatra niṣedha-viśeṣaḥ sudurlabhatvaṃ ca yan mṛgākṣīṇām |
children.translated_text: Where there is a special prohibition, and where there is great unattainability of the doe-eyed women,

children.text: tatraiva nāgarāṇāṃ nirbharam āsajjate hṛdayam // RUnm_3.21 //
children.translated_text: there indeed do the hearts of the sophisticated become intensely attached. // RUnm_3.21 //

children.text: āḥ kiṃvānyad yatas tasyām idam eva mahāmuniḥ |
children.translated_text: Ah, what more [need be said]? For the great sage

children.text: jagau pāramahaṃsyāṃ ca saṃhitāyāṃ svayaṃ śukaḥ // RUnm_3.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śuka</s> himself sang this very thing in the <s>Pāramahaṃsī Saṃhitā</s> (the <s>Bhāgavata</s>): // RUnm_3.22 //
As in the Tenth [Canto] (<s>Bhāgavata</s> 10.33.19):
Having made Himself into as many forms as there were cowherd women (<s>gopayoṣits</s>),

children.text: reme sa bhagavāṃs tābhir ātmārāmo æpi līlayā // RUnm_3.23 //
children.translated_text: the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), though self-delighted (<s>ātmārāma</s>), enjoyed with them in sport (<s>līlā</s>). // RUnm_3.23 //
And also in the same place (<s>Bhāgavata</s> 10.33.31, 36):

children.text: naitat samācarej jātu manasāpi hy anīśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is not the Supreme Lord should never imitate this, even in mind;

children.text: vinaśyaty ācaran mauṭhyād yathārudro æbdhi-jaṃ viṣam // RUnm_3.26 //
children.translated_text: one who does so out of folly perishes, like one who is not <s>Rudra</s> [drinking] the ocean-born poison. // RUnm_3.26 //
To bestow grace upon His devotees, having assumed a human form,

children.text: bhajate tādṛśīḥ krīḍā yāḥ śrutvā tat-paro bhavet // RUnm_3.27 //
children.translated_text: He performs such sports that one who hears of them becomes devoted to Him. // RUnm_3.27 //

body.text: śrī-mukhena tu māhātmyam āsāṃ prāha svayaṃ hariḥ // RUnm_3.28 //
body.translated_text: And from His own holy mouth, <s>Hari</s> Himself declared their greatness: // RUnm_3.28 //

children.translated_text: I am unable to repay you,
whose association is blameless, for your good deeds, even in a lifetime of the gods;
you who have broken the hard-to-break chains of household life — let your own goodness be your reward. // RUnm_3.29 //

children.text: saṃvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā // RUnm_3.29 //

body.translated_text: <s>Uddhava</s> too, the foremost among all devotees, sang beautifully: // RUnm_3.30 //

children.translated_text: Oh, may I become any [plant] — a bush, a creeper, or a herb — in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
that is graced by the dust of the feet of these [<s>gopīs</s>],

children.text: yā dustyajaṃ sva-janam ārya-pathaṃ ca hitvā
children.translated_text: who, abandoning their hard-to-leave families and the path of propriety,
have worshipped the path of <s>Mukunda</s>, sought [even] by the <s>Vedas</s>! // RUnm_3.31 //
Through <s>Māyā</s>'s creation of replicas resembling those women, without any jealousy [on the part of their husbands],

children.text: na jātu vraja-devīnāṃ patibhiḥ saha saṅgamaḥ // RUnm_3.32 //
children.translated_text: never did the goddesses of <s>Vraja</s> have [actual] union with their [nominal] husbands. // RUnm_3.32 //
Thus in the Tenth [Canto] (<s>Bhāgavata</s> 10.33.37):

children.text: nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā |
children.translated_text: The residents of <s>Vraja</s> did not bear jealousy toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, deluded by His <s>Māyā</s>,

children.text: manyamānāḥ svapārśvasthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ // RUnm_3.33 //
children.translated_text: thinking that their own wives were at their own sides. // RUnm_3.33 //
Among them, the unmarried maidens (<s>kanyakāḥ</s>) —
Those who are unmarried are called <s>kanyakāḥ</s> (maidens); they are modest, protected by their fathers,
confident in the company of their female friends, and mostly endowed with the quality of <s>mugdhā</s> (artless innocence). // RUnm_3.34 //
Among them, the maidens devoted to the <s>Durgā</s>-vow, such as <s>Dhanyā</s> and others, are recognized;

children.text: hariṇā pūritābhīṣṭās tena tās tasya vallabhāḥ // RUnm_3.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> fulfilled their desires, and therefore they are His beloveds. // RUnm_3.35 //
O friend, you are at ease in the dust-play, your chest covered by a cloth —

children.text: bālāsīti na vallavas tava pitā jāmātaraṃ mṛgyati |
children.translated_text: you are [still] a girl! — your cowherd father does not [yet] seek a bridegroom for you.

children.text: tvaṃ tu bhrānta-vilocanās tam acirād ākarṇya vṛndāvane
children.translated_text: But you, with wandering eyes, as soon as you hear in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>
the flute of the peacock-feather-crested one cooing — you tremble and swirl! // RUnm_3.36 //
Now, the married women (<s>paroḍhāḥ</s>) —

children.text: gopair vyūḍhā api hareḥ sadā sambhoga-lālasāḥ |
children.translated_text: Though married to cowherds, always longing for union with <s>Hari</s>,
the married beloveds of His are the women of <s>Vraja</s> who have not [yet] given birth. // RUnm_3.37 //
With what purpose, out of curiosity, have you gone
to the deep hollow of the wilderness to [pick] flowers for <s>Kātyāyanī</s>?
Look at the thorn-marks on the clusters of your breasts —

children.text: gopaḥ sukaṇṭhi bata paśyasi jāta-kopaḥ // RUnm_3.38 //
children.translated_text: O beautiful-necked one, alas, the cowherd sees [them] and is angry! // RUnm_3.38 //
These [<s>gopīs</s>] surpass all in the splendor of beauty and virtuous qualities,
adorned with the weight of vast love and sweetness, [surpassing] even <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) and others. // RUnm_3.39 //

children.text: nāyaṃ śriyo æṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ
children.translated_text: This [grace] is not the favor of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), who is ever intimately devoted,
nor of the heavenly women of lotus-fragrance and beauty — how then of others?
In the <s>Rāsa</s> festival, whose necks were embraced by His arm,
that [grace] arose for the beloveds of <s>Vraja</s> whose wishes were fulfilled. // RUnm_3.40 //

body.text: tās tridhā sādhana-parā devyo nitya-priyās tathā // RUnm_3.41 //
body.translated_text: They are of three kinds: those engaged in spiritual practice (<s>sādhanaparā</s>), the divine ones (<s>devīs</s>), and the eternal beloveds (<s>nitya-priyāḥ</s>). // RUnm_3.41 //

children.text: syur yauthikyas tv ayauthikya iti tatrādimā dvidhā // RUnm_3.42 //
children.translated_text: they are divided into two: <s>yauthikī</s> (congregational) and <s>ayauthikī</s> (individual), the first being of two kinds. // RUnm_3.42 //

body.translated_text: Among them, the <s>sādhanaparā</s> (those engaged in practice) —

children.translated_text: Among them, the <s>yauthikīs</s> (congregational) —

children.text: yauthikyas tatra saṃbhūya gaṇaśaḥ sādhane ratāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>yauthikīs</s> are those engaged in spiritual practice collectively, in groups;

children.text: dvividhās tās tu munayas tathopaniṣado matāḥ // RUnm_3.43 //
children.translated_text: they are of two kinds: <s>munis</s> (sages) and <s>Upaniṣads</s> (personified Vedic texts). // RUnm_3.43 //
Among them, the <s>munis</s> (sages) —
They were formerly worshippers of <s>Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) who had not yet attained the fulfillment of their desires;
their devotion was awakened after a long time through the vision of the beauty of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s> or <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). // RUnm_3.44 //
These sages, devoted to attaining the fulfillment of their own cherished desires,

children.text: labdha-bhāvā vraje gopyo jātāḥ pādma itīritam // RUnm_3.45 //
children.translated_text: having attained the [appropriate] emotional disposition (<s>bhāva</s>), were born as <s>gopīs</s> in <s>Vraja</s> — thus it is stated in the <s>Padma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]. // RUnm_3.45 //

children.text: kathāpy anyā kila bṛhad-vāmane ceti viśrutiḥ |
children.translated_text: There is also reportedly another account in the <s>Bṛhadvāmana</s> [Purāṇa].
Some of them attained perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) at the very commencement of the <s>rāsa</s> [dance] —
thus declare certain [authorities] who follow the surface meaning. // RUnm_3.46 //
Now [regarding] the <s>Upaniṣads</s> —
All the great <s>Upaniṣads</s>, being seers of subtle [truths] from every direction,

children.text: gopīnāṃ vīkṣya saubhāgyam asamordhvaṃ suvismitāḥ // RUnm_3.47 //
children.translated_text: beholding the unequalled and unsurpassed good fortune of the <s>gopīs</s>, were greatly amazed. // RUnm_3.47 //

children.text: tapāṃsi śraddhayā kṛtvā premāḍhyā jajñire vraje |
children.translated_text: Having performed austerities with faith, they were born in <s>Vraja</s>, rich in <s>prema</s> (divine love),

children.text: vallavya iti paurāṇī tathaupaniṣadī prathā // RUnm_3.48 //
children.translated_text: as cowherd women — such is the Purāṇic as well as the Upaniṣadic tradition. // RUnm_3.48 //
Now [regarding] the solitary ones (<s>ayauthikīs</s>) —

children.text: tad-bhāva-baddha-rāgā ye janās te sādhane ratāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those persons whose passion is bound to His nature, being devoted to the means [of attaining Him],
having obtained the flood of love appropriate to Him, following [their] intense longing, // RUnm_3.49 //

children.text: tā ekaśo'thavā dvi-trāḥ kāle kāle vraje'bhavan |
children.translated_text: they appeared in <s>Vraja</s> singly or in twos and threes, from time to time;

children.text: prācīnāś ca navāś ca syur ayauthikyas tato dvidhā // RUnm_3.50 //
children.translated_text: they may be of former times or new — thus the solitary ones are of two kinds. // RUnm_3.50 //
The former ones, having long ago attained co-residence (<s>sālokya</s>) with the eternal beloveds,

children.text: vraje jātā navās tv etā martyāmartyādi-yonitaḥ // RUnm_3.51 //
children.translated_text: were born in <s>Vraja</s>; the new ones [are born] from mortal, immortal, and other wombs. // RUnm_3.51 //
Now [regarding] the goddesses (<s>devīs</s>) —

children.text: deveṣv aṃśena jātasya kṛṣṇasya divi tuṣṭaye |
children.translated_text: Of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who was born with a portion [of the Supreme] among the gods, for His delight in heaven,

children.text: nitya-priyāṇām aṃśās tu yā yātā deva-yonayaḥ // RUnm_3.52 //
children.translated_text: the portions of the eternal beloveds who descended into divine wombs — // RUnm_3.52 //
here, in the divine descent, having been born as cowherd girls,

children.text: tā aṃśinīnām evāsāṃ priya-sakhyo'bhavan vraje // RUnm_3.53 //
children.translated_text: they became the dear friends of those very [eternal beloveds] of whom they are portions, in <s>Vraja</s>. // RUnm_3.53 //
Now [regarding] the eternal beloveds (<s>nityapriyās</s>) —
Those headed by <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Candrāvalī</s> are called the eternal beloveds in <s>Vraja</s>,
like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, they are the abode of eternally present beauty, cleverness, and other qualities. // RUnm_3.54 //
Relished by those who are permeated by the essence of bliss, consciousness, and <s>rasa</s>,
with those very [beloveds] who are His own expansions (<s>kalās</s>) in His own form —
He dwells in <s>Goloka</s> alone, being the Self of all —

children.text: govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi // RUnm_3.55 //
children.translated_text: I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person. // RUnm_3.55 //
Among those established by scripture: <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Candrāvalī</s>,

children.text: viśākhā lalitā śyāmā padmā śaibyā ca bhadrikā |
children.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Śaibya</s>, and <s>Bhadrikā</s>,

children.text: tārā vicitrā gopālī dhaniṣṭhā pālikādayaḥ // RUnm_3.56 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Vicitrā</s>, <s>Gopālī</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Pālikā</s>, and others. // RUnm_3.56 //
<s>Candrāvalī</s> is indeed <s>Somābhā</s>; <s>Gāndharvā</s> is <s>Rādhikā</s> herself;

children.text: anurādhā tu lalitā naitāstenoditāḥ pṛthak // RUnm_3.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>Anurādhā</s> is <s>Lalitā</s> — hence these are not mentioned separately. // RUnm_3.57 //
But those known by popular names: <s>Khañjanākṣī</s>, <s>Manoramā</s>,

children.text: maṅgalā vimalā līlā kṛṣṇā śārī viśāradā |
children.translated_text: <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Līlā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Śārī</s>, <s>Viśāradā</s>,
<s>Tārāvalī</s>, <s>Cakorākṣī</s>, <s>Śaṅkarī</s>, <s>Kuṅkumā</s>, and others. // RUnm_3.58 //
Of these and others, there are hundreds of groups (<s>yūthas</s>) of the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: lakṣasaṅkhyāstu kathitā yūthe yūthe varāṅganāḥ // RUnm_3.59 //
children.translated_text: in each group, the excellent women are counted in hundreds of thousands. // RUnm_3.59 //
All these, from <s>Rādhā</s> to <s>Kuṅkumā</s>, are group-leaders (<s>yūthādhipās</s>),

children.text: viśākhāṃ lalitāṃ padmāṃ śaibyāñca prohya kīrtitāḥ // RUnm_3.60 //
children.translated_text: mentioned excluding <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, and <s>Śaibya</s>. // RUnm_3.60 //
However, eight, headed by <s>Rādhā</s>, are considered the foremost in good fortune;
though possessing fitness for group-leadership, <s>Lalitā</s> and the others,
out of desire for the mood of their beloved <s>Rādhā</s> and the others, chose the joy of friendship (<s>sakhya</s>). // RUnm_3.61 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on <s>Śrī Hari's</s> beloveds (<s>Śrī-hari-priyā-prakaraṇam</s>) in the illustrious <s>Ujjvalanīlamaṇi</s>. ||3||
(4) Now begins the chapter on <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> (<s>Śrī-rādhā-prakaraṇam</s>).

children.translated_text: Among them too, in every way the most excellent are these two — <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Candrāvalī</s>,

children.text: yūthayos tu yayoḥ santi koṭi-saṅkhyā mṛgīdṛśaḥ // RUnm_4.1 //
children.translated_text: in whose groups there are tens of millions of doe-eyed [women]. // RUnm_4.1 //
The <s>rāsa</s> [dance] became tumultuous with hundreds of millions of young women

children.text: puline yāmune tasminn ity eṣāgamikī prathā // RUnm_4.2 //
children.translated_text: on that bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> — such is the tradition of the <s>Āgamas</s>. // RUnm_4.2 //

children.text: tayor apy ubhayor madhye rādhikā sarvathādhikā |
children.translated_text: Of the two, <s>Rādhikā</s> is in every way superior;
she is the very form of <s>mahābhāva</s> (the supreme ecstatic love), surpassing all in qualities. // RUnm_4.3 //
In the <s>Gopālottaratāpanī</s> [Upaniṣad], she is celebrated as <s>Gāndharvā</s>;
and in the <s>Ṛk-pariśiṣṭa</s>, she is mentioned as <s>Rādhā</s>, together with <s>Mādhava</s>;
therefore, her greatness has been proclaimed by the divine sage [<s>Nārada</s>] in the <s>Padma</s> [Purāṇa]. // RUnm_4.4 //
Thus indeed —

children.text: yathā rādhā priyā viṣṇos tasyāḥ kuṇḍaṃ priyaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Rādhā</s> is dear to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so is her pond (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) dear to Him;
among all the <s>gopīs</s>, she alone is the supremely beloved of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // RUnm_4.5 //
That great power which is the <s>Hlādinī</s> (bliss-giving) <s>śakti</s>, the greatest of all powers —
she is the very essence and form of that — thus is established in the <s>Tantras</s>. // RUnm_4.6 //
She is of supremely beautiful form, always, this daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>;
adorned with the sixteen decorations (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) and endowed with the twelve ornaments. // RUnm_4.7 //

body.translated_text: Regarding her supremely beautiful form, as stated by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.translated_text: Your hair is beautifully curled, your face has restless, elongated eyes,
your chest bears firm, full breasts, your waist is graced with slenderness,
with your bowed head and vine-like arms, your hands are lovely with jewel-like nails —

children.text: vidhūnayati rādhike tri-jagad eṣa rupotsavaḥ // RUnm_4.8 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhike</s>, this festival of beauty shakes all three worlds! // RUnm_4.8 //

body.translated_text: Now [regarding her being] adorned with the sixteen decorations —

children.translated_text: Bathed, with a jewel gleaming at the tip of her nose, wearing a cloth tinged [with saffron], with a waist-cord, her braid bound,
with an ear-ornament, her body anointed with sandal-paste, flowers in her hair, wearing a garland, holding a lotus in her hand,
her lips reddened with betel, her chin dotted with clusters of beauty-marks (<s>bindu</s>), her eyes lined with collyrium (<s>kajjala</s>), beautifully painted,
<s>Rādhā</s>'s feet shine with lac-dye (<s>alakta</s>), she bears a <s>tilaka</s> — she is adorned with the sixteen decorations. // RUnm_4.9 //

body.translated_text: Now [regarding her being] adorned with the twelve ornaments —

body.text:
divyaś cūḍā-maṇīndraḥ puraṭa-viracitāḥ kuṇḍala-dvandva-kāñci-
niṣkāś cakrī-śalākā-yuga-valaya-ghaṭāḥ kaṇṭha-bhūṣormikāś ca |
hārās tārānukāra bhuja-kaṭaka-tulākoṭayo ratna-k ptās

children.text: tuṅgā pādāṅgurīya-cchavir iti ravibhir bhūṣaṇair bhāti rādhā // RUnm_4.10 //|
children.translated_text: pearl necklaces imitating stars, armlets, toe-rings studded with gems — with [these] twelve ornaments, <s>Rādhā</s> shines resplendently. // RUnm_4.10 //

body.translated_text: A divine crest-jewel, earrings fashioned of gold, waist-chain, necklace-medallion, hairpin-pair, bangles, anklets, neck-ornaments, and finger-rings,

children.translated_text: Now the excellent qualities of the Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> are proclaimed:
she is sweet (<s>madhurā</s>), of fresh youth (<s>nava-vayāḥ</s>), with restless glancing eyes (<s>calāpāṅgī</s>), radiant in her smile (<s>ujjvala-smitā</s>), // RUnm_4.11 //

endowed with beautiful lines of good fortune (<s>saubhāgya-rekhā</s>), her fragrance drives <s>Mādhava</s> to ecstasy, she is learned in the art of music, of delightful speech, and an expert in witty repartee, // RUnm_4.12 //
she is modest (<s>vinītā</s>), full of compassion (<s>karuṇā-pūrṇā</s>), clever (<s>vidagdhā</s>), possessed of dexterity (<s>pāṭava</s>),
of a bashful nature (<s>lajjā-śīlā</s>), well-mannered (<s>sumaryādā</s>), endowed with steadfastness and depth, // RUnm_4.13 //
supremely graceful (<s>suvilāsā</s>), thirsting for the supreme height of <s>mahābhāva</s>,
the dwelling-place of the love of <s>Gokula</s>, her fame shining across the ranks of all the worlds, // RUnm_4.14 //
she has bestowed great affection upon her elders, she is under the sway of her friends' love,
she is the foremost among <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s beloveds, <s>Keśava</s> constantly listens [to hear of her],
in short — her qualities, like <s>Hari</s>'s, are beyond counting. // RUnm_4.15 //

children.text: bahunā kiṃ guṇās tasyāḥ saṅkhyātītā harer iva // RUnm_4.15 //
children.translated_text: Thus, [these qualities] — pertaining to the body, speech, and mind, and those relating to connections with others —
the qualities of the Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> are here stated to be of four kinds. // RUnm_4.16 //

children.text: guṇā vṛndāvaneśvaryā iha proktāś caturvidhāḥ // RUnm_4.16 //
children.translated_text: Sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) is beauty; the fresh age is the middle of adolescence (<s>kaiśora</s>);
the lines of good fortune (<s>saubhāgya-rekhā</s>) are [marks] situated on the feet and so on, such as the crescent moon and the like. // RUnm_4.17 //
Not deviating from the path of the righteous — this is called propriety (<s>maryādā</s>) by the wise;
steadfastness (<s>dhairya</s>) is the capacity to endure suffering, [arising] from modesty, noble birth, and natural disposition. // RUnm_4.18 //
Because of their being self-evident or well-known, the definitions of the others have not been given. // RUnm_4.19 //

body.text: vyaktatvāl lakṣitatvāc ca nānyeṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtam // RUnm_4.19 //
body.translated_text: Regarding [the quality of being] sweet (<s>madhurā</s>), as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (1.32) —
The beauty (<s>lakṣmī</s>) of [her] eyes forcibly swallows fresh blue lotuses,

children.text: balād akṣṇor lakṣmīḥ kavalayati navyaṃ kuvalayaṃ
children.translated_text: the radiance of [her] face surpasses a fully blossomed lotus grove,
the loveliness of [her] limbs drives even the eight-footed [<s>Śarabha</s>] to a wretched state —

children.text: daśāṃ kaṣṭām aṣṭā-padam api nayaty āṅgika-rucir
children.translated_text: wondrous indeed is the indescribable beauty of <s>Rādhā</s> that shines forth! // RUnm_4.20 //

children.text: vicitraṃ rādhāyāḥ kim api kila rūpaṃ vilasati // RUnm_4.20 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding] fresh youth (<s>nava-vayāḥ</s>) —

children.text: śroṇiḥ syandanatāṃ kṛśodari kuca-dvandvaṃ kramāc cakratāṃ
children.translated_text: your eyebrow has attained the beauty of a bow, this pair of eyes has acquired swiftness;

children.text: bhrūś cāpa-śriyam īkṣaṇa-dvayam idaṃ yāty āśugatvaṃ tava |
children.translated_text: therefore, having bestowed the generalship upon you on earth, <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love),

children.text: saināpatyam ataḥ pradāya bhuvi te kāmaḥ paśūnāṃ patiṃ
children.translated_text: vanquishing the lord of beasts [<s>Śiva</s>], the proud one who shakes [the worlds], has placed in you his own imperial burden. // RUnm_4.21 //

children.text: dhunvan jitvara-māninaṃ tvayi nijaṃ sāmrājya-bhāraṃ nyadhāt // RUnm_4.21 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding] restless-glanced (<s>capalāpāṅgī</s>) —

body.translated_text: O slender-waisted one, your hips have become a chariot, your pair of breasts gradually [have become] wheels,

children.translated_text: or is this corner of your eye itself a lightning bolt?

children.text: vidhu-mukhi taḍito vā kiṃ tavāyaṃ dṛgantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Surely, O <s>Rādhe</s>, the corner of your eye has great weight,
for it conquers even the mind of me, the most excellent of swift-moving ones. // RUnm_4.22 //

children.text: varam atijavināṃ me yena jigye mano'pi // RUnm_4.22 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding her] radiant smile (<s>ujjvala-smitā</s>) —

body.translated_text: O moon-faced one, did lightning learn its excessive flickering from the corner of your eye,

children.translated_text: washed by the nectar of your smile,
O friend, the excellent <s>cakora</s>-bird that is the destroyer of sin [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]
rises up, his mind intoxicated by the thrill of delight. // RUnm_4.23 //
Now [regarding her being] endowed with beautiful lines of good fortune —

body.translated_text: Beholding, in the creation of your face, the line of your lower lip

children.translated_text: pervaded by the spreading lines of good fortune,
with their portions resembling crescents, circles, flowers, vines, and earring-shapes,
beautifully point out <s>Rādhā</s> hidden here. // RUnm_4.24 //
Now [regarding] her fragrance driving <s>Mādhava</s> to ecstasy —

body.translated_text: O destroyer of sins, be content — behold: the footprints of <s>Rādhā</s>,
O <s>Mādhavī</s>, O empress of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, do not make futile efforts

children.translated_text: to conceal yourself among clusters of creeper-leaves and sprouts!

children.text: mā vṛndāvana-cakravartini kṛthā yatnaṃ mudhā mādhavi |
children.translated_text: O friend, that rogue <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lord of bees,
swaying about, will surely pursue you, indicated by his own intoxicating rival-fragrances. // RUnm_4.25 //

children.text: kṛṣṇas tāṃ bhramādhipaḥ sakhi dhuvan dhūrto dhruvaṃ dhāsyati // RUnm_4.25 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding her being] learned in the art of music —

body.translated_text: O <s>Rādhike</s>, abandon your eagerness for singing in the fifth note (<s>pañcama</s>)

children.translated_text: which steals the black deer [attracting them],
before [your] husband, the most irascible one, looks upon
you being chased by [those] deer! // RUnm_4.26 //

children.text: tvāṃ na yāvad atiroṣaṇaḥ patiḥ // RUnm_4.26 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding her] delightful speech —
that shimmers on your lips?
The <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) feels inadequate thereby, O friend,
and even nectar becomes futile today. // RUnm_4.27 //
Now [regarding her being] an expert in witty repartee —

body.translated_text: O <s>Rādhike</s>, of beautiful face, what is this sweetness of syllables

children.translated_text: or is Your flute the female teacher here?
For both of you have no other occupation
than stealing the virtue of family women.' // RUnm_4.28 //
Or, as another example —

body.translated_text: [<s>Rādhā</s> to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:] 'Are You the teacher of the flute-lineage,

children.translated_text: eternally purified by the worship of the breasts of virtuous women!
I offer you the churning [in exchange] for sun-worship —
alas, I have bathed [for worship]; do not touch, do not touch my body!' // RUnm_4.29 //

children.text: snātāsmi hanta mama na spṛśa na spṛśāṅgam // RUnm_4.29 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding her being] modest (<s>vinītā</s>) —

body.translated_text: 'O Lord, be gracious, O <s>Vṛṣavardhana</s> (increaser of bulls), of sacred fame,

children.translated_text: Though famous in <s>Gokula</s>, though restrained by her companions from [her] eyebrow-flirtations,

children.text: api gokule prasiddhā bhrū-bhramibhiḥ parijanair niṣiddhāpi |
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> left [her] seat even upon seeing <s>Bhadrikā</s> from afar. // RUnm_4.30 //

children.text: pīṭhaṃ mumoca rādhā bhadrikām api dūrataḥ prekṣya // RUnm_4.30 //
children.translated_text: Or, as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (5.15) —
I have been accepted by the praiseworthy enemy of sin [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>];
therein, O slender-waisted friends, what other reason can there be

children.text: tatra kṣāmodari kim aparaṃ kāraṇaṃ vaḥ sakhīnāṃ
children.translated_text: except the spreading cluster of [your] abundant compassion?' // RUnm_4.31 //
Now [regarding her being] full of compassion (<s>karuṇā-pūrṇā</s>) —

body.translated_text: 'Though I, <s>Rādhā</s>, was again and again at fault through the play of quarrels,

children.translated_text: with tear-filled eyes,
<s>Rādhā</s>, having shared its pain, compassionately
applies saffron to its wound. // RUnm_4.32 //
Now [regarding her being] clever (<s>vidagdhā</s>) —

body.translated_text: Seeing a calf with its face pricked even by a blade of straw,

children.translated_text: she bewilders even a master in debates of speech, learned in the craft of garland-making,

children.text: vāg-yuddhe mugdhayantī gurum api ca girāṃ paṇḍitā mālya-gumphe |
children.translated_text: clever in training <s>śārī</s>-birds and parrots, victorious even against the undefeated in games of dice —

children.text: pāṭhe śārī-śukānāṃ paṭur ajitam api dyūta-keliṣu jiṣṇur
children.translated_text: this <s>Rādhikā</s> shines, her intellect radiant with arts, endowed with the art of love. // RUnm_4.33 //
Now [regarding her] dexterity (<s>pāṭava</s>), as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (3.3) —

body.translated_text: A teacher in mineral painting, of charming mind skilled in the art of cooking,
'O friend, my dear pearl necklace has broken — let me',

children.translated_text: she said, 'gather the round pearls' — with this pretext,
innocently revealing a sidelong glance toward me,
<s>Rādhā</s> artfully cast it out of love, even before her elder. // RUnm_4.34 //

children.text: rādhā guror api puraḥ praṇayād vyatānīt // RUnm_4.34 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding her] bashful nature (<s>lajjā-śīlā</s>) —

body.translated_text: 'This son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, so rare to behold, appears;

children.translated_text: this person too is languishing from thirst [to see him];

children.text: sphurati rahasi tāmyaty eṣa tarṣāj jano'pi |
children.translated_text: withdraw a little, O mother Modesty! Opening my face slightly,

children.text: virama janani lajje kiñcid udghāṭya vaktraṃ
children.translated_text: let me just cast a corner-glance, if only for a blink!' // RUnm_4.35 //

children.text: nimiṣam iha manāg apy akṣi-koṇaṃ kṣipāmi // RUnm_4.35 //
children.translated_text: Now [regarding her being] well-mannered (<s>sumaryādā</s>) —
'O friend, <s>Rādhā</s>, like a <s>cātaka</s> bird [who drinks only rain], would rather give up her life-breath unfed,

children.text: prāṇān akṛtāhārā sakhi rādhā-cātakī varaṃ tyajati |
children.translated_text: [than accept anything from another source].'

children.text: na tu kṛṣṇa-mudira-muktād amṛtād vṛttiṃ bhajed aparām // RUnm_4.36 //
children.translated_text: but would not resort to any other sustenance than the nectar released from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s rain-cloud [lips]. // RUnm_4.36 //
Or, for example —

children.text: āhūyamānā vrajanāthayāsmi yukto'bhisāraḥ sakhi nādhunā me |
children.translated_text: 'I have been summoned by the lord of <s>Vraja</s> — the rendezvous (<s>abhisāra</s>) is fitting, dear friend, but not for me just now;

children.text: na tādṛśīnāṃ hi gurūttamānām ājñāsv avajñā valate śivāya // RUnm_4.37 //
children.translated_text: for in the commands of such greatly revered elders, disobedience does not conduce to auspiciousness.' // RUnm_4.37 //

children.text: pūrṇāśīḥ pūrṇimāsāv anavahitatayā yā tvayāsyai vitīrṇā
children.translated_text: 'The full blessing you bestowed upon her on the full-moon night through inattention —

children.text: vaṣṭi tvām eva tanvann akhila-madhurimotsekam asyāṃ mukundaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Mukunda</s> himself, overflowing with all sweetness, desires you alone in her;

children.text: diṣṭyā parvodagāt te svayam abhisaraṇe cittam ādhatsva vatse
children.translated_text: fortunately the festival-night has arrived — set your mind upon going to meet him, child' —

children.text: yuktyāpy uktā mayeti dyumaṇi-sakha-sutā prāhiṇod eva citrām // RUnm_4.38 //
children.translated_text: thus counseling wisely, the daughter of <s>Dyumaṇi</s>'s friend sent <s>Citrā</s> forth. // RUnm_4.38 //

children.text: tīvras tarjati bhinna-dhīr gṛha-patiś chadma-jñayā padmayā
children.translated_text: The confused householder fiercely threatens; <s>Padmā</s>, who knows the secret,

children.text: hāraṃ hārayati hari-praṇihitaṃ kīśena bhartuḥ svasā |
children.translated_text: makes off with the necklace that <s>Hari</s> had placed [as a love-token], through [the agency of] a monkey; her husband's sister, <s>Śaivyā</s>,

children.text: mallīṃ lumpati kṛṣṇa-kāmya-kusumāṃ śaivyā priyā varkarī
children.translated_text: plucks the <s>mallī</s> [jasmine] blossoms desired by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; her dear [co-wife] <s>Varkarī</s> [also obstructs] —

children.text: rādhā paśya tathāpy atīva sahanā tuṣṇīm asau tiṣṭhati // RUnm_4.39 //
children.translated_text: yet look, <s>Rādhā</s>, even so, she remains exceedingly forbearing and silent. // RUnm_4.39 //

body.translated_text: Now, the one endowed with fortitude (<s>dhairya-śālinī</s>) —

children.translated_text: In the state [called] '<s>kalahāntaritā</s>' (separated by a quarrel),
dear friend, <s>Rādhikā</s>, having assumed the posture of a composed (<s>dhīrā</s>) woman today —
outwardly displaying the signs of exalted pride (<s>māna</s>),
became unfathomable, even for <s>Lalitā</s>'s intellect. // RUnm_4.40 //

body.translated_text: Now, the one endowed with gravity (<s>gāmbhīrya-śālinī</s>) —

children.translated_text: With the beauty of her glancing, darting, sidelong eyes, with eyebrow-creepers shimmering in dance,
with her face radiant as the moon of a jasmine-white smile, with earrings swaying upon her cheeks,
drawing forth speech dense with the perfected <s>mantras</s> of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Love's) arrival,

children.text: hāriṇy adya harer jahāra hṛdayaṃ rādhā vilāsormibhiḥ // RUnm_4.41 //
children.translated_text: today, enchanting <s>Rādhā</s> stole <s>Hari</s>'s heart with waves of her <s>vilāsa</s> (graceful charm). // RUnm_4.41 //

body.translated_text: Now, the one who thirsts for the supreme exaltation of <s>mahābhāva</s> (<s>mahābhāva-paramotkarṣa-tarṣiṇī</s>) —

children.translated_text: Doubling the cascade of the daughter of <s>Arka</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) with excessive downpours of tears,
bearing a body that is the semblance of a moonstone streaming with moonlight,
today, having attained the form of a <s>kadamba</s> tree through <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation) breaking forth to the tips of her throat-syllables,

children.text: rādhā veṇu-dhara pravāta-kadalī-tulyā kvacid vartate // RUnm_4.42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, O bearer of the flute, stands somewhere like a plantain tree swaying in the wind. // RUnm_4.42 //

body.translated_text: Now, the abode of the love of <s>Gokula</s> (<s>gokula-prema-vasati</s>) —

children.translated_text: Surely by the continuous streams of love alone
did the Creator fashion the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>;
she has attained such a state [that] she renders
the minds of all of us <s>Gokula</s>-dwellers affectionate. // RUnm_4.43 //

body.translated_text: Now, the one whose fame shines throughout the ranks of the universe (<s>jagac-chreṇī-lasad-yaśāḥ</s>) —

children.translated_text: Making the blue lotus bloom upon reaching the ears of the wife of <s>Devendra</s> (<s>Śacī</s>),
casting down the <s>kunda</s> [jasmine], delighting the locks of the wife of <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>),
melting the moon-gem jewel that adorns the ear — O auspicious-limbed one,

children.text: lakṣmīm apy adhunā cakāra cakitāṃ rādhe yaśaḥ-kaumudī // RUnm_4.44 //
children.translated_text: your fame-moonlight, O <s>Rādhā</s>, has now made even <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself agitated. // RUnm_4.44 //

body.translated_text: Now, the one who has offered deep affection to her elders (<s>gurv-arpita-guru-snehā</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'You are not the daughter of <s>Kīrtidā</s>,
but mine alone' — thus I declare the truth.
'I live only upon seeing your face —
it is just like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s' — why are you ashamed? // RUnm_4.45 //

body.translated_text: Now, the one dependent on the love of her friends (<s>sakhī-praṇayādhīnā</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'Instruct him, friend <s>Vṛndā</s>, the son of the lord of cowherds —

children.text: kim ayam iha sakhīnāṃ mām adhīnāṃ dunoti |
children.translated_text: why does he torment me here, who am under the authority of my friends?
Let him depart apprehensively from the abodes of the proud women;

children.text: kalayati lalitāyāḥ kiṃ na śauṭīrya-dhāṭīm // RUnm_4.46 //
children.translated_text: does he not reckon with the bold audacity of <s>Lalitā</s>?' // RUnm_4.46 //

body.translated_text: Now, the foremost among the beloved companions of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (<s>kṛṣṇa-priyāvalī-mukhyā</s>), as in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (10.10) —

children.translated_text: 'Let there be fair-browed women who are the playground of the sport of darting sidelong glances;

children.text: svasti syān madirekṣaṇe kṣaṇam api tvām antarā me kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: blessings upon the doe-eyed ones — but without you, even for a moment, where is [joy] for me?
Even when the moon, attended by a cluster of stars, is embraced in the sky,

children.text: nākāśe vṛṣabhānujāṃ śriyam ṛte niṣpadyate svaś-chaṭā // RUnm_4.47 //
children.translated_text: without the splendor of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, the radiant glow does not manifest.' // RUnm_4.47 //

body.translated_text: Now, the one to whom <s>Keśava</s> perpetually yields (<s>santatāśrava-keśavā</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'Heaps of flowers tormented by swarms of bees I have gathered,
and the entire, unbroken peacock plumage [as well], O <s>Rādhikā</s>, at your command;
I have left untouched the fresh sprouts blazing with the rising sun —

children.text: karotu vaśago janaḥ kim ayam anyad-ājñāpaya // RUnm_4.48 //
children.translated_text: let this obedient servant do as you will; command something else!' // RUnm_4.48 //
In whose supreme group are fair-browed women adorned with every noble quality,
whose enchanting charms attract <s>Mādhava</s> from all sides. // RUnm_4.49 //

children.text: tās tu vṛndāvaneśvaryāḥ sakhyaḥ pañca-vidhā matāḥ |
children.translated_text: The friends of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> are considered to be of five kinds:

children.text: sakhyaś ca nitya-sakhyaś ca prāṇa-sakhyaś ca kāścana |
children.translated_text: ordinary friends (<s>sakhī</s>s), constant friends (<s>nitya-sakhī</s>s), life-friends (<s>prāṇa-sakhī</s>s),

children.text: priya-sakhyaś ca parama-preṣṭha-sakhyaś ca viśrutāḥ // RUnm_4.50 //
children.translated_text: dear friends (<s>priya-sakhī</s>s), and most beloved friends (<s>parama-preṣṭha-sakhī</s>s) — thus they are celebrated. // RUnm_4.50 //
The ordinary friends (<s>sakhīs</s>) are <s>Kusumikā</s>, <s>Vindhyā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, and the like.
The constant friends (<s>nitya-sakhīs</s>) are <s>Kastūrī</s>, <s>Maṇi-mañjarī</s>, and the like. // RUnm_4.51 //
The life-friends (<s>prāṇa-sakhīs</s>) are <s>Śaśimukhī</s>, <s>Vāsantī</s>, <s>Lāsikā</s>, and the like;
these have mostly attained the very form (<s>svarūpa</s>) of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. // RUnm_4.52 //
The dear friends (<s>priya-sakhīs</s>) are <s>Kuraṅgākṣī</s>, <s>Sumadhyā</s>, <s>Madanālasā</s>,
<s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Mādhurī</s>, <s>Mañju-keśī</s>, <s>Kandarpa-sundarī</s>,
<s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Mālatī</s>, <s>Kāma-latā</s>, <s>Śaśikalā</s>, and the like. // RUnm_4.53 //
The most beloved friends (<s>parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs</s>) are <s>Lalitā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>,
<s>Citrā</s>, <s>Campakalatā</s>, <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>, <s>Indulekhā</s>,
<s>Raṅgadevī</s>, and <s>Sudevī</s> — these eight are the foremost of all groups. // RUnm_4.54 //

children.text: āsāṃ suṣṭhu dvayor eva premṇaḥ parama-kāṣṭhayā |
children.translated_text: Of these, in the case of two alone, by the supreme limit of love,

children.text: kvacij jātu kvacij jātu tad-ādhikyam ivekṣate // RUnm_4.55 //
children.translated_text: sometimes, very rarely, a slight excess [of love over the others] is perceived. // RUnm_4.55 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> in the illustrious <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>. ||4||
(5) Now begins the chapter on the classification of heroines (<s>nāyikā-bheda-prakaraṇa</s>).

children.text: yūthe'py avāntara-gaṇās teṣu ca kaścid gaṇas tri-caturābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Within a group (<s>yūtha</s>), there are also sub-groups (<s>avāntara-gaṇas</s>); and among them, one sub-group consists of three or four;

children.text: iha pañca-ṣābhir anyaḥ saptāṣṭābhis tathety ādyāḥ // RUnm_5.1 //
children.translated_text: another of five or six here; another of seven or eight — and so forth in the beginning. // RUnm_5.1 //

children.text: nāsau nāṭye rase mukhye yat paroḍhā nigadyate |
children.translated_text: The <s>paroḍhā</s> (another's wife) that is mentioned in dramatic [theory] for the principal <s>rasa</s> —
that classification applies [only] to the ordinary, base heroines and the like. // RUnm_5.2 //

children.text: neṣṭā yad aṅgini rase kavibhir paroḍhā
children.translated_text: 'That the <s>paroḍhā</s> is not desired by poets in the principal <s>rasa</s> of the heroine —
that [rule holds] except for the family of the lotus-eyed women of <s>Gokula</s>,
who were brought down with the hope of the practice of <s>rasa</s>
by the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the crest-jewel of the assembly of <s>rasikas</s>.' // RUnm_5.3 //
They have perfectly attained firm devotion to the status of <s>Vrajendranandana</s> (the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>);

children.text: yāsāṃ bhāvasya sā mudrā sad-bhaktair api durgamā // RUnm_5.4 //
children.translated_text: the seal of their <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) is inaccessible even to true devotees. // RUnm_5.4 //

children.text: gopīnāṃ paśupendra-nandana-juṣo bhāvasya kas tāṃ krtī
children.translated_text: 'Who is the capable person that can comprehend the nature
of the <s>bhāva</s> of the <s>gopīs</s> toward the son of the lord of cowherds — a <s>bhāva</s> that traverses unfathomable paths?

children.text: āviṣkurvati vaiṣṇavīm api tanuṃ tasmin bhujair jiṣṇubhi*
children.translated_text: Even when he reveals his <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (four-armed) form before them, with his victorious arms,

children.text: ryāsāṃ hanta caturbhir adbhuta-ruciṃ rāgodayaḥ kuñcati // RUnm_5.5 //
children.translated_text: alas, the rising passion of those women contracts [in disappointment] at that wondrous, four-armed beauty.' // RUnm_5.5 //
Even when <s>Hari</s> sometimes displays his four arms in jest,
by the love of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, he is made two-armed [again]. // RUnm_5.6 //
'At the commencement of the <s>Rāsa</s> [dance], when the doe-eyed women who had been hiding in the bower

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ gopayituṃ svam uddhura-dhiyā yā suṣṭhu sandarśitā |
children.translated_text: saw [his four-armed form] and he, with exuberant intention, wished to conceal his own [identity], she was beautifully revealed [as supreme] —

children.text: rādhāyāḥ praṇayasya hanta mahimā yasya śriyā rakṣituṃ
children.translated_text: alas, such is the greatness of <s>Rādhā</s>'s love that, to protect its splendor,

children.text: sā śakyā prabhaviṣṇunāpi hariṇā nāsīc catur-bāhutā // RUnm_5.7 //
children.translated_text: even all-powerful <s>Hari</s> could not maintain his four-armed form.' // RUnm_5.7 //
Moreover —
Because of the connection with <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>), even such a <s>sāmānyā</s> (common woman) is [classified] thus;

children.text: bhāva-yogāt tu sairindhrī parakīyaiva sammatā // RUnm_5.8 //
children.translated_text: but by virtue of [genuine] <s>bhāva</s>-connection, a <s>sairindhrī</s> (maidservant) is indeed considered <s>parakīyā</s> (belonging to another). // RUnm_5.8 //

body.text:
sāmānyā vanitā veśyā sā dravyaṃ param icchatā |
guṇa-hīne ca na dveṣo nānurāgo guṇiny api |
śṛṅgārābhāsa etāsu na śṛṅgāraḥ kadācana // RUnm_5.9 // iti |
body.translated_text: 'A <s>sāmānyā</s> (common) woman is a courtesan; she desires only wealth. She has no hatred toward the unmeritorious, nor attachment to the meritorious. In regard to such women, there is only <s>śṛṅgārābhāsa</s> (semblance of erotic <s>rasa</s>), never true <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.' // RUnm_5.9 //

children.text: svakīyāś ca paroḍhāś ca yā dvidhā parikīrtitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those [heroines] who are celebrated as twofold — <s>svakīyā</s> (one's own wife) and <s>paroḍhā</s> (another's wife) —

children.text: mugdhā madhyā pragalbheti pratyekaṃ tās tridhā matāḥ // RUnm_5.10 //
children.translated_text: each of them is further considered threefold: <s>mugdhā</s> (innocent), <s>madhyā</s> (moderate), and <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold). // RUnm_5.10 //

children.text: bheda-trayam idaṃ kaiścit svīyāyā eva varṇitam |
children.translated_text: This threefold division has been described by some as applying to the <s>svīyā</s> (one's own wife) alone;
nevertheless, since it is observed in the works of excellent poets, that [restriction] is disregarded. // RUnm_5.11 //

body.translated_text: And thus the ancient authorities state —

children.translated_text: 'Some extend this differentiation of examples to all [types of heroines];

children.text: tās tu prāyeṇa dṛśyante sarvatra vyavahārataḥ // RUnm_5.12 //
children.translated_text: and indeed, they are generally observed in practice everywhere.' // RUnm_5.12 //
Of these, the <s>mugdhā</s> (innocent one) —
The <s>mugdhā</s> is of fresh youth, newly awakened to desire, contrary in love-making, under the authority of her friends,
and in the acts of love, she makes charmingly bashful, hidden efforts. // RUnm_5.13 //
When the beloved is at fault, her gaze is choked with tears;

children.text: priyāpriyoktau cāśaktā māne ca vimukhī sadā // RUnm_5.14 //
children.translated_text: unable to speak words both pleasing and displeasing, and in the state of <s>māna</s> (love-anger), she always turns her face away. // RUnm_5.14 //
Of these, one of fresh youth (<s>nava-vayāḥ</s>) —
'As the winter of childhood recedes and the springtime of youth enters for <s>Viśākhā</s>,

children.text: dīvyati locana-kamalaṃ, vadana-sudhāṃśuś ca visphurati // RUnm_5.15 //
children.translated_text: her lotus-eyes bloom, and the moon of her face radiates.' // RUnm_5.15 //

children.text: bālya-dhvānta sakhe prayāhi tarasā rādhā-vapur dvīpata-
children.translated_text: 'O darkness of childhood, friend, depart quickly from the island of <s>Rādhā</s>'s body,

children.text: stāruṇya-dyumaṇer yad eṣa vijayārambhaḥ puro jṛmbhate |
children.translated_text: for the sun of her youth — behold — this triumphant onset is unfolding before us!

children.text: kṛṣṇa-vyomni rucir darottaralatā tārā-dyutau kāpy uraḥ-
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-sky of her complexion, a certain surpassing radiance; in the starlight of her eyes, a wave of boldness; upon the eastern mountain

children.text: pūrvādrau suṣamonnatiḥ smita-kalā paśyādya vaktrāmbuje // RUnm_5.16 //
children.translated_text: of her bosom, an elevation of loveliness; in the lotus of her face, a crescent of smiles — behold today!' // RUnm_5.16 //
'O young girl, when the erotic festival (<s>smarotsava</s>) of the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> is being praised by deceit
by the mature cowherd women, you sit with lowered face, lending your ear;
even in the fashioning of forest garlands, you assume delight with a pretext —

children.text: raṅgaḥ ko'yam avātarad vada sakhi svānte navīnas tava // RUnm_5.17 //
children.translated_text: what is this new drama, tell me, dear friend, that has descended into your heart?' // RUnm_5.17 //

body.translated_text: One newly awakened to desire (<s>nava-kāmā</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: 'I am a young, fresh girl — do not make such jests;
release my path, O you crowned with a peacock feather!
See — the skilled [friends] are fashioning the bank of this
river, the daughter of the friend of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), with arching brows.' // RUnm_5.18 //

body.translated_text: Contrary in love-making (<s>ratau vāmā</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: 'On the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, [I remember her] turning away from my gaze,
her hand held by her smiling friend,
saying "Please release my hand" with words
that trembled sweetly — I remember that wagtail-eyed one.' // RUnm_5.19 //
'O prince of the cowherds, harsh one —
I shall not entrust this tender girl to you;
who, being wise, would place a newly blooming

children.text: nalinīṃ kaḥ kurute janaḥ kṛtī // RUnm_5.20 //
children.translated_text: lotus into the trunk of a young elephant?' // RUnm_5.20 //

body.translated_text: Under the authority of her friends (<s>sakhī-vaśā</s>) —

body.text:
yathā vā-
na svīkṛtā sakhi mayā srag ihāsti kaundī
kiṃ dīrgha-roṣa-vikaṭāṃ bhru-kuṭīṃ tanoṣi |
kṣipteyam atra mama maṇḍana-peṭikāyāṃ

children.text: ced vṛndayā caṭulayā kim ahaṃ kariṣye // RUnm_5.21|
children.translated_text: if mischievous <s>Vṛndā</s> did it, what am I to do?' // RUnm_5.21 //

body.translated_text: Or, for example — 'This <s>kunda</s> garland here, friend, was not accepted by me — why do you knit those fearfully long, angry brows? It was thrown here into my ornament-casket;

children.text: dvitrāṇy etya padāni kuñja-vasater dvāre vilāsonmukhī
children.translated_text: 'Having advanced two or three steps toward the entrance of the bower-dwelling, inclined toward amorous play,
her body-creeper suddenly trembling with waves of agitation, she turned sideways out of modesty;
then again, drawn by the fragrance of her intimate friend's words toward the bed,

children.text: svāntaṃ hanta jahāra hāri-hariṇī-netrā mama śyāmalā // RUnm_5.22 //
children.translated_text: alas, she stole my heart — that dark-complexioned one with the beautiful deer-like eyes.' // RUnm_5.22 //

body.translated_text: One whose efforts in love are bashful (<s>savrīḍa-rata-prayatnā</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: 'Even when you, of pure heart, have committed an offense, my friend —
how can she, tongue-tied, speak to you, the ungracious one?
Do not torment her, O serpent of the <s>kadamba</s> grove —

children.text: vaktraṃ pidhāya kurutām iyam aśru-mokṣam // RUnm_5.23 //
children.translated_text: let her cover her face and shed her tears.' // RUnm_5.23 //

body.translated_text: One whose silence and tears are caused by anger (<s>roṣa-kṛta-bāṣpa-maunā</s>), for example —

children.text: mṛdvī tathākṣamā ceti sā māne vimukhī dvidhā // RUnm_5.24 //
children.translated_text: She who turns away in <s>māna</s> is of two kinds: the gentle (<s>mṛdvī</s>) and the impatient (<s>akṣamā</s>). // RUnm_5.24 //
