body.translated_text: Now, the one who turns away in <s>māna</s> (love-anger) —

children.translated_text: 'Even as my feet endeavored to turn away, upon his approaching they resumed their course [toward him];

children.text: bhrūbhedo'pi tad īkṣaṇa-vyasaninā vyasmāri me cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: even my knitting of brows was undone by my eyes, addicted to gazing at him;
my burnt tongue utters flattering words even to the harsh-lettered one —

children.text: sakhyaḥ kiṃ karavāṇi māna-samaye saṅghāta-bhedo mama // RUnm_5.25 //
children.translated_text: what shall I do, friends? In the time of my <s>māna</s>, my resolve is shattered.' // RUnm_5.25 //

body.translated_text: Of these, the gentle one (<s>mṛdvī</s>), as in <s>Rasa-sudhākara</s> (1.44) —

children.translated_text: 'Alas, the audacity of the lotus-eyed cowherd women,

children.text: yā keśave kṣaṇam api praṇayanti mānam |
children.translated_text: who display <s>māna</s> (love-anger) toward <s>Keśava</s> even for a moment!
Even as the two syllables "<s>mā-na</s>" arrive at the courtyard of my ears,
my inner self trembles.' // RUnm_5.26 //
Now, the <s>madhyā</s> (moderate heroine) —
She in whom bashfulness and desire are equal, who possesses the splendor of dawning youth,
Speaking somewhat boldly, capable of love-making unto the point of swooning,

children.text: madhyā syāt komalā kvāpi māne kutrāpi karkaśā // RUnm_5.27 //
children.translated_text: the <s>madhyā</s> (intermediate heroine) is sometimes tender, sometimes harsh in her wounded pride (<s>māna</s>). // RUnm_5.27 //
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, full of longing, gazes, she scatters the lotus of her eyes;
<s>Rādhā</s> lowers her face, concealing an inner smile;
she places her gaze on him, then looks elsewhere — [then looks at] him again;

children.text: tad api sarasijākṣī tasya modaṃ vyatānīt // RUnm_5.28 //
children.translated_text: even so, the lotus-eyed one gave him delight. // RUnm_5.28 //

body.translated_text: Therein, [an example of] one whose shyness and passion are equal —

children.translated_text: The play of your eyebrows swallows the glory of the bow of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love);
your pair of thighs mocks the beauty of the plantain tree;
your pair of breasts bears the playfulness of the chariot-wheels [of the love-god];

children.text: varorūṇāṃ rādhe taruṇimani cūrāmaṇir asi // RUnm_5.29 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhā</s>, among beautiful women, you are the crest-jewel of youth. // RUnm_5.29 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] one in the bloom of dawning youth —

children.translated_text: 'O black bee of [my] lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who persistently serves, intoxicated by the fragrance of my lotus-face,
why do you create further obstacles?
If you, with mind distracted by longing for sweet sounds, [seek nectar] then go ahead

children.text: puṣpaiḥ pāṇḍu-cchavim aviralair yāhi puṃnāga-kuñjam // RUnm_5.30 //
children.translated_text: to the bower of <s>punnāga</s> trees, [adorned] with abundant pale blossoms.' // RUnm_5.30 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] somewhat bold speech, as in the <s>Uddhava-sandeśa</s> (54) —

children.translated_text: Drenched in the perspiration of exertion, her eyes closed,
her hair loosened, her vine-like arms no longer under her control,
her mind joyful, all other thoughts forgotten —
I remember the <s>gopī</s> on the bed of love at night. // RUnm_5.31 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] one capable of love-making unto swooning —

children.text: prāṇās tvam eva kim iva tvayi gopanīyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'You are my very life — what could be concealed from you?
O friend, I am not capable of holding my pride (<s>māna</s>) against the slayer of <s>Keśī</s>.
Come, let us go to the grove on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
O auspicious one, on the pretext of gathering blossoming flowers.' // RUnm_5.32 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] tender in her wounded pride (<s>māna</s>) —

children.text: mudhā mānonnāhād glapayasi kim aṅgāni kaṭhine
children.translated_text: 'Why do you uselessly exhaust your limbs, O hard-hearted one, through the exertion of wounded pride?
Or why do you hold anger when your beloved companions entreat you?
The lord of your bower-dwelling languishes before you —

children.text: kṛpā-lakṣmīvantaṃ caṭulaya dṛgantaṃ kṣaṇam iha // RUnm_5.33 //
children.translated_text: cast a glance of compassion from the corner of your eye for but a moment.' // RUnm_5.33 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] harsh in her wounded pride, as in the <s>Vidagdha-mādhava</s> (5.30) —
She is threefold according to her behavior in wounded pride (<s>māna</s>): <s>dhīrā</s> (steadfast), <s>adhīrā</s> (unsteadfast), and of both natures (<s>ubhayātmikā</s>). // RUnm_5.34 //

children.text: dhīrā tu vakti vakroktyā sotprāsaṃ sāgasaṃ priyam // RUnm_5.35 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dhīrā</s> (steadfast) speaks to her beloved with indirect speech (<s>vakrokti</s>), with sarcasm, pointing out his offenses. // RUnm_5.35 //
'O Lord, it is fitting for you — whose body bears blue and red [marks] from the collyrium
and fresh lac-dye transferred [from another woman] everywhere — to wear the crescent moon.

children.text: ekaṃ kintv avalocayāmy anucitaṃ haṃho paśūnāṃ pate
children.translated_text: But I observe one thing unfitting — alas, O Lord of animals,

children.text: dehārdhe dayitāṃ vahan bahumatām atrāsi yan nāgataḥ // RUnm_5.36 //
children.translated_text: bearing your beloved on half your body with great esteem, you have not come here [as Ardhanārīśvara]!' // RUnm_5.36 //

children.text: adhīrā paruṣair vākyair nirasyed vallabhaṃ ruṣā // RUnm_5.37 //

children.text: jhaṅkāronmukhara prayāhi tarasā yuktātra nāvasthitiḥ // RUnm_5.38 //
children.translated_text: buzzing loudly with the humming of your fabricated stories — depart quickly! It is not right to stay here!' // RUnm_5.38 //

children.text: dhīrādhīra tu vakroktyā sa-bāṣpaṃ vadati priyam // RUnm_5.39 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dhīrādhīrā</s> (steadfast-unsteadfast) speaks to her beloved with indirect speech, with tears. // RUnm_5.39 //
'O son of the chief of the cowherds, do not weep — go, go!
She, the presiding deity of your heart, will show you her anger.
The saffron paste from the garland on your head [has stained] her feet —
now adorn that pair of feet again with this [paste].' // RUnm_5.40 //

children.text: tām eva pratipadya kāma-varadāṃ sevasva devīṃ sadā
children.translated_text: 'Serve her always, that goddess who grants the desires of love,
by whose great favor, O <s>Dāmodara</s>, you now rejoice!
Your head is marked with the lac of her feet, your mouth glows with the remnants of her betel,

children.text: sarva eva rasotkarṣo madhyāyām eva yujyate |
children.translated_text: The highest excellence of <s>rasa</s> is appropriate only in the <s>madhyā</s> (intermediate heroine),

children.text: visphāraṃ ca nitamba-maṇḍalam idaṃ rodhaḥ-śriyaṃ luṇṭhati |
children.translated_text: and this broad region of your hips plunders the beauty of a river-bank;

children.text: tāruṇyāmṛta-sampadā tvam adhikaṃ candrāvali kṣālitā // RUnm_5.44 //

body.translated_text: Therein, [an example of] one of full youth —

children.text: rnāhaṃ tatra vidāmbabhūva kim abhūt kṛtyaṃ kilātaḥparam // RUnm_5.45 //
children.translated_text: I was not conscious there — what indeed happened after that?' // RUnm_5.45 //

body.translated_text: Now, [an example of] one blind with passion —

children.translated_text: 'Of the love-play with rising abandon, [the bed] marked with pairs of broad nail-prints,
the peacock-feather ornament slipping, the necklace of pure and shining <s>guñjā</s> berries breaking,

children.text: manas tām evoccair maṇita-ramaṇīyāṃ mṛgayate // RUnm_5.46 //
children.translated_text: O friend, my mind seeks that very [play], made beautiful by the moaning [of passion].' // RUnm_5.46 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] one greatly eager for love-making —

children.translated_text: 'With sidelong glances darting in chains, eyebrows fully arched,
face covered with the budding of a meaningful smile, hair standing on end,
you sit radiantly in the bower for long, your voice [like the] cooing of a <s>vīṇā</s> —

children.text: baddhuṃ bandhura-gātri kṛṣṇa-hariṇaṃ śaṅke tvam ākāṅkṣasi // RUnm_5.47 //
children.translated_text: O beautiful-limbed one, I suspect you desire to ensnare the dark deer that is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' // RUnm_5.47 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] one experienced in abundant emotional expressions —

children.translated_text: 'Gather the beautiful flowers in the forest,
fashion splendid ornaments from them again,
O churner of <s>Madhu</s>, arrange these decorations upon my limbs —

children.text: ryuvatiṣu mama bhīmaṃ rautu saubhāgya-bherī // RUnm_5.48 //
children.translated_text: let the drum of my good fortune thunder fearfully among the women!' // RUnm_5.48 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] one who overwhelms her beloved with <s>rasa</s> —

children.translated_text: 'Why do you plead, O gambler, hiding your limbs in a corner of the house among the dung-heaps?

children.text: gūḍhāṅga kiṃ nanu vṛthā kitava prayāhi |
children.translated_text: Depart, it is useless! Where is your vaunted cleverness today
in mocking the groups of cowherd women, terrified
by the movement of the worn-out boat?' // RUnm_5.49 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] extremely bold speech, as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (280) —

children.translated_text: 'In the festival of the battle of love with your friend,
the pearl necklace danced upon her breasts;
O friend, the playful hero, leaping up,

children.text: dhīraṃ muhur me prajahāra kaustubham // RUnm_5.50 //
children.translated_text: steadily struck at my <s>Kaustubha</s> gem again and again.' // RUnm_5.50 //

children.text: medinyāṃ te luṭhati dayitā mālatī mlāna-puṣpā
children.translated_text: 'Your beloved, a jasmine with withered blossoms, rolls on the ground;

children.text: tiṣṭhan dvāre ramaṇi vimanāḥ khidyate padmanābhaḥ |
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, <s>Padmanābha</s> stands at the door, distressed and dejected;

children.text: tvaṃ connidrā kṣapayasi niśām rodayantī vayasyā
children.translated_text: and you, sleepless, spend the night weeping, O friend!

children.text: māne kas te nava-madhurimā taṃ tu nālokayāmi // RUnm_5.51 //
children.translated_text: What new sweetness is there in your wounded pride? I do not see it.' // RUnm_5.51 //

body.translated_text: [An example of] exceedingly harsh in wounded pride, as in the <s>Uddhava-sandeśa</s> (53) —
The <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold heroine) too is threefold according to her behavior in wounded pride: <s>dhīrā</s>, etc. // RUnm_5.52 //

children.text: udāste surate dhīrā sāvahitthā ca sādarā // RUnm_5.53 //
children.translated_text: The steadfast one, in love-making, remains indifferent, with concealment (<s>avahitthā</s>) and composure. // RUnm_5.53 //

children.text: devī nādya mayārciteti na hare tāmbūlam āsvāditaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The goddess has not been worshipped by me today, O <s>Hari</s>' — so she did not taste the betel;

children.text: śilpaṃ te paricitya tapsyati gṛhīty aṅgī kṛtā na srajaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Your craft will be examined and you will be rebuked' — having said this, she did not accept the garlands;

children.text: āhūtāsmi gṛhe vrajeśitur iti kṣipraṃ vrajantyā vaca-
children.translated_text: 'I have been summoned to the house of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>' — with these words, she quickly departed;

children.text: stasyāśrāvi na bhadrayeti vinayair mānaḥ pramāṇīkṛtaḥ // RUnm_5.54 //
children.translated_text: her words 'Stay well' were not heard — through such polite gestures, her wounded pride was given authority. // RUnm_5.54 //

children.text: kaṇṭhe nādya karomi durvrata-hatā ramyām imāṃ te srajaṃ
children.translated_text: 'I will not place this lovely garland on your neck today, O breaker of vows!

children.translated_text: I am not able to speak properly, being made to observe silence by your harsh [actions].

children.text: kā tvāṃ projjhya calet khaleyam aciraṃ śvaśrūr na ced āhvaye-
children.translated_text: What — who would leave and walk away from you, O rogue? If only my mother-in-law would summon me!' —

children.text: ditthaṃ pālikayā harau vinayato manyur gabhīrīkṛtaḥ // RUnm_5.55 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the keeper <s>Pālikā</s>, [<s>Rādhā</s>'s] anger toward <s>Hari</s> was politely deepened. // RUnm_5.55 //

children.text: kucālambhe pāṇir na hi mama bhavatyā vighaṭito
children.translated_text: 'When [he] touched my breasts, my hand did not push him away;

children.text: muhuś cumbārambhe mukham api na sācīkṛtam abhūt |
children.translated_text: when [he] repeatedly attempted to kiss, my face was not turned aside;

children.text: parīrambhe candrāvali na ca vapuḥ kuñcitam idaṃ
children.translated_text: in the embrace, O <s>Candrāvalī</s>, my body was not contracted —

children.text: kva labdhā mānasya sthitir iyam anālokita-carī // RUnm_5.56 //
children.translated_text: where has this stability of wounded pride been found, [this one] whose conduct is unseen?' // RUnm_5.56 //

children.text: santarjya niṣṭhuraṃ roṣād adhīrā tāḍayet priyam // RUnm_5.57 //
children.translated_text: The <s>adhīrā</s> (unsteadfast), having threatened harshly, strikes her beloved in anger. // RUnm_5.57 //

children.text: mugdhāḥ kaṃsaripo vayaṃ racayituṃ jānīmahe nocitaṃ
children.translated_text: 'We are naive, O foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — we do not know how to fashion fitting [responses].
We bow to that dear friend <s>Śyāmalā</s>, expert in the ways of statecraft,
by whom, binding [you] at the neck with jasmine garlands buzzing with bees,

children.text: sākṣepaṃ cakitekṣaṇas tvam asakṛt karṇotpalais tāḍyase // RUnm_5.58 //
children.translated_text: you are reproachfully struck again and again with the lotuses from her ears, while you look on in alarm!' // RUnm_5.58 //
She is called <s>dhīrādhīrā</s> (steadfast-unsteadfast), endowed with the qualities of both. // RUnm_5.59 //

children.text: sphurati na mama jātu krodha-gandho'pi citte
children.translated_text: 'Not even a trace of anger ever arises in my heart;

children.text: vratam anu gahanābhūt kintu maune manīṣā |
children.translated_text: my intention in maintaining silence has simply become a deep vow.

children.text: aghahara laghu yāhi vyāja āstāṃ yad etāḥ
children.translated_text: O destroyer of sin, go quickly — let pretexts be! For these

children.text: kusuma-rasanayā tvāṃ bandhum icchanti sakhyaḥ // RUnm_5.60 //
children.translated_text: friends of mine desire to bind you with a garland of flowers.' // RUnm_5.60 //

children.text: kṛtāgasi harau puraḥ sphurati taṃ bhramad-bhrū-latā
children.translated_text: When the offending <s>Hari</s> stood before her, she, with her vibrating brow-creeper,
wishing to strike him, impetuously pulled the lotus from the edge of her ear;

children.text: na tena tam atāḍayat kim api yāhi yāhīti sā
children.translated_text: but she did not strike him with it — 'Go! Go!' she said,

children.text: bruvaty ajani maṅgalā sakhi paraṃ parāñcan-mukhī // RUnm_5.61 //
children.translated_text: and turning her face away, O friend, auspiciousness was born [in that scene]. // RUnm_5.61 //

children.text: kiśorikāṇām apy āsām ākṛteḥ prakṛter api |
children.translated_text: Even among younger girls (<s>kiśorikā</s>), some are called <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold)

children.text: prāgalbhyād iva kāsāṃcit pragalbhātvam udīryate // RUnm_5.62 //
children.translated_text: because of bold appearance or bold nature, as it were. // RUnm_5.62 //

children.text: madhyā tathā pragalbhā ca dvidhā sā paribhidyate |
children.translated_text: Both the <s>madhyā</s> (intermediate) and the <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold) are each divided into two:

children.text: jyeṣṭhā cāpi kaniṣṭhā ca nāyaka-praṇayaṃ prati // RUnm_5.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>jyeṣṭhā</s> (senior) and <s>kaniṣṭhā</s> (junior), with respect to the hero's affection. // RUnm_5.63 //

children.text: supte prekṣya pṛthak puraḥ priyatame tatrārpayan puṣpajaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Seeing her beloved sleeping separately before her, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] placed Cupid's

children.text: līlāyā nayanāñcale kila rajaś cakre prabodhodyamam |
children.translated_text: pollen-dust at the corner of her eyelid playfully, making an effort to awaken her;
then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, look — by the stratagem of fanning with a cool palm-leaf fan,

children.text: stārāyāḥ praṇayād iva praṇayate nidrābhivṛddhi-kramam // RUnm_5.64 //
children.translated_text: as if out of affection for <s>Tārā</s>, cultivates the progressive deepening of her sleep.' // RUnm_5.64 //

children.text: dīvyantyau dayite samīkṣya rabhasād akṣais tryahātma-glahai-
children.translated_text: 'Seeing the two beloveds playing dice eagerly, with dice of self-mortification [played over] three days,
advising <s>Gaurī</s>, who was swaying [with emotion], well-meaningly with the eyebrow regarding the method of [placing] stakes,

children.text: tasyās tūrṇam upārjayann iva jayaṃ śikṣā-vaśenācyutaḥ
children.translated_text: as if quickly winning victory for her through his expertise, <s>Acyuta</s>

children.text: śyāmām eva cakāra dhūrta-nagarī-saṅketa-vij jitvarām // RUnm_5.65 //
children.translated_text: made <s>Śyāmā</s> alone the winner, knowing the signals of the gambler's city.' // RUnm_5.65 //

children.text: kācit kāñcid apekṣya syāj jyeṣṭhety āpekṣikī bhidā |
children.translated_text: One is called <s>jyeṣṭhā</s> (senior) only in relation to another — hence this is a relative distinction;

children.text: ato bheda-dvayam idaṃ na kṛtaṃ gaṇanāntare // RUnm_5.66 //
children.translated_text: therefore this twofold division is not included in a separate enumeration. // RUnm_5.66 //

children.text: kanyā mugdhaiva sā kintu svīyānyoḍhe ubhe budhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: A maiden (<s>kanyā</s>) is always <s>mugdhā</s> (naive); but both the <s>svīyā</s> (own wife) and the <s>anyoḍhā</s> (another's wife), according to the wise,
are proclaimed to have six divisions — by the subdivision of <s>mugdhā</s>, <s>madhyā</s>, and the like. // RUnm_5.67 //
The <s>madhyā</s> and the <s>prauḍhā</s> (mature/bold) are stated to have twelve divisions, by the subdivision of <s>dhīrā</s> and the like;

children.text: kanyā svīyā paroḍheti mugdhā ca trividhā matā |
children.translated_text: a maiden, one's own [wife], and another's [wife] — and the <s>mugdhā</s> is considered threefold;

children.text: iti tāḥ kīrtitā pañcadaśa bhedā ihākhilāḥ // RUnm_5.68 //
children.translated_text: thus all fifteen divisions of heroines are declared here in full. // RUnm_5.68 //
Now the eightfold states (<s>avasthā</s>) of all heroines are described.
Among them: the <s>abhisārikā</s> (one who goes to meet her lover), the <s>vāsa-sajjā</s> (one dressed for the tryst), and the <s>utkaṇṭhitā</s> (the longing one). // RUnm_5.69 //
The <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (one whose lover has been unfaithful), the <s>vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one), and the <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (one separated by a quarrel),
the <s>proṣita-preyasī</s> (one whose lover is away), and the <s>svādhīna-bhartṛkā</s> (one whose lord is under her control). // RUnm_5.70 //
Therein, the <s>abhisārikā</s> (one who goes to meet her lover) — for example —
She who sends [a messenger] to bring her lover to her, or who herself goes to meet him —
she is the <s>abhisārikā</s>, [going] by moonlight or in darkness, dressed in attire suitable for the journey. // RUnm_5.71 //
As if merged into her own limbs with shyness, all her ornaments silent,
with her face veiled, accompanied by a single affectionate friend, she goes to her beloved. // RUnm_5.72 //

children.text: jānīte na harir yathā mama manaḥ-kandarpa-kaṇḍūm imāṃ

children.text: cāturyaṃ tarasā prasāraya tathā sasneham āsādya taṃ
children.translated_text: so do you quickly extend your cleverness — go to Him with affection,

children.text: yāvat prāṇaharo na candrahatakaḥ prācī-mukhaṃ cumbati // RUnm_5.73 //
children.translated_text: before the accursed life-stealing moon kisses the eastern horizon!' // RUnm_5.73 //

body.translated_text: Therein, [an example of] one who sends [a messenger] —

children.translated_text: 'The moon produces a swelling orb; in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, he showers dense moonlight;

body.translated_text: Now the <s>abhisārikā</s> who goes out herself in the moonlight, for example —

children.translated_text: 'Their limbs veiled by the ink of darkness, in the midst of the <s>kadamba</s> grove,

but around you, the signs of your body's radiance — like lightning flashes —

children.text: hari hari ghana-dhvāntānyetāḥ svavairiṇi bhindate // RUnm_5.75 //
children.translated_text: alas, alas! — split asunder the dense darkness, [which is] your own enemy!' // RUnm_5.75 //
Now the <s>vāsaka-sajjā</s> (one who adorns herself in her chamber) —

children.text: anyā yato'sti na nyūnā sā syād ātyantikī laghuḥ |
children.translated_text: She who is inferior to no other — she is the absolutely subordinate;
though the threefold division [prakharā etc.] is possible, only the gentle type is appropriate for her. // RUnm_6.22 //
'Through the persistence of all my companions, the enemy of <s>Agha</s>

children.text: katham api sa mayādya vyaktam āmantrito'sti |
children.translated_text: has somehow, this very day, been clearly invited by me;
O goddesses of the cowherds, for a moment, with great compassion, restrain my shame —
display the beauty that [once] resided in me!' // RUnm_6.23 //

children.text: na samā na laghuś cādyā bhaven naivādhikāntimā |
children.translated_text: The first [<s>ātyantikī adhikā</s>] cannot be equal or subordinate; the last [<s>ātyantikī laghu</s>] cannot be superior;

children.text: anyās tridhādhikāś ca syuḥ samāś ca laghavaś ca tāḥ // RUnm_6.24 //
children.translated_text: the others may be of three kinds each — superior, equal, and subordinate. // RUnm_6.24 //
Therefore, every [group-leader] except the absolutely superior has subordination to someone;

children.text: sarvāsv adhikatā ca syād vinaivātyantikīṃ laghum // RUnm_6.25 //
children.translated_text: and every one except the absolutely subordinate has superiority over someone. // RUnm_6.25 //
The first is unique; the last is of two kinds; the middle ones are stated as nine-fold;

children.text: ity asau yūthanāthānāṃ bhidā dvādaśadhoditā // RUnm_6.26 //
children.translated_text: thus this classification of the group-leaders is declared as twelvefold. // RUnm_6.26 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the section on the varieties of the group-leaders (<s>yūtheśvarī</s>) in the glorious <s>Ujjvala Nīlamaṇi</s>. ||6||

(8)
Now the section on the female companions (<s>sakhīs</s>).

children.translated_text: The <s>sakhī</s> (female companion) is one who fully expands the pastimes of love,

children.text: viśrambha-ratna-peṭī ca tataḥ suṣthu vivicyate // RUnm_8.1 //
children.translated_text: and is the jewel-casket of intimate confidence — therefore she is carefully examined. // RUnm_8.1 //
Among the companions attached to the same group,

children.text: adhikāder bhidā jñeyā prakharādeś ca pūrvavat // RUnm_8.2 //
children.translated_text: the distinctions of superior and the like, as well as bold and the like, should be known as before. // RUnm_8.2 //
The superior (<s>adhikā</s>) companion is one who surpasses in love, good fortune, virtuous qualities, and the like;

children.text: samā tat-sāmyato jñeyā tal-laghutvāt tathā laghuḥ // RUnm_8.3 //
children.translated_text: the equal (<s>samā</s>) is one who matches therein; the subordinate (<s>laghu</s>), one who falls below. // RUnm_8.3 //
The bold (<s>prakharā</s>) is famous for her irresistible words, worthy of respect;

children.text: tad-ūnatve bhaven mṛdvī madhyā tat-sāmyam āgatā // RUnm_8.4 //
children.translated_text: the gentle (<s>mṛdvī</s>) possesses less of that; the moderate (<s>madhyā</s>) has attained equality therein. // RUnm_8.4 //
The subdivision into absolute superiority and the like is the same here as before;
within her own group, the group-leader herself would be the absolutely superior one;

children.text: sā kvāpi prakharā yūthe kvāpi madhyā mṛduḥ kvacit // RUnm_8.5 //
children.translated_text: she may be bold in some groups, moderate in some, and gentle in others. // RUnm_8.5 //
Among them, the triad of the absolutely superior (<s>ātyantikādhikā</s>) —
that triad, though referencing all [companions], is not overly subordinate to others;
it is stated again to clarify their behavior within their own group. // RUnm_8.6 //

children.text: nīle nīla-nicolam arthaye maghe dehi srajaṃ dāmanīṃ
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Nīlā</s>, I ask for a dark-blue robe; O <s>Maghā</s>, give me a garland, a rope of flowers;

children.text: tvaṃ kālāguru-kardamaiḥ sakhi tanuṃ limpasva campe mama |
children.translated_text: you, O friend <s>Campā</s>, anoint my body with pastes of black aloe;

children.text: jānīhi bhramarākṣi kutra guravaḥ paśya pradoṣodgame
children.translated_text: O bee-eyed one, find out where the elders are — look, at the rise of evening
the dense darkness urges me to enter the bower!' // RUnm_8.7 //

body.translated_text: The superior-bold ones are celebrated as <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Maṅgalā</s>, and others. // RUnm_8.8 //

children.text: anaṅga-śara-jarjaraṃ sphuṭati cen mano vas tadā
children.translated_text: 'If your heart, pierced by the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid), is breaking,
then enough of this pleading and importuning me — go by yourselves!
In the pathway of your gaze, a befitting lover for those like you

children.text: yad atra rata-hiṇḍakaḥ sa kila pāti go-maṇḍalam // RUnm_8.9 //
children.translated_text: is happily tending the cattle here — that love-wanderer!' // RUnm_8.9 //

body.translated_text: The superior-moderate ones are <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>'s [companions such as] <s>Pālikā</s> and others. // RUnm_8.10 //

children.text: śṛṇu sakhi vacas tathyaṃ māna-grahe mama kā kṣatiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Listen, O friend, to truthful words: what harm is there to me in the grip of <s>māna</s> (love-anger)?

children.text: sphurati muralī-nāde ko vā śramaḥ śravaṇāvṛtau |
children.translated_text: What fatigue is there in closing the ears when the flute's melody resounds?
But hearing your accusation of excessive hardheartedness, [I wished] in <s>Vraja</s>

children.text: damayitum amuṃ kintu kṣipraṃ dṛg-ardham agha-dviṣi // RUnm_8.11 //
children.translated_text: to quickly subdue him — [yet] I [cannot control even] a half-glance toward the enemy of <s>Agha</s>!' // RUnm_8.11 //

body.translated_text: The superior-gentle ones are considered to be <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s [companions such as] <s>Bhadrā</s> and others. // RUnm_8.12 //

children.translated_text: Now, the triad of the relatively superior (<s>āpekṣikādhikā</s>) —

children.text: yauthikīṣu sakhīṣv eva yūtheśāto laghuṣv iha |
children.translated_text: Among the congregational (<s>yauthikī</s>) companions who are subordinate to the group-leader,

children.text: yādhikaikām apekṣānyā sā syād āpekṣikādhikā // RUnm_8.13 //
children.translated_text: she who is superior when compared to a particular other one — she is called the relatively superior. // RUnm_8.13 //

children.text: sumadhye mā yāsīs tvam adhikam amībhir mṛdulatāṃ
children.translated_text: 'O slender-waisted one, do not go excessively soft
from the honey-words, the gifts of intoxication, of that preceptor of the rogue-clan;
O you who are greedy for play, have you, at the whispered words of the great bee-lord,

children.text: kuḍuṅge rādhāyāḥ klamam api visasmāra bhavatī // RUnm_8.14 //
children.translated_text: forgotten even fatigue in the bower of <s>Rādhā</s>?' // RUnm_8.14 //
'O artless one, be silent! By that <s>Indra</s> of the circle of rogue-arts,

children.text: tvaṃ mantreṇa sphuṭam iha vaśīkṛtya tenānuśiṣṭā |
children.translated_text: you have clearly been enchanted by his <s>mantra</s> and instructed;
in the bower on the peak of <s>Govardhana</s>, despite having seen <s>Rādhā</s> in her night-vigil today,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāpy uccaiḥ sakhi yad asi me cāṭu-vāde pravṛttā // RUnm_8.15 //
children.translated_text: you, O friend, have begun flattering speech on my behalf!' // RUnm_8.15 //

body.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> and others in <s>Gāndharvā</s>'s (<s>Rādhā</s>'s) group are the bold-superior [companions] here. // RUnm_8.16 //

children.translated_text: 'Let the rope be handed over — it was sent to <s>Dāmodara</s> by my dear friend, by you yourself;
let a flower be picked here by me;
I am not to be hinted at, O clever friend, out of delusion —

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ kadarthayati mām adhikaṃ yad eṣaḥ // RUnm_8.17 //
children.translated_text: [it is] because this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> despises me excessively.' // RUnm_8.17 //

children.text: gīro gambhīrārthāḥ katham iva hitās te na śṛṇuyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'How could I not listen to your profound and beneficial words?

children.text: nigūḍho māṃ kintu vyathayati murārer avinayaḥ |
children.translated_text: But what secretly torments me is the discourtesy of <s>Murāri</s>;

children.text: mayollāsāt tasmai svayam upahṛtā hanta sakhi yā
children.translated_text: the garland that I myself joyfully offered to Him, alas, O friend —

children.text: kuraṅgākṣī-keśopari paricitā sā srag adhunā // RUnm_8.18 //
children.translated_text: that very garland is now placed upon the hair of a doe-eyed girl!' // RUnm_8.18 //

body.text: atra yūthe viśākhādyā bhavanty adhika-madhyamāḥ // RUnm_8.19 //
body.translated_text: In this group, <s>Viśākhā</s> and others are the superior-moderate ones. // RUnm_8.19 //

children.text: darāpi na dṛg-arpitā sakhi śikhaṇḍa-cūḍe mayā
children.translated_text: 'Not even a slight glance was cast by me upon the peacock-crested one, O friend —

children.text: prasīda bata mā kṛthā mayi vṛthā purobhāgitām |
children.translated_text: please be appeased; do not pointlessly harbor hostility toward me!
With dancing <s>makara</s>-earrings, His playful gait

children.text: tanoty ayam adūrataḥ kim iha saṃvidheyaṃ mayā // RUnm_8.20 //
children.translated_text: unfolds nearby — what am I to do here?' // RUnm_8.20 //

body.text: adhikā mṛdavaś cātra citrā madhurikādayaḥ // RUnm_8.21 //
body.translated_text: The superior-gentle ones here are <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Madhurikā</s>, and others. // RUnm_8.21 //

children.translated_text: The equal triad is bound by deep, intimate, unwavering love. // RUnm_8.22 //

body.translated_text: Now, the triad of the equal (<s>samā</s>) —

children.text: praviśati harir eṣa prekṣya nau hṛṣṭa-cetāḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Hari</s> is entering, seeing us two, with a delighted heart;

children.text: sakhi sapadi mudhā tvaṃ sambhramān mā prayāsīḥ |
children.translated_text: O friend, do not hastily depart in confusion!
With His broad arms placed on [our] shoulders,

children.text: taṭa-bhuvi sukham āvāṃ maṇḍite paryaṭāvaḥ // RUnm_8.23 //
children.translated_text: let us two happily stroll together on the decorated riverbank.' // RUnm_8.23 //

children.text: śyāme gauri hariḥ kva dīvyati sakhi kṣauṇībhṛtaḥ kandare
children.translated_text: 'O dark one, O fair one, where does <s>Hari</s> sport? In the cave of the mountain, O friend.
What, are there lion-claw [marks] upon the pitcher of your bosom, [won] by His own prowess?

children.text: ākarṣaty abhitaḥ sa nāga-mathanas tvām eva kṛtvā ravaṃ
children.translated_text: He, the subduer of the serpent, draws [you] from all sides, making you alone resound —

children.text: mithyālāsya-naṭi tvam eva ramase tasmin sukaṇṭhi-rave // RUnm_8.24 //
children.translated_text: you actress of false indolence, you alone delight in him, O beautiful-throated one!' // RUnm_8.24 //
'O moon-faced one, whatever pendant was given to you by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇena tubhyam aparaṃ sakhi tādṛśaṃ me |
children.translated_text: another just like it [was given] to me, O friend;

children.text: tvaṃ cen madīyam api ditsasi nādya mā dā
children.translated_text: if you wish to give me yours as well — no, don't give it today!

children.text: hāsyaṃ vimuñca calitā tava pārśvato'smi // RUnm_8.25 //
children.translated_text: Stop laughing — I am right at your side!' // RUnm_8.25 //
The subordinate triad acts for the enhancement of the dear friend's happiness. // RUnm_8.26 //

body.translated_text: Now, the triad of the subordinate (<s>laghu</s>) —

children.text: yadapy anyonya-niṣṭhaṃ syāt sakhyaṃ tad api yujyate |
children.translated_text: Even though mutual friendship may exist,

children.text: sadā sāhāyya-hetutvān mukhyaṃ tat tu laghu-trike // RUnm_8.27 //
children.translated_text: it is appropriate, since [the subordinate's role] is always to render assistance; this is primary in the subordinate triad. // RUnm_8.27 //

body.text: laghur āpekṣikī cātyantikī ceti dvidheritā // RUnm_8.28 //
body.translated_text: The subordinate is said to be of two kinds: relative (<s>āpekṣikī</s>) and absolute (<s>ātyantikī</s>). // RUnm_8.28 //

children.translated_text: The relatively subordinate here are described as <s>Lalitā</s> and others. // RUnm_8.29 //

children.text: dhārā bāṣpa-mayī na yāti viratiṃ lokasya nimitsataḥ
children.translated_text: 'The stream of tears does not cease, [yet] from this, the world

children.text: premāsminn iti nanda-nandana-rataṃ lobhonmanā mā kṛthāḥ |
children.translated_text: infers love — do not be covetous and greedy for the delight of <s>Nanda</s>'s son!

children.text: itthaṃ bhūri nivāritāpi tarale mad-vāci sācīkṛta-
children.translated_text: Though repeatedly restrained thus, O fickle one, making sidelong glances

children.text: bhrū-dvandvā na hi gauravaṃ tvam akaroḥ kiṃ nādya rodiṣyasi // RUnm_8.30 //
children.translated_text: with [your] pair of brows at my words, you showed no respect — will you not weep today?' // RUnm_8.30 //

body.translated_text: Among them, the subordinate-bold (<s>laghu-prakharā</s>), as in <s>Vidagdha Mādhava</s> (5.32) —

body.text: sā laghu-prakharā dvedhā bhaved vāmātha dakṣiṇā // RUnm_8.31 //
body.translated_text: That subordinate-bold one is further of two kinds: <s>vāmā</s> (contrary) and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (compliant). // RUnm_8.31 //

children.translated_text: Among them, the <s>vāmā</s> (contrary) —

children.text: māna-grahe sadodyuktā tac chaithilye ca kopanā |
children.translated_text: She who is always eager to seize <s>māna</s> (love-anger), who is wrathful when it loosens,

children.text: abhedyā nāyake prāyaḥ krūrā vāmeti kīrtyate // RUnm_8.32 //
children.translated_text: who is generally impervious to the hero, and harsh — she is called <s>vāmā</s>. // RUnm_8.32 //
'O you who are skilled in deception,
contrive your <s>māna</s> toward the destroyer of <s>Mura</s>;
for when a man has many beloveds,
courtesy brings suffering.' // RUnm_8.33 //

body.translated_text: She who is always eager to seize <s>māna</s>, as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (222) —

children.translated_text: 'When the new torrent of discourtesy burst forth impetuously,
and she was brought to gentleness and appeasement by the flattering skill of the enemy of <s>Agha</s>,
trembling from the circling glance-serpents of her insincere friend,

children.text: vimukhitamukhī bhūyo bhadrā haṭhād bhrukuṭiṃ dadhe // RUnm_8.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadrā</s>, turning her face away, stubbornly knit her brows once more.' // RUnm_8.34 //

body.translated_text: She who is wrathful when <s>māna</s> loosens, for example —

children.text: kāmaṃ dūre vasatu paṭimā cāṭu-vṛndas tatrāyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Let the flattering words stay far away, let this portrait [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] remain there;

children.text: rājyaṃ svāmin viracaya mama prāṅgaṇaṃ mā prayāsīḥ |
children.translated_text: O Lord, [you may] rule your kingdom — do not trouble yourself to visit my courtyard!

children.text: hanta klāntā mama sahacarī rātrim ekākinī iyaṃ
children.translated_text: Alas, this companion of mine, alone for the night, exhausted,
was kept [awake] in the bower by the night-vigil of the chief of all the cowherd girls!' // RUnm_8.35 //

body.translated_text: She who is impervious to the hero, as in the <s>Uddhava Sandeśa</s> (52) —

children.translated_text: 'These doe-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>, exceeding eighty-four <s>lakṣas</s> (8.4 million),
have each been proclaimed as belonging to you by this companion of yours;

children.text: ihāpi bhuvi viśrutā priya-sakhī mahārghyety asau
children.translated_text: and even here on earth, my dear friend is celebrated as most precious —

children.text: kathaṃ tad api sāhasī śaṭha! jighṛkṣur enām asi // RUnm_8.36 //
children.translated_text: how then, O audacious rogue, do you dare seize even her?' // RUnm_8.36 //

body.translated_text: She who is harsh toward the hero, as in the <s>Dāna Keli Kaumudī</s> (57) —

body.text: yūthe ætra vāma-prakharā lalitādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // RUnm_8.37 //
body.translated_text: In this group, the contrary-bold (<s>vāma-prakharā</s>) ones are celebrated as <s>Lalitā</s> and others. // RUnm_8.37 //

children.translated_text: Now, the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (compliant) —
She who cannot endure insistence on <s>māna</s>, who speaks reasonably to the hero,

children.text: sāmabhis tena bhedyā ca dakṣiṇā parikīrtitā // RUnm_8.38 //
children.translated_text: who can be won over by him through gentle means — she is proclaimed as <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. // RUnm_8.38 //

children.text: snigdhe yat paruṣāsi praṇamati stabdhāsi yad rāgiṇi
children.translated_text: 'That you are harsh when [He is] tender, stubborn when [He] bows, hostile when [He is] passionate,

children.text: dveṣasthāsi yad unmukhe vimukhatāṃ yātāsi tasmin priye |
children.translated_text: that you have turned away when [He is] eager, that toward [Him,] the beloved —

children.text: tad yuktaṃ viparīta-kāriṇi tava śrī-khaṇḍa-carcā viṣaṃ
children.translated_text: that is fitting for you, O perverse one: sandalwood-paste is poison [to you],

children.text: śītāṃśus tapano himaṃ hutavahaḥ krīḍā-mudo yātanāḥ // RUnm_8.39 //
children.translated_text: the cool-rayed moon is the scorching sun, snow is fire, and joyful play is torment.' // RUnm_8.39 //

body.translated_text: She who cannot endure insistence on <s>māna</s>, as in the <s>Śrī Gīta Govinda</s> (9.10) —

children.text: adoṣād doṣād vā tyajati vipine tāṃ yadi bhavān
children.translated_text: 'Whether without fault or with fault, if You abandon her in the forest,

children.text: abhadraṃ bhadraṃ vā tribhuvana-pate tvāṃ vadatu kaḥ |
children.translated_text: O Lord of the three worlds, who may call You auspicious or inauspicious?

children.text: idaṃ tu krūraṃ me smarati hṛdayaṃ yat kila tayā
children.translated_text: But this is what is cruel to my heart — that she,

children.text: tvad-arthaṃ kāntāre kula-tilaka nātmāpi gaṇitaḥ // RUnm_8.40 //
children.translated_text: O ornament of the lineage, did not count even her own self for Your sake in the wilderness.' // RUnm_8.40 //

body.translated_text: She who speaks reasonably to the hero, as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (297) —

children.text: na vyarthāṃ kuruṣe mamaiva bhaṇitiṃ madhye sakhīnām iti
children.translated_text: '"She does not make my speech fruitless among the companions" —

children.text: śrutvā khyātim asau kṛtī madhuripur māṃ bāḍham āśiśriye |
children.translated_text: hearing this reputation, that accomplished enemy of <s>Madhu</s> forcefully approached me;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mad-vadanaṃ prasīda rabhasād enaṃ puraḥ kātaraṃ
children.translated_text: seeing my face, be graciously appeased — [see] before [you] this trembling, timid one'

children.text: kalyāṇībhir alaṃ kṛśodari dṛśor bhaṅgībhir aṅgīkuru // RUnm_8.41 //
children.translated_text: O slender-waisted one, enough with auspicious [pretexts] — accept [his love] through the gestures of your eyes!' // RUnm_8.41 //

body.translated_text: She who can be won over by the hero, for example —
<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> and the like would be a <s>dakṣiṇā-prakharā</s> (right-inclined bold one) in this context. // RUnm_8.42 //

children.text: tvayā racita-saṃkathāṃ pathi samīkṣya māṃ māninī
children.translated_text: 'Seeing me on the path conversing with you, my proud (<s>māninī</s>)
friend, with a dejected mind, is casting sidelong glances and reproaching me;
O son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, heed my counsel, I tell you —
without taking refuge in <s>Lalitā</s>, this scheme of yours is futile.' // RUnm_8.43 //

children.text: sakhi tava muhur mūrdhnā pāda-graho'pi mayā kṛta-
children.translated_text: 'Friend, I have repeatedly bowed at your feet with my head,

children.text: stad api ca harau jātāsi tvaṃ prasāda-parāṅ-mukhī |
children.translated_text: yet even so, you remain averse to showing grace toward <s>Hari</s>;
so be it — when the fifth [note] of the flute rises on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: vicalita-dhṛtis tvaṃ lolākṣī mayāpi hasiṣyase // RUnm_8.44 //
children.translated_text: you, with wavering composure and restless eyes, will be laughed at even by me!' // RUnm_8.44 //
Now, the extremely lesser-ranking one (<s>ātyantika-laghu</s>) —
The one called <s>ātyantika-laghu</s> (extremely subordinate) here is <s>Kusumikā</s> and the like;

children.text: sarvathā mṛdur eveyaṃ yan nitānta-laghīyasī // RUnm_8.45 //
children.translated_text: she is entirely gentle, since she is most exceedingly subordinate. // RUnm_8.45 //

children.text: vande sundari sandiśa priya-sakhīṃ mānaṃ vimuñcatv asau
children.translated_text: 'I bow to you, O beautiful one — send word to your dear friend: let her abandon her <s>māna</s>;
though yearning, she sits like a proud woman in her chamber, out of suspicion regarding you;

children.text: dūre tvan-mukham īkṣate harir iyaṃ maunaṃ śukaḥ śikṣate
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> gazes at your face from afar; her parrot is learning silence;

children.text: lāsyaṃ necchati candrakī savayasaḥ kvāsīmit na svaṃ viduḥ // RUnm_8.46 //
children.translated_text: <s>Candrakī</s> (the peahen) does not desire to dance; her companions do not know where she has gone.' // RUnm_8.46 //
Among the bold (<s>prakharā</s>) and the other [types], only a single group-leader (<s>yūtheśā</s>) is mentioned [for each];

children.text: madhyasthā navadhaivantyā samā laghur iti dvidhā // RUnm_8.47 //
children.translated_text: the neutral (<s>madhyasthā</s>) is ninefold, ending in: equal (<s>samā</s>) and subordinate (<s>laghu</s>) — thus twofold. // RUnm_8.47 //
