children.text: khedaṃ na vyasane tanoṣi vahase nollāsam asyāḥ śubhe
children.translated_text: 'You do not express grief in misfortune, nor do you carry joy in her good fortune;

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ prakaṭīkṛtau na hi dhiyaṃ dhatse guṇānām api |
children.translated_text: you do not apply your mind to revealing faults, nor to [revealing] virtues either.',
'O beautiful-faced <s>Śyāme</s>, your mental disposition is unaffected;

children.text: tvaṃ śyāme muni-vṛttir atra satataṃ candrāvalau dṛśyase // RUnm_9.8 //
children.translated_text: you are constantly seen like a sage in [your conduct toward] <s>Candrāvalī</s>, with neither hatred nor attachment.' // RUnm_9.8 //
The rival faction is one characterized by mutual hostility, which destroys what is desired and causes what is undesired. // RUnm_9.9 //
'O <s>Rādhe</s>, knowing that <s>Hari</s> was in the bower with his gaze directed toward your path,

children.text: padmā tatra nināya hanta kuṭilā candrāvalīṃ chadmanā |
children.translated_text: the crooked <s>Padmā</s> led <s>Candrāvalī</s> there by a ruse — alas!',

children.text: ity ākarṇya mukunda sā subalataḥ stabdhā tathādya sthitā
children.translated_text: 'Having heard this from <s>Subala</s>, O <s>Mukunda</s>, she stood stunned, just as',

children.text: dṛṣṭvā nīla-paṭīṃ tanau jaṭilayā prātar yathā tarjitā // RUnm_9.10 //
children.translated_text: 'when she was scolded by <s>Jaṭilā</s> in the morning upon seeing a dark cloth on [her] body.' // RUnm_9.10 //

body.translated_text: Regarding the destruction of what is desired, for example —

children.text: kutaḥ padme putri kṣiti-dhara-taṭād amba jaṭile
children.translated_text: 'From where [have you come], O <s>Padmā</s>, daughter? From the mountain slope! O mother <s>Jaṭilā</s>,

children.text: vadhūr dṛṣṭvā kva nu ravi-niketasya purataḥ |
children.translated_text: have you seen the young wife? Where? In front of the sun-temple!',

children.text: ciraṃ nāyāty eṣā katham iva niruddhātra hariṇā
children.translated_text: 'This one has not come for a long time — how indeed has she been detained here by <s>Hari</s>?',

children.text: tavādhvānaṃ paśyaty ahaha bhavatī dhāvatu ruṣā // RUnm_9.11 //
children.translated_text: 'She is watching your path — alas! You, madam, should run [there] in anger!' // RUnm_9.11 //

body.translated_text: Now regarding causing what is undesired, for example —

children.translated_text: Deceit (<s>chadma</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), fickleness (<s>cāpala</s>), fault-finding (<s>āsūyā</s>), envy (<s>matsara</s>), indignation (<s>amarṣa</s>), and pride (<s>garvita</s>) —

children.text: vyaktiṃ yāty ukti-ceṣṭābhiḥ pratipakṣa-sakhīṣv idam // RUnm_9.12 //
children.translated_text: these are manifested through speech and gestures among the friends of the rival faction. // RUnm_9.12 //

children.text: śrutvā kīcakam adri-mūrdhni paśavaḥ śyāmaṃ ca dṛṣṭvāmbudaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The cattle have heard the <s>kīcaka</s> [bamboo sound] on the mountain-top and have seen the dark cloud;

children.text: dhāvantv adhiyaḥ kathaṃ tvam api dhig dhīrādhikaṃ dhāvasi |
children.translated_text: the cows are running — why do you too, O steadfast one, disgracefully run even more?'

children.text: ity uccair anṛtottareṇa taralāṃ prayāyya padmām asau
children.translated_text: Thus, having sent the fickle <s>Padmā</s> away with a false reply,

children.text: prāptā paśya gṛhaṃ karoti lalitā rādhā-prayāṇe tvarām // RUnm_9.13 //
children.translated_text: look — <s>Lalitā</s> now makes haste to prepare <s>Rādhā</s>'s departure! // RUnm_9.13 //
'O Goddess, what is it that you are showing — opening up
your crooked tress of hair — a forest garland?',
'Rather, look at this garland-wearer [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], like a dark staff,
right on my balcony, O friend!' // RUnm_9.14 //
'This necklace, which was previously being offered to me persistently by the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,

children.text: prājyaṃ doṣam avekṣya nāyaka-maṇau na svīkṛto'bhūn mayā |
children.translated_text: was not accepted by me, seeing grave fault in the jewel among lovers —',

children.text: hāraḥ samprati so'yam eva viṣamo lubdhe kva labdhas tvayā
children.translated_text: 'Now this very troublesome [necklace] — where did you, O greedy one, obtain it?

children.text: drāgiṣṭho'py uraga-kṣatāṅguli-nibho duṣṭaḥ sakhi tyajyatām // RUnm_9.15 //
children.translated_text: Even the most massive [necklace], resembling a snake-bitten finger — wicked! O friend, throw it away!' // RUnm_9.15 //
'Do not torment yourself in vain in the midst of the bower,
making a passionate firefly-glow here.',
'When the dark <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-cloud meets the great mountain,

children.text: somābhā vilāsitum atra vidyud eva // RUnm_9.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Somābhā</s> [Candrāvalī] is fit to sport here as mere lightning!' // RUnm_9.16 //

children.text: yad bhāṇḍīre tava sahacarī tāṇḍavaṃ sā vyatānīt
children.translated_text: 'The fact that your companion performed that <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance

children.text: padme śaivyā samajani na tat kasya vismāpanāya |
children.translated_text: at the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> [tree], O <s>Padme</s> — O <s>Śaibya</s> — that was no wonder to anyone.',

children.text: sā cet tanvī prakṛti-laḍahā śikṣitā cābhaviṣya-
children.translated_text: 'If that slender one, naturally playful, had also been trained,

children.text: nmanye sarvaṃ jagad api tataḥ prekṣayāmohayiṣyat // RUnm_9.17 //
children.translated_text: I believe she would have enchanted the entire world with her gaze!' // RUnm_9.17 //
'Enough! <s>Hari</s>, the rogue, has contented <s>Rādhā</s>'s heart with a great necklace,

children.text: srajā dhūrteneyaṃ tava tu kavara-śrīr avarayā |
children.translated_text: and with a garland, [he has graced] the beauty of your braid with an inferior [offering].',

children.text: mano dvandvātītaṃ munivad avikalpaṃ ca dadhatī
children.translated_text: 'Holding your mind beyond duality, free of conceptual thought like a sage,

children.text: tathāpi tvaṃ mugdhe na vipina-vinodād viramasi // RUnm_9.18 //
children.translated_text: yet, O innocent one, you do not desist from forest-amusements!' // RUnm_9.18 //

children.text: sphuṭadbhir iva korakair alaghubhiś ca guñjā-phalia-
children.translated_text: 'Having fashioned today from <s>guñjā</s>-berries with their weighty buds that seem to burst
open, [an earring] and given it to the slayer of <s>Mura</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] —',
'O bird [i.e., parrot], seeing that earring of his, bestowed by you who listen to <s>Rādhikā</s>,

children.text: manaḥ svam udaghāṭi yat tad atilāghavāyaiva naḥ // RUnm_9.19 //
children.translated_text: my mind was agitated — and that serves only to diminish us.' // RUnm_9.19 //
Now pride (<s>garvita</s>) —
Egoism (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), self-regard (<s>abhimāna</s>), haughtiness (<s>darpa</s>), derision (<s>uddhasita</s>),

children.text: mada auddhatyam ity eṣa garvaḥ ṣoḍhā nigadyate // RUnm_9.20 //
children.translated_text: intoxication (<s>mada</s>), and insolence (<s>auddhatya</s>) — thus pride is declared to be of six kinds. // RUnm_9.20 //
Egoism is the censure of another through the description of one's own faction's virtues. // RUnm_9.21 //
'In the sky, <s>Somābhā</s> [Candrāvalī], of indistinct beauty in the sapphire-splendor,
produces a mere particle of radiance;',
'the excellent light that removes the darkness of the eyes —

children.text: sā yāvan na hi vṛṣabhānujābhyudeti // RUnm_9.22 //
children.translated_text: [shines] only so long as the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>] has not risen!' // RUnm_9.22 //
Self-regard is the indirect proclamation of the excellence of one's own love. // RUnm_9.23 //
'You are of steady mind — when she commenced to narrate steadfastly

children.text: niṣkampam eva yad iyaṃ gadituṃ pravṛttā |
children.translated_text: the story of <s>Hari</s>'s leap into the serpent-lake,',
'at the mere incidental mention of the <s>kadamba</s> tree therein,

children.text: vakṣaḥ pinaṣṭi rudatī taralā sakhī me // RUnm_9.24 //
children.translated_text: my trembling friend beats her breast and weeps!' // RUnm_9.24 //

body.translated_text: Regarding the proclamation of one's own faction's love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, for example —

children.translated_text: 'You are fortunate, O <s>Ramālikā</s>, the leaf-pattern (<s>patra-vallī</s>) fashioned by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s hand —
you play about with limbs languid with rapture!',
'Alas! I was deceived! When the moon-face of <s>Lalitā</s> was perceived,
even He who is the master of all arts becomes stupefied!' // RUnm_9.25 //

body.translated_text: Regarding the proclamation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s love for one's own faction, for example —

children.translated_text: That pride which indicates the excellence of one's amusements is called haughtiness (<s>darpa</s>). // RUnm_9.26 //

children.text: vidmaḥ puṇyavatī-śikhāmaṇim iha tvām eva harmye yayā
children.translated_text: 'We know you to be the crest-jewel of virtuous women here in this palace,
by whom the nights, white with the light of autumn moons, are spent in festivals of sleep.',

children.text: ko'yaṃ naḥ phalati sma karma-viṭapī vṛndāṭavī-kandare
children.translated_text: 'What is this tree of karma that bears fruit for us in the hollow of the <s>Vṛndā</s> forest —

children.text: śyāmaḥ ko'pi karī karoti hṛdayonmādena nidrā-kṣayam // RUnm_9.27 //
children.translated_text: some dark elephant who with the intoxication of the heart destroys sleep?' // RUnm_9.27 //

children.text: upahāso vipakṣasya sākṣād uddhasitaṃ bhavet // RUnm_9.28 //
children.translated_text: Direct mockery of the rival faction is called derision (<s>uddhasita</s>). // RUnm_9.28 //

children.text: noccair niḥśvasihi prasīda parame muñca grahaṃ durlabhe
children.translated_text: 'Do not sigh aloud, be at peace, O supreme one! Release your [frustrated] grasp, O hard-to-attain one!',

children.text: mlāniṃ te sakhi vīkṣya hanta kṛpayā mac-cittam uttāmyati |
children.translated_text: 'O friend, seeing your dejection, alas, my heart melts with compassion!',
'Look — bound here in the net-trap of <s>Lalitā</s>'s eloquent words,

children.text: jānīte na kila svam eva sarale śyāmaḥ kuraṅgī-patiḥ // RUnm_9.29 //
children.translated_text: the dark deer-lord [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], O guileless one, does not even know himself!' // RUnm_9.29 //

children.text: sevādy-utkarṣakṛd garvo mada ity abhidhīyate // RUnm_9.30 //
children.translated_text: That pride which is produced by the excellence of worship and the like is called intoxication (<s>mada</s>). // RUnm_9.30 //

children.text: jagati lalite dhanyā yūyaṃ sugandhibhir adbhutai-
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Lalite</s>, you are fortunate in the world — with these wondrous fragrant
flowers, by which He is worshipped ceaselessly!',

children.text: bata vidhi-vaśāj jātaṃ vanya-sraji vyasanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: 'Alas, by the force of fate, such is our misfortune regarding forest-garlands

children.text: dalam api na naḥ kātyāyanyai yathā pariśiṣyate // RUnm_9.31 //
children.translated_text: that not even a petal remains for [offering to] <s>Kātyāyanī</s> [goddess]!' // RUnm_9.31 //

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ svotkṛṣṭatākhyānam auddhatyam iti kīrtyate // RUnm_9.32 //
children.translated_text: The explicit proclamation of one's own superiority is celebrated as insolence (<s>auddhatya</s>). // RUnm_9.32 //

children.text: kas tāvad vraja-maṇḍale sa valate gāndharvikā spardhatāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Who indeed in the circle of <s>Vraja</s> dares compete with <s>Gāndharvikā</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>]?',
'Alas! She is a person whose fame is a banner spreading across the entire world!',
'Out of compassion, the hearts of whose pitiful servitors melt —

children.text: yasyāḥ preraṇayā kṣaṇaṃ bhavati vaḥ padme niṣevyo hariḥ // RUnm_9.33 //
children.translated_text: by whose prompting, O <s>Padme</s>, <s>Hari</s> becomes your servant even for a moment!' // RUnm_9.33 //

children.text: śliṣṭoktiś ca kvacit tāsāṃ nindā-garbhopajāyate // RUnm_9.34 //
children.translated_text: Occasionally, equivocal speech (<s>śliṣṭokti</s>) among them gives rise to hidden blame. // RUnm_9.34 //
'Adorned by <s>Govinda</s>, free from the occasion of obtaining distress,
expert in abundant arts, repeatedly displaying the beauty of dense youth with her body,',
'a doer of the most supremely excellent holy deed, O auspicious one — your friend

children.text: nāsau bhāgya-bharāt kadāpi viratiṃ prāpnoti saudāminī // RUnm_9.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saudāminī</s> (Lightning) never attains cessation from the weight of [her] fortune!' // RUnm_9.35 //

body.text:
yathā vā-
samasta-jana-locanotsava-vinoda-niṣpādinī
vilakṣaṇa-gati-kriyā-vicalitāṅga-hāra-sthitiḥ |
nirasya haritālajaṃ ruci-taraṅgam ātmorjitaiḥ

children.text: sakhī naṭati te rasa-skhalitam atra khelāvatī // RUnm_9.36|
children.translated_text: your friend dances here with stumbling rasa, O sportive one!' // RUnm_9.36 //

body.translated_text: 'Accomplishing entertainment that is a festival for the eyes of all people, with extraordinary gait, movements, and swaying gestures of her limbs, having surpassed the radiance-wave of orpiment by her own splendors,

children.text: yās tu yūthābhināthāḥ syuḥ sākṣān nerṣyanti tāḥ sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: But those who are group-leaders themselves do not openly display jealousy
toward the rival faction, because of the arising of their own qualities of depth, propriety, and the like. // RUnm_9.37 //
'Seeing the friend of the rival's beloved, whose boastful display of great pride was exposed,
<s>Maṅgalā</s>, sparkling with the foam of rare laughter,',

children.text: tatāna tam anākulaṃ vinaya-nirjharaṃ yena sā
children.translated_text: 'extended that unperturbed stream of modesty by which [the rival]',

children.text: nije tarasi majjitā sapadi lajjitā vivyathe // RUnm_9.38 //
children.translated_text: 'was immediately submerged in her own pool, and humiliated, she suffered.' // RUnm_9.38 //
The lesser ones, even if sharp, generally do not speak jealously

children.text: jalpanti laghavaḥ serṣyaṃ prāyaśaḥ prakharā api // RUnm_9.39 //
children.translated_text: openly before the leader of the rival group. // RUnm_9.39 //

children.text: diṣṭyā dustarato mad-ukti-nigaḍān muktāsi mugdhe kṣaṇā-
children.translated_text: 'Fortunately, O innocent one, you have been freed in a moment from the hard-to-escape fetters of my words!',

children.text: dabhyarṇe vṛṣabhānujā vijayate yad bhānujāyās taṭe |
children.translated_text: 'The daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>] is victorious near the bank of [your] daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>]!',

children.text: nātathyaṃ prathayāmi devy api girāṃ vāg-dyūta-kelīṣu me
children.translated_text: 'O Goddess, I do not spread falsehood — but in my word-gambling-games,
even the venerable Goddess of Modesty, her counter-arguments swept away, drowns in the ocean of shame!' // RUnm_9.40 //
Those who declare that emotions such as hatred and the like are not fitting among <s>Hari</s>'s beloved people

children.text: ye vyāharanti te jñeyā apūrva-rasikāḥ kṣitau // RUnm_9.41 //
children.translated_text: should be known as unparalleled connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s> on earth. // RUnm_9.41 //
Or for example —
More enchanting than even hosts of <s>Kandarpas</s> (Cupids), the enemy of sin [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]'s

children.text: mūrto narma-priya-sakhaḥ śṛṅgāro vartate vraje // RUnm_9.42 //
children.translated_text: dear friend of humor (<s>narmapriya-sakha</s>) — <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic rasa) personified — exists in <s>Vraja</s>. // RUnm_9.42 //
This [<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>] would cast upon these two mutually opposite factions
jealousy and the other [emotions] as his own retinue, in their union, for the delight of their own beloved;

children.text: ataeva hi viśleṣe snehas tāsāṃ prakāśate // RUnm_9.43 //
children.translated_text: for this very reason, in separation, their mutual affection becomes manifest. // RUnm_9.43 //

children.text: sāndraiḥ sundari vṛndaśo hari-pariṣvaṅgair idaṃ maṅgalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'O beautiful one, this auspicious sight has been seen by you in groups — the dense embraces of <s>Hari</s>!',

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ te hata-rādhayāṅgam anayā diṣṭyādya candrāvali |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Candrāvalī</s>, by good fortune, this <s>Rādhā</s> whose limbs are [now] ruined [by love-marks] today!',

children.text: drāg enāṃ nihitena kaṇṭham abhitaḥ śīrṇena kaṃsa-dviṣaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Quickly, kindle her with your own pair of arms placed around [her] neck,
fragrant with the ear-ornament of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>!' // RUnm_9.44 //
Now the cause of the own-faction and other divisions of the group-leader is stated:

children.text: bhāvasya sarvathaivātra sājātye syāt sapakṣatā // RUnm_9.45 //
children.translated_text: Where there is complete homogeneity of emotion (<s>bhāva</s>), there is own-faction status. // RUnm_9.45 //
Where there is slight heterogeneity of this [emotion], it is declared to be allied-faction status;
when the homogeneity is slight, neutrality should be understood;

children.text: sarvathā khalu vaijātye niścitā pratipakṣatā // RUnm_9.46 //
children.translated_text: when there is complete heterogeneity, rival-faction status is certain. // RUnm_9.46 //

children.text: mitho-bhāvasya vaijātye na bhāvo rocate mithaḥ |
children.translated_text: When there is heterogeneity of mutual emotion, mutual emotion does not please;
by that very displeasure, it gives rise to supreme intolerance. // RUnm_9.47 //

children.text: yā madhyastha-padena saṅkulatarā śuddhā prakṛtyā jaḍā
children.translated_text: 'She who is so thoroughly confused with neutrality, pure by nature, dull,
skilled at closing the lotus of cleverness, delighting in hidden faults —',

children.text: āśāyāḥ sphuraṇaṃ harer janayituṃ yuktātra candrāvalī
children.translated_text: 'that even <s>Candrāvalī</s> might generate a flash of hope in <s>Hari</s> here —',

children.text: sāpi syād iti locayan sakhi janaḥ kaḥ soḍhum īṣṭe kṣitau // RUnm_9.48 //
children.translated_text: 'reflecting thus, O friend, what person on earth can endure it?' // RUnm_9.48 //

children.text: ṣoḍaśyās tvam uḍor vimuñca sahasā nāmāpi vāmāśaye
children.translated_text: 'O [woman] of the sixteenth [night, i.e., the full moon], instantly release even the name of the moon in your perverse heart!',

children.text: tasyā durvinayair muner api manaḥ śāntātmanaḥ kupyati |
children.translated_text: 'By her ill-mannered behavior, even the mind of a sage, serene-natured, becomes angered.'
Shame on her! When the son of the lord of the cowherd settlement, the crest-jewel of all virtuous ones, worshipped by all of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: pādānte patite'pi naiva kurute bhrū-kṣepam apy atra yā // RUnm_9.49 //
children.translated_text: has fallen at her feet, she does not even cast a glance of her eyebrow here! // RUnm_9.49 //
Where there is generally equal measure of one's own emotion (<s>bhāva</s>),

children.text: pakṣaḥ sa eva maitrāya vidveṣāya ca yujyate // RUnm_9.50 //
children.translated_text: that very faction is suited for both friendship and enmity. // RUnm_9.50 //
Not even a fraction of <s>Rādhā</s>'s wealth of qualities such as <s>prema</s> (divine love) and others

children.text: rasenaiva vipakṣādau mithaḥ sāmyam ivārpyate // RUnm_9.51 //
children.translated_text: is found elsewhere; only by <s>rasa</s> is a semblance of mutual equality bestowed upon the rival faction and others. // RUnm_9.51 //
When there is extreme excess of emotion, complete homogeneity between the two,

children.text: tathā tulya-pramāṇatvam evaṃ prāyaḥ sudurghaṭam // RUnm_9.52 //
children.translated_text: and likewise equal measure — such a combination is generally very difficult to achieve. // RUnm_9.52 //
If it should occur by the principle of the worm-and-letter analogy (<s>ghūṇākṣara-nyāya</s>), only friendship is accepted here;

children.text: rasa-svabhāvād atrāpi vaipakṣyam iti kecana // RUnm_9.53 //
children.translated_text: but some say that even in this case, rivalry arises due to the nature of <s>rasa</s>. // RUnm_9.53 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on <s>Hari</s>'s beloveds (<s>Hari-vallabhā-prakaraṇam</s>) in the illustrious <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>. ||9||
Now, the chapter on stimulant causes (<s>Uddīpana-vibhāva-prakaraṇam</s>).

children.translated_text: Now, among the causes (<s>vibhāvas</s>), the stimulants (<s>uddīpanas</s>):
The stimulant causes (<s>uddīpana-vibhāvas</s>) of <s>Hari</s> and of His beloveds
are described as being related to qualities, names, pastimes, and ornaments, as well as incidental ones. // RUnm_10.1 //

children.text: guṇās tridhā mānasā syur vācikāḥ kāyikās tathā // RUnm_10.2 //
children.translated_text: Qualities are threefold: mental, verbal, and physical. // RUnm_10.2 //
The mental qualities are gratitude, forbearance, compassion, and the like. // RUnm_10.3 //
Seeing my <s>Hari</s>, who is won over even by the slightest service,
who remains smiling-faced even when an unbearable offense has been committed,
who is distressed even by a trace of another's suffering —

children.text: harim udvīkṣya manas tanoti tṛṣṇām // RUnm_10.4 //
children.translated_text: my mind expands with longing. // RUnm_10.4 //

children.text: vācikās tu guṇāḥ proktāḥ karṇānandakatādayaḥ // RUnm_10.5 //
children.translated_text: The verbal qualities are declared to be those such as delighting the ears and the like. // RUnm_10.5 //
Of ear-stealing expression,
practiced with unprecedented sweetness —
O friend, the <s>rasa</s>-filled speech of <s>Mādhava</s>,
I am never satiated even after savoring it. // RUnm_10.6 //
Now, the physical ones:
Those are age, form, gracefulness, beauty, comeliness,

children.text: mādhuryaṃ mārdavādyāś ca kāyikāḥ kathitā guṇāḥ // RUnm_10.7 //
children.translated_text: sweetness, softness, and the like — these are stated to be physical qualities. // RUnm_10.7 //
Among these, age (<s>vayas</s>):

children.text: vayaś caturvidhaṃ tv atra kathitaṃ madhure rase |
children.translated_text: Age is described here as fourfold in the sweet <s>rasa</s>:

children.text: vayaḥ-sandhis tathā navyaṃ vyaktaṃ pūrṇam iti kramāt // RUnm_10.8 //
children.translated_text: the junction of ages (<s>vayaḥ-sandhi</s>), new (<s>navya</s>), manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), and full (<s>pūrṇa</s>), in that order. // RUnm_10.8 //
The qualities beginning with age, having been previously described in relation to <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: tena te'tra pravakṣyante prāyaśas tat-priyānugāḥ // RUnm_10.9 //
children.translated_text: therefore here they will be described mostly as they follow His beloveds. // RUnm_10.9 //
The junction of childhood and youth is called <s>vayaḥ-sandhi</s>. // RUnm_10.10 //

body.translated_text: Among these, the junction of ages (<s>vayaḥ-sandhi</s>):

children.translated_text: Relinquishing its tawny shade and turning dark, O king of love,
the line of body-hair attains the path of a row of letters of <s>Smara</s>'s (Cupid's) royal decree;
it slightly desires the surging spray of fresh youth,

children.text: labdhvā kiñcid adhīram akṣi-śaphara-dvandvaṃ ca kaṃsadviṣaḥ // RUnm_10.11 //
children.translated_text: and the pair of fish-like eyes of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> has become somewhat restless. // RUnm_10.11 //

body.translated_text: That, in the case of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, for example —

children.translated_text: Seeing the unsteady hunter with five arrows [<s>Kāmadeva</s>], desiring his target,
now ascending the peak of your beautiful body's limbs,
O great lord of <s>Vraja</s>, in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, the host of doe-eyed maidens, constantly soaked with tears,
has become slightly agitated. // RUnm_10.12 //

children.text: vādyaṃ kiṅkiṇim āharaty upacayaṃ jñātvā nitambo guṇī
children.translated_text: The talented hip, knowing its increased fullness, brings forth the jingling of ankle-bells as music;

children.text: svasya dhvaṃsam avetya vaṣṭi balibhir yogaṃ hrasan-madhyamam |
children.translated_text: the narrowing waist, perceiving its own diminishment, desires alliance with the sash;
the chest seeks out a pair of worthy fruits fit as a royal offering —

children.text: rādhāyās tanu-rājyam añcati nave kṣauṇī-patau yauvane // RUnm_10.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>'s body-kingdom advances as the new sovereign, Youth, ascends the throne. // RUnm_10.13 //
The bee of the sidelong glance hopes to slowly alight upon the blue lotus of the eye;
the young swan-cygnet of the mind seeks out the slightly sprouting shoots of bashfulness;
today, a flood of honey of playful conversation arises in the lotus of your face —

children.text: śaṅke sundari mādhavotsava-karīṃ kāñcid daśām añcasi // RUnm_10.14 //
children.translated_text: I suspect, O beautiful one, you are entering some state that will create a festival for <s>Mādhava</s>. // RUnm_10.14 //
Now, the new (<s>navya</s>) stage:
With slightly budding breasts, somewhat restless eyes, a slow smile,

children.text: manāg abhisphurad-bhāvaṃ navyaṃ yauvanam ucyate // RUnm_10.15 //
children.translated_text: and faintly emerging emotions — this is called new youth (<s>navya yauvana</s>). // RUnm_10.15 //
The chest slightly swelling, speech touched by a trace of rising coquetry,
the gaze somewhat reeling, the surface of the hips slightly fuller,

children.text: manāg vyaktā romāvalir apacitaṃ kiñcid udaraṃ
children.translated_text: the line of body-hair faintly visible, the belly slightly reduced —

children.text: hareḥ sevaucityaṃ tava suvadane vindati vayaḥ // RUnm_10.16 //
children.translated_text: O fair-faced one, your age is acquiring the fitness for <s>Hari</s>'s service. // RUnm_10.16 //

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ vicarasi harer adya viśrāma-vedyā-
children.translated_text: Again and again today you wander near <s>Hari</s>'s resting platform;

children.text: mudbhrāntāsi sphurati pavane tad vapur gandha-bhāji |
children.translated_text: you become bewildered when the wind carries the fragrance of His body;

children.text: bāle netre vikirasi muhur naicikīnāṃ padavyāṃ
children.translated_text: O young girl, you repeatedly cast your eyes upon the path of the sentinels —

children.text: bhāvāgnis te sphuṭam iha mano-dhāmni dhūmāyito'sti // RUnm_10.17 //
children.translated_text: clearly, the fire of <s>bhāva</s> (love) in the abode of your mind has begun to smoke. // RUnm_10.17 //
Now, the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) stage:
The chest with fully manifest breasts, the waist with beautiful three folds,

children.text: ujjvalāni tathāṅgāni vyakte sphurati yauvane // RUnm_10.18 //
children.translated_text: and resplendent limbs — these shine forth in manifest youth. // RUnm_10.18 //
The radiance of the breasts reveals a new pair of <s>cakravāka</s> birds;
the pair of eyes manifests the movement of <s>śaphara</s> fish, O <s>Indrāvalī</s>;
and you bear three folds that arise like the cresting of waves —

children.text: tvam atra sarasīkṛtā taruṇima-śriyā rājasi // RUnm_10.19 //
children.translated_text: you have been transformed into a lake and shine with the splendor of youth. // RUnm_10.19 //
The clusters of pearls from your beautiful teeth gleam, scored by the nails;
these, their luster veiled by lotus garlands, are scattered in bower after bower.
How was it that while you, O ocean of audacity, were reclining upon the surface of the cage of your breasts,

children.text: sa śrīmān hariṇekṣaṇe harir abhūn netreṇa baddhas tvayā // RUnm_10.20 //
children.translated_text: that glorious <s>Hari</s>, O doe-eyed one, was bound by you with merely a glance? // RUnm_10.20 //
Now, the full (<s>pūrṇa</s>) stage:

children.text: nitambo vipulo madhyaṃ kṛśam aṅgaṃ vara-dyuti |
children.translated_text: The hips broad, the waist slender, the body of excellent radiance,

children.text: pīnau kucāv uru-yugmaṃ rambhābhaṃ pūrṇa-yauvane // RUnm_10.21 //
children.translated_text: the breasts full, the pair of thighs resembling plantain stems — such are the marks of full youth. // RUnm_10.21 //
The pair of eyes steals the curving wave of delight from <s>śaphara</s> fish;
the beauty of the face wholly subdues the sweetness of the moon;
the breasts repeatedly produce an unbroken illusion of golden water-pots —

children.text: stavāpūrvaṃ līlāvati vayasi pūrṇe vapur abhūt // RUnm_10.22 //
children.translated_text: O playful one, your body has become unprecedented in the fullness of age. // RUnm_10.22 //

children.text: na vitrastā kā te pratiyuvatir āsīn mukha-rucā
children.translated_text: Which rival maiden was not frightened by the radiance of your face?

children.text: dadhāra staimityaṃ praṇaya-ghana-vṛṣṭyā tava na kā |
children.translated_text: Which one maintained composure under the dense rain of your love?

children.text: vraje śiṣyā kābhūn na hi tava kalāyām iti hare-
children.translated_text: Who in <s>Vraja</s> was not a pupil of your art? Therefore, of <s>Hari</s>'s

children.text: rnikuñja-svārāje tvam asi rasike paṭṭa-mahiṣī // RUnm_10.23 //
children.translated_text: bower-kingdom, O connoisseur of <s>rasa</s>, you are the crowned queen. // RUnm_10.23 //
Even when youth is still in its new stage, for some beautiful-browed ladies of <s>Vraja</s>,
it appears as though full, due to a special perfection of beauty. // RUnm_10.24 //
Now, form (<s>rūpa</s>):
When the limbs, though unadorned by any ornament whatsoever,

children.text: yena bhūṣitavad bhāti tad rūpam iti kathyate // RUnm_10.25 //
children.translated_text: shine as if adorned — that is called <s>rūpa</s> (form). // RUnm_10.25 //
<s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) feels ashamed upon seeing
the graceful <s>Rādhā</s> even without ornaments.
Therefore, enough with the labor
of fashioning arrays of jeweled ornaments! // RUnm_10.26 //

children.text: nītaṃ te punar uktatāṃ bhramarakaiḥ kastūrikā-patrakaṃ
children.translated_text: Your <s>kastūrikā</s> (musk) leaf-mark has been rendered redundant by the bees;
the pair of <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) flowers placed at the ears has been made futile by your eyes;
the necklace has been thoroughly surpassed by the waves of radiance of your smile —

children.text: kiṃ rādhe tava maṇḍanena nitarām aṅgair asi dyotitā // RUnm_10.27 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhā</s>, what need is there for your ornaments? You are most resplendent by your limbs alone! // RUnm_10.27 //
Now, gracefulness (<s>lāvaṇya</s>):
As there is an inner quivering of luster within pearls,

children.text: pratibhāti yad aṅgeṣu lāvaṇyaṃ tad ihocyate // RUnm_10.28 //
children.translated_text: that which similarly gleams within the limbs is here called <s>lāvaṇya</s> (gracefulness). // RUnm_10.28 //
O <s>Rādhā</s>, having searched the world for pure radiance,
the Creator surely fashioned your limbs;
O doe-eyed one, they put to shame
jeweled mirrors with their clusters of rays. // RUnm_10.29 //

children.text: śṛṇu sakhi tava karṇe varṇayāmy atra nīcai-
children.translated_text: 'Listen, O friend, I whisper this in your ear softly:
do not make your moon-like face pale without cause!

children.text: iyam urasi murārer asti nānyā mṛgākṣī
children.translated_text: This one upon the chest of <s>Murāri</s> is no other doe-eyed maiden —
on the emerald-mirror-like chest, it is you yourself reflected!' // RUnm_10.30 //
Now, beauty (<s>saundarya</s>):
That which is the proper arrangement of the major and minor limbs,

children.text: susliṣṭa-sandhi-bandhaḥ syāt tat saundaryam itīryate // RUnm_10.31 //
children.translated_text: with well-joined and well-bound connections — that is called <s>saundarya</s> (beauty). // RUnm_10.31 //
A face equal to the full moon, a chest illuminated by ample breasts,

children.text: bhujau srastāv aṃse kara-parimitaṃ madhyam abhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: arms gracefully drooping from the shoulders, a waist spanned by the hands on all sides,
expansive hips, a pair of thighs possessing graduated slenderness —

children.text: tavāpūrvaṃ rādhe kim api kamanīyaṃ vapur abhūt // RUnm_10.32 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhā</s>, your body has become something indescribably beautiful and unprecedented. // RUnm_10.32 //
Now, comeliness (<s>abhirūpatā</s>):
That by which, through the excellence of one's own qualities, another object standing nearby

children.text: sārūpyaṃ nayati prājñair ābhirūpyaṃ tad ucyate // RUnm_10.33 //
children.translated_text: is made to assume a resemblance — that is called <s>ābhirūpya</s> (comeliness) by the wise. // RUnm_10.33 //
Immersed in the bright ray of His teeth, it gleams like crystal;
attached to the red lotus of His hand, it appears like a ruby, O fair one;
near His cheek, due to the luster of the blue lotus, it appears to have become a sapphire —

children.text: sūte ratna-traya-dhiyam asau paśya kṛṣṇasya vaṃśī // RUnm_10.34 //
children.translated_text: behold, this flute of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> produces the illusion of three gems! // RUnm_10.34 //
Upon your breasts, resembling magnificent golden water-pots, the luster of <s>campaka</s> flowers;
O <s>Rādhā</s>, upon your beautiful palms, the beauty of red lotuses from the vermillion;
bearing in the lovely dark tresses the appearance of blue lotuses —
the fingernail, like a white water-lily bud, produces the illusion of a triad of flowers. // RUnm_10.35 //

children.text: rūpaṃ kim apy anirvācyaṃ tanor mādhuryam ucyate // RUnm_10.36 //
children.translated_text: That indescribable something of the body's form is called <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). // RUnm_10.36 //

children.text: kim api hṛdayam abhra-śyāmalaṃ dhāma rundhe
children.translated_text: Some ineffable cloud-dark radiance obstructs the heart;

children.text: dṛśam ahaha viluṇṭhaty āṅgikī kāpi mudrā |
children.translated_text: alas, some bodily gesture plunders the sight;
it makes fickle the righteous conduct of a noble woman — the form of the enemy of <s>Baka</s>;

children.text: sumukhi nava-vivartaḥ ko'py asau mādhurīṇām // RUnm_10.37 //
children.translated_text: O beautiful-faced one, this is some unprecedented revolution of sweetnesses. // RUnm_10.37 //
Now, softness (<s>mārdava</s>):
<s>Mārdava</s> (softness) is described as intolerance of touch even by what is itself soft.

children.text: uttamaṃ madhyamaṃ proktaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ ceti tat tridhā // RUnm_10.38 //
children.translated_text: It is said to be threefold: superior, middling, and inferior. // RUnm_10.38 //
That <s>Rādhikā</s> lay upon a splendid bed
of fresh new <s>mālikā</s> (jasmine) garlands at night;
the layer of flowers was not crushed even slightly,
yet from the experience of them, her body itself became bruised. // RUnm_10.39 //
How wondrous, O <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>! Even from a thin garment
of Chinese silk, from its contact with her full breasts,
your form appeared as if smeared with red sandalwood —
her body became reddened with marks, O friend. // RUnm_10.40 //
Bestowing fragrance and delight,
with bee-like dark locks resting upon it,
in a moment, the lotus-face of <s>Padmā</s> became
coppery-red from the luster of the sun, gentle though it was. // RUnm_10.41 //
'O fair-limbed one, look — upon the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>], a colorful one
gleams amidst a group of does: a <s>Kṛṣṇasāra</s> (black-spotted deer)!'
Hearing her own name [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] thus in my words,
that slender-bodied one became filled with a flood of intense agitation. // RUnm_10.42 //
Now, pastimes (<s>carita</s>):

children.text: anubhāvāś ca līlā cety ucyate caritaṃ dvidhā |
children.translated_text: Pastimes (<s>carita</s>) are said to be twofold: <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) and <s>līlās</s> (divine play).
The <s>anubhāvas</s> are to be described later; the <s>līlā</s> is described now. // RUnm_10.43 //
<s>Līlā</s> consists of charming play (<s>cāru-vikrīḍā</s>), <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance, flute-playing (<s>veṇu-vādana</s>),
cow-milking (<s>godoha</s>), mountain-lifting (<s>parvatoddhāra</s>), cow-calling (<s>gohūti</s>), going forth, and the like. // RUnm_10.44 //
The <s>rāsa</s> dance, ball-play, and the like are here celebrated as charming play. // RUnm_10.45 //
O graceful one, seeing that lotus-eyed one in the <s>rāsa</s> circle,
the celestial women,
having beheld Him replete with the charm of amorous sport,
wandered about, tossed by waves of amorous agitation. // RUnm_10.46 //
Dispelling the radiance of the reddish dawn, with curved tip, the whip [of his gaze],
running impetuously, his long braid swinging wildly —
Mukunda performs a ball-bouncing dance
with playful sidelong glances of his wide eyes — he creates wonder in us! // RUnm_10.47 //
With his earrings swinging and dangling violently,
surrounded by the circling dance (<s>carcarī</s>) of his own circle of friends —
<s>Hari</s>, dancing today on the stage of the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>],
extends delight to me! // RUnm_10.48 //
With his right foot resting against the lower part of his calf, his waist slightly bent,
his neck held sideways, O friend, with sidelong-moving glances from the corner of his eyes,
holding the flute to his budding lips, joined by playful fingers,

children.text: riṅgad-bhrū-bhramaraṃ varāṅgi paramānandaṃ puraḥ svīkuru // RUnm_10.49 //
children.translated_text: with brow-bees creeping — O beautiful-limbed one, embrace this supreme bliss before you! // RUnm_10.49 //
With his fingers controlled by the tip of his thumb, his body restrained at the level of the feet,
having thoroughly moistened the tips of the udder with drops of milk —
with the stream falling through the space of the pot-mouth held between his two bent knees,

children.text: ddhārādhvāna-manoharaṃ sakhi payo gāṃ dogdhi dāmodaraḥ // RUnm_10.50 //
children.translated_text: O friend, <s>Dāmodara</s> milks the cow, charming with the streaming path of milk! // RUnm_10.50 //

body.translated_text: Milking the cows (<s>go-doha</s>), as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (262) —

children.translated_text: Having lifted the mountain <s>Mandara</s>, tossing it like a ball, bearing its playful belly,

children.text: savyaṃ karaṃ kaṭim anu sthagayann asavyam |
children.translated_text: his left hand placed and his right concealing against his hip —
with a smiling face, the bees of his moving sidelong glances
<s>Hari</s> made the lotus of my mind restless! // RUnm_10.51 //
O tawny one! O jewel-uddered one! O one with bowed horns! O tawny-eyed one!
O drum-faced one! O smoky one! O speckled one! O swan! O flute-lover!
Thus, repeatedly calling his own herd of cows, with his resounding cry of 'hīhī,'

children.text: rvidūra-gatam āhvayan harati hanta cittaṃ hariḥ // RUnm_10.52 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> — alas — steals my heart, who has gone not far! // RUnm_10.52 //
The splendor of his arms, bars [of a gate], swaying with incomparable, intoxicating, gentle oscillation,
his profound sport subduing the great pride of <s>Airāvata</s>, the chief of divine elephants —
O companion, the sweetness of the gait-gesture (<s>gati-mudrā</s>) of <s>Mādhava</s>,
with his beautiful crest-jewel slightly trembling, intoxicates me! // RUnm_10.53 //
Ornamentation is fourfold: by garments, ornaments, garlands, and unguents. // RUnm_10.54 //
The garment, fashioning composure and restraint,
beautiful, blazing with the radiance of the sky-jewel [sun],
O fair-browed one, do you not see it
at the hip-ornament of the lotus-eyed one? // RUnm_10.55 //
This silk cloth of yours, having the hue of a spotless lotus,
shines forth, manifestly wondrous!
Though placing upon it its own color [passion], O <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: dadhad api yad dviguṇaṃ babhūva raktam // RUnm_10.56 //
children.translated_text: in my heart, it became doubly dyed [passionate]! // RUnm_10.56 //
Let <s>Hari</s> strike with the <s>kadamba</s> flower
worn as a crest-ornament, O dear friend, which is the weapon of <s>Kāma</s> (Love)!
Alas, how is it that this peacock feather (<s>nīlakaṇṭha-pakṣa</s>)
worn as an ear-ornament by him pierces my heart! // RUnm_10.57 //
With a necklace of brilliant luster, [touching] the cheeks,
with the swaying pair of earrings,
with the towering radiance of a golden armlet —
this <s>Lalitā</s>, cherished, delights me! // RUnm_10.58 //
The wearing of garlands on the hair is inferred from the bees' gazes,

children.text: kāntiḥ kāpi kapolayoḥ prathayate tāmbūlam antargatam |
children.translated_text: some extraordinary radiance on the cheeks reveals betel-nut consumed within,
the process of anointing the limbs is experienced through their fragrance —

children.text: veṣaḥ ko'pi vidagdha eṣa sudṛśaḥ sūte sukhaṃ cakṣuṣoḥ // RUnm_10.59 //
children.translated_text: this ineffably elegant adornment of the beautiful one produces delight for the eyes! // RUnm_10.59 //

body.translated_text: Garlands and unguents (<s>mālyānulepana</s>), as in the <s>Rasasudhākara</s> (1.86) —

children.translated_text: Did your body-color (<s>aṅga-rāga</s>) instantly become
a cause of passion (<s>anaṅga-rāga</s>) among women?
Likewise, did your cord (<s>dāma</s>) become a cause
of unrestrained emotion (<s>uddāma-bhāva</s>), O <s>Dāmodara</s>? // RUnm_10.60 //

children.text: lagnāḥ sannihitāś ceti dvidhā sambandhino matāḥ // RUnm_10.61 //
children.translated_text: The associated objects are considered twofold: attached (<s>lagna</s>) and proximate (<s>sannihita</s>). // RUnm_10.61 //
Among these, the attached ones (<s>lagna</s>) —
The sound of the flute and horn, song, fragrance, the jingling of ornaments,
footprints and the like, the sounds of the <s>vīṇā</s> and other instruments, skill in crafts —

children.text: ity ādayo'tra kathitā lagnāḥ sambandhino budhaiḥ // RUnm_10.62 //
children.translated_text: these and others are declared by the learned to be the attached associated objects. // RUnm_10.62 //
This melodious sound of the flute, fostering the blossoming of trees and creepers,
a mass of twilight roaring, a recitation for the Vedic study of the cuckoo-birds' cooing —
a playful breeze for the blazing fire of love in the moon-faced <s>Ābhīra</s> women,
a deceptive flood rises to destroy the mountain-king of <s>Rādhā</s>'s composure! // RUnm_10.63 //

body.translated_text: Among these, the sound of the flute (<s>vaṃśī-rava</s>), in the <s>Dānakelikaumudī</s> (32) —

children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s>, in the bower of sweet <s>mādhavī</s> creepers,
where bees are buzzing loudly,
sang with his flute, charming to the ears,
which is a fish-hook for the pride of the <s>gopīs</s>! // RUnm_10.64 //

body.translated_text: Or for example, in the <s>Rasasudhākara</s> (1.100) [in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (246)] —

children.translated_text: The nectar of the <s>muralī</s> flute's sound, spat forth from the moon-face of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: uddīpanānāṃ sarveṣāṃ madhye pravaram īryate // RUnm_10.65 //
children.translated_text: is proclaimed as the foremost among all stimulants (<s>uddīpana</s>). // RUnm_10.65 //
Let the flute (<s>muralī</s>) drink from the face-moon of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — she who is born of a noble bamboo lineage,
straightforward, weighty with five melodic notes (<s>pañcamodgāra</s>)!
But you too, O crooked one, black as live coal, having tasted this [sweetness],

children.text: tuṅgaṃ śṛṅgi dhvanasi yad idaṃ tat tu duḥkhākaroti // RUnm_10.66 //
children.translated_text: O horn (<s>śṛṅgi</s>), that you resound so loudly — this indeed causes distress! // RUnm_10.66 //
Extinguishing the blazing fire of my jealous anger,
the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-cloud showers the nectar of song —
do not be angry, O friend, you are a tempest — be gracious!
Let us carry this away far with our own playful charm! // RUnm_10.67 //
Whose wave of fragrance is this, mixed with the beauty of body-hair,
causing buds to form on the creeper of my body?
O friend, it is known — <s>Mādhava</s> has appeared here before,

children.text: bhuvi surabhitayā yaḥ khyātim aṅgīkaroti // RUnm_10.68 //
children.translated_text: who assumes fame on earth through his fragrance! // RUnm_10.68 //

Your row of glances approaches obliquely with arrested neck, like a bud;

children.text: ghūrṇan karṇa-latāṃ manāg vikasitā bhrū-vallarī nṛtyati |
children.translated_text: the revolving ear-creeper slightly blossoms, and the eyebrow-vine dances;

children.text: atra prādurabhūt taṭe sumanasām ullāsakas tvat-puro
children.translated_text: here, upon the river-bank of beautiful flowers, an exultation has first arisen before you —

children.text: gaurāṅgi prathamaṃ vana-priaya-bandhuḥ sphuṭaṃ mādhavaḥ // RUnm_11.10 //
children.translated_text: O fair-limbed one, clearly <s>Mādhava</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], the dear friend of the forest, [has appeared]! // RUnm_11.10 //

children.text: hāva eva bhaved dhelā vyakta-śṛṅgāra-sūcakaḥ // RUnm_11.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hāva</s> itself becomes <s>helā</s> when it clearly indicates <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love). // RUnm_11.11 //

children.text: śrute veṇau vakṣaḥ sphurtia-kucam ādhmātam api te
children.translated_text: Upon hearing the flute, your bosom with heaving breasts was puffed up,
your face with sidelong-cast eyes had its cheeks horripilated,
and your hips with loosened girdle and perspiration-moistened garment — O friend, be not careless! An elder walks at your left side! // RUnm_11.12 //

children.text: pramādaṃ mā kārṣīḥ sakhi carati savye gurujanaḥ // RUnm_11.12 //
sā śobhā rūpa-bhogādyair yat syād aṅga-vibhūṣaṇam // RUnm_11.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śobhā</s> is the adornment of the body through beauty of form, enjoyment, and the like. // RUnm_11.13 //
<s>Viśākhā</s>, holding a <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) branch with her red shoot-like fingers,
emerging from the house of ritual fasting in the morning with rolling eyes,

children.text: veṇīm aṃsopari viluṭhatīm ardham uktāṃ vahantī
children.translated_text: wearing her braid half-spoken-of, tumbling over her shoulder —

children.text: lagnā svānte mama na hi bahiḥ seyam adyāpy ayāsīt // RUnm_11.14 //
children.translated_text: she has remained fastened in my heart; indeed, she has not gone outside even to this day! // RUnm_11.14 //
<s>Śobhā</s> itself is called <s>kānti</s> when it is brilliant with the nourishment of love. // RUnm_11.15 //
With a form naturally sweet, and even here embraced by
the fresh line of beauty of rising youth,
and now even there, noble with the excellent sports of love,

children.text: madayati hṛdayaṃ me rundhatī rādhikeyam // RUnm_11.16 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Rādhikā</s> intoxicates my heart, overpowering [all]! // RUnm_11.16 //
Now <s>dīpti</s> —
<s>Kānti</s> itself, when kindled by age, enjoyment, place, time, qualities, and the like,

children.text: uddīpitātivistāraṃ prāptā ced dīptir ucyate // RUnm_11.17 //
children.translated_text: and having attained an extremely vast expansion, is called <s>dīpti</s> (radiance). // RUnm_11.17 //
With the beauty of half-closed eyes, her perspiration absorbed by the still sandalwood-mountain breeze,
with breasts radiant from a snapping spotless pearl necklace,
her body reclined in a bower on a bank glistening with moonbeams —

children.text: kiśorī sā tene hari-manasi rādhā manasijam // RUnm_11.18 //
children.translated_text: that young maiden <s>Rādhā</s> aroused <s>Manasija</s> (Cupid) in the mind of <s>Hari</s>! // RUnm_11.18 //

children.text: mādhuryaṃ nāma ceṣṭānāṃ sarvāvasthāsu cārutā // RUnm_11.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness) is the charm of [a woman's] gestures in all conditions. // RUnm_11.19 //
Placing her horripilated left arm upon the shoulder-head of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
her right hand on her own hip, with feet placed crookedly,
bearing her head slightly drooping to one side —

children.text: babhau rāsottīrṇā muhur alasa-mūrtiḥ śaśimukhī // RUnm_11.20 //
children.translated_text: this moon-faced one, having come from the <s>rāsa</s> dance, shone with a languid form, again and again! // RUnm_11.20 //

children.text: niḥśaṅkatvaṃ prayogeṣu budhair uktā pragalbhatā // RUnm_11.21 //
children.translated_text: Fearlessness in love-play is called <s>pragalbhatā</s> (boldness) by the wise. // RUnm_11.21 //
<s>Rādhikā</s>, who displayed what seemed like opposition,
bold with the offering of teeth and nails,
attained expertise in the art of love-play,

children.text: tena tuṣṭim atulāṃ harir yayau // RUnm_11.22 //
children.translated_text: and by that <s>Hari</s> attained unequaled satisfaction. // RUnm_11.22 //

children.text: audāryaṃ vinayaṃ prāhuḥ sarvāvasthāgataṃ budhāḥ // RUnm_11.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Audārya</s> (nobility), the wise say, is propriety present in all conditions. // RUnm_11.23 //
A certain sincerity settled at the corner of her eye,
and in her speech, a strain of hymning dwelt with modesty;

children.text: ajani ca mayi bhūyān sambhramas tena tasyā
children.translated_text: and great agitation arose in her toward me — therefore

children.text: vyavṛṇuta hṛdi manyuṃ suṣṭhu dākṣiṇyam eva // RUnm_11.24 //
children.translated_text: her <s>dākṣiṇya</s> (graciousness) itself thoroughly dispelled the anger in her heart. // RUnm_11.24 //
Though grateful, though brilliant-minded with love, though possessed of great modesty,
though the crest-jewel of the wise, though an ocean of compassion,

children.text: yad antaḥ-svaccho'pi smarati na harir gokulabhuvaṃ
children.translated_text: yet, that <s>Hari</s>, though inwardly pure, does not remember <s>Gokula</s> —
this is indeed the fruit of the evil tree corrupted by the sins of my former lives! // RUnm_11.25 //

children.text: sthirā cittonnatir yā tu tad dhairyam iti kīrtyate // RUnm_11.26 //
children.translated_text: That which is a steady elevation of the mind is celebrated as <s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness). // RUnm_11.26 //
'Let the dark-complexioned handsome one [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], his heart pervaded by the burden of indifference, cling to harshness',

children.text: kāmaṃ śyāmala-sundaro mayi sakhi svairī sahasraṃ samāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'toward me, O friend, as a libertine, for a thousand years if he pleases;'

children.text: kintu bhrānti-bharād api kṣaṇam idaṃ tatra priyebhyaḥ priye
children.translated_text: 'but even through the weight of confusion, let this [heart of mine] — to the dearest among beloved ones, O dear one —',

children.text: ceto janmani janmani praṇayitād āsyaṃ na me hāsyati // RUnm_11.27 //
children.translated_text: 'my mind shall not turn its face away from that beloved, birth after birth!' // RUnm_11.27 //
<s>Līlā</s> (playful imitation) is the imitation of the beloved through charming dress, actions, and the like. // RUnm_11.28 //
As in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> (5.13.27) —
'O wicked <s>Kāliya</s>, stay! I am <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' — thus another [<s>gopī</s>],

children.text: bāhum āsphoṭya kṛṣṇasya līlā-sarvasvam ādade // RUnm_11.29 //
children.translated_text: slapping her arms, assumed the entire essence of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>līlā</s>. // RUnm_11.29 //
Anointed with musk, clad in yellow silk garments,
wearing a beautiful peacock-feather crest with her braided hair bound up,
playing the flute placed crookedly on her shoulder —
may <s>Mālinī</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>], having assumed the guise of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], protect you! // RUnm_11.30 //
Now <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry) —
The temporary distinction in gait, posture, sitting, and other [movements],

children.text: tātkālikaṃ tu vaiśiṣṭyaṃ vilāsaḥ priya-saṅgajam // RUnm_11.31 //
children.translated_text: and in the actions of the face, eyes, and the rest, born from the company of the beloved, is <s>vilāsa</s>. // RUnm_11.31 //

children.text: ruṇatsi purataḥ sphuraty aghahare kathaṃ nāsikā-
children.translated_text: 'You obstruct [the path] before [him]; when the destroyer of <s>Agha</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] appears, how [can you help it]? The tip of [your] nose —'
'with a pearl strung upon the crest, rising up with a semblance of smile —'
'instantly transcended the sweetness of the moonbeam's <s>kaumudī</s> radiance;

children.text: manāg api tavodgatā madhura-danti danta-dyutiḥ // RUnm_11.32 //
children.translated_text: even slightly risen, O sweet-toothed one, the luster of your teeth!' // RUnm_11.32 //
'As you eagerly gaze ahead at him seated near the <s>kadamba</s> [tree],
at the site of the pleasure-pavilion — that prince of the cowherds —'
'anointed by the charm-dripping waves of the milky ocean's gentle billows,

children.text: kālindī tava dṛk-taraṅgita-bharais tanvaṅgi gaṅgāyate // RUnm_11.33 //
children.translated_text: O slender-limbed one, <s>Kālindī</s> [<s>Yamunā</s>] becomes the <s>Gaṅgā</s> through the flood of your wave-like glances!' // RUnm_11.33 //
<s>Vicchitti</s> is the enhancement of beauty even by a slight arrangement of ornaments. // RUnm_11.34 //
With a mango leaf that delights the heart of <s>Mukunda</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
trembling in the wind,
red, made into an ear-ornament —
<s>Rādhā</s>'s lotus-face shone resplendently. // RUnm_11.35 //
Or as in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> —
With a single spotless leaf of a peacock's feather, hanging from a neck-cord,
she shone, [adorned] with that peacock feather swaying in a gentle breeze. // RUnm_11.36 //
Steadfastness in adorning [oneself] despite the beloved's offense, as if by the effort of a friend,

children.text: serṣyāvajñā vara-strībhir vicchittir iti kecana // RUnm_11.37 //
children.translated_text: and jealous disdain among excellent women — some call this <s>vicchitti</s>. // RUnm_11.37 //
'Apply a very tight seal! Remove the armlet that has been placed [by him]!

children.text: granthiṃ nyasya kaṭhoram arpita-matiḥ kaṇṭhān maṇiṃ bhraṃśaya |
children.translated_text: Tie a hard knot and with resolute mind, detach the jewel from [my] neck!'
'O innocent one, contaminated by the irresistible gaze-sting of that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-serpent,

children.text: ratnālaṅkaraṇe manāg api manas tṛṣṇāṃ na puṣṇāti me // RUnm_11.38 //
children.translated_text: my mind does not nourish even the slightest desire for jeweled ornaments!' // RUnm_11.38 //
Now <s>vibhrama</s> (confusion) —
At the moment of the beloved's arrival, from the agitation caused by the onset of passion,
<s>vibhrama</s> is the misplacement of ornaments such as necklaces, garlands, and the like. // RUnm_11.39 //
'The necklace set with blue gems has been placed by you upon the topknot,
the inner bodice fashioned as a row of blue lotuses has been placed upon the pair of breast-pitchers;'

children.text: aṅge carcitam añjanaṃ vinihitā kastūrikā netrayoḥ
children.translated_text: 'collyrium has been applied to the body, musk has been placed on the eyes —'

children.text: kaṃsārer abhisāra-sambhrama-bharān manye jagad vismṛtam // RUnm_11.40 //
children.translated_text: 'from the overwhelming confusion of the <s>abhisāra</s> (secret rendezvous) with the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], I think [she has] forgotten the world!' // RUnm_11.40 //
Or as in the blessed tenth [canto of <s>Bhāgavata</s>] (10.29.7) —

children.text: limpantyaḥ pramṛjantyo'nyā añjantyaḥ kāś ca locane |
children.translated_text: Some were applying cosmetics, others wiping off [old ones], some painting their eyes;
some went to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s presence with their garments and ornaments transposed. // RUnm_11.41 //
Not rejoicing in the service of the beloved even when he is submissive —

children.text: vibhramo vāmatodrekāt syād ity ākhyāti kaścana // RUnm_11.42 //
children.translated_text: some say <s>vibhrama</s> arises from the excess of <s>vāmatā</s> (contrarian coyness). // RUnm_11.42 //

children.text: tvaṃ govinda mayāsi kiṃ nu kavarī-bandhārtham abhyarthitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'You, <s>Govinda</s> — have you been entreated by me for the purpose of tying [my] braid?

children.text: kleśenālam abaddha eva cikura-stomo mudaṃ dogdhi me |
children.translated_text: Enough of this trouble! Even unbound, the mass of [my] hair gives me delight!'

children.text: vaktrasyāpi na mājjanaṃ kuru ghanaṃ gharmāsu me rocate
children.translated_text: 'Do not wash my face either — in the hot season the dense [perspiration] pleases me.'

children.text: naivottaṃsaya mālatīr mama śiraḥ khedaṃ bhareṇāpsyati // RUnm_11.43 //
children.translated_text: 'Do not crown [my] head with <s>mālatī</s> flowers — my head will suffer from the weight!' // RUnm_11.43 //
Now <s>kilakiñcita</s> —
The mingling together, from joy, of pride, longing, weeping, smiling, jealousy, fear, and anger
is called <s>kilakiñcita</s>. // RUnm_11.44 //
'When I, having become elated, forcibly placed [my] lotus-hands
upon <s>Rādhā</s>'s breast-buds, [which were] in the sight of [her] dear companion —'
'with rising eyebrow-play, with horripilation, steadfastly restrained and distorted,

children.text: smrāmy antas tasyāḥ smita-rudita-kānta-dyuti mukham // RUnm_11.45 //
children.translated_text: I remember that face of hers, radiant with smiling and weeping.' // RUnm_11.45 //
'Shining with inner smiling, with tear-drops scattered upon the sprouts of eyelashes,
slightly reddened at the edges, overflowing with connoisseurial sentiment, shrinking in front;'
'of <s>Rādhā</s>, blocked on the path by <s>Mādhava</s>, sweetly twisted in successive responses —'

children.text: rādhāyāḥ kilakiñcita-stavakinī dṛṣṭiḥ śriyaṃ vaḥ kriyāt // RUnm_11.46 //
children.translated_text: 'may the glance, a cluster of <s>kilakiñcita</s>, bestow beauty upon you!' // RUnm_11.46 //
Now <s>moṭṭāyita</s> (manifestation of desire) —
When, through conversation about remembering the beloved and other [topics], the inner experience of that emotion
causes desire to become manifest — that is called <s>moṭṭāyita</s>. // RUnm_11.47 //

children.text: na brūte klama-bījam ālibhir alaṃ pṛṣṭāpi pālī yadā
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Pālī</s>, though asked by her friends, did not speak of the seed of [her] fatigue,

children.text: cāturyeṇa tad-agratas tava kathā tābhis tadā prastutā |
children.translated_text: then with cleverness those [friends] introduced the topic of you [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] before her;'
'O wearer of yellow garments [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], listening for a moment with a yawning lotus-face,

children.text: bimboṣṭhī pulakari viḍambitavatī phullāṃ kadamba-śriyam // RUnm_11.48 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bimba</s>-lipped one, her hair standing on end, put to shame the beauty of a blossoming <s>kadamba</s>!' // RUnm_11.48 //
Now <s>kuṭṭamita</s> (feigned anger) —
When, at the grasping of the breasts, lips, and so on, though the heart is pleased, out of modesty,

children.text: bahiḥ krodho vyathitavat proktaṃ kuṭṭamitaṃ budhaiḥ // RUnm_11.49 //
children.translated_text: outward anger [is displayed] as if in pain — the wise call this <s>kuṭṭamita</s>. // RUnm_11.49 //

children.text: karauddhatyaṃ hanta sthagaya kavarī me vighaṭate
children.translated_text: 'Alas, restrain the audacity of [your] hands! My braid is becoming undone!

children.text: dukūlaṃ ca nyañcaty aghahara tavāstāṃ vihasitam |
children.translated_text: My silk garment is slipping! O destroyer of <s>Agha</s>, stop that laughter of yours!'

children.text: kim ārabdhaḥ kartuṃ tam anavasare nirdaya madāt
children.translated_text: 'What have you begun to do in this inopportune moment? O merciless one, from intoxication —'

children.text: patāmy eṣā pī̀ade vitara śayituṃ me kṣaṇam api // RUnm_11.50 //
children.translated_text: 'I am falling on this [ground] — grant me even a moment to lie down!' // RUnm_11.50 //

children.text: na bhrū-latāṃ kuṭilaya kṣipa naiva hastaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Do not arch the eyebrow-creeper, do not cast [your] hand,

children.text: vaktraṃ ca kaṇṭakita-gaṇḍam idaṃ na rundhi |
children.translated_text: and do not cover this face with its cheeks bristling [with horripilation]!'
'O beautiful one, may it delight the life-friend of your lips [i.e., the lower lip] —'
'that <s>Madhusūdana</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], having drunk the sweet honey!' // RUnm_11.51 //

children.text: bibboko māna-garvābhyāṃ syād abhīṣṭe'py anādaraḥ // RUnm_11.52 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bibboka</s> is the indifference, from pride and arrogance, even toward the desired one. // RUnm_11.52 //
'Behold! In the presence of the rival, she who was won over
by the indication of loving words from the peacock-feather-crowned one [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] —'
'the exceedingly coy dark one [<s>Śyāmā</s>], though it was dear to [her] heart,
slightly smelled the garland and cast it aside with disdain!' // RUnm_11.53 //

body.translated_text: There, [<s>bibboka</s>] arising from pride, for example —

children.text: sphuraty agre tiṣṭhan sakhi tava mukha-ksipta-nayanaḥ
children.translated_text: 'O friend, standing right before you, his gaze cast upon your face,
this destroyer of <s>Agha</s>, having awaited your favorable moment —'
'with a gaze intensely deep, knotted with weighty disdain,

children.text: hasantīva kṣīve tvam iha vanamālāṃ racayasi // RUnm_11.54 //
children.translated_text: as if laughing at the intoxicated one, you are here weaving a forest-garland!' // RUnm_11.54 //
'When <s>Hari</s> was making a series of flattering speeches,
disregarding them out of pique —'
'today do not in vain, O <s>Gaurī</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>], teach even the well-trained [parrot] yourself;
teach the <s>śārikā</s> bird yourself!' // RUnm_11.55 //

body.translated_text: [<s>Bibboka</s>] arising from jealous pride (<s>māna</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: Now <s>lalita</s> (gracefulness) —
Where the delicate movements of arrangement, gestures, and playfulness

children.text: sukumārā bhaved yatra lalitaṃ tad-udīritam // RUnm_11.56 //
children.translated_text: are charming through the coquetry of eyebrows — that is called <s>lalita</s>. // RUnm_11.56 //
'Gazing with beautiful eyebrow-play at the creepers that give birth to <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (Cupid's) arrows,

children.text: sollāsaṃ pada-paṅkaje diśi diśi preṅkholayanty ujjvalā |
children.translated_text: joyfully swinging [her] lotus feet in every direction, radiant,
gently waving away the bees attracted by fragrance with [her] soft hand —

children.text: rādhā nandati kuñja-kandara-taṭe vṛndāvana-śrīr iva // RUnm_11.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> delights at the edge of the bower-cave, like the beauty of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> itself!' // RUnm_11.57 //
Now <s>vikṛta</s> (disguised expression) —
Where, due to modesty, pride, jealousy, and the like, one's intended meaning is not spoken,

children.text: vyajyate ceṣṭayaivedaṃ vikṛtaṃ tad vidur budhāḥ // RUnm_11.58 //
children.translated_text: but is expressed only through gesture — the wise know this as <s>vikṛta</s>. // RUnm_11.58 //
'Hearing from before your face, O <s>Mukunda</s>,
your entreaty, that beautiful one —'
'did not assent with words, but rather
with the horripilation beautifying [her] cheeks alone.' // RUnm_11.59 //

body.translated_text: There, [<s>vikṛta</s>] arising from modesty (<s>hrī</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: 'A glance at another man, O beautiful-eyed one, is not proper for you —

children.text: stvam asi kulajā sādhvī vaktraṃ prasīda vivartaya |
children.translated_text: you are of noble birth, a virtuous wife; be pleased, turn away your face!'

children.text: iti pathi mayā narmaṇy ukte harer nava-vīkṣaṇe
children.translated_text: 'When I spoke thus in jest on the path, regarding the fresh glance of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: sadayam udayat-kārpaṇyaṃ mām avaikṣata rādhikā // RUnm_11.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> looked at me compassionately with arising pitifulness.' // RUnm_11.60 //
'When I, being attached [to her], in the course of appeasement, having forgotten the lunar eclipse,

children.text: tad-vijñapti-samutsukāpi vijahau maunaṃ na sā māninī |
children.translated_text: and she, though eager to inform [me] of that, did not abandon her silence, that proud one —'
'but covering her face slightly with the opening of a dark gem-casket,

children.text: satyā smārayati sma vismṛtam asau mām auparāgīṃ śriyam // RUnm_11.61 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Satyā</s> she reminded me of the forgotten splendor of the eclipse.' // RUnm_11.61 //

body.translated_text: [<s>Vikṛta</s>] arising from jealous pride (<s>māna</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: 'Give back my flute, O thief! It was stolen!'
'— thus, as she turned away from my entreating speech,
with a frown-play on her brow, on the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>],
I was immediately regarded by <s>Rādhikā</s>.' // RUnm_11.62 //
Thus twenty ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>), arising from body and mind, have been described;

children.text: amī yathocitaṃ jñeyā mādhave'pi manīṣibhiḥ // RUnm_11.63 //
children.translated_text: these should be understood as applicable to <s>Mādhava</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] as well, as appropriate, by the wise. // RUnm_11.63 //

children.text: kaiścid anye'py alaṅkārāḥ proktā nātra mayoditāḥ |
children.translated_text: Some others have described additional ornaments, which I have not stated here,
since they are not accepted by the sage [<s>Bharata</s>]; but two are mentioned

children.text: maugdhyaṃ ca cakitaṃ ceti kiñcin mādhurya-poṣaṇāt // RUnm_11.64 //
children.translated_text: because they somewhat nourish sweetness — <s>maugdhya</s> (feigned naivety) and <s>cakita</s> (startlement). // RUnm_11.64 //

children.text: jñātasyāpy ajñavat pṛcchā priyāgre maugdhyam īritam // RUnm_11.65 //
children.translated_text: Asking about something already known as if ignorant before the beloved is called <s>maugdhya</s>. // RUnm_11.65 //
As in the <s>Muktācarita</s> —

children.text: kās tā latāḥ kva vā santi kena vā kila ropitāḥ |
