with the jingling crest-ornament at the end of her arm-creepers swaying in fright —'

children.text: rādhe vyākulatāṃ gatāpi bhavati modaṃ mamādhyasyati // RUnm_13.35 //
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>, even though you have become agitated, you bestow delight upon me!' // RUnm_13.35 //

body.translated_text: From a fearsome creature, as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (5.44) —

children.translated_text: '"You are my friend" — this saying
has been made true by you after a long time, O joyful one!
For upon my chest, by the rumblings [of thunder] being repelled,
<s>Rādhā</s>, her trembling newly arisen, was placed today.' // RUnm_13.36 //

body.translated_text: From a fierce sound, for example —

body.text: atha āvegaḥ, sa priya-darśanajo, yathā lalita-mādhave (2.11)-

children.translated_text: 'O companion, who is this fearless youth of cloud-like luster
who has arrived in the land of <s>Vraja</s>, with the gait of an intoxicated lordly elephant?'
'Alas! With his charming, creeping, sidelong-glance-thieves,

children.text: mama dhṛtir-dhanaṃ cetaḥ-koṣād viluṇṭhayatīha yaḥ // RUnm_13.37 //
children.translated_text: he plunders the treasure of my steadfastness from the treasury of my heart!' // RUnm_13.37 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>āvega</s> (agitation) — that born from seeing the beloved, as in the <s>Lalitamādhava</s> (2.11) —

children.translated_text: 'Having recognized <s>Lalitā</s> at the nearby tree, and immediately
beholding the naturally sweet form of <s>Rādhā</s>,
examining even the jewel with its crest of conch-shells —

children.text: muhur aham udghūrṇaṃ bhūriṇā sambhrameṇa // RUnm_13.38 //
children.translated_text: again and again I whirled about in great agitation.' // RUnm_13.38 //
'O <s>Dhanyā</s>, with collyrium-freed left eye! O <s>Padmā</s>, with an armlet placed upon the foot!
O <s>Sāraṅgī</s>, bearing a single jingling anklet! O <s>Pālī</s>, with slipping girdle!'
'O <s>Gaṇḍodyattilakā</s>! O <s>Lavaṅgī</s>! O <s>Kamalā</s>, with lac applied to the eyes!'

children.text: mādhāvottaralaṃ tvam atra muralī dūre kalaṃ kūjati // RUnm_13.39 //
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Mādhāvī</s>, be agitated — here, in the distance, the flute sounds sweetly!' // RUnm_13.39 //

body.translated_text: [<s>Āvega</s>] born from hearing of the beloved, as in the <s>Lalitamādhava</s> (1.25) —

children.translated_text: 'Now she cries out and rolls before the <s>śatāṅga</s> [chariot of her husband];

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ bāṣpa-grastāṃ kirati kila dṛṣṭiṃ hari-mukhe |
children.translated_text: now she casts a tear-choked glance upon <s>Hari</s>'s face;'
'now she falls before <s>Rāma</s> [<s>Balarāma</s>] with a blade of grass held between her teeth —

children.text: na rādheyaṃ kaṃ vā kṣipati karuṇāmbhodhi-kuhare // RUnm_13.40 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Rādhā</s> — whom does she not cast into the abyss of the ocean of compassion?' // RUnm_13.40 //

body.translated_text: [<s>Āvega</s>] born from seeing the undesired, as in the same [work] (3.18) —

children.text: vraja-narapater eṣa kṣattā karoti girā prage
children.translated_text: 'The attendant of the king of <s>Vraja</s> at dawn

children.text: nagara-gataye ghoraṃ ghoṣe ghanāṃ sakhi ghoṣaṇām |
children.translated_text: makes a dreadful, resounding announcement in the pasture about departing for the city;'
'by which [proclamation], ascending the pathway of the ears, fierce as a thunderbolt,

children.text: racitam acirād ābhīrīṇāṃ kulaṃ muhur ākulam // RUnm_13.41 //
children.translated_text: the community of cowherd women was instantly thrown into repeated agitation.' // RUnm_13.41 //

body.translated_text: [<s>Āvega</s>] born from hearing the undesired, for example —
Thus the others should also be inferred.

children.text: prasīda madirākṣi māṃ sakhi milantam āliṅgituṃ
children.translated_text: 'Be gracious, O intoxicating-eyed one! Embrace me, your companion, who approaches!
Restrain that dark-hued young man [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] before [us]!'
'Thus she entreats even a <s>bhramarikā</s> (bee-like wasp), mistaking it for a dear friend —
the cowherd-woman, bewildered by the madness and joy of seeing <s>Hari</s>.' // RUnm_13.42 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>unmāda</s> (madness) — that arising from intense joy, for example —

children.translated_text: 'Now tossing her hair here, now cracking her knuckles there,

children.text: stvaṅgad-bhrūr-daśanair vidaśya daśanān kaṃsaṃ śapaty uddhūrā |
children.translated_text: arching her brows and biting her lips with her teeth, she curses <s>Kaṃsa</s>, wildly agitated;'

children.text: kutrāpy adya tamālam uttarala-dhīr ālokya dhāvaty alaṃ
children.translated_text: 'somewhere, seeing a <s>tamāla</s> tree today with unsteady mind, she runs swiftly —

children.text: rādhā tvad-viraha-jvareṇa pṛthunā dūnā yadūnāṃ pate // RUnm_13.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, tormented by the vast fever of separation from you, O lord of the <s>Yadus</s>!' // RUnm_13.43 //
'With limb-flinging movements, with dense, towering delirious ravings,
with eye-pupils rolling upward violently, with eruptions of foam —'
'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, seeing my friend seized by the inner waves of transformation

children.text: rgrastāṃ prekṣya vitarkayanti guravaḥ sampraty apasmāriṇīm // RUnm_13.44 //
children.translated_text: arising from separation from you, the elders now consider her an epileptic.' // RUnm_13.44 //
'The flower-bed attains the state of being [mere] pollen through the touch of [her] limbs;
the lotus-leaves nearby and the fan-palm fronds wilt from the heat of [her] body;'

children.text: nyastaṃ ca stana-maṇḍale malayajaṃ śīrṇāntaraṃ lakṣyate
children.translated_text: 'the sandalwood paste applied to the breast-circles is seen to crack within;

children.text: kvāthād āśu bhavanti phenila-mukhā bhūṣā-mṛṇālāṅkurāḥ // RUnm_13.45 //
children.translated_text: from the [medicinal] decoction, the ornamental lotus-stalk sprouts quickly become foam-mouthed.' // RUnm_13.45 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>vyādhi</s> (illness) — that is, as in the <s>Rasasudhākara</s> (2.52) —

body.text: atha mohaḥ, sa harṣād, yathā vidagdha-mādhave (2.6)-

children.translated_text: 'From the firmly blossoming blue lotus-petal-like radiance of his [gaze],
immediately sprouting from the eagerness of the lotus-hand's touch —'

children.text: vahantī kṣobhāṇāṃ nivaham iha nājñāsiṣam idaṃ
children.translated_text: 'bearing a flood of agitations, I did not know here:

children.text: kva vāhaṃ kā vāhaṃ cakara kim ahaṃ vā sakhi tadā // RUnm_13.46 //
children.translated_text: where was I, who was I, and what indeed did I do then, O friend?' // RUnm_13.46 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>moha</s> (delusion) — that arising from joy, as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (2.6) —

children.translated_text: 'Seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the embodiment of festive delight for women, beautiful in form and character,
and hearing the wondrous song of his resonating flute —'
'the divine women in their aerial chariots, their hearts pierced by <s>Smara</s> (Cupid),
with their flower-braids loosening, became utterly bewildered, with their girdle-knots slipping.' // RUnm_13.47 //

body.translated_text: Or as in the illustrious tenth [canto] (10.21.12) —

children.text: sā palyaṅke kiśalaya-dalaiḥ kalpite tatra suptā
children.translated_text: 'She sleeps there on a couch prepared with tender leaves,
surrounded by circles of friends whose thirsts have been reduced to tears;'
'to be seen by you — her throat wasted by emaciation, the neck almost invisible,
that beautiful-limbed one, whose life-connection is inferred only by the stirring within her body.' // RUnm_13.48 //
'With the leaf-marks of his own lotus-feet — flag, thunderbolt,
lotus, and goad — with those wondrous emblems,
soothing the pain of the hooves upon the land of <s>Vraja</s>,
bearing the weight of the foremost, his gait celebrated, his flute praised —' // RUnm_13.49 //

body.translated_text: From despair (<s>viṣāda</s>), as in the illustrious tenth [canto] (10.35.16-17) —

children.translated_text: 'when he goes forth, we, struck by the force of desire
from his coquettish, sidelong glances —'
'having reached a state of utter bewilderment, we do not know,
due to stupefaction, [whether we have] our hair-braids or our garments!' // RUnm_13.50 //

children.text: mṛter adhyavayāyo'tra varṇyaḥ sākṣād iyaṃ na hi // RUnm_13.51 //
children.translated_text: Here the semblance of death is to be described, not death itself. // RUnm_13.51 //
'As long as the connection with the son of <s>Gāndinī</s> [<s>Akrūra</s>] does not become manifest,

children.text: tāvan natvā sumukhi bhavatīṃ kiṃcid abhyarthayiṣye |
children.translated_text: until then, having bowed, O fair-faced one, I shall request you for something small:'

children.text: puṣpair yasyā muhur akaravaṃ karṇa-pūrān murāreḥ
children.translated_text: 'this <s>mālatī</s> creeper, now blossoming in the courtyard of [her] house,

children.text: seyaṃ phullā gṛha-parisare mālatī pālanīyā // RUnm_13.52 //
children.translated_text: with whose [flowers] I repeatedly made ear-ornaments for the enemy of <s>Mura</s> — may it be tended!' // RUnm_13.52 //

children.text: sākṣād aṅgaṃ na cālasyaṃ bhaṅgyā tena nibadhyate // RUnm_13.53 //
children.translated_text: Indolence itself is not directly [described]; it is conveyed by suggestion. // RUnm_13.53 //
'Having churned unceasingly the yogurt-filled pot,
O friend, with body bent, performing copious yawning,

children.text: bhuvam anupatitā te patyur āste savitrī
children.translated_text: your <s>Savitrī</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>] has fallen upon the ground before [her] husband —

children.text: viracaya tad-aśaṅkaṃ tvaṃ harer mūrdhni cūḍām // RUnm_13.54 //
children.translated_text: therefore, without apprehension, fashion the crest-ornament upon <s>Hari</s>'s head!' // RUnm_13.54 //
'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s anklet jingled at the gateway,
[though] she had seized the excitement to rush out,
as if nailed down, with eyes closed,
<s>Manoramā</s> sank down in the house.' // RUnm_13.55 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>jāḍya</s> (stupor) — that arising from hearing the desired, for example —

children.translated_text: 'Repeatedly stricken by the deceptive words of her friends,
alas! her half-strung lotus-garland coming undone —'

children.text: hā hanta hanta kim api pratipanna-tandrā
children.translated_text: 'alas, alas! having somehow fallen into a torpor,
<s>Candrāvalī</s> indeed ascended to another state.' // RUnm_13.56 //

body.translated_text: From hearing the undesired, as in the <s>Lalitamādhava</s> (3.10) —

children.translated_text: 'Oh, fortunate are those <s>gopīs</s> who, with abundant, fresh, playful witticisms

children.text: vilāsair āmodaṃ dadhati madhurair yā madhubhidaḥ |
children.translated_text: and charming coquetry, bestow delight upon the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]!'

children.text: dhig astu svaṃ bhāgyaṃ yad iha mama rādhā priya-sakhī
children.translated_text: 'Shame upon my own fortune! For here my dear friend <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: puras tasmin prāpte jaḍima-niviḍāṅgī viluṭhati // RUnm_13.57 //
children.translated_text: when that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] arrived before her, rolls about with limbs rigid from stupor.' // RUnm_13.57 //

body.translated_text: From seeing the desired, as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (3.29) —

children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s>, sporting with <s>Hari</s> at the forest's edge,
upon seeing <s>Abhimanyu</s> [her husband], became rigid and bore [herself] thus —'
'even as he angrily approached her presence quickly,
she gave the impression of being a statue of <s>Bhavānī</s> [<s>Pārvatī</s>].' // RUnm_13.58 //

body.translated_text: From seeing the undesired, for example —

children.translated_text: 'The fair-faced one, the betel taken [but untouched], does not remember,

children.text: smaraty antaḥśūnyā murahara gatāyām api niśi |
children.translated_text: despite the words of her attendants — inwardly void — even though the night of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> has passed;'
'her hand still holds the betel-leaf creeper sprout,
and her mouth still bears the familiarity of the areca-nut slice.' // RUnm_13.59 //

children.text: vidhumukhi bhaja śayyāṃ vartase kiṃ natāsyā
children.translated_text: 'O moon-faced one, take to the bed! Why do you stand with downcast face?

children.text: muhur ayam anuvartī yācate tvāṃ prasīda |
children.translated_text: Again and again this importunate one entreats you — be gracious!'
'Thus besought by me with many charming words,

children.text: vyarucad iha nikuñja-śrīr iva dvāri rādhā // RUnm_13.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> shone at the doorway here like the beauty of the bower itself.' // RUnm_13.60 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>vrīḍā</s> (shame/bashfulness) — that arising from a new union, for example —

children.text: paṭuḥ kim api bhāgya-tattvam asi putri vittārjane
children.translated_text: 'You are indeed clever in the truth of fortune-earning, O daughter,

children.text: yad etam atulyaṃ balād apajahartha hāraṃ hareḥ |
children.translated_text: for you have forcibly stolen this incomparable necklace from <s>Hari</s>!'
'Hearing this deep reproach from the elders,
<s>Mālatī</s>, upon seeing the jeweled garland, lowered her face.' // RUnm_13.61 //

body.translated_text: From an improper deed, for example —

children.translated_text: 'Do not shrink from truthful words —
the moonlight of your fame cleanses the worlds!'
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, you are upon the chest of <s>Hari</s> —
for the saffron anointing there is imperishable!' // RUnm_13.62 //
'Before your watching eyes, as if spreading outward the passion —
my heart, reddened and stained with the lac from the beloved's feet —'
'today, O deceiver, through the destruction of my widely-known love's weight,

children.text: tvad-ālokaḥ śokād api kim api lajjāṃ janayati // RUnm_13.63 //
children.translated_text: your very sight produces, beyond grief, even some shame.' // RUnm_13.63 //

body.translated_text: From contempt, as in the illustrious <s>Gītagovinda</s> (8.10) —

body.text: atha avahitthā, sā jaihmyena, yathā śrī-jagannātha-vallabhe-

children.translated_text: 'Having drunk, as it were, her words like nectar-streams from a blooming lotus,

children.text: nipīya kṣībatvaṃ gata iva calan-maulir adhikam |
children.translated_text: as if become intoxicated, his head swaying excessively —'
'though desire arose within, devoted to concealing the art of his own heart,

children.text: hariḥ svairaṃ svairaṃ smita-subhagam ūce katham ayam // RUnm_13.64 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> freely, freely spoke with a charming smile — how [remarkable] was this!' // RUnm_13.64 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation) — that arising from duplicity, as in the illustrious <s>Jagannāthavallabha</s> —

children.translated_text: 'Speak no more, O [messenger]! Tell not the news of the rogue on the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>]!

children.text: gantavyā me na khalu tarale dūti sīmāpi tasya |
children.translated_text: I shall certainly not go even to the border of that fickle one, O messenger!'

children.text: vikhyātāham jagati kaṭhinā yat pidhatte madaṅgaṃ
children.translated_text: 'I am known in the world as hard-hearted — as for what covers my body,

children.text: romāñco.ayaṃ sapadi pavano haimanastatra hetuḥ // RUnm_13.65 //
children.translated_text: this horripilation — the winter breeze is the cause of that!' // RUnm_13.65 //

body.translated_text: From duplicity and shame combined, as in the <s>Uddhavasandeśa</s> (52) —

children.translated_text: 'While she bashfully tried to somehow conceal that theatrical show,
sweet as the fresh ninth [note] of <s>Dāmodara</s>'s [flute] —'
'the unsteady vine of the body, on the bank of <s>Kālindī</s> [<s>Yamunā</s>], directly proclaims in the heart of the bower

children.text: sarojākṣyāḥ sākṣād vadati hṛdi kuñje tanuvanī // RUnm_13.66 //
children.translated_text: the victory of the young elephant-lord [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] of the lotus-eyed one.' // RUnm_13.66 //

children.text: uddhūtā smita-kaumudī na madhurā vaktrendu-bimbāt tayā
children.translated_text: She did not radiate the moonlight of a smile from the moon-orb of her face,

children.text: mṛdvīnāṃ na nirākṛtā nija-girāṃ mādhurya-lakṣmīr api |
children.translated_text: nor did she reject the beauty-and-grace of her own soft words;
rather, with warm, irrepressible sighs — betraying the hidden anguish of her heart —

children.text: śvāsair eva daroddhūta-stana-paṭais tasyā ruṣaḥ kīrtitāḥ // RUnm_13.67 //
children.translated_text: which slightly displaced the garment over her breasts, her anger was expressed. // RUnm_13.67 //
Through modesty (<s>hrī</s>) and fear (<s>bhaya</s>), as follows —

children.text: hṛdaye tvadīya-rāgaṃ, mādhava dadhatī śamīva sā dahanam |
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, she, bearing love for You in her heart like a <s>śamī</s> tree bears fire,

children.text: antarjvalitāpi bahiḥ, sarasā sphurati kṣamā-guṇataḥ // RUnm_13.68 //
children.translated_text: though inwardly ablaze, outwardly appears moist and fresh, by virtue of her quality of forbearance. // RUnm_13.68 //
<s>Candrāvalī</s>, while roaming for a long time
before the circles of [her] mansion skillfully,
upon sprouting trembling at the sound of the flute,
the cunning one blamed the thundering of the clouds! // RUnm_13.69 //
Seeing the garland she had woven with her own hands
tumbling upon the hair of the rival —
even though vexed, <s>Candramukhī</s>, concealed by the wave of affectionate regard
for the crusher of sin [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], remained silent. // RUnm_13.70 //

body.translated_text: Through deference (<s>gaurava</s>) and graciousness (<s>dākṣiṇya</s>), as follows —

body.text: atha smṛtiḥ | sā sadṛśekṣayā, yathā haṃsadūte (23)-
body.translated_text: Now <s>smṛti</s> (memory). That [arises] from seeing something similar — as in the <s>Haṃsadūta</s> (23) —

children.translated_text: By the sight of the <s>tamāla</s> tree in the vicinity of the mountain, the agitated
<s>Pulinda</s> women, their bodies scorched by the intensity of remembering <s>Govinda</s> —

children.text: śanais tāsāṃ tāpaṃ kṣaṇam apanayan yāsyati bhavān
children.translated_text: you [O swan-messenger] will slowly pass by, dispelling their fever for a moment
with the breezes of your wings, cool from the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s> [<s>Yamunā</s>]. // RUnm_13.71 //

children.text: te pīyūṣikirāṃ girāṃ parimalāḥ sā piñcha-cūḍojjvalā
children.translated_text: Those nectarean fragrances of [His] words, that brilliance of the peacock-feather crest,

children.text: tās tāpiñcha-manoharās tanurucas te kelayaḥ peśalāḥ |
children.translated_text: those complexion-radiances as enchanting as a dark <s>tamāla</s> tree, those artful love-sports,
that face surpassing the autumn moon, those eyes with the beauty of lotuses —

children.text: tasyeti kṣaṇam apy avismarad idaṃ ceto mamāghūrṇate // RUnm_13.72 //
children.translated_text: this heart of mine, not forgetting Him even for a moment, whirls about! // RUnm_13.72 //

body.text: atha vitarkaḥ, sa vimarśād yathā vidagdha-mādhave (6.29)-

children.text: vighūrṇantaḥ pauṣpaṃ na madhu lihate'mī madhulihaḥ
children.translated_text: These hovering bees do not lick the floral nectar;
this parrot, seized by stupor, does not take the pomegranate fruit;

children.text: vivarṇā parṇāgraṃ carati hariṇīyaṃ na haritaṃ
children.translated_text: this doe, grown pale, does not eat the green tips of leaves —

children.text: pathānena svāmī tad-ibha-vara-gāmī dhruvam agāt // RUnm_13.73 //
children.translated_text: surely the master, walking with the gait of a lordly elephant, has gone by this path! // RUnm_13.73 //

body.translated_text: Now <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture). That [arises] from deliberation, as in the <s>Vidagdha-mādhava</s> (6.29) —

children.translated_text: There in the distance, the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, crowned with an array of peacock feathers,
in the city, sports embraced by fair-limbed women;
no, I suspect this is not the beloved — sweet with the splendor of <s>Indra</s>'s bow [rainbow],
a cloud, stealing the lines of lightning, has clung to the mountain! // RUnm_13.74 //
Cessation from eating, supreme withdrawal from the entire realm of sense-objects,

children.text: nāsāgre nayanaṃ yad etad aparaṃ yac caikatānaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: the eye fixed on the tip of the nose, and further, the mind single-pointed,

children.text: maunaṃ cedam idaṃ ca śūnyam akhilaṃ yad viśvam ābhāti te
children.translated_text: and this silence, and the entire world appearing void to you —

children.text: tad brūyāḥ sakhi yoginī kim asi bhoḥ kiṃ viyoginy api // RUnm_13.75 //
children.translated_text: tell me, O friend, are you a <s>yoginī</s> or are you one suffering separation? // RUnm_13.75 //
The pair of eyes of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] extend with slightly rolling pupils;

children.text: śvāsāḥ k ptāṃ kila vicakilair mālikāṃ mlāpayanti |
children.translated_text: his sighs wilt the garland strung on [his chest], with restless [breaths];

children.text: keyaṃ dhanyā vasati ramaṇī gokule kṣipram etāṃ
children.translated_text: who is this fortunate woman who dwells in <s>Gokula</s>? Quickly find her —

children.text: nītas tīvrāmayam api yayā kām api dhyāna-niṣṭhām // RUnm_13.76 //
children.translated_text: she by whom he has been led into some profound meditative absorption, even though afflicted with intense love-sickness! // RUnm_13.76 //
As the childhood was gradually stripped away, and upon <s>Rādhā</s>'s limbs
the moonlight of sweetness increasingly blazed forth,

children.text: vrajaṃ muṣṭi-grāhye tamasi nigiraty aṅgam iha me
children.translated_text: In the darkness, dense enough to be grasped by the fist, which swallows my body in <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: sakhi sparśaṃ daivād yad-avadhi paraṃ kasyacid agāt |
children.translated_text: O friend, from the time when by fate I experienced the supreme touch of someone —
from that time, seized constantly by the hosts of <s>Kāma</s>'s [Cupid's] forces, apprehensive,

children.text: sa-śaṅkair yā paśya kṣaṇam api na sādyānpy uparatā // RUnm_14.12 //
children.translated_text: see — she has not ceased even for a moment, even today! // RUnm_14.12 //

children.text: kṛtākṛṣṭi-krīḍaṃ kim api tava rūpaṃ mama sakhī
children.translated_text: Having once glimpsed from afar your form, which performs some inexplicable sport of attraction,
my friend, her mind bereft of the knowledge of what is harmful and what is beneficial —

children.text: hatā seyaṃ premānalam anu viśantī sarabhasaṃ
children.translated_text: that stricken one, rushing impetuously into the fire of love,
like a moth, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, has burned herself again and again! // RUnm_14.13 //
That her body bristles with horripilation, that it assumes contortions of the limbs,

children.text: vahati hṛdi taraṅgaṃ sadya evādya mugdhā |
children.translated_text: that waves immediately surge in the heart of this innocent one today —
clearly, O friend, a small amount of betel chewed from the mouth of the slayer of <s>Agha</s>

children.text: sphuṭam aviditam āsye nyastam asyās tvayāli // RUnm_14.14 //
children.translated_text: was placed in her mouth by you without her knowing! // RUnm_14.14 //

children.text: vibhrājante kva sakhi sukhinaḥ śākhino mohanās te
children.translated_text: Where do those happy, enchanting trees flourish, O friend,

children.text: yeṣāṃ puṣpair iyam anupamā vaijayantī kṛtāsti |
children.translated_text: from whose flowers this incomparable <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland has been made?
See — though long past its freshness, still attracting swarms of bees,

children.text: yā bhūyobhir mama parimalaiḥ stambhayaty adya cetaḥ // RUnm_14.15 //
children.translated_text: it arrests my mind today yet again with its abundant fragrance! // RUnm_14.15 //
The power of transcendent objects is somehow unstoppable;

children.text: ratiṃ tad-viṣayaṃ cāsau bhāsayet tūrṇam ekadā // RUnm_14.16 //
children.translated_text: it may cause love (<s>rati</s>) directed toward that [object] to blaze forth instantly at once. // RUnm_14.16 //
Relationship is the weightiness of the aggregate of lineage, beauty, and the like. // RUnm_14.17 //
His prowess makes a ball of [mountains]; his beauty is the ornament of the entire circle of the earth;
his birth is in the house of the <s>Indra</s> of the cowherds; his qualities are beyond the highest count;
his pastimes (<s>līlā</s>) somehow create astonishment in the universe — thus his transcendent

children.text: vṛttir veṇu-dharasya durmukhi dhṛtiṃ kasyāḥ kṣaṇaṃ rakṣati // RUnm_14.18 //
children.translated_text: conduct, O sullen-faced one — whose composure does the bearer of the flute not destroy in an instant? // RUnm_14.18 //
Now self-conception (<s>abhimāna</s>) —

children.text: santu ramyāṇi bhūrīṇi prārthyaṃ syād idam eva me |
children.translated_text: 'Let there be many charming [persons], but this alone should be my aspiration' —

children.text: iti yo nirṇayo dhīrair abhimānaḥ sa ucyate // RUnm_14.19 //
children.translated_text: such a firm conviction is called self-conception (<s>abhimāna</s>) by the wise. // RUnm_14.19 //
Let many jewels among the clever appear on earth,
champions of waves of sweetness, chosen by women who select the lord of virtues!

children.text: na yasya śikhi-candraṃ śirasi naiva veṇur mukhe
children.translated_text: One who has no peacock-moon [feather] on his head, no flute at his mouth,

children.text: na dhātu-vacanā tanau sakhi tṛṇāya manye na tam // RUnm_14.20 //
children.translated_text: no mineral-pigment words on his body — O friend, I consider him [worth] a blade of grass! // RUnm_14.20 //
The distinguishing features belonging to him are: his footprints, his pasture (<s>goṣṭha</s>), his dear ones (<s>priya</s>), and so on. // RUnm_14.21 //

body.translated_text: Now the things belonging to him (<s>tadīya-viśeṣa</s>) —

children.translated_text: Footprints here mean foot-impressions (<s>padāṅka</s>). // RUnm_14.22 //
O friend, this clear row of footprints on the bank, bearing
the wheel, lotus, thunderbolt [marks] — whose is it?
Opening up my heart, churned by merciless agitation,

children.text: mama tanu-latikāyāṃ kuḍmalaṃ yā tanoti // RUnm_14.23 //
children.translated_text: it causes buds to form on the creeper of my body! // RUnm_14.23 //
The <s>goṣṭha</s> is that situated within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. // RUnm_14.24 //
O friend, this <s>Vraja</s> intoxicates my heart
with sweetnesses never before witnessed anywhere!
Know that here sports some supreme hero among the gallant,
the embodiment of the ornament of the three worlds! // RUnm_14.25 //

children.text: prauḍha-bhāvānubiddho yas tasya priya-jano'tra saḥ // RUnm_14.26 //
children.translated_text: His dear one is here one who is pervaded by a mature sentiment (<s>prauḍha-bhāva</s>). // RUnm_14.26 //

children.text: gurubhir niṣiddhā tām ahaṃ yāvad akṣṇoḥ
children.translated_text: As soon as I — forbidden by elders — from my eyes
directed <s>Rādhā</s>, the abode of infinite blessings, to [some other] place —

children.text: tṛṣitam iva mano me prekṣate tanvi tāvad
children.translated_text: my mind, as if thirsting, O slender one, beholds

children.text: diśi diśi viharantīṃ śyāmalāṃ śālabhañjīm // RUnm_14.27 //
children.translated_text: the dark <s>Śāla-bhañjī</s> [<s>Śyāmalā</s>] sporting in every direction! // RUnm_14.27 //

children.text: yathā kathañcid apy asya sādṛśyam upamoditā // RUnm_14.28 //
children.translated_text: That which is praised for resemblance to him in any way whatever is called analogy (<s>upamā</s>). // RUnm_14.28 //
The sweetness of a fresh rain-cloud shines forth in bodily form on the earth's surface —

children.text: kṛśodari dṛśor iyāt pathi kim īdṛśo vā yuvā |
children.translated_text: O slender-waisted one, would such a youth come along the path to your eyes?

children.text: puraḥ sumukhi gopateḥ sadai sanniviṣṭasya me
children.translated_text: Before me, who always sits near the lord of the cowherds,

children.text: pitur vitanute naṭo yam anukṛtya nṛtya-kramam // RUnm_14.29 //
children.translated_text: this dancer, imitating him, extends a sequence of dances by my father! // RUnm_14.29 //

children.text: sphuraty eṣa preyān iva nava-ghanas tasya subhage
children.translated_text: 'This beloved one shines forth like a fresh rain-cloud, O beautiful one!
This row of peacocks is a match for the rainbow of the king of gods!

children.text: asau vāso lakṣmīr iva viharate vidyud iti sā
children.translated_text: That garment sports like lightning and <s>Lakṣmī</s>!' — thus she,
hearing this, with tear-filled eyes, dwells with her mind fixed on you! // RUnm_14.30 //
Now innate nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) —
That meaning which is independent of causes is called innate nature (<s>svabhāva</s>);

children.text: nisargaś ca svarūpaṃ cety eṣo'pi bhavati dvidhā // RUnm_14.31 //
children.translated_text: it is also twofold: natural disposition (<s>nisarga</s>) and essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>). // RUnm_14.31 //
Here, natural disposition (<s>nisarga</s>) —
Natural disposition (<s>nisarga</s>) is called a mental impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born of firmly established practice;

children.text: tad-udbhodhasya hetuḥ syād guṇa-rūpa-śrutir manāk // RUnm_14.32 //
children.translated_text: the cause of its awakening is a slight hearing of [his] qualities and form. // RUnm_14.32 //

children.text: sa tarjatu batāgrajaṃ tyajatu māṃ suhṛn-maṇḍalaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Let him threaten my elder brother! Let my circle of friends abandon me!

children.text: pitā kila vilajjatāṃ ghana-dṛg-ambur ambāstu me |
children.translated_text: Let my father be put to shame! Let the tears of my dark-eyed mother flow!
My mind, O friend, desires in every way

children.text: tam eva yadu-puṅgavaṃ na tu kadāpi caidyaṃ nṛpam // RUnm_14.33 //
children.translated_text: that very bull among the <s>Yadus</s> — and never the king <s>Caidya</s> [<s>Śiśupāla</s>]!' // RUnm_14.33 //
'Whether he is ugly or the crest-jewel of the beautiful,
devoid of virtues or the best among the virtuous,
hostile toward me or an ocean of mercy —

children.text: śyāmaḥ sa evādya gatir mamāyam // RUnm_14.34 //
children.translated_text: that dark <s>Śyāma</s> alone is now my refuge!' // RUnm_14.34 //
Now essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) —

children.text: ajanyas tu svataḥsiddhaḥ svarūpaṃ bhāva iṣyate |
children.translated_text: The essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) is the sentiment that is self-established, not produced [by causes];
it is threefold, based on its focus on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, on the woman (<s>lalanā</s>), or on both. // RUnm_14.35 //

children.text: kṛṣṇa-niṣṭhaṃ svarūpaṃ syād adaityaiḥ sugamaṃ janaiḥ // RUnm_14.36 //
children.translated_text: The essential nature focused on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is easily accessible to non-demonic people. // RUnm_14.36 //

body.translated_text: Now that which is focused on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (<s>kṛṣṇa-niṣṭha</s>) —

children.text: iyaṃ vyaktir gopī na bhavati puraḥ kintu kutukī
children.translated_text: 'This apparition is no <s>gopī</s> before us, but rather <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: harir nārīveśo yad akhila-sura-strīr dhuvati naḥ |
children.translated_text: the curious one, in woman's disguise, who confounds all divine women!
Without the sky-jewel [sun] who removes the darkness of the world's rows of eyes,

children.text: vinā kasyānyasya priyasakhi bhaved aupayikatā // RUnm_14.37 //
children.translated_text: whose else, O dear friend, could such suitability be?' // RUnm_14.37 //
Now that which is focused on the woman (<s>lalanā-niṣṭha</s>) —
The essential nature focused on the woman awakens of its own accord;

children.text: adṛṣṭe'py aśrute'py uccaiḥ kṛṣṇe kuryād drutaṃ ratim // RUnm_14.38 //
children.translated_text: even without seeing or hearing of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, it would quickly produce intense love. // RUnm_14.38 //

children.text: jihīte yaḥ kakṣāṃ kvacid alam adṛṣṭāśruta-cara-
children.translated_text: 'Who is this that exceeds all limits — whose course has been unseen and unheard of

children.text: trilokyām astīti kṣaṇam api na sambhāvana-mayīm |
children.translated_text: in the three worlds, about whom there is not even a moment's conjecture that he exists —',
'imagining someone dark-complexioned, in yellow garments, alas,

children.text: janaṃ kañcid goṣṭhe sakhi mama vṛthā dīryati manaḥ // RUnm_14.39 //
children.translated_text: O friend, in the pasture-land, my mind splits apart in vain!' // RUnm_14.39 //

children.text: tat syād ubhaya-niṣṭhaṃ yat svarūpaṃ kṛṣṇa-subhruvoḥ // RUnm_14.40 //
children.translated_text: That which is the essential nature of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the fair-browed ones [<s>gopīs</s>] would be established in both. // RUnm_14.40 //

body.translated_text: Now that which is focused on both (<s>ubhaya-niṣṭha</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'O companion, this <s>Hari</s> has assumed the guise of <s>Brahman</s> [i.e., a brāhmaṇa] —

children.text: kim ayam itarathā me vidravaty antarātmā |
children.translated_text: why else does my inner self melt away before him?'
'The moonstone terrace produces streams of perspiration —

children.text: na kila kumuda-bandhoḥ kaumudīm antareṇa // RUnm_14.41 //
children.translated_text: surely not without the moonlight of the friend of the night-lotus [the moon]!' // RUnm_14.41 //
The <s>abhiyoga</s> and other [types of rati] mentioned here serve to enhance <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry);

children.text: ratiḥ svabhāvajaiva syāt prāyo gokula-subhruvām // RUnm_14.42 //
children.translated_text: the <s>rati</s> of the fair-browed women of <s>Gokula</s> is generally self-born (<s>svabhāvaja</s>). // RUnm_14.42 //
The <s>sādhāraṇī</s> (common), <s>samañjasā</s> (proper), and <s>samarthā</s> (complete) [types of rati]

children.text: kubjādiṣu mahiṣīṣu ca gokula-devīṣṇḍ ca kramataḥ // RUnm_14.43 //
children.translated_text: are found respectively in <s>Kubjā</s> and the like, in the queens, and in the goddesses of <s>Gokula</s>. // RUnm_14.43 //
Like an [ordinary] gem, like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), and like the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem — thus the three are regarded;

children.text: nātisulabheyam abhitaḥ sudurlabhā syād ananya-labhyā ca // RUnm_14.44 //
children.translated_text: the first is not very easily obtained, the [second is] very difficult to obtain, and the [third] is obtainable by no other [means]. // RUnm_14.44 //
There, <s>sādhāraṇī</s> (common love) —
Not very intense, arising generally from the direct sight of <s>Hari</s>,
having as its basis the desire for amorous enjoyment — this is considered <s>sādhāraṇī rati</s>. // RUnm_14.45 //
As in the illustrious tenth [canto] (10.48.9) —

children.text: sahoṣyatām iha preṣṭha dināni katicin mayā |
children.translated_text: 'Stay here with me for a few days, O dearest one!

children.text: ramasva notsahe tyaktuṃ saṅgaṃ te'mburuhekṣaṇa // RUnm_14.46 //
children.translated_text: Enjoy [yourself]! I cannot bear to abandon your company, O lotus-eyed one!' // RUnm_14.46 //
Because this <s>rati</s> is not intense, the desire for enjoyment is disrupted;

children.text: etasyā hrāsato hrāsas tad-dhetutvād rater api // RUnm_14.47 //
children.translated_text: from the diminution of this [desire], there is also diminution of the <s>rati</s>, since it is the cause thereof. // RUnm_14.47 //
Now <s>samañjasā</s> (proper love) —
Characterized by the self-identification as wife (<s>patnī-bhāva</s>), arising from hearing of qualities and so on,
sometimes with the desire for enjoyment disrupted, [yet] intense — this is <s>samañjasā</s>. // RUnm_14.48 //
'What woman of noble family, of good character, beauty,
learning, youth, and wealth — equal to you in these qualities —'

children.text: dhīrā patiṃ kulavatī na vṛṇīta kanyā
children.translated_text: 'what wise maiden of good family would not choose as husband,
O man-lion [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], one who delights the minds of the human world, at the proper time?' // RUnm_14.49 //
When the desire for enjoyment is disrupted from [the nature of] <s>samañjasā</s>,

children.text: tadā tad-utthitair bhāvair vaśyatā duṣkarā hariḥ // RUnm_14.50 //
children.translated_text: then <s>Hari</s> is difficult to bring under control by the emotions arising from that. // RUnm_14.50 //
'With the bewitching eyebrow-arches dispatching amorous mantras,
shown through glimpses of sidelong smiles revealing their feelings —'
'his sixteen thousand wives could not,

children.text: yasyendriyaṃ vimathituṃ karaṇair na śekuḥ // RUnm_14.51 //
children.translated_text: with the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid) and [their] faculties, agitate his senses.' // RUnm_14.51 //
Now <s>samarthā</s> (complete love) —
That by which the desire for enjoyment, attaining some special distinction, has everywhere

children.text: ratyā tādātmyam āpannā sā samartheti bhaṇyate // RUnm_14.52 //
children.translated_text: achieved identity with <s>rati</s> — that is called <s>samarthā</s>. // RUnm_14.52 //
Born from her own essential nature or from his, [even] from the slightest connection,
<s>samarthā</s> is considered the most intense, with an aroma that makes one forget everything else. // RUnm_14.53 //

children.text: prekṣyāśeṣe jagati madhurāṃ svāṃ vadhūṃ śaṅkayā te
children.translated_text: 'Seeing you regard every sweet woman in the world as your own bride, with suspicion,

children.text: tasyāḥ pārśve gurubhir abhitas tvat-prasaṅgo nyavāri |
children.translated_text: her contact with you was everywhere prohibited by the elders at her side;'

children.text: śrutvā dūre tad api bhavataḥ sā tulā-koṭi-nādaṃ
children.translated_text: 'yet hearing even from afar the sound of the tip of a balance [at the marketplace signaling your approach],

children.text: hā kṛṣṇety aśruta-caram api vyāharanty unmadāsīt // RUnm_14.54 //
children.translated_text: crying "Hā <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!" — even [a cry] that had never been heard before — she became maddened.' // RUnm_14.54 //
The special beauty of this [<s>samarthā rati</s>], which produces wonder through waves of all-astonishing sport —
the special desire for enjoyment is never separated from this <s>rati</s>;

children.text: ity asyāṃ kṛṣṇa-saukhyārtham eva kevalam udyamaḥ // RUnm_14.55 //
children.translated_text: hence, in this, the effort is solely for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s happiness. // RUnm_14.55 //

body.text: pūrvasyāṃ sva-sukhāyāpi kadācit tatra sambhavet // RUnm_14.56 //
body.translated_text: In the former [<s>samañjasā</s>], the effort may sometimes be for one's own happiness as well. // RUnm_14.56 //

children.text: iyam eva ratiḥ prauḍhā mahābhāva-daśāṃ vrajet |
children.translated_text: This very <s>rati</s>, when fully matured, would reach the stage of <s>mahābhāva</s>,

children.text: yā mṛgyā syād vimuktānāṃ bhaktānāṃ ca varīyasām // RUnm_14.57 //
children.translated_text: which is to be sought by the liberated and by the best of devotees. // RUnm_14.57 //
'These cowherd wives are indeed the supreme embodied beings on earth,
whose love for <s>Govinda</s>, the Self of all, has fully matured;'

children.text: vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: 'what even those sages who fear worldly existence, and we, desire —
of what use are births even as <s>Brahmā</s>, [compared to tasting] the nectar of stories of the Infinite?' // RUnm_14.58 //

children.text: syād dṛḍheyaṃ ratiḥ premā prodyan snehaḥ kramād ayam |
children.translated_text: When this <s>rati</s> becomes firm, it is <s>prema</s>; when it sprouts, it is <s>sneha</s>; then in sequence

children.text: syān mānaḥ praṇayo rāgo'nurāgo bhāva ity api // RUnm_14.59 //
children.translated_text: come <s>māna</s>, <s>praṇaya</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>anurāga</s>, and <s>bhāva</s>. // RUnm_14.59 //

children.text: bījam ikṣuḥ sa ca rasaḥ sa guḍaḥ khaṇḍa eva saḥ |
children.translated_text: [Like] a seed, sugarcane, juice, molasses, raw sugar,

children.text: sa śarkarā sitā sā ca sā yathā syāt sitopalā // RUnm_14.60 //
children.translated_text: refined sugar, white sugar, and then rock candy — [such is the progression]. // RUnm_14.60 //

children.text: ataḥ prema-vilāsāḥ syur bhāvāḥ snehādayas tu ṣaṭ |
children.translated_text: Therefore the sports of <s>prema</s> would be the six <s>bhāvas</s> beginning with <s>sneha</s>;
generally these are referred to by scholars with the word '<s>prema</s>.' // RUnm_14.61 //
Whatever type of <s>prema</s> arises in her toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: tasyāṃ tādṛśa-jātīyaḥ sa kṛṣṇasyāpy udīyate // RUnm_14.62 //
children.translated_text: that same type also arises in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> toward her. // RUnm_14.62 //
There, <s>prema</s> —
That which is entirely free from destruction even in the presence of causes of destruction,

children.text: yad-bhāva-bandhanaṃ yūnoḥ sa premā parikīrtitaḥ // RUnm_14.63 //
children.translated_text: the bond of emotion between the young couple — that is celebrated as <s>prema</s>. // RUnm_14.63 //
'I swear to you, O friend — though I, fleeing with determination from [our] law and fury,

children.text: viśuddhām ugrābhir muhur api nirasto bhaṇitibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: have been repeatedly rejected even by pure and severe speeches —'

children.text: sa mugdhe śyāmātmā tyajati na hi me vartma bata māṃ
children.translated_text: 'that dark-souled one, O innocent one, does not abandon my path! Alas,
let the dreadful misfortune befall me — let the master of the house punish me!' // RUnm_14.64 //
'Though <s>Rādhā</s>'s [love], O friend, through daily [growing] virtues, beauty, passion and the like,
has obtained an intense infatuation, [even though] distracted by the hearts of other beautiful women —'

children.text: prāpa kvāpi parasparopari yayor na mlānatāṃ yas tayo-
children.translated_text: 'the [love] of those two, wherever it went, one upon the other, never faded —

children.text: staṃ candrāvali-candrakābharaṇayoḥ ko vetti bhāva-kramam // RUnm_14.65 //
children.translated_text: who knows the course of emotion of those [two], adorned by <s>Candrāvalī</s> and <s>Candraka</s>?' // RUnm_14.65 //

body.translated_text: This [<s>prema</s>] is described in three types — intense (<s>prauḍha</s>), middle (<s>madhya</s>), and mild (<s>manda</s>). // RUnm_14.66 //

children.translated_text: There, intense (<s>prauḍha</s>) —
When the mental state of the beloved person is unknown due to delay and the like,

children.text: itara-kleśa-kārī yaḥ sa premā prauḍha ucyate // RUnm_14.67 //
children.translated_text: that which causes distress to the other — that <s>prema</s> is called intense (<s>prauḍha</s>). // RUnm_14.67 //

children.text: gatvā brūhi nikuñja-sadmani sakhe khinnāṃ mama preyasīṃ
children.translated_text: 'Go, O friend, and tell my beloved in the bower-abode, who is distressed:

children.text: mā kālātyayam ākalayya kamale mayy apratītiṃ kṛthāḥ |
children.translated_text: "O <s>Kamalā</s>, do not, calculating the delay of time, lose faith in me!'

children.text: duṣṭaṃ dānavam atra gokula-śiraḥ-śūlaṃ cikitsann ahaṃ
children.translated_text: '"Here I am treating this wicked demon, the tormentor of <s>Gokula</s>'s summit —

children.text: drāg eṣa praṇayena pallava-mayīṃ labdho'smi śayyāṃ tava // RUnm_14.68 //
children.translated_text: I shall soon, with love, have obtained the bed of sprouts [prepared by] you!"' // RUnm_14.68 //

children.text: itarānubhavāpekṣāṃ sahate yaḥ sa madhyamaḥ // RUnm_14.69 //
children.translated_text: That which tolerates the expectation of another's experience is called the middle. // RUnm_14.69 //
'Finding <s>Candrāvalī</s>, who is captivating in all her undertakings, instantly before me,
the festive arena suited to an autumnal night has reached complete satisfaction;'
'yet [seeing] that <s>Rādhā</s>, [radiant] with waves of sport creating wonder for Cupid's army —

children.text: rādhāṃ hanta tathāpi cittam adhunā sākṣān mamāpekṣate // RUnm_14.70 //
children.translated_text: alas, even so, my mind now directly yearns for her!' // RUnm_14.70 //
Now the mild (<s>manda</s>) —

children.text: sadā paricitatvādeḥ karoty atyantikāt tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: That which, from constant familiarity and the like, produces neither

children.text: naivopekṣāṃ na cāpekṣāṃ sa premā manda ucyate // RUnm_14.71 //
children.translated_text: utter neglect nor anxious expectation — that <s>prema</s> is called mild (<s>manda</s>). // RUnm_14.71 //
For example —

children.text: anumīya rūḍhamānām ānaya bhāmāṃ sakhīm aśoka-latām |
children.translated_text: 'Inferring the firmly established jealous pride [of <s>Rādhā</s>], bring the angry beloved — my friend, the <s>aśoka</s> creeper!

children.text: bhavati premavatīnāṃ manāg upekṣāpi doṣāya // RUnm_14.72 //
children.translated_text: For those who possess <s>prema</s>, even the slightest neglect becomes a fault.' // RUnm_14.72 //

children.text: prauḍhaḥ premā sa yatra syād viśleṣasyāsahiṣṇutā // RUnm_14.73 //
children.translated_text: Intense (<s>prauḍha</s>) <s>prema</s> is that where there is intolerance of separation. // RUnm_14.73 //

children.text: nirmāya tvaṃ vitara phalakam hāri kaṃsārimūrtyā
children.translated_text: 'Having fashioned [a portrait], give me a charming tablet with the form of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>!

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ diśasi yadi māṃ mānanirvāhanāya |
children.translated_text: If again and again you send me for the fulfillment of [my] proud anger —'
'gazing upon it in the recess of the dwelling, with ears closed [to outside sounds],

children.text: sāhaṃkārā priyasakhi sukham yāpayiṣyāmi yāmam // RUnm_14.74 //
children.translated_text: I, self-possessed with pride, dear friend, shall happily pass the watches of the night!' // RUnm_14.74 //

body.text: kṛcchrāt sahiṣṇutā yatra sa tu madhyama ucyate // RUnm_14.75 //
body.translated_text: Where there is tolerance of separation only with difficulty, that is called the middle. // RUnm_14.75 //

children.text: avitatham asau kiṃ drāghīyān gamiṣyati vāsaraḥ
children.translated_text: 'Truly, will this long day ever pass, O fair-faced one?

children.text: sumukhi sa niśārambhaḥ kiṃvā sameṣyati maṅgalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Or will that auspicious beginning of night arrive —'
'when the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, smiling-faced like the moon, his locks mingled with cow-dust,

children.text: kṣapayati dṛśām ārtiṃ yatra vrajeśvara-nandanaḥ // RUnm_14.76 //
children.translated_text: dispels the affliction of [our] eyes?' // RUnm_14.76 //

body.text: sa mandaḥ kathito yatra bhavet kutrāpi vismṛtiḥ // RUnm_14.77 //
body.translated_text: That is called mild where there may be forgetfulness somewhere. // RUnm_14.77 //

children.translated_text: 'From jealousy toward the rival's people, I had no
recollection in the weaving of the forest garland;'
'O friend, what shall I do? Before the cows,
this deep lowing sound now swells.' // RUnm_14.78 //
Now <s>sneha</s> (tender affection) —
When <s>prema</s>, ascending to the highest peak, igniting the lamp of consciousness,

children.text: hṛdayaṃ drāvayann eṣa sneha ity abhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: melts the heart — that is called <s>sneha</s>;

children.text: atrodite bhavej jātu na tṛptir darśanādiṣu // RUnm_14.79 //
children.translated_text: when this arises, there is never satiation in seeing [the beloved] and the like. // RUnm_14.79 //
'With eyes — lotuses languid and tremulous,
bearing streams of love-water —
eager for the drinking of the nectar-rasa of the beauty of
that exceedingly sweet, charming form —' // RUnm_14.80 //
'Though your glance-<s>cakora</s> birds drink deeply

children.text: nāntas tṛptiṃ tava katham api prāpnuto dṛk-cakorau |
children.translated_text: the moonlight-nectar of <s>Hari</s>'s moon-face, they do not find inner satisfaction;'

children.text: āghūrṇantau mada-kalatayā suṣṭhu mugdhau yad etau
children.translated_text: 'whirling about, bewildered from intoxication,

children.text: bhūyo bhūyas tam iha vamato bāṣpa-pūra-cchalena // RUnm_14.81 //
children.translated_text: they disgorge it again and again, under the pretext of a flood of tears.' // RUnm_14.81 //

children.text: aṅga-saṅge viloke ca śravaṇādau ca sa kramāt |
children.translated_text: In bodily contact, in gazing, and in hearing and the like, it is in sequence

children.text: kaniṣṭho madhyamaḥ śreṣṭhas trividho'yaṃ manodravaḥ // RUnm_14.82 //
children.translated_text: the least, the middle, and the best — this melting of the heart is of three kinds. // RUnm_14.82 //
There, in bodily contact, for example —
'You, O <s>Mādhava</s>, are the form of dense <s>rasa</s>; <s>Pālī</s> is an embodiment of the essence of charm —

children.text: mādhava bhavad-āśleṣe bhavitā nāsyāḥ kathaṃ dravatā // RUnm_14.83 //
children.translated_text: in your embrace, how could she not have melting?' // RUnm_14.83 //

children.text: asyās tvad-vadane saroja-suhṛdi vyaktiṃ purastād gate
children.translated_text: 'When her beloved's lotus-like face appeared clearly before her,
it is no wonder if her heart's fresh butter melted;'

children.text: kintv āścaryam idaṃ mukunda milite śyāmā-mukhendau bhava-
children.translated_text: 'but this is wondrous: O <s>Mukunda</s>, upon meeting the moon-face of <s>Śyāmā</s>,

children.text: ccetaś candra-maṇir dravan jalatayā bhūyo babhūvācalaḥ // RUnm_14.84 //
children.translated_text: your moonstone-heart, melting into liquid, became all the more unsteady!' // RUnm_14.84 //
'As even half of your name reaches the vicinity of [her] ear,
O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, with limbs washed by the ocean-rain of [her] eyes —'
'the lotus-eyed one, her mind's abundance intoxicated by the honey-wine of love,

children.text: skhalati kuvalayākṣī jṛmbhate stambhate ca // RUnm_14.85 //
children.translated_text: stumbles, becomes stiff, and swells [with emotion].' // RUnm_14.85 //
'Having fixed your attention on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s path,
now you are one whose body trembles;'
'has not your mind, being of the nature of the full ripening of

children.text: kiṃ bhaviṣyati mano na vilīnam // RUnm_14.86 //
children.translated_text: the flood of affection, melted?' // RUnm_14.86 //

body.translated_text: By the word 'and the like' [is meant] in remembering, for example —

body.text: sa ghṛtaṃ madhu cetyuktaṃ sneho dvedhā svarūpataḥ // RUnm_14.87 //
body.translated_text: This <s>sneha</s> is said to be of two kinds by its essential nature — <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee) and <s>madhu</s> (honey). // RUnm_14.87 //

children.translated_text: Affection characterized by extreme reverence (<s>ādara</s>) is called <s>ghṛta</s>. // RUnm_14.88 //

children.text: bhāvāntarānvitao gacchan svādodrekaṃ na tu svayam |
children.translated_text: Combined with other emotions it progresses, but not in its own sweet excess;
it solidifies from the innate, extreme coolness, from mutual reverence;

children.text: gāḍhādaramayas tena snehaḥ syād ghṛtavad ghṛtam // RUnm_14.89 //
children.translated_text: therefore, affection that is filled with deep reverence would be like <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee). // RUnm_14.89 //
'She who rises and from afar embraces the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> with reverence,

children.text: yā snehena vaśīkaroti guruṇā pāvitrya-pūrṇena tam |
children.translated_text: who, with great affection full of purity, brings him under her sway —'

children.text: kṣipraṃ yāti sitopaleva vilayaṃ tat-keli-vṛṣṭyā ca yā
children.translated_text: 'she who swiftly dissolves like rock candy in the rain of his amorous sport —

children.text: yuktā hanta kayopamātum api sā candrāvalī me sakhī // RUnm_14.90 //
children.translated_text: alas, with whom can that <s>Candrāvalī</s>, my friend, even be compared?' // RUnm_14.90 //
'Drawing back her left arm placed on the shoulder of the enemy of <s>Agha</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
placing the right [hand elsewhere], with eyes moist with tears,
timidly shifting both feet with apprehension —
<s>Gaurī</s> [<s>Candrāvalī</s>] smiled at the friend of the rival maiden.' // RUnm_14.91 //
The reverence (<s>ādara</s>) arises from awe (<s>gaurava</s>) — these two are mutually dependent;

children.text: ratyādau sad api snehe suvyaktatvād ihocyate // RUnm_14.92 //
children.translated_text: though present also in <s>rati</s> and the like, it is stated here in [the context of] <s>sneha</s> because of its prominence. // RUnm_14.92 //
<s>Madhu</s> (honey-like affection) would be the <s>sneha</s> toward the beloved that partakes of the utmost sense of 'mine-ness,'
that which is self-manifestly sweet, a gathering of various <s>rasas</s>. // RUnm_14.93 //

body.translated_text: Affection that bears intoxicated warmth is called <s>madhu</s> from its similarity to honey. // RUnm_14.94 //

children.text: rādhā snehamayena hanta racitā mādhurya-sāreṇa sā
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s>, alas, is fashioned of the essence of sweetness, made entirely of affection;

children.text: saudhīva pratimā ghanāpy uru-guṇair bhāvoṣmaṇā vidrutā |
children.translated_text: like a statue in a palace, though solid, she is melted by the warmth of <s>bhāva</s> and great qualities;'

children.text: yan-nāmany api dhāmani śravaṇayor yāti prasaṅgena me
children.translated_text: 'when even [his] names, by mere mention, reach [her] ears in [his] abode —'

children.text: sāndrānandamayī bhavaty anupamā sadyo jagad-vismṛti // RUnm_14.95 //
children.translated_text: becomes dense with bliss, incomparable, and instantaneous oblivion of the world [arises]. // RUnm_14.95 //
Now <s>māna</s> (jealous indignation/wounded pride) —
Love (<s>sneha</s>), by attaining a sense of superiority, honoring a fresh sweetness,

children.text: yo dhārayaty adākṣiṇyaṃ sa māna iti kīrtyate // RUnm_14.96 //
children.translated_text: which maintains an ungracious demeanor — that is called <s>māna</s>. // RUnm_14.96 //
'My eyes were made to overflow with a flood of tears
merely by the dust of your cows, O hero of the cowherds!
Now what use are these breezes from your mouth [i.e., sweet words]?
Cease!' — The fair-browed one knit her brows. // RUnm_14.97 //

body.text: udātto lalitaś ceti māno'yaṃ dvividho mataḥ // RUnm_14.98 //
body.translated_text: This <s>māna</s> is considered to be of two kinds: <s>udātta</s> (noble) and <s>lalita</s> (charming). // RUnm_14.98 //

children.translated_text: Among these, <s>udātta</s> (noble [māna]) —
<s>Udātta</s> is that which, though love is firmly established, maintains a profound course,
possessing graciousness toward the gracious side, and a trace of perverseness occasionally. // RUnm_14.99 //

children.text: rādheti skhilābhidhe mayi haṭhād biddhāntarāpy ārtibhir
children.translated_text: 'When I mistakenly called [her] "<s>Rādhā</s>," though inwardly pierced by distress,
she, to pacify my embarrassment, doubled the smile on her lotus-face,

children.text: jalpe ca mradimānubiddham adhikaṃ mādhuryam ātanvatī
children.translated_text: and in conversation, extending even greater sweetness softly infused with tenderness —
<s>Candrāvalī</s> made my dear friend-circles seem as if painted [i.e., frozen in wonder].' // RUnm_14.100 //

body.translated_text: Among these, the gracious-noble (<s>dākṣiṇya-udātta</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: Now the trace-of-perverseness-noble (<s>vāmya-gandha-udātta</s>), as in the illustrious <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> (5.13.45) —
'One [<s>gopī</s>], having furrowed her brow on the expanse of her forehead, gazing at <s>Hari</s>,
drank in His lotus-face with the bee-like pair of her eyes.' // RUnm_14.101 //
'Though defeated in the dice-game by <s>Mādhava</s>
with an embrace as the wager, the doe-eyed one,
with averted gaze, pretending displeasure,
restrained Him with her hand as He tried to embrace [her].' // RUnm_14.102 //
Now <s>lalita</s> (charming [māna]) —
That which bears sweet love, crookedness endearing to the heart of independence,
and a special playful humor — is called <s>lalita</s>. // RUnm_14.103 //
Among these, the crookedness-charming (<s>kauṭilya-lalita</s>), as in the illustrious Tenth [Canto] (10.32.6) —
'One [<s>gopī</s>], knitting her brows, overwhelmed by love's passionate fury,
glared as if striking [Him], biting her lip.' // RUnm_14.104 //
'On the path, your friend, intoxicated by the god of love,
gave me an unsolicited embrace of her own accord!'
Hearing him say this, <s>Maṅgalā</s>, twisting her face into a crooked [expression],
struck <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with her ear-ornament. // RUnm_14.105 //
'Wonderfully, as He was kissing [her] slowly for the pleasure of prolonged touch,
this one of restless eyes,
with perspiring fingers and a form adorned with horripilation,
flung <s>Keśava</s> away with her left breast.' // RUnm_14.106 //

children.text: mithyā jalpatu te kathaṃ nu rasanā sādhvī-sahasrasya yā
children.translated_text: 'How can your tongue speak falsely — it which became sanctified
through assiduous service of the lip-nectar of a thousand virtuous women, O enemy of <s>Agha</s>!',

children.text: kasmād eva balṃt-karotu ca karaḥ soḍhuṃ kṣamaḥ subhruvāṃ
children.translated_text: 'And why should your hand use force? Is it capable of enduring the fair-browed ones —

children.text: raktaḥ suṣṭhu na nIvi-bandham api yaḥ kā vānya-bandhe kathā // RUnm_14.107 //
children.translated_text: that [hand] which cannot even properly manage a waist-knot — what talk of other bonds?' // RUnm_14.107 //

body.translated_text: Now the humor-charming (<s>narma-lalita</s>), as in the <s>Dānakelikaumudī</s> (90) —

children.text: māno dadhāno viśrambhaṃ praṇayaḥ procyate budhaiḥ // RUnm_14.108 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māna</s> bearing intimacy (<s>viśrambha</s>) is called <s>praṇaya</s> by the wise. // RUnm_14.108 //
'Touched by the conqueror of <s>Mura</s> near her breast, with her neck
firmly placed upon the tip of His arm, bending her brow with an oblique glance,
horripilated, her garment's golden luster dimmed [by perspiration],

children.text: pramodāsrair dhautaṃ nija-mukham iyaṃ mārṣṭi sumukhī // RUnm_14.109 //
children.translated_text: this fair-faced one wipes her own face, washed with tears of delight.' // RUnm_14.109 //
The essential nature of this <s>praṇaya</s> has been described by the wise as intimacy (<s>viśrambha</s>);

children.text: viśrambho'pi dvidhā maitraṃ sakhyaṃ ceti nigadyate // RUnm_14.110 //
children.translated_text: this <s>viśrambha</s> is also of two kinds, called <s>maitra</s> (friendly) and <s>sakhya</s> (companionate). // RUnm_14.110 //

children.text: bhāvajñaiḥ procyate maitraṃ viśrambho vinayānvitaḥ // RUnm_14.111 //
children.translated_text: Intimacy accompanied by respectfulness is called <s>maitra</s> by those who know emotions. // RUnm_14.111 //
As in the illustrious Tenth [Canto] (10.32.4) —
'One [<s>gopī</s>] joyfully took the lotus-hand of <s>Śauri</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] in her joined palms;

children.text: kācid dadhāra tad-bāhum aṃse candana-rūṣitam // RUnm_14.112 //
children.translated_text: another placed His sandalwood-smeared arm upon her shoulder.' // RUnm_14.112 //
'Do not shrink, O lotus-eyed one!
Let him place the anklets on your feet!
Let the rival-beloved be put to shame
by the sounds of these [anklets], like a <s>cakravākī</s> bird!' // RUnm_14.113 //
Intimacy that is boldly unrestrained, consisting of making [the beloved] one's own — is <s>sakhya</s>. // RUnm_14.114 //
'Having impetuously placed both of her own creeper-arms
around the neck of the enemy of the demon [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
bowing his forehead, at his ear —

children.text: sakhi kathitaṃ kim iva tvayā rahasyam // RUnm_14.115 //
children.translated_text: O friend, what secret did you whisper?' // RUnm_14.115 //
Or as in the illustrious <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s> (5.30.34) —

children.text: yadi te tad-vacaḥ satyaṃ satyātyarthaṃ priyeti me |
children.translated_text: 'If your word is true — and you are truly exceedingly dear to me —
then let this tree be taken to the garden of my house!' // RUnm_14.116 //
'Placing the pair of breast-buds, captivating,
upon the chest of the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
this moon-faced friend of mine draws a leaf-sprout pattern

children.text: likhaty asau candra-mukhī sakhī mama // RUnm_14.117 //
children.translated_text: upon [His chest] with saffron drops and a pen of [her] nails.' // RUnm_14.117 //
Or as in the illustrious Tenth [Canto] (10.30.38) —

children.text: tato gatvā vanoddeśe dṛptā keśavam abravīt |
children.translated_text: 'Then, having gone to a forest region, the proud one said to <s>Keśava</s>:

children.text: na pāraye'haṃ calituṃ naya māṃ yatra te manaḥ // RUnm_14.118 //
children.translated_text: "I cannot walk [further]; take me wherever your heart desires!"' // RUnm_14.118 //

children.text: janitvā praṇayaḥ snehāt kutracin mānatāṃ vrajet |
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇaya</s>, born from <s>sneha</s> (love), sometimes proceeds to the state of <s>māna</s>;

children.text: snehān mānaḥ kvacid bhūtvā praṇayatvam athāśnute // RUnm_14.119 //
children.translated_text: <s>māna</s>, having arisen from <s>sneha</s>, sometimes attains the state of <s>praṇaya</s>. // RUnm_14.119 //
Therefore there is mutual cause-and-effect relationship between <s>praṇaya</s> and <s>māna</s>;

children.text: ity atra pṛthag evāsau viśrambhodāhṛtiḥ kṛtā // RUnm_14.120 //
children.translated_text: hence <s>viśrambha</s> (intimacy) has been illustrated separately here. // RUnm_14.120 //
When <s>udātta</s> and <s>lalita</s> are respectively well-combined with <s>maitra</s> and <s>sakhya</s>,
two [types] called <s>sumaitrya</s> (excellent friendliness) and <s>susakhya</s> (excellent companionship) are declared. // RUnm_14.121 //
'When the soft one, with fluttering brows, began to recount before her friends
the secret of the night with the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>,
raising her hand to cover her face,
the beautiful-eyed one, lowering her face, wept again.' // RUnm_14.122 //
'When the paint-pot was playfully thrown by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the palace of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>],

children.text: kṛṣṇena bhruvam āracayya kuṭilām ālokayantī tiraḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Tārā</s>, arching her crooked brow, looking sideways,
completed the wonderful half-drawn [<s>Śrīvatsa</s>] mark on His chest, adorned with <s>Śrīvatsa</s>,

children.text: kāśmīreṇa ghana-śriyā nija-kucākṛṣṭena pūrṇaṃ vyadhāt // RUnm_14.123 //
children.translated_text: with saffron of dense splendor drawn by her own breast.' // RUnm_14.123 //
'In a game of dice, when a drink was made the stake,
having won, as <s>Acyuta</s> was drinking [from] both lips [of hers] —'
'she, with eyes made crooked, bound him by the neck
with the perverse creeper of her left arm — that cowherd-woman!' // RUnm_14.124 //
'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was displaying the gleaming fresh nail-marks on His own chest-surface,
smiling before the friends while arranging His yellow silk garment —'

children.text: abhraśyāmam uro rurodha valita-bhrūr ānanaṃ dhunvatī
children.translated_text: '<s>Gāndharvikā</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>], with arched brows, shaking her face, blocked
[His] cloud-dark chest with the pair of her breasts wearing a corselet of rising horripilation.' // RUnm_14.125 //
Now <s>rāga</s> (deep attachment) —

children.text: duḥkham apy adhikaṃ citte sukhatvenaiva rajyate |
children.translated_text: Even intense suffering is colored in the mind as nothing but happiness;

children.text: yatas tu praṇayotkarṣāt sa rāga iti kīrtyate // RUnm_14.126 //
children.translated_text: that which, arising from the excellence of <s>praṇaya</s>, is called <s>rāga</s>. // RUnm_14.126 //
'On the mountain slope, scorched by the fierce rays of the blazing sun,
paved with terrifying streams of sword-blade-like crystal-discs —'
'beholding the son of the Lord of cowherds, <s>Rādhikā</s>

children.text: talpe nyasta-padāmbujeva muditā na spandate rādhikā // RUnm_14.127 //
children.translated_text: stands delighted, as if her lotus-feet were placed on a bed strewn with blue lotuses, and does not stir.' // RUnm_14.127 //
'O star-<s>abhisārikā</s> (one who ventures out for a tryst), O fourth-night moon,
O one who swells the ocean of desire — to you, O god,

children.text: argho namo bhavatu me saha tena yūnā
children.translated_text: may this offering and homage be mine — along with that youth,
even by a word of false accusation, may the fulfillment of [my] pride be achieved!' // RUnm_14.128 //

body.text: nīlimā raktimā ceti rāgo'yaṃ dvividho mataḥ // RUnm_14.129 //
body.translated_text: This <s>rāga</s> is considered to be of two kinds: <s>nīlimā</s> (dark hue) and <s>raktimā</s> (red hue). // RUnm_14.129 //

children.text: nīlī-śyāmābhavo rāgo nīlimā kathyate budhaiḥ // RUnm_14.130 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> born of <s>nīlī</s> (indigo) and <s>śyāmā</s> (dark) is called <s>nīlimā</s> by the wise. // RUnm_14.130 //
Among these, <s>nīlī-rāga</s> (indigo attachment) —
That which is devoid of the thought of expenditure, not very manifest outwardly,
and concealing the emotions attached to one's own [beloved] — is <s>nīlī-rāga</s> according to the virtuous;
and this is observed in [the relationship of] <s>Candrāvalī</s> and <s>Mukunda</s>. // RUnm_14.131 //
'With a clear, pure heart, always accepting as a virtue

children.text: pratāraṇam api tvayā guṇatayā sadā gṛhṇatī |
children.translated_text: even the deception fashioned by You through various devices,
<s>Candrāvalī</s>, O prince of <s>Vraja</s>, so conducted herself

children.text: sakhībhir api tarkitā tvayi yathā taṭasthety asau // RUnm_14.132 //
children.translated_text: that even her friends suspected she was indifferent toward You.' // RUnm_14.132 //
Now <s>śyāmā-rāga</s> (dark attachment) —
That which, from the first [the indigo stage], possesses slightly more manifestation,

children.text: yaś cireṇaiva sādhyaḥ syāt sa śyāmā-rāga ucyate // RUnm_14.133 //
children.translated_text: requiring a long time to achieve, like [applying] a timid [woman's] herbal cosmetic — is called <s>śyāmā-rāga</s>. // RUnm_14.133 //
'She who formerly, in a charming bower joined with deep darkness, was frightened

children.text: murārer yā pārśve na taruṇi divāpy antaram agāt |
children.translated_text: and would not go even by day to the side of the enemy of <s>Mura</s>, O young woman —'
'that same one now, even when darkness is doubled by <s>tamāla</s> trees, delightedly,

children.text: tamisrārdhe māniny ahaha bhavatī taṃ mṛgayate // RUnm_14.134 //
children.translated_text: in the deep midnight, O proud one — alas — seeks Him out!' // RUnm_14.134 //
<s>Rāga</s> born of <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower) and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder) is considered <s>raktimā</s>. // RUnm_14.135 //
Among these, <s>kusumbha-rāga</s> (safflower attachment) —

children.text: kusumbha-rāgaḥ sa jñeyo yaś citte sajjati drutam |
children.translated_text: <s>Kusumbha-rāga</s> is that which attaches to the heart quickly,
displays the hue of another's attachment, and shines as is fitting. // RUnm_14.136 //

children.text: tvayy eva śravaṇāvadhi priya-sakhī yā kṛṣṇa-baddhāntarā
children.translated_text: 'Your dear friend, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who was bound inwardly to You even up to [the limit of] hearing —
who, even upon seeing a serpent, became mad with delight at its resemblance to Your arm —'

children.text: prekṣya tvāṃ purato'dya kām api daśāṃ prātāsti seyaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: 'seeing You before her today, she has attained some condition such

children.text: na jñāyeta yathā kim eṣa balavān rāgo virāgo'thavā // RUnm_14.137 //
children.translated_text: that it cannot be known whether this is intense passion (<s>rāga</s>) or dispassion (<s>virāga</s>)!' // RUnm_14.137 //
Even <s>kusumbha</s> [dye], in always-excellent substrates, can become permanent;

children.text: iti kṛṣṇa-praṇayiṣu mlānir asya na yujyate // RUnm_14.138 //
children.translated_text: thus, among those devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, its fading is not appropriate. // RUnm_14.138 //
Now <s>mañjiṣṭha-rāga</s> (madder attachment) —
That which is irremovable, not dependent on another, and always grows in radiance —
that is <s>mañjiṣṭha-rāga</s>, as [seen] between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>. // RUnm_14.139 //

children.text: dhatte drāg anupādhi janma vidhinā kenāpi nākampate
children.translated_text: 'It arises quickly, unconditionally, by some [inexplicable] creative power; it is never shaken;

children.text: sūte'ty āhita-sañcayair api rasaṃ te cen mitho vartmane |
children.translated_text: it produces rasa even through accumulated offerings of devotion, if you both [walk] the same path;
it gathers a prosperity that causes wonder, overflowing with unrestrained supreme delight —
this incomparable festival of the bond of <s>prema</s> between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>!' // RUnm_14.140 //

children.text: mayā te nirbandhān murajayini rāgaḥ parihṛtya
children.translated_text: 'By my insistence, O conqueror of <s>Mura</s>, [even if] attachment is abandoned by me,

children.text: mayi snigdhe kintu prathaya paramāśīs tatim imām |
children.translated_text: yet, O affectionate one, bestow upon me this supreme blessing:',
'that with my mind captivated by the exhalation of the fragrance of [Your] face, from this very day,
at the onset of dusk, I may become a bee of the spotless forest-garland [on Your chest]!' // RUnm_14.141 //

children.text: pūrva-pūrvas tu yo bhāvaḥ somābhādau sa rājate |
children.translated_text: The earlier-mentioned emotional state [in the ascending scale] shines in <s>Somābhā</s> and others;

children.text: tathā bhīṣma-sutādau ca śrī-harer mahiṣī-gaṇe // RUnm_14.142 //
children.translated_text: likewise in the granddaughter of <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others, among the queens of illustrious <s>Hari</s>. // RUnm_14.142 //

children.text: ya uttarottaro dviyo rādhikādau sa dīvyati |
children.translated_text: The successive later emotional states shine in <s>Rādhikā</s> and others;

children.text: tathā śrī-satyabhāmāyāṃ lakṣmaṇāyām api kvacit // RUnm_14.143 //
children.translated_text: likewise in the illustrious <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, and also sometimes in <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>. // RUnm_14.143 //
Thus, through the differentiation of <s>bhāvas</s>, the own-faction, rival-faction,
and other divisions of all the fair-browed women of <s>Gokula</s> have been previously stated. // RUnm_14.144 //
The various further distinctions of <s>bhāvas</s> that arise

children.text: aparā api bhāvānāṃ jñeyās tāḥ prajñayā budhaiḥ // RUnm_14.145 //
children.translated_text: from connection with other emotional states should be understood by the wise through discernment. // RUnm_14.145 //
Now <s>anurāga</s> (intense loving attachment) —

children.text: sadānubhūtam api yaḥ kuryān nava-navaṃ priyam |
children.translated_text: That which makes the beloved ever new-and-new, even though always experienced —

children.text: rāgo bhavan nava-navaḥ so'nurāga itīryate // RUnm_14.146 //
children.translated_text: that <s>rāga</s> which becomes ever-new is called <s>anurāga</s>. // RUnm_14.146 //
'<s>Hari</s> has traversed the path of our eyes more than once, [yet]

children.text: apūrvo'yaṃ pūrvaṃ kvacid api na dṛṣṭo madhurimā |
children.translated_text: this unprecedented sweetness was never seen before anywhere.',

children.text: pratīke'py ekasya sphurati muhur aṅgasya sakhi yā
children.translated_text: 'Of even a single limb's reflection, O friend, that beauty

children.text: śriyas tasyāḥ pātuṃ lavam api samarthā na dṛg iyam // RUnm_14.147 //
children.translated_text: which flashes again and again — this eye is unable to drink even a fraction of it!' // RUnm_14.147 //

children.text: ko'yaṃ kṛṣṇa iti vyudasyati dhṛti yas tanvi karṇaṃ viśan
children.translated_text: 'Who is this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?' — thus she casts off composure when [His name] enters her ear.

children.text: rāgāndhe kim idaṃ sadaiva bhavatī tasyorasi krīḍati |
children.translated_text: 'O love-blinded one, what is this? Are you constantly playing upon His chest?'

children.text: hāsyaṃ mā kuru mohite tvam adhunā nyastāsya haste mayā
children.translated_text: 'Do not laugh, O deluded one! My face has now been placed in [His] hand [by me]!'

children.text: satyaṃ satyam asau dṛgaṅganam agād adyaivaa vidyun-nibhaḥ // RUnm_14.148 //
children.translated_text: 'Truly, truly, He has entered my eye this very day — that lightning-like one!' // RUnm_14.148 //
Mutual subjugation, and likewise <s>prema-vaicitya</s>,
intense longing for birth even in inanimate things, and

children.text: vipralambhe'sya visphūrtir ity ādyāḥ syur iha kriyāḥ // RUnm_14.149 //
children.translated_text: manifestation in separation — these and other such activities are found here. // RUnm_14.149 //
O crusher of <s>Agha</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], what is this unprecedented wave of intensity
between the two of you, spreading as an endeavor for mutual conquest?

children.text: mano-hastī bandhas tava yad anayā rāga-nigaḍai-
children.translated_text: The elephant of Your mind is bound by her with the fetters of passion,
and the deer of her heart is [captured] by You with the new ropes of the festival of love! // RUnm_14.150 //

body.text: prema-vaicittya-saṃjñas tu vipralambhaḥ sa kathyate // RUnm_14.151 //
body.translated_text: That separation which is called <s>prema-vaicitya</s> is now described. // RUnm_14.151 //

children.translated_text: 'O slender-waisted one, let us perform austerities to obtain birth among bamboos;'

children.text: vareṇyam manyethāḥ sakhi tad akhilānāṃ sujanuṣām |
children.translated_text: 'O friend, you would consider that the best of all good births;'
'for by the excellence of austerities, this flute, having obtained the honor,
savors the sweetness of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]!' // RUnm_14.152 //

body.translated_text: An intense longing for birth even in inanimate things — as in the <s>Dāna-keli-kaumudī</s> (17) —

children.text: brūyās tvaṃ mathurādhvanīna mathurānāthaṃ tam ity uccakaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Tell him, O traveler to <s>Mathurā</s>, tell loudly to the lord of <s>Mathurā</s>:',

children.text: sandeśaṃ vraja-sundarī kam api te kācin mayā prāhiṇot |
children.translated_text: 'a certain beauty of <s>Vraja</s> has sent some message to you through me;'

children.text: tatra kṣmāpati-pattane yadi gataḥ svacchanda gacchādhunā
children.translated_text: 'if He has gone to the king's city, go freely now;'

children.text: kiṃ kliṣṭām api visphuran diśi diśi kliśnāsi hā me sakhīm // RUnm_14.153 //
children.translated_text: 'why do you torment, appearing in every direction, alas, my distressed friend?' // RUnm_14.153 //

body.translated_text: Now manifestation in separation (<s>vipralambhe visphūrti</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: Now <s>bhāva</s> —
<s>Anurāga</s> (deep attachment), having reached a state that is self-apprehended,

children.text: yāvad-āśraya-vṛttiś ced bhāva ity abhidhīyate // RUnm_14.154 //
children.translated_text: if it functions throughout the full extent of its locus, is called <s>bhāva</s>. // RUnm_14.154 //

children.text: rādhāyā bhavataś ca citta-jatunī svedair vilāpya kramāt
children.translated_text: Gradually melting the lac of <s>Rādhā</s>'s and Your hearts with the perspiration [of love],
joining them together, O lord of the elephant [that sports in] the mountain bower, removing all delusion of difference,
the craftsman of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love) Himself has painted within the palace of the universe
a wondrous [picture] with abundant loads of fresh vermilion of passion! // RUnm_14.155 //
This [<s>bhāva</s>] is extremely difficult to attain even by the hosts of <s>Mukunda</s>'s queens;
it is known only to the queen of <s>Vraja</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>] alone, and is called <s>mahā-bhāva</s>. // RUnm_14.156 //

body.text: varāmṛta-svarūpa-śrīḥ svaṃ svarūpaṃ mano nayet // RUnm_14.157 //
body.translated_text: The beauty of the supreme nectarean nature draws even one's own essential self and mind [into it]. // RUnm_14.157 //

body.text: sa rūḍhaś cādhirūḍhaś cety ucyate dvividho budhaiḥ // RUnm_14.158 //
body.translated_text: It is declared to be of two kinds by the wise: <s>rūḍha</s> (established) and <s>adhirūḍha</s> (transcendently established). // RUnm_14.158 //

children.text: uddīptā sāttvikā yatra sa rūḍha iti bhaṇyate // RUnm_14.159 //
children.translated_text: Where the <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s> (involuntary physical responses) are blazing, that is called <s>rūḍha</s>. // RUnm_14.159 //
Intolerance of the blinking of the eye, churning of the hearts of people nearby,
an entire cosmic age seeming like a moment, distress even in happiness from the apprehension of suffering, // RUnm_14.161 //
even in the absence of bewilderment and the like, constant forgetting of oneself and everything,
a moment becoming a cosmic age — these and other [signs] are found there, in both union and separation. // RUnm_14.162 //

children.text: gopyaś ca kṛṣṇam upalabhya cirād abhīṣṭaṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s>, having obtained <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, their long-desired one, after a long time —
Him at whose sight they cursed the eyelids for blinking —
having drawn Him with their eyes into their hearts and fully embraced Him there,

children.text: tad-bhāvam āpur api nitya-yujāṃ durāpam // RUnm_14.163 //
children.translated_text: all attained that state [of union] which is difficult even for those eternally yoked [in meditation] to achieve. // RUnm_14.163 //

body.translated_text: Among these, intolerance of blinking — as in the illustrious Tenth [Canto] (10.82.38) —

children.text: sakhyaḥ prokṣya kurūn guru-kṣiti-bhṛtām āghūrṇayantī śiraḥ
children.translated_text: O friends, beholding the <s>Kuru</s> women, the heavy mountain-kings' [queens], she makes their heads whirl;

children.text: svasthā viślathayanty aśeṣa-ramaṇīr āplāvya sarvaṃ janam |
children.translated_text: poised and composed, she melts all women, flooding all people;
the wave of the ocean of the <s>gopīs</s>' deep attachment, through its onslaughts, crossing into another realm,

children.text: rākramya stimitāṃ vyadhād api parāṃ vaikuṇṭha-kaṇṭha-śriyam // RUnm_14.164 //
children.translated_text: rendered even the supreme glory of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>'s neck [<s>Lakṣmī</s>] motionless! // RUnm_14.164 //

body.translated_text: Churning of the hearts of nearby people, for example —

children.translated_text: In the <s>rāsa</s> dance, the autumn moonlight — though it became the creator of [infinite] forms — was to them [the <s>gopīs</s>]

children.text: datikṣudrā tāsāṃ yad ajani na tad vismaya-padam |
children.translated_text: but a blink of the eye, extremely small — that this was so is no wonder;
for at the commencement of the surge of bliss, even a moment seems like a fraction of a blink,
and alas, the passage of time, even a great cosmic age, seems inadequate [for them]! // RUnm_14.165 //

body.translated_text: A cosmic age seeming like a moment, for example —

body.text:
tat-saukhye'py ārti-śaṅkayā khinnatvam, yathā śrī-daśame (10.31.19)-
yat te sujāta-caraṇāmbu-ruhaṃ staneṣu;

children.translated_text: fearfully and gently, O beloved, we hold them there, for our breasts are rough;

children.text: tenāṭavīm aṭasi tad vyathate na kiṃ svit;
children.translated_text: with those [feet] You walk through the forest — does that not cause pain?

children.text: kūrpādibhir bhramati dhīr bhavad-āyuṣāṃ naḥ // RUnm_14.166 //
children.translated_text: Our mind trembles for Your life — [even] at the [thought of] pebbles and the like! // RUnm_14.166 //

body.translated_text:
Distress even in happiness from the apprehension of suffering — as in the illustrious Tenth [Canto] (10.31.19) —
Your lotus feet, which are so delicately formed, we place upon our breasts;

body.text:
mohādy-abhāve'pi sarva-vismaraṇaṃ, yathā ekādaśe (11.12.12)-
tā nāvidan mayy anuṣaṅga-baddha-

children.translated_text: did not know their own selves, or this [world], or that [other world],
just as sages in <s>samādhi</s> [do not know], or like rivers
that have entered the ocean [lose] name and form. // RUnm_14.167 //

body.translated_text:
Forgetting everything even in the absence of bewilderment — as in the Eleventh [Canto] (11.12.12) —
