Those [<s>gopīs</s>], their minds bound by constant association with Me,

children.translated_text: Those nights, passed with their most beloved one,
namely Me, who moved about in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
seemed to them like half a moment; but O dear one, those same [nights] for them,
bereft of Me, became equal to a cosmic age! // RUnm_14.168 //

body.translated_text: A moment becoming a cosmic age, as in the same [Eleventh Canto] (11.12.11) —

children.translated_text: By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādya</s>), the power to cause the manifestation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indicated here;

children.text: sambhoga-bhede vispaṣṭaṃ sā purastāt pravakṣyate // RUnm_14.169 //
children.translated_text: that will be clearly explained further ahead in the section on the varieties of union (<s>sambhoga</s>). // RUnm_14.169 //
Now <s>adhirūḍha</s> (transcendently established) —
Where the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent signs) are seen to have attained some indescribable superiority
beyond those stated for <s>rūḍha</s>, that is declared to be <s>adhirūḍha</s>. // RUnm_14.170 //

children.text: lokātīatam ajāṇḍa-koṭigam api traikālikaṃ yat sukhaṃ
children.translated_text: 'If all the happiness that is beyond the world, pervading billions of universes, across all three times,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ ceti pṛthag yadi sphuṭam ubhe te gacchataḥ kuṭatām |
children.translated_text: and all the suffering were each manifested separately — both together becoming a [single] heap —'

children.text: naivābhāsa-tulāṃ śive tad api tat kuṭa-dvayaṃ rādhikā-
children.translated_text: 'even a semblance of a particle of that double heap, O <s>Śiva</s>,',
'could not be found in even a drop of the ocean of joy and sorrow arising from <s>Rādhikā</s>'s <s>prema</s>!' // RUnm_14.171 //

body.text: modano mādanaś cāsāv adhirūḍho dvidhocyate // RUnm_14.172 //
body.translated_text: This <s>adhirūḍha</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>modana</s> (rapture) and <s>mādana</s> (supreme rapture). // RUnm_14.172 //

children.text: modanaḥ sa dvayor yatra sāttvikoddīpta-sauṣṭhavam // RUnm_14.173 //
children.translated_text: <s>Modana</s> is that in which the <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s> (involuntary responses) blaze forth with excellence in both [lovers]. // RUnm_14.173 //
Producing an incomparable sweet melodious sound, bursting forth with the beauty of paralysis,
abundantly sprouting with buds and bearing fruit as pearl-drops of perspiration,
though swaying with blossoms of tears of nectar, trembling with the flurries [of love] —
the wish-fulfilling tree of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>'s ecstasy has long been resplendent! // RUnm_14.174 //
Where, by the weight of agitation of <s>Hari</s> together with His beloved,
the beloved surpasses [all others], renowned for the great wealth of <s>prema</s> — // RUnm_14.175 //

children.text: rādhikā-yūtha evāsau modano na tu sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: this <s>modana</s> exists only in the group of <s>Rādhikā</s>, not everywhere;

children.text: yaḥ śrīmān hlādinī-śakteḥ suvilāsaḥ priyo varaḥ // RUnm_14.176 //
children.translated_text: it is the dear, excellent, beautiful play of the <s>hlādinī</s> (bliss) potency. // RUnm_14.176 //

children.text: hanta stambha-karambitā bhuvi kuror bhadrā sarasvaty abhū-
children.translated_text: 'Alas! <s>Sarasvatī</s> of the auspicious <s>Kuru</s> realm became transfixed with paralysis;

children.text: dbāṣpaṃ bhāskarajā mumoca tarasā satyābhraman narmadā |
children.translated_text: the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>] shed tears swiftly; <s>Satyā</s> wandered about [distraught]; <s>Narmadā</s> [trembled];'

children.text: bheje bhīṣma-sutā ca varṇa-vikṛtiṃ gāmbhīrya-bhāg apy asau
children.translated_text: 'even <s>Bhīṣmasutā</s> [<s>Gaṅgā</s>], though possessing depth, underwent a change of complexion,'
'when the dark ocean of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was overcome by the waves of <s>Rādhikā</s>'s wondrous love!' // RUnm_14.177 //

body.translated_text: Among these, causing agitation in <s>Hari</s> together with His beloved, for example —

children.translated_text: 'From non-duality, [surpassing] <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), who is <s>Hara</s>'s half-body; from friendship, <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
who resides on <s>Acyuta</s>'s chest — the lotus of His bee-like mind; and <s>Satyā</s> from good fortune;'
'from sweetness, <s>Candrāvalī</s>, the life-companion of the lord of sweetness — surpassing [all these],

children.text: paśyāruddha hariṃ prasārya laharīṃ rādhānurāgāmbudhiḥ // RUnm_14.178 //
children.translated_text: behold — the ocean of <s>Rādhā</s>'s deep attachment, spreading its waves, has arrested <s>Hari</s>!' // RUnm_14.178 //

body.translated_text: Surpassing those who possess the great wealth of <s>prema</s>, for example —

children.translated_text: This <s>modana</s>, in the state of imminent separation, becomes <s>mohana</s> (bewildering),

children.text: yasmin viraha-vaivaśyāt sūddīptā eva sāttvikāḥ // RUnm_14.179 //
children.translated_text: in which, by the helplessness of separation, the <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s> are *sūddīpta* (super-blazing). // RUnm_14.179 //
<s>Rādhā</s>, with arising trembling making her teeth chatter, her speech tumbling into the cavity of her throat,
making the circle of <s>Gokula</s> watered as by a river with her tears,
with her horripilated body putting to shame the jackfruit,

children.text: citraṃ tad-ghana-rāga-rāśibhir api śvetī-kṛtā vartate // RUnm_14.180 //
children.translated_text: wondrously, even by those dense masses of passion, she has been rendered pale! // RUnm_14.180 //
Here the <s>anubhāvas</s> [are]: swooning even when <s>Govinda</s> is embraced by the beloved;
desire for His happiness even while accepting unbearable suffering;
causing agitation in the entire universe; making even animals weep;
thirst for union with Him even by one's own material elements, from the prospect of death;
divine madness (<s>divyonmāda</s>) and other [signs] are also enumerated by the learned. // RUnm_14.182 //
This <s>mohana</s> generally arises in the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>];
its effects are entirely distinct from ordinary transitory bewilderment (<s>sañcāri-moha</s>). // RUnm_14.183 //

body.text: tatra kāntāśliṣṭe'pi harau mūrcchā-kāritvaṃ, yathā padyāvalyām (371)-

children.translated_text: 'In the palace of <s>Dvārakā</s> upon the ocean shimmering with the luster of gems,
even when embraced by <s>Rukmiṇī</s> with intense horripilation —'
'may the enemy of <s>Mura</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], swooning in meditation upon the fullness of the fragrance of <s>Rādhā</s>'s love-play
in a <s>vānīra</s>-creeper bower on the smooth bank of <s>Yamunā</s>, protect the entire world!' // RUnm_14.184 //

body.translated_text: Among these, causing swooning in <s>Hari</s> even when embraced by a beloved — as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (371) —

children.text: syān naḥ saukhyaṃ yad api balavad goṣṭham āpte mukunde
children.translated_text: 'Should we have abundant happiness if <s>Mukunda</s> returns to the cowherds' settlement,

children.text: yady alpāpi kṣatir udayate tasya māgāt kadāpi |
children.translated_text: may not even the slightest harm ever befall Him;

children.text: aprāpte'smin yad api nagarād ārtir ugrā bhaven naḥ
children.translated_text: should fierce suffering be ours if He does not return from the city,

children.text: saukhyaṃ tasya sphurati hṛdi cet tatra vāsaṃ karotu // RUnm_14.185 //
children.translated_text: if happiness shines in His heart, let Him dwell there!' // RUnm_14.185 //

body.translated_text: Desire for His happiness even while accepting unbearable suffering —

children.text: nāraṃ cukrośa cakraṃ phaṇi-kulam abhavad vyākulaṃ svedam ūhe
children.translated_text: 'The waters cried out; the discus-host [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>] became agitated; the serpent clans bore perspiration;

children.text: vṛndaṃ vṛndārakāṇāṃ pracura-mudam amucann aśru vaikuṇṭha-bhājaḥ |
children.translated_text: the host of gods released tears of abundant joy; the inhabitants of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> —'

children.text: rādhāyāś citram īśa bhramati diśi diśi prema-niḥśvāsa-dhūme
children.translated_text: 'wondrous! O Lord, when the smoke of <s>Rādhā</s>'s sighs of love wanders in every direction,',

children.text: pūrṇānande'py uṣitvā bahir idam abahiś cārtam āsīd ajāṇḍam // RUnm_14.186 //
children.translated_text: 'even though dwelling in perfect bliss, the universe became outwardly — and inwardly too — pained!' // RUnm_14.186 //

body.translated_text: Causing agitation in the entire universe, for example —

children.text: aurva-stomāt kaṭur api kathaṃ durbalenorasā me
children.translated_text: 'How can this intense suffering born of separation from <s>Hari</s>, fiercer than the submarine fire,

children.text: tāpaḥ prauḍho hari-virahajaḥ sahyate tan na jāne |
children.translated_text: be borne by my feeble breast? That I do not know;'

children.text: niṣkrāntā ced bhavati hṛdayād yasya dhūma-cchaṭāpi
children.translated_text: 'for if even a wisp of its smoke were to escape from my heart,

children.text: brahmāṇḍānāṃ sakhi kulam api jvālayā jājvalīti // RUnm_14.187 //
children.translated_text: it would, O friend, set ablaze all the families of universes with its flame!' // RUnm_14.187 //
'When the enemy of <s>Mura</s> departed for the city of <s>Dvārakā</s>, <s>Rādhā</s>,
clinging with longing to a <s>vañjula</s> creeper in a bower on the bank of <s>Kālindī</s> [<s>Yamunā</s>], wrapped in His garment,
sang in a voice broken with heavy tears and stammering, in a high pitch —'

children.text: yenāntarjalacāribhir jalacarair apy utkam utkūjitam // RUnm_14.188 //
children.translated_text: 'by which even the aquatic creatures dwelling beneath the waters crooned with longing!' // RUnm_14.188 //

body.translated_text: Making even animals weep — as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (373) —

body.text: mṛtyu-svīkārāt svabhūtair api tat-saṅga-tṛṣṇā, yathā tatraiva (336)-

children.text: pañcatvaṃ tanur etu bhūta-nivahāu svāṃśe viśantu sphuṭaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Let this body perish! Let the hosts of elements clearly merge into their own portions!

children.text: dhātāraṃ praṇipatya hanta śirasā tatrāpi yāce varam |
children.translated_text: Bowing my head before the Creator, alas, even there I pray for a boon:',
'may the water [of my body] be in His pools, the light in His mirror, the space

children.text: vyomni vyoma tadīya-vartmani dharā tat-tāla-vṛnte'nilaḥ // RUnm_14.189 //
children.translated_text: in His courtyard, the earth on His path, and the wind in the fan of His palm-leaves!' // RUnm_14.189 //

body.translated_text: Thirst for union with Him even by one's own material elements, from the acceptance of death — as in the same [<s>Padyāvalī</s>] (336) —

children.translated_text: Now <s>divyonmāda</s> (divine madness) —
When this state called <s>mohana</s> has reached some [indescribable] culmination,

children.text: bhramābhā kāpi vaicitrī divyonmāda itīryate // RUnm_14.190 //
children.translated_text: a certain variegation resembling delirium is called <s>divyonmāda</s> (divine madness). // RUnm_14.190 //

body.translated_text: <s>Udghūrṇā</s> (wild agitation), <s>citra-jalpa</s> (variegated speech), and others — its varieties are considered many. // RUnm_14.191 //

children.translated_text: <s>Udghūrṇā</s> is an extraordinary array of helpless actions. // RUnm_14.192 //

children.text: śayyāṃ kuñja-gṛhe kvacid vitanute sā vāsa-sajjāyitā
children.translated_text: She prepares a bed in a bower-house somewhere, as if dressed for His stay;

children.text: nīlābhraṃ dhṛta-khaṇḍitā vyavahṛtiś caṇḍī kvacit tarjati |
children.translated_text: somewhere, with the disposition of a wronged woman (<s>khaṇḍitā</s>), she furiously threatens a dark cloud;
<s>Rādhā</s>, tormented by the frenzy of separation from you, swirling with the agitation of going forth to meet [you] in the terrible darkness —

children.text: rādhā te virahodbhrama-pramathitā dhatte na kāṃ vā daśām // RUnm_14.193 //
children.translated_text: what condition does she not assume? // RUnm_14.193 //
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> arrived at the city of <s>Mathurā</s>, in the <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>,

children.text: udghūrṇeyaṃ tṛtīyāṅke rādhāyāḥ sphuṭam īritā // RUnm_14.194 //
children.translated_text: this <s>udghūrṇā</s> (whirling delirium) of <s>Rādhā</s> is clearly expressed in the third act. // RUnm_14.194 //
Now <s>citra-jalpa</s> (variegated speech) —
Upon seeing a friend of her most beloved, speech imbued with a profusion of emotions,
bursting forth with concealed anger, culminating in intense longing — // RUnm_14.195 //
This <s>citra-jalpa</s> has ten limbs: <s>prajalpa</s>, <s>parijalpita</s>,
<s>vijalpa</s>, <s>ujjalpa</s>, <s>saṃjalpa</s>, <s>avajalpa</s>, <s>abhijalpita</s>,

children.text: ājalpaḥ pratijalpaś ca sujalpaś ceti kīrtitāḥ // RUnm_14.196 //
children.translated_text: <s>ājalpa</s>, <s>pratijalpa</s>, and <s>sujalpa</s> — thus they are enumerated. // RUnm_14.196 //

body.translated_text: This is revealed in the tenth [canto of the Bhāgavata], known as the <s>Bhramara-gīta</s> (Song of the Bee). // RUnm_14.197 //

children.translated_text: Though this <s>citra-jalpa</s> is extremely difficult to appreciate, being replete with

children.text: api cec citrajalpo'yaṃ manāk tad api kathyate // RUnm_14.198 //
children.translated_text: innumerable varieties of emotion and wonder, still it will be explained to some extent. // RUnm_14.198 //
Among these, <s>prajalpa</s> (rambling reproach) —
That which, joined with envy, jealousy, and pride, bears the mark of disdain,

children.text: priyasyākauśalodgāraḥ prajalpaḥ sa tu kīrtyate // RUnm_14.199 //
children.translated_text: and pours out the beloved's lack of skill — that is called <s>prajalpa</s>. // RUnm_14.199 //
'O bee, friend of a cheat! Do not touch the feet of our rival,
whose garland, smeared with saffron from [her] breasts, stains your whiskers!
Let the lord of honey-wine (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) carry the favor of those proud women —

children.text: yadu-sadasi viḍambyaṃ yasya dūtas tvam īdṛk // RUnm_14.200 //
children.translated_text: he whose messenger is someone like you is a laughingstock in the assembly of the <s>Yadus</s>!' // RUnm_14.200 //
Now <s>parijalpita</s> (indirect self-justification) —
That which, by demonstrating the Lord's cruelty, deceitfulness, fickleness, and the like,
indirectly reveals one's own discernment — that is <s>parijalpita</s>. // RUnm_14.201 //
'Having once made [us] drink the intoxicating nectar of his lips,
he immediately abandoned us, just as one like you [a bee] does flowers!
How then does <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) serve his lotus feet?

children.text: hy api bata hṛta-cetā hy uttamaḥ-śloka-jalpaiḥ // RUnm_14.202 //
children.translated_text: Surely she too has had her mind stolen by the sweet words of the Most Praised One!' // RUnm_14.202 //
Now <s>vijalpa</s> (envious retort) —
That which, with manifest envy concealing within it the seal of hidden wounded pride,

children.text: aghadviṣi kaṭākṣoktir vijalpo viduṣāṃ mataḥ // RUnm_14.203 //
children.translated_text: is a sidelong-glance utterance toward the enemy of <s>Agha</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — is <s>vijalpa</s>, according to the learned. // RUnm_14.203 //

children.text: kim iha bahu ṣaḍaṅghre gāyasi tvaṃ yadūnām
children.translated_text: 'Why, O six-legged one [bee], do you sing here so much before us
of the ancient lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, who has taken no home?
Let the praises of that one be sung to the friends of <s>Arjuna</s> —
they, the beloved ones, whose breast-wounds [of love] he can heal, will grant your desire!' // RUnm_14.204 //
Now <s>ujjalpa</s> (prideful denunciation) —
The narration of <s>Hari</s>'s deceptiveness, with jealousy impregnated with pride,

children.text: sāsūyaś ca tad-ākṣepo dhīrair ujjalpa īryate // RUnm_14.205 //
children.translated_text: and envious censure of him — this is called <s>ujjalpa</s> by the discerning. // RUnm_14.205 //

children.text: divi bhuvi ca rasāyāṃ kāḥ striyas tad-durāpāḥ
children.translated_text: 'In heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld — what women are unattainable for him
whose deceptively charming laughter and brow-play [captivate all]?

children.text: caraṇa-raja upāste yasya bhūtir vayaṃ kā
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself serves the dust of his feet — what are we then?

children.text: api ca kṛpaṇa-pakṣe hy uttamaḥ-śloka-śabdaḥ // RUnm_14.206 //
children.translated_text: And yet, on behalf of the wretched, the epithet "Most Praised" [is still used]!' // RUnm_14.206 //
Now <s>saṃjalpa</s> (accusatory reproach) —
That which, with a certain profound, arrogant gesture of censure,
declares his ingratitude and the like — that is called <s>saṃjalpa</s> by the wise. // RUnm_14.207 //

children.text: visṛja śirasi pādaṃ vedmy ahaṃ cāṭu-kārair
children.translated_text: 'Remove [his] foot from [my] head! I know [his] flatterers well —
you who are skilled in cajolery, having come as an envoy from <s>Mukunda</s>!
One who, having acted on his own, abandoned wife, children, and other people —

children.text: vyasṛjad akṛta-cetāḥ kiṃ nu sandheyam asmin // RUnm_14.208 //
children.translated_text: he, the ungrateful one — why should I make a pact with him?' // RUnm_14.208 //
Now <s>avajalpa</s> (fearful criticism) —
Where, because of <s>Hari</s>'s hardness, lustfulness, and roguishness, the unfitness for attachment

children.text: yatra serṣyaṃ bhiyevoktā so'vajalpaḥ satāṃ mataḥ // RUnm_14.209 //
children.translated_text: is spoken with jealousy, as if from fear — that is <s>avajalpa</s>, according to the virtuous. // RUnm_14.209 //
'Like a hunter he pierced the king of monkeys [<s>Vāli</s>], acting with the ways of a greedy one;
he disfigured a woman [<s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>], conquered as he was by a woman, that follower of desire;

children.text: balim api balim attvāveṣṭayad dhvāṅkṣa-vad yas
children.translated_text: having accepted the offering of <s>Bali</s>, he bound even mighty <s>Bali</s>, like a crow!

children.text: tad alam asita-sakhyair dustyajas tat-kathārthaḥ // RUnm_14.210 //
children.translated_text: Enough then of friendship with the dark one — [yet] the talk of him is hard to abandon!' // RUnm_14.210 //
Now <s>abhijalpita</s> (indirect lamentation) —

children.text: bhaṅgyā tyāgaucitī tasya khagānām api khedanāt |
children.translated_text: Where, by implication, his fitness for abandonment and the suffering of even birds [by his deeds]

children.text: yatra sānuśayaṃ proktā tad bhaved abhijalpitam // RUnm_14.211 //
children.translated_text: is spoken with remorse — that is <s>abhijalpita</s>. // RUnm_14.211 //
'Those who have once tasted a drop of the ear-nectar of the accounts of his pastimes,
their sense of duality-dharma swept away, are ruined!
Immediately abandoning their wretched homes and families, the wretched ones —

children.text: bahava iha vihaṅgā bhikṣu-caryāṃ caranti // RUnm_14.212 //
children.translated_text: many birds here wander about, living the life of beggars!' // RUnm_14.212 //
Now <s>ājalpa</s> (despairing accusation) —

children.text: jaihmyaṃ tasyārtidatvaṃ ca nirvedād yatra kīrtitam |
children.translated_text: Where his crookedness and his causing of pain are proclaimed from despair,

children.text: bhaṅyānya-sukhadatvaṃ ca sa ājalpa udīritaḥ // RUnm_14.213 //
children.translated_text: and his giving pleasure to others is indirectly [stated] — that is called <s>ājalpa</s>. // RUnm_14.213 //

body.text:
yathā (10.47.19)--
vayam ṛtam iva jihma-vyāhṛtaṃ śraddadhānāḥ

children.translated_text: like ignorant she-deer [trusting] the song of a hunter — we, the wives of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!
We have seen this again and again — the intense love-wound from the touch of his nails!
O counselor, speak of something else!' // RUnm_14.214 //

body.translated_text: For example (Bhāg. 10.47.19) — 'We, trusting his crooked speech as if it were truth,

children.translated_text: Now <s>pratijalpa</s> (concessive address) —
Where, in this state of hard-to-abandon duality, one humbly says 'attainment is not deserved,'
while honoring the messenger — that is <s>pratijalpa</s>. // RUnm_14.215 //

children.text: priya-sakha punar āgāḥ preyasā preṣitaḥ kiṃ
children.translated_text: 'O dear friend, have you come again, sent by the beloved?
Choose — what do you entreat? You are honorable to me, O friend!
But how can you lead us to the side of that one of hard-to-abandon duality?

children.text: satatam urasi saumya śrīr vadhūḥ sākam āste // RUnm_14.216 //
children.translated_text: On his chest, O gentle one, <s>Śrī</s>, his consort, always abides!' // RUnm_14.216 //
Now <s>sujalpa</s> (heartfelt inquiry) —
Where, with sincerity, gravity, humility, restlessness,

children.text: sotkaṇṭhaṃ ca hariḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sa sujalpo nigadyate // RUnm_14.217 //
children.translated_text: and longing, <s>Hari</s> is asked about — that is called <s>sujalpa</s>. // RUnm_14.217 //
'Does the son of the noble one [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] now dwell in the city of <s>Mathurā</s>?

children.text: smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṃś ca gopān |
children.translated_text: Does he remember, O gentle one, his paternal home and his kinsmen, the cowherds?

children.text: kvacid api sa kathāṃ naḥ kiṅkarīṇāṃ gṛṇīte
children.translated_text: Does he ever speak of us, his maidservants?

children.text: bhujam aguru-sugandhaṃ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu // RUnm_14.218 //
children.translated_text: When will he place upon our heads his arm, fragrant with <s>aguru</s> [incense]?' // RUnm_14.218 //
Now <s>mādana</s> (the highest love-madness) —
This <s>mādana</s>, the supreme beyond the supreme, blazing with the emergence of all emotions,

children.text: rājate hlādinī-sāro rādhāyām eva yaḥ sadā // RUnm_14.219 //
children.translated_text: shines as the essence of the <s>hlādinī</s> (bliss) potency, existing always in <s>Rādhā</s> alone. // RUnm_14.219 //

body.text:
yathā-
āsṛṣṭer akṣayiṣṇuṃ hṛdaya-vidhu-maṇi-drāvaṇaṃ vakrimāṇaṃ
pūrṇatve'py udvahantaṃ nija-ruci-ghaṭayā sādhvasaṃ dhvaṃsayantam |
tanvānaṃ śaṃ pradoṣe dhṛta-nava-navatā-sampadaṃ mādanatvā-
dadvaitaṃ naumi rādhā-danuja-vijayinor adbhutaṃ bhāva-candram
// RUnm_14.220 //
body.translated_text: For example — 'Imperishable since before creation, melting the moon-gem of the heart, [yet] crooked; even in fullness, bearing a certain awe through the splicing of its own radiance; bestowing bliss at nightfall, possessing the treasure of ever-renewed freshness, through the quality of mādana — I praise this wondrous, non-dual moon of emotion of <s>Rādhā</s> and the Conqueror of Demons [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]!' // RUnm_14.220 //

children.translated_text: Herein, even toward an unworthy object, the arousal of intense jealousy;
even in constant enjoyment, praise whose basis is the mere fragrance of that [enjoyment], and so on — // RUnm_14.221 //
'O garland of the forest [<s>vanamālā</s>], why do you constantly cultivate enmity

children.text: tvam addhā vidveṣaṃ kim iti vanamāle racayasi |
children.translated_text: with the pure, doe-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>?

children.text: tṛṇīkurvaty asmān vapur agharipor āśikham idaṃ
children.translated_text: You who, belittling us, on the broad chest of the enemy of <s>Agha</s>,

children.text: pariṣvajyāpāda mahati hṛdaye yā viharasi // RUnm_14.222 //
children.translated_text: embracing this body from head to foot, sport in his great heart!' // RUnm_14.222 //

body.translated_text: Now jealousy even toward the unworthy, as in the <s>Dānakelikaumudī</s> (92) —

children.translated_text: 'The <s>Pulinda</s> women, fulfilled by the blessed saffron
from the lotus feet of the Most Praised One, which had adorned the breasts of his beloveds —
afflicted with love-sickness upon seeing that [saffron], they smeared it, stained upon the grass,
upon their faces and breasts, and thus abandoned their anguish.' // RUnm_14.223 //

body.translated_text: Praise whose basis is merely the fragrance of that, even in constant enjoyment — as in the blessed Tenth [Canto] (10.21.17) —

children.translated_text: 'What severe austerity did this tender <s>mālatī</s> [jasmine] creeper
perform in a former life, and on which side?
Alas — she who now embraces, with spotless [limbs],
a <s>tamāla</s> tree resembling the son of the lord of the cowpen!' // RUnm_14.224 //

children.text: yoga eva bhaved eṣa vicitraḥ ko'pi mādanaḥ |
children.translated_text: This <s>mādana</s> exists only in union — some wondrous [state];
its amorous displays shine forth as the eternal pastimes (<s>nitya-līlā</s>), a thousandfold. // RUnm_14.225 //
The path of <s>mādana</s> is as impenetrable as that of <s>Madana</s> (Cupid) himself;

children.text: na nirvaktuṃ bhavec chakyā tenāsau munināpy alam // RUnm_14.226 //
children.translated_text: it cannot be fully described — hence even a sage is incapable [of doing so]. // RUnm_14.226 //
Moreover —
<s>Rati</s>, first quickly attaining the state of <s>rāga</s> and <s>anurāga</s>, then <s>sneha</s> (affection),

children.text: mānatvaṃ praṇayatvaṃ ca kvacit paścāt prapadyate // RUnm_14.227 //
children.translated_text: subsequently sometimes attains the states of <s>māna</s> (wounded pride) and <s>praṇaya</s> (loving intimacy). // RUnm_14.227 //
For this very reason, in the scriptures, regarding <s>Rādhikā</s> and others,
even in the context of <s>pūrva-rāga</s> (first love), the characteristics of <s>rāga</s> are clearly manifested. // RUnm_14.228 //

children.text: sphuranti vraja-devīṣu parā bhāva-bhidāś ca yāḥ |
children.translated_text: The supreme differentiations of emotion that appear in the goddesses of <s>Vraja</s>

children.text: tās tarkāygocaratyā na samyag iha varṇitāḥ // RUnm_14.229 //
children.translated_text: are beyond the reach of logical reasoning and have not been fully described here. // RUnm_14.229 //
In ordinary love (<s>sādhāraṇī rati</s>), [the <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s>] are considered to be in the 'smoking' (<s>dhūmāyita</s>) state;
they are 'blazing' (<s>jvalita</s>) in <s>rati</s> and <s>prema</s>; 'radiant' (<s>dīpta</s>) in <s>sneha</s> and the five [stages] following;

children.text: rūḍhe bhāve tathoddīptāḥ sudīptā mohanādiṣu // RUnm_14.230 //
children.translated_text: in the established emotion (<s>rūḍha-bhāva</s>), they are 'brightly radiant' (<s>uddīpta</s>); and 'supremely radiant' (<s>sudīpta</s>) in <s>mohana</s> and the rest. // RUnm_14.230 //
This is the general principle; but according to the weight of the superior, middling, and other [heroines],

children.text: deśa-kāla-janādīnāṃ kvāpy eṣāṃ syād viparyayam // RUnm_14.231 //
children.translated_text: and of place, time, persons, and so on, there may sometimes be a reversal among these. // RUnm_14.231 //
The first [ordinary <s>rati</s>] properly attains the ultimate limit up to <s>prema</s>;

children.text: ratir bhāvāntimāṃ sīmāṃ samarthaiva prapadyante // RUnm_14.232 //
children.translated_text: only the competent <s>rati</s> (<s>samarthā</s>) attains the limit up to <s>anurāga</s> and the limit ending in <s>bhāva</s>. // RUnm_14.232 //
The <s>rati</s> of the humorous companions (<s>narma-vayasya</s>) reaches the ultimate state of <s>anurāga</s>;

children.text: teṣv eva subalādīnāṃ bhāvāntām eva gacchati // RUnm_14.233 //
children.translated_text: among them, that of <s>Subala</s> and others alone reaches the state ending in <s>bhāva</s>. // RUnm_14.233 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on the permanent sentiment (<s>sthāyī-bhāva-prakaraṇa</s>) in the illustrious <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>. || 14 ||
(15) Now the chapter on the divisions of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (<s>śṛṅgāra-bheda-prakaraṇa</s>).

body.text: sa vipralambhaḥ sambhoga iti dvedhojjvalo mataḥ // RUnm_15.1 //
body.translated_text: The radiant [<s>ujjvala</s>, i.e., <s>śṛṅgāra</s> rasa] is considered twofold: separation (<s>vipralambha</s>) and union (<s>sambhoga</s>). // RUnm_15.1 //

children.text: yūnor ayuktayor bhāvo yuktayor vā tayor mithaḥ |
children.translated_text: The emotion of the two youths, whether separated or united,
which intensifies when the desired embrace and the like are not obtained —
that should be known as <s>vipralambha</s>, which is the cause of the heightening of union (<s>sambhoga</s>). // RUnm_15.2 //
And thus it has been said —

children.text: na vinā vipralambhena sambhogaḥ puṣṭim aśnute |
children.translated_text: 'Without separation (<s>vipralambha</s>), union (<s>sambhoga</s>) does not attain fullness;

children.text: kāṣāyite hi vastrādau bhūyān evābhivardhate // RUnm_15.3 //
children.translated_text: just as when a cloth is first dyed [with mordant], the [final] color increases all the more.' // RUnm_15.3 //

children.text: pūrva-rāgas tathā mānaḥ prema-vaicittyam ity api |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrva-rāga</s> (first love), then <s>māna</s> (jealous anger), <s>prema-vaicittya</s> (love's bewilderment), also

children.text: pravāsaś ceti kathito vipralambhaś catur-vidhaḥ // RUnm_15.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>pravāsa</s> (sojourn/absence) — thus separation is declared to be fourfold. // RUnm_15.4 //
That love (<s>rati</s>) which, prior to union, arises from seeing, hearing, and the like,

children.text: tayor unmīlati prājñaiḥ pūrva-rāgaḥ sa ucyate // RUnm_15.5 //
children.translated_text: which unfolds in both [the hero and heroine] — that is called <s>pūrva-rāga</s> by the wise. // RUnm_15.5 //

children.text: sākṣāt kṛṣṇasya citre ca syāt svapnādau ca darśanam // RUnm_15.6 //
children.translated_text: Seeing may be direct, or through a portrait, or in a dream, and so on. // RUnm_15.6 //
Bearing a dark splendor like the inner petal of a blue lotus,
wearing a garment resembling a cluster of flowing gold —
his chest adorned with a beautiful pearl necklace —
who is this youth who makes the whole world pervaded by <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid)? // RUnm_15.7 //

body.translated_text: Among these, direct sight (<s>sākṣāt</s>), as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (159) —

children.text: śiśiraya dṛśau dṛṣṭvā divyaṃ kiśoram itīkṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Cool your eyes by beholding this divine youth!' — thus addressed,
through the confidence of conversational words, you are marked by the fruit of playfulness;

children.text: śiva śiva kathaṃ jānīmas tvām avakra-dhiyo vayaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Auspicious, auspicious! How can we, of uncrooked understanding, recognize you
who blossoms forth with the mass of flames of the dense submarine fire?' // RUnm_15.8 //

body.translated_text: Through a portrait (<s>citra</s>), as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (2.23) —

children.translated_text: 'In a dream, O companion, I saw a river with dark waters;
on its bank, a bower-hall of <s>mādhavī</s> creepers with humming bees;
within it, a lover — dark-hipped, a mass of darkness embodied —

children.text: citraṃ candrāvalim api sa māṃ pātum icchann arautsīt // RUnm_15.9 //
children.translated_text: wondrously, he who wished to drink even <s>Candrāvalī</s>, made me weep!' // RUnm_15.9 //

children.text: vandi-dūtī-sakhī-vaktrād gītādeś ca śrutir bhavet // RUnm_15.10 //
children.translated_text: Hearing may come from the mouth of a bard, a messenger-woman, a friend, or from a song, and so on. // RUnm_15.10 //
As the best among bards here recites the hymn of valor
composed for the conquest of the king of <s>Magadha</s>, O friend —
tell me, how is it that <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s> became
extraordinary, covered with a host of goosebumps? // RUnm_15.11 //

body.translated_text: From the mouth of a bard, for example —

children.translated_text: 'When I revealed an account of you, O <s>Mukunda</s>,
<s>Tārāvalī</s>, with body-creeper bristling with horripilation, with lowered eyes,
though eager to hear, with throat blocked by a heavy stammer —'

children.text: praṣṭuṃ tavākṣamata sā na kathā-viśeṣam // RUnm_15.12 //
children.translated_text: was unable to ask You about any particular topic of conversation. // RUnm_15.12 //

body.translated_text: From the mouth of a messenger-woman, for example —

children.translated_text: As long as that one with crazed <s>cakora</s>-bird eyes
heard the account of You from my mouth,
so long, day after day, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, does my friend
advance toward an irresistible autumnal emaciation. // RUnm_15.13 //

body.translated_text: From the mouth of a friend (<s>sakhī</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: Making my two eyes tearful
instantly, in the assembly of the king,
who is this expert-minded one who plays the <s>vīṇā</s>?

children.text: kam udaśruḥ sakhi vaiṇiko muniḥ // RUnm_15.14 //
children.translated_text: O friend, which tearful minstrel-sage is he? // RUnm_15.14 //
The previously mentioned causes of the birth of <s>rati</s> (love), such as direct approach and others,

children.text: atra te pūrva-rāge'pi jñeyā dhīrair yathocitam // RUnm_15.15 //
children.translated_text: should be understood by the wise as applicable here in <s>pūrva-rāga</s> (love-in-anticipation) as well, as is fitting. // RUnm_15.15 //
Moreover, even when <s>Mādhava</s>'s attachment arises first,

children.text: ādau rāge mṛgākṣīṇāṃ prokte syāc cārutādhikā // RUnm_15.16 //
children.translated_text: when the initial love of the doe-eyed maidens is described, there is greater charm. // RUnm_15.16 //

children.text: atra sañcāriṇo vyādhiḥ śaṅkāsūyā śramaḥ klamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the transitory emotions (<s>sañcāri-bhāvas</s>) are: illness, apprehension, jealousy, fatigue, exhaustion,
self-deprecation, eagerness, wretchedness, anxiety, sleep, and awakening, // RUnm_15.17 //
despondency, stupor, madness, delusion, death, and the like are mentioned.

children.text: prauḍhaḥ samañjasaḥ sādhāraṇaś ceti sa tu tridhā // RUnm_15.18 //
children.translated_text: This [<s>pūrva-rāga</s>] is threefold: intense (<s>prauḍha</s>), moderate (<s>samañjasa</s>), and ordinary (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>). // RUnm_15.18 //
Among these, the intense (<s>prauḍha</s>):
That which has the form of <s>samartha-rati</s> (fully capable love) is called intense (<s>prauḍha</s>).

children.text: lālasādir iha prauḍhe maraṇāntā daśā bhavet |
children.translated_text: In the intense type, stages beginning with longing (<s>lālasā</s>) up to death occur;
they take many forms due to the intensity of their respective transitory emotions (<s>sañcāri-bhāvas</s>). // RUnm_15.19 //
Nevertheless, the ancients have summarized its stages as ten;

children.text: proktās tad-anurodhena tāsāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate // RUnm_15.20 //
children.translated_text: in accordance with them, the characteristics of each are now stated. // RUnm_15.20 //
Longing, anxiety, sleeplessness, emaciation, stupor,

children.text: vaiyagryaṃ vyādhir unmādo moho mṛtyur daśā daśa // RUnm_15.21 //
children.translated_text: distraction, illness, madness, delusion, and death — these are the ten stages. // RUnm_15.21 //

body.text: prauḍhatvāt pūrva-rāgasya prauḍhāḥ sarvā daśā api // RUnm_15.22 //
body.translated_text: Because of the intensity of this <s>pūrva-rāga</s>, all the stages are also intense. // RUnm_15.22 //

children.translated_text: Among these, longing (<s>lālasa</s>):
Longing (<s>lālasa</s>) is defined as intense craving with deep avidity to obtain what is desired.
Here, eagerness, restlessness, dizziness, sighing, and the like are present. // RUnm_15.23 //

children.text: tvam avasitān niṣkrāmantī punaḥ praviśanty asau
children.translated_text: 'You go out and come back in again repeatedly;
within a moment you go a hundred times to the boundary of <s>Vraja</s>;
heedless of the great terrors, releasing sigh after sigh —

children.text: kṣipasi bahuśo nīpāraṇye kiśori dṛśor dvayam // RUnm_15.24 //
children.translated_text: why do you cast your pair of eyes so many times into the <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) forest, O young girl?' // RUnm_15.24 //

children.text: dūrād apy anuṣaṅgataḥ śrutim ite tvan-nāma-dheyākṣare
children.translated_text: 'Even from afar, when the syllables of Your name incidentally reach the ear,

children.text: sonmādaṃ madirekṣaṇā viruvatī dhatte muhur vepathum |
children.translated_text: the intoxicated-eyed one cries out madly and repeatedly trembles;

children.text: āḥ kiṃ vā kathanīyam anyad-asite daivād varāmbhodhare
children.translated_text: ah, what more can be said? When by chance a dark and excellent rain-cloud

children.text: dṛṣṭe taṃ parirabdhum utsuka-matiḥ pakṣa-dvayīm icchati // RUnm_15.25 //
children.translated_text: is seen, she, eager-minded to embrace it, desires a pair of wings!' // RUnm_15.25 //
Now, anxiety (<s>udvega</s>):
Anxiety (<s>udvega</s>) is the trembling of the mind; in it, sighing, restlessness,
stupor, worry, tears, pallor, perspiration, and the like are mentioned. // RUnm_15.26 //

children.text: cintā-santatir adya kṛntati sakhi svāntasya kiṃ te dhṛtiṃ
children.translated_text: 'Does the continuous stream of worry today cut away the composure of your heart, O friend?

children.text: kiṃvā siñcati tāmram ambaram ati-svedāmbhasāṃ ḍambaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Or does the flood of profuse perspiration drench your reddened garment?

children.text: kampaś campaka-gauri lumpati vapuḥ-sthairyaṃ kathaṃ vā balāt
children.translated_text: Does trembling, O <s>campaka</s>-golden one, forcibly steal away your bodily steadiness?

children.text: tathyaṃ brūhi na maṅgalā parijane saṅgopanāṅgīkṛtiḥ // RUnm_15.27 //
children.translated_text: Tell the truth — among attendants, O <s>Maṅgalā</s>, concealment is not to be sanctioned!' // RUnm_15.27 //
Loss of sleep is <s>jāgaryā</s> (sleeplessness); it produces stupor, wasting, illness, and the like. // RUnm_15.28 //

children.text: śyāmaṃ kañcana kāñcanojjvala-paṭaṃ sandarśya nidrā kṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having shown me a certain dark youth wearing a garment brilliant as gold, Sleep

children.text: mām ājanma sakhī vimucya calitā ruṣṭeva nāvartate |
children.translated_text: departed, abandoning me, O friend, for the rest of my life, and like one angered, does not return.

children.text: cintāṃ prohya sakhi prapañcaya matiṃ tasyās tvam āvartane
children.translated_text: Cast aside worry, O friend, and devise a plan for her return —

children.text: nānyaḥ svāpnika-taskaropaharaṇe śakto janas tāṃ vinā // RUnm_15.29 //
children.translated_text: for no one else, without her, is capable of recovering that thief of dreams!' // RUnm_15.29 //
Emaciation (<s>tānava</s>) is thinness of the body; it produces weakness, dizziness, and the like. // RUnm_15.30 //
'The collection of bangles having slipped off, and the row of rings, though placed to remedy
the defect of acute emptiness, also falling away easily,

children.text: niśamya muralī-kalaṃ sakhi sakṛd viśākhe tanu-
children.translated_text: O friend, having heard just once the melody of the <s>muralī</s> (flute), O <s>Viśākhā</s>, the body
of yours has wasted to a sliver of moon on the dark fourteenth night.' // RUnm_15.31 //

body.text: kaiścit tu tānava-sthāne vilāpaḥ paripaṭhyate // RUnm_15.32 //
body.translated_text: But some read lamentation (<s>vilāpa</s>) in place of emaciation. // RUnm_15.32 //

children.translated_text: 'Here, at the base of a young <s>nīpa</s> tree, <s>Hari</s> was playing;
here, on the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>], He performed <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance with His friends;

children.text: paśyantī latikāntare kṣaṇam ahaṃ vyagrā nilīya sthitaṃ
children.translated_text: I, hiding for a moment among the creepers, gazing intently, stood —

children.text: sakhyaḥ kiṃ kathayāmi dagdha-vidhinā kṣiptāsmi dāvopari // RUnm_15.33 //
children.translated_text: O friends, what can I say? By cursed fate, I have been cast upon a wildfire!' // RUnm_15.33 //
Now, stupor (<s>jaḍimā</s>):
Where there is no discernment of what is desired or undesired, no response to questions,
no perception through sight or hearing —
that is called <s>jaḍimā</s> (stupor); here, sudden exclamations, rigidity, sighing, bewilderment, and the like occur. // RUnm_15.34 //
'You utter sudden exclamations without cause; you do not hear the words

children.text: kulānāṃ nālāpaṃ dṛtir iva muhur niḥśvasiṣi ca |
children.translated_text: of your dear friends' circles; like a bellows, you repeatedly sigh.',
'Therefore I suspect, O lotus-faced one, that the honey-stream of the flute's melody

children.text: madhulī te pāli śruti-caṣakayoḥ prāghūṇikatām // RUnm_15.35 //
children.translated_text: has arrived as a guest in the cup-like vessels of your ears.' // RUnm_15.35 //
Now, distraction (<s>vaiyāgrya</s>):
<s>Vaiyāgrya</s> (distraction) is described as inability to endure the disturbance of the depth of one's emotion (<s>bhāva</s>).
Here, lack of discrimination, self-deprecation, sorrow, jealousy, and the like are recognized. // RUnm_15.36 //

children.text: pratyāhṛtya muniḥ kṣaṇaṃ viṣayato yasmin mano dhitsate
children.translated_text: 'The mind that the sage, withdrawing it from sense-objects even for a moment, desires to fix —

children.text: bālāsau viṣayeṣu dhitsati tataḥ pratyāharantī manaḥ |
children.translated_text: this girl withdraws that very mind from sense-objects, which then desires to run toward them;

children.text: yasya sphūrti-lavāya hanta hṛdaye yogī sumutkaṇṭhate
children.translated_text: that for a trace of whose manifestation, alas, the yogī yearns intensely in his heart —

children.text: mugdheyaṃ kila tasya paśya hṛdayān niṣkrāntim ākāṅkṣati // RUnm_15.37 //
children.translated_text: this innocent girl, look, longs for Him to come out of her heart!' // RUnm_15.37 //
Now, illness (<s>vyādhi</s>):
Illness (<s>vyādhi</s>) arises from not obtaining what is desired; it is characterized by pallor and fever.
Here, craving for coolness, delusion, sighing, falling down, and the like occur. // RUnm_15.38 //
'O auspicious <s>Bhadrā</s>, hearing that You are a quencher of forest fires,
she, blazing with the wildfire of <s>Madana</s> (Cupid), held You in her heart;
tormented by the agony of doubled burning,
she became pale as if reduced to ashes, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>!' // RUnm_15.39 //
Now, madness (<s>unmāda</s>):
In all states and everywhere, due to the mind being always absorbed in Him,

children.text: atasmiṃs tu tad iti bhrāntir unmāda iti kīrtyate |
children.translated_text: the delusion of perceiving Him where He is not — that is celebrated as <s>unmāda</s> (madness).
Here, attraction and aversion, sighing, blinking, feeling of separation, and the like occur. // RUnm_15.40 //
'Producing with His slender body a beauty among those lustrous as emerald,
a new youth emerged wearing a peacock-crest.',

children.text: bhruvaṃ tena kṣiptvā kim api hasatonmādita-mateḥ
children.translated_text: 'Casting a glance at her and somehow smiling, He drove her mind to madness —

children.text: śaśī vṛtto vahniḥ param ahaha vahnir mama śaśī // RUnm_15.41 //
children.translated_text: the moon has become fire, and alas, fire has become my moon!' // RUnm_15.41 //
Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is defined as confusion of mind; it produces loss of consciousness, falling, and the like. // RUnm_15.42 //
'Her breath turning away from the nose, the eyes of your daughter-in-law becoming unfocused — how?

children.text: hā dhik kṛṣṇa-tilān mamārpaya kare kuryām apāmārjanam |
children.translated_text: Alas, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, place black sesame seeds in my hand so I may perform the rites of purification!',

children.text: ity ārohati karṇayoḥ parisaraṃ kṛṣṇeti karṇa-dvaye
children.translated_text: 'Thus, when "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" [the word for both the Lord and "black"] ascends to the vicinity of her ears,

children.text: kampenācyuta tatra sūtritavatī tvām eva hetuṃ sakhī // RUnm_15.43 //
children.translated_text: with a tremor, O <s>Acyuta</s>, the friend there concluded that You alone were the cause.' // RUnm_15.43 //
Now, death (<s>mṛtyu</s>):

children.text: tais taiḥ kṛtaiḥ pratīkārair yadi na syāt samāgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: If, despite all remedies attempted, union does not come about,
then, from the ravage of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Cupid's) arrows, there arises an impulse toward death. // RUnm_15.44 //
Therein, the surrendering of one's dear possessions to friends,
and experiences of bees, gentle breezes, moonlight, <s>kadamba</s> trees, and the like occur. // RUnm_15.45 //

children.text: rādhā rodhasi ropitāṃ mukulinīm āliṅgya mal-līlatāṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s>, embracing the <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) creeper planted on the riverbank as "my <s>Līlā</s>-vine,"
entrusting the jeweled necklace of excellent beauty into the hand of <s>Lalitā</s>,

children.text: mūrcchām āpnuvatī praviśya madhupair gītāṃ kadambāṭavīṃ
children.translated_text: falling into a swoon upon entering the <s>kadamba</s> grove hummed about by bees,

children.text: nāma vyāharatā hareḥ priya-sakhī-vṛndena sandhukṣitā // RUnm_15.46 //
children.translated_text: was revived by the host of dear friends uttering the name of <s>Hari</s>.' // RUnm_15.46 //

children.text: akāruṇyaḥ kṛṣṇo yadi mayi tavāgaḥ katham idaṃ
children.translated_text: 'If <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is merciless — how is that your fault, O friend?

children.text: mudhā mā rodīr me kuru param imām uttara-kṛtim |
children.translated_text: Do not weep in vain; rather, grant me this supreme final favor:',
'that this body, with arms entwined like creepers upon the trunk of a <s>tamāla</s> tree,

children.text: yathā vṛndāraṇye ciram avicalā tiṣṭhati tanuḥ // RUnm_15.47 //
children.translated_text: may remain unmoved for a long time in the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>).' // RUnm_15.47 //
That which has the form of <s>samañjasa-rati</s> (moderate love) is this moderate type. // RUnm_15.48 //
Here [the stages are]: desire, anxiety, remembrance, praise of qualities, agitation,

children.text: savilāpā unmāda-vyādhi-jaḍatā mṛtiś ca tāḥ kramaśaḥ // RUnm_15.49 //
children.translated_text: lamentation accompanied by madness, illness, stupor, and death — these in order. // RUnm_15.49 //
Among these, desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>):
Desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>) is the resolve born from the longing for union with the beloved.
It produces self-adornment, drawing near, manifestation of attachment, and the like. // RUnm_15.50 //

children.text: yad iha sakhi subhadrā-sakhyam ākhyāya dhūrte
children.translated_text: 'In that you declare to the cunning one your friendship with <s>Subhadrā</s> here, O friend,
and go from your father's house to the palace of <s>Devakī</s>,

children.text: racayasi bata satye maṇḍane ca prayatnaṃ
children.translated_text: and indeed make earnest effort at self-adornment —

children.text: sphuṭam ajani tad antar vastu gūḍhaṃ tavādya // RUnm_15.51 //
children.translated_text: clearly, that hidden inner reality of yours has now become manifest today.' // RUnm_15.51 //
Now, anxiety (<s>cintā</s>):
Meditation on the means of obtaining what is desired is declared to be anxiety (<s>cintā</s>).
It produces tossing on the bed, sighing, vacant gazing, and the like. // RUnm_15.52 //
'Your sighing, O lotus-faced one, withers the <s>bimba</s>-fruit of your lip;
your emaciated body-staff tosses about upon the bed;

children.text: dvandvaṃ cākṣṇor vikirati ciraṃ rukmiṇi śyāma ambho
children.translated_text: and the pair of your eyes, O <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, scatters dark water for a long time —

children.text: na śvo-bhāviny upayama-vidhau śobhate vikriyeyam // RUnm_15.53 //
children.translated_text: this transformation does not befit the wedding ceremony that is to take place tomorrow.' // RUnm_15.53 //
Now, remembrance (<s>smṛti</s>):
Remembrance (<s>smṛti</s>) is the recollection of previously experienced beloved things and the like.
Here, trembling, loss of bodily control, tears, sighing, and the like occur. // RUnm_15.54 //
'The pair of lotus-eyes is flooded all around with streams of water;
the pair of <s>cakravāka</s>-bird-like breasts, O daughter of <s>Satrājit</s>, bears sustained trembling;

children.text: ślathārambhaṃ caitad bhuja-visala-yugaṃ tat tava mana-
children.translated_text: and this broad pair of arms has become slack in its embrace — that is because in the lake of your mind,
the elephant-king named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is sporting within.' // RUnm_15.55 //
Now, the praise of qualities (<s>guṇa-kīrtana</s>):
The extolling of qualities such as beauty and the like is called praise of qualities (<s>guṇa-kīrtana</s>).
Here, trembling, horripilation, choking of the voice, and the like occur. // RUnm_15.56 //

children.text: yāntyas tṛṣṇāpi yuvatayo yeṣu ghūrṇāṃ bhajante
children.translated_text: 'Those honeys of Your beauty's wealth, O Lord of bees (<s>Madhupati</s>), toward which

children.text: yāny ācamya svayam api bhavān romaharṣaṃ prayāti |
children.translated_text: even women going past are seized by dizzying thirst,
and tasting which even You Yourself experience horripilation —

children.text: dūre vindan mama na hi dhṛtiḥ citta-bhṛṅgas tanoti // RUnm_15.57 //
children.translated_text: finding their fragrance even from afar, the bee of my mind cannot maintain composure.' // RUnm_15.57 //
The six stages from anxiety onward were previously illustrated in the intense type;

children.text: sāmañjasyād rater atra kintu tāḥ syur yathocitam // RUnm_15.58 //
children.translated_text: but here, due to the moderate nature of the love, they occur as is fitting. // RUnm_15.58 //
Now, the ordinary (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>):
That which mostly has the form of <s>sādhāraṇa-rati</s> (ordinary love) is called ordinary (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>).

children.text: atra proktā vilāpāntāḥ ṣaḍ-daśāntāś ca komalāḥ // RUnm_15.59 //
children.translated_text: Here, the stages up to lamentation, and the six stages [from anxiety onward], are described as gentle. // RUnm_15.59 //
'These women truly embody supreme womanhood, having cast aside coquetry,
having abandoned propriety — alas, they do well!
They whose husband is the lotus-eyed Lord,

children.text: na jātv apaity āhṛtibhir hṛdi spṛśan // RUnm_15.60 //
children.translated_text: who never departs from their hearts, touching them with His allurements.' // RUnm_15.60 //

body.translated_text: Now desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>), as in the First Canto (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 1.10.30) —

body.text: cintādīnāṃ tathānyāsām ūhyā dhīrair udāhṛtiḥ // RUnm_15.61 //
body.translated_text: The illustrations of anxiety and the other stages should be inferred by the wise. // RUnm_15.61 //

children.translated_text: In <s>pūrva-rāga</s>, love-letters, garlands, and the like may be sent
here through friends and others, by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as well as by His beloved. // RUnm_15.62 //
Among these, the love-letter (<s>kāma-lekha</s>):

children.text: sa lekhaḥ kāma-lekhaḥ syāt yaḥ sva-prema-prakāśakaḥ |
children.translated_text: That letter which reveals one's own love is called a love-letter (<s>kāma-lekha</s>).

children.text: yuvatyā yūni yūnā ca yuvatyāṃ saṃprahīyate // RUnm_15.63 //
children.translated_text: It is sent by a young woman to a young man, and by a young man to a young woman. // RUnm_15.63 //

body.text: nirakṣaraḥ sākṣaraś ca kāma-lekho dvidhā bhavet // RUnm_15.64 //
body.translated_text: The love-letter is of two kinds: without letters (<s>nirakṣara</s>) and with letters (<s>sākṣara</s>). // RUnm_15.64 //

children.translated_text: Among these, the one without letters (<s>nirakṣara</s>):
Made of deeply colored shoots, bearing crescent-moon and other nail-marks,
and devoid of the arrangement of written characters — such is the letterless [love-letter]. // RUnm_15.65 //
on the tip of the sprout-leaf of <s>Viśākhikā</s>,
this half-moon scratched by the tip of a nail,
bearing the nature of a half-moon of <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god),

children.text: hṛdi mama hanta kathaṃ haṭhād viveśa // RUnm_15.66 //
children.translated_text: has forcibly entered my heart — alas, how? // RUnm_15.66 //

children.text: gāthāmayī lipir yatra svahastāṅkaiṣa sākṣaraḥ // RUnm_15.67 //
children.translated_text: Where there is a message in verse-form, inscribed in one's own handwriting — that is <s>sākṣara</s>. // RUnm_15.67 //
As in the <s>Jagannāthavallabha</s> —

children.text: suiraṃ vijjhasi hiaaṃ lambha-i maaṇo kkhu dujjasaḥ baliaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'For long you pierce [my] heart; <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god) certainly obtains strong ill-repute;

children.text: dīsasi saaladisāsuṃ dīsa-i maaṇo ṇa kuttābi // RUnm_15.68 //
children.translated_text: you are seen in all directions, [yet] <s>Madana</s> is seen nowhere.' // RUnm_15.68 //

children.text: (suciraṃ bidhyasi hṛdayaṃ labhate madanaḥ khalu duryaśo balīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: (You pierce my heart for so long; the Love-god certainly obtains overwhelming notoriety;

children.text: dṛśyase sakala-diśāsu dṛśyate madano na kutrāpi //)
children.translated_text: You are seen in all directions, yet Madana is seen nowhere.)
The binding is with lotus-fiber thread; the ink is musk (<s>kastūrikā</s>);

children.text: pṛthu-puṣpa-dalaṃ patraḥ mudrā-kṛt kuṅkumair iha // RUnm_15.69 //
children.translated_text: a broad flower-petal is the leaf; the seal is [made] with saffron. // RUnm_15.69 //
'Well-knit, displaying the fullness of her own artisanal skill, wondrous —

children.text: goṣṭhādhīśvara-nandanaṃ srajam imāṃ tubhyaṃ sakhi prāhiṇot |
children.translated_text: O friend, the son of the Lord of the pastures has sent you this garland!'
Upon hearing these words, from the lotus-eyed one, splashing with drops of perspiration,

children.text: daṅgebhyaḥ kula-dharma-dhairyam abhitaḥ śaṅke bahir niryayau // RUnm_15.70 //
children.translated_text: the family-honor, dharma, and fortitude, I suspect, departed outwardly from all her limbs. // RUnm_15.70 //

body.translated_text: Now the offering of a garland (<s>mālyārpaṇa</s>) —

children.translated_text: Some, however, [state] —
Delight of the eyes is first, then mental attachment, then resolve,
loss of sleep, emaciation, turning away from [worldly] objects, loss of shame,

children.text: unmādo mūrcchā mṛtir ity etāḥ smara-daśā daśaiva syuḥ // RUnm_15.71 //
children.translated_text: madness, fainting, and death — these are the ten stages of <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god). // RUnm_15.71 //

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa vijñeyaḥ pūrva-rāgo harer api |
children.translated_text: In this manner, <s>pūrvarāga</s> (pre-union love) of <s>Hari</s> too should be understood progressively;
as an illustration thereof, one example is given: // RUnm_15.72 //
'He let go of His flute, with the impetuous delight of its melodious fragrance;
He forgot the elaborate flower-ornament arrangements;
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> abandoned His thirst for the charming activities of His companion-host —
O friend, [He whose] fluttering mind-wind has been sipped by the serpent-creeper of Your eyebrows!' // RUnm_15.73 //

children.text: dampatyor bhāva ekatra sator apy anuraktayoḥ |
children.translated_text: When the emotion of a couple, though both are present and mutually enamored,
obstructs the desired embrace, glance, and so forth — that is called <s>māna</s>. // RUnm_15.74 //
The <s>sañcāri</s> (transitory) emotions here include <s>nirveda</s> (self-deprecation), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), accompanied by restlessness,

children.text: garvāsūyāvahitthāś ca glāniś cintādayo'py amī // RUnm_15.75 //
children.translated_text: <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), and <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), and others. // RUnm_15.75 //

children.text: ahetor neti nety uker hetor yan māna ucyate |
children.translated_text: That which [arises] without cause is expressed through 'no, no' utterances; that from a cause is called <s>māna</s>;

children.text: asya praṇaya eva syān mānasya padam uttamam // RUnm_15.76 //
children.translated_text: <s>praṇaya</s> (deep affection) itself is the supreme ground of this <s>māna</s>. // RUnm_15.76 //
Among these, the one with cause (<s>sa-hetu</s>) —
The cause is the special preference shown by the beloved to the rival's faction and others, by jealousy;
this emotion, principally <s>praṇaya</s>, attains the state of jealous-<s>māna</s>. // RUnm_15.77 //
And thus it is stated (in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s> 2.53) —

children.text: snehaṃ vinā bhayaṃ na syān nerṣyā ca praṇayaṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: 'Without love (<s>sneha</s>) there would be no fear, and without <s>praṇaya</s> there would be no jealousy;
therefore this variety of <s>māna</s> is a revealer of the <s>prema</s> of both.' // RUnm_15.78 //
Hence in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> (2.66.4, 2.65.50) —

children.text: ruṣitām iva tāṃ devīṃ snehāt saṅkalpayann iva |
children.translated_text: 'Imagining her, the goddess, as if angered, out of love,
the son of the <s>Yadu</s> [clan] entered very softly, as if timid and afraid.' // RUnm_15.79 //
'Endowed with beauty and youth, proud of her own good fortune,
the self-respecting goddess, upon hearing [of the rival], fell under the sway of jealousy.' // RUnm_15.80 //

children.text: tatrāpi ca susakhyādi hṛdi yasyā virājate |
children.translated_text: Moreover, she in whose heart <s>susakhya</s> (excellent companionship) and the like shine —

children.text: tasyā vipakṣa-vaiśiṣṭye na syād eva sahiṣṇutā // RUnm_15.81 //
children.translated_text: for her, there can be no tolerance toward the excellence of the rival faction. // RUnm_15.81 //
Therefore, for <s>Satyā</s> [<s>Satyabhāmā</s>], since <s>susakhya</s> and the like were absent in the others,

children.text: śrute'pi pārijātasya dāne māno na cābhavat // RUnm_15.82 //
children.translated_text: even upon hearing of the gift of the <s>Pārijāta</s> [tree], <s>māna</s> did not arise [in them]. // RUnm_15.82 //

body.text: śrutaṃ cānumitaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tad-vaiśiṣṭyaṃ tridhā matam // RUnm_15.83 //
body.translated_text: The excellence of the rival is considered threefold: heard, inferred, and seen. // RUnm_15.83 //

children.text: śravaṇaṃ tu priya-sakhī-śukādīnāṃ mukhād bhavet // RUnm_15.84 //
children.translated_text: Hearing occurs from the mouths of dear friends, parrots, and the like. // RUnm_15.84 //
'O moon-faced one, having heard false chatter from the mouth of a harsh friend,

children.text: praṇayini harau mā viśrambhaṃ kṛthāḥ śithilaṃ vṛthā |
children.translated_text: do not vainly loosen your trust in the affectionate <s>Hari</s>!',
'Abandon the weariness of your mind, O goddess, be gracious, O enchanting one!

children.text: tava mukham anālocya preyān vane'dya viśīryati // RUnm_15.85 //
children.translated_text: Without beholding your face, your beloved withers in the forest today!' // RUnm_15.85 //

body.translated_text: Among these, from the mouth of a friend, for example —

children.text: ahaha gahanā keyaṃ vārtā śrutau patitādya me
children.translated_text: 'Alas, what profound news has fallen upon my ears today!

children.text: viditam anṛtaṃ hāsyād brūṣe vimuñca kadarthanām |
children.translated_text: It is known to be untrue — you say it in jest; abandon [this] vexation!',

children.text: sahacari kuto jīvaty asmin jane'pi janārdano
children.translated_text: 'O companion, how can <s>Janārdana</s> live if even this person [perishes]?

children.text: dyutaru kusumaṃ tasyai hā dhik kṛtī vitariṣyati // RUnm_15.86 //
children.translated_text: Alas, shame! The skillful one will give a flower of the wishing-tree to that one!' // RUnm_15.86 //

children.text: āste kācid dayita-kalahā krūra-cetāḥ sakhī te
children.translated_text: 'Some cruel-hearted friend of yours who quarrels with her beloved

children.text: kīro vanyaḥ sphuṭam iha yayā śyāmale pāṭhito'sti |
children.translated_text: has clearly taught this wild parrot here, O dark one!',
'So do not trust the vain prattle of a bird,

children.text: mānārambhe na kuru hṛdayaṃ kātaro'smi prasīda // RUnm_15.87 //
children.translated_text: do not begin <s>māna</s> — make your heart [soft] — I am anxious — be gracious!' // RUnm_15.87 //

body.translated_text: From the mouth of a parrot (<s>śuka</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: Inference is threefold: through love-marks (<s>bhogāṅka</s>), slips of name (<s>gotra-skhalana</s>), and dreams (<s>svapna</s>). // RUnm_15.88 //

children.text: bhogāṅko dṛśyate gātre vipakṣasya priyasya ca // RUnm_15.89 //
children.translated_text: Love-marks are seen on the body of the rival and of the beloved. // RUnm_15.89 //
'O rogue of the <s>Kālindī</s> bank, enough of your flattery! Let <s>Candrāvalī</s> sleep!

children.text: khinnākṣī kṣaṇa-maṅganād apasara kruddhāsti vṛddhā gṛhe |
children.translated_text: She has weary eyes from momentary dalliance — go away! The angry elder is at home!'
'Yet now, by the slightly reflected pattern of cosmetic-leaf fish-designs on her [forehead],

children.text: sarvā te lalitā lalāṭa-phalakenodghāṭitā cāturī // RUnm_15.90 //
children.translated_text: all your cleverness, O <s>Lalitā</s>, has been exposed by the tablet of [her] forehead!' // RUnm_15.90 //

body.translated_text: Among these, seeing love-marks on the body of the rival, for example —

children.translated_text: 'Without blinking, gazing constantly at my path,
I know that the redness of your eyes is caused by fallen pollen from <s>keśara</s> flowers;'

children.text: śītaiḥ kānana-vāyubhir viracito bimbādhare ca vraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: 'and the wound on your <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip was made by the cool forest breezes.',

children.text: saṅkocaṃ tyaja deva daiva-hatayā na tvaṃ mayā dūṣyase // RUnm_15.91 //
children.translated_text: 'Abandon your apprehension, O Lord — struck by fate, I do not blame you.' // RUnm_15.91 //

body.translated_text: Seeing love-marks on the beloved's body, as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (4.40) —

children.translated_text: Among these, slipping of the name (<s>gotra-skhalana</s>) —
Calling [the beloved] by the name of the rival is the cause of excessive jealousy;

children.text: āsāṃ tu gotra-skhalanaṃ duḥkhadaṃ maraṇād api // RUnm_15.92 //
children.translated_text: for these [heroines], the slipping of the name is more painful than death. // RUnm_15.92 //
'Coming from <s>Rādhā</s>'s enchanting temple, he addressed <s>Candrāvalī</s>:

children.text: rādhe kṣemam iheti tasya vacanaṃ śrutvāha candrāvalī |
children.translated_text: "<s>Rādhe</s>, is all well here?" Hearing his words, <s>Candrāvalī</s> said:',

children.text: kaṃsa kṣemam aye vimugdha-hṛdaye kaṃsaḥ kva dṛṣṭas tvayā
children.translated_text: '"<s>Kaṃsa</s> is well!" "Oh, bewildered-hearted one, where did you see <s>Kaṃsa</s>?"

children.text: rādhā kveti vilajjito nata-mukhaḥ smero hariḥ pātu vaḥ // RUnm_15.93 //
children.translated_text: '"Where is <s>Rādhā</s>?" — Embarrassed, face downcast, smiling — may <s>Hari</s> protect you!' // RUnm_15.93 //
'Alas, the radiant <s>Candrāvalī</s> shines before [you]!

children.text: kitava kalitā tārā sātra tvayā kva nu ṣoḍaśī |
children.translated_text: O rogue, the star (<s>Tārā</s>) [has been] seized by you — but where is the sixteenth [digit of the moon]?',
'O you of darkness-dark form, go quickly before the dawn-circle [appears],

children.text: mama sahacarī yāvan-manyu-dyutiṃ na vimuñcati // RUnm_15.94 //
children.translated_text: while my companion does not yet release the radiance of her anger!' // RUnm_15.94 //

children.text: harer vidūṣakasyāpi svapnaḥ svapnāyitaṃ mataḥ // RUnm_15.95 //
children.translated_text: The dreams of <s>Hari</s> or of [His] jester (<s>vidūṣaka</s>) are considered dream-[evidence]. // RUnm_15.95 //

children.text: śape tubhyaṃ rādhe tvam asi hṛdaye tvaṃ mama bahi-
children.translated_text: 'I swear to you, <s>Rādhe</s> — you are in my heart, you are before me,

children.text: stvam agre tvaṃ pṛṣṭhe tvam iha bhavane tvaṃ girivane |
children.translated_text: you are behind me, you are here in the house, you are in the mountain-forest!'

children.text: iti svapne jalpaṃ niśi niśamayantī madhuripo-
children.translated_text: Hearing [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] babble thus in a dream at night, the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>'s

children.text: rabhūt talpe candrāvalir atha parāvartita-mukhī // RUnm_15.96 //
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s> then turned her face away on the bed. // RUnm_15.96 //
'The friend of <s>Padmā</s> was not deceived by the clever flattery of the slayer of <s>Agha</s> today!

children.text: tatas tvaraya rādhikāṃ kim iti mādhavi dhyāyasi |
children.translated_text: So hurry <s>Rādhikā</s>! Why do you hesitate, O <s>Mādhavī</s>?'

children.text: niśamya madhumaṅgalād iti giraṃ puraḥ svapnajāṃ
children.translated_text: Hearing from <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> this dream-born speech before her,

children.text: vidūna-vadanā sakhi jvalati paśya candrāvalī // RUnm_15.97 //
children.translated_text: O friend, look — <s>Candrāvalī</s>, face shaken, burns [with jealousy]! // RUnm_15.97 //

children.text: mithyā mā vada kandare sama sakhīṃ hitvā tvam ekākinīṃ
children.translated_text: 'Do not speak falsely in the bower! Having left that friend of yours alone,

children.text: niṣkrāntaḥ pṛthu-sambhrameṇa kim api prakhyāpayan kaitavam |
children.translated_text: you emerged with great agitation, revealing some kind of deception!',
'From afar, by the faint sound of your girdle-bells, by the frightened one,

children.text: niṣkramyātha tayā śaṭhendra puline dṛṣṭo'si rādhā-sakhaḥ // RUnm_15.98 //
children.translated_text: coming out, O king of rogues, you were seen on the sandbank — <s>Rādhā</s>'s companion!' // RUnm_15.98 //
'O companion, the <s>guñjā</s>-berry garland that was strung by me this very morning
and placed with longing upon the neck of the son of the Lord of <s>Vraja</s> today —'

children.text: api hṛdi lalitāyās tasthuṣī hanta hṛn me
children.translated_text: 'resting upon the heart of <s>Lalitā</s> — alas, my heart!

children.text: dahati dahana-dīptiḥ paśya guñjāvalī sā // RUnm_15.99 //
children.translated_text: That <s>guñjā</s> garland, look, burns like a flame of fire!' // RUnm_15.99 //
Now the causeless (<s>nirhetu</s>) [māna] —
Without any reason, or from a mere semblance of reason for both,

children.text: prodyan praṇaya evāyaṃ vrajen nirhetu-mānatām // RUnm_15.100 //
children.translated_text: the surging <s>praṇaya</s> itself proceeds to the state of causeless <s>māna</s>. // RUnm_15.100 //

children.text: ādyaṃ mānaṃ parīṇāmaṃ praṇayasya jagur budhāḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise declare the first <s>māna</s> to be a transformation of <s>praṇaya</s>;
the second, again, is the splendor of the abundance of <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry) of this very [<s>praṇaya</s>];

children.text: budhaiḥ praṇayamānākhyaṃ eṣa eva prakīrtitaḥ // RUnm_15.101 //
children.translated_text: this is celebrated by the wise as <s>praṇayamāna</s> (affection-born indignation). // RUnm_15.101 //
And thus it is stated (in the <s>Sarasvatīkaṇṭhābharaṇa</s> 5.48) —

children.text: aher iva gatiḥ premṇaḥ svabhāva-kuṭilā bhavet |
children.translated_text: 'The course of love is by nature crooked, like a serpent's;

children.text: ato hetor ahetoś ca yūnor māna udañcati // RUnm_15.102 //
children.translated_text: therefore <s>māna</s> arises in the young couple both from a cause and without one.' // RUnm_15.102 //

body.text: avahitthādayo hy atra vijñeyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ // RUnm_15.103 //
body.translated_text: <s>Avahitthā</s> (dissimulation) and others are to be understood here as transitory emotions. // RUnm_15.103 //

children.text: avyakta-smita-dṛṣṭim arpaya puraḥ svalpo'pi mantur na me
children.translated_text: 'Cast an imperceptibly smiling glance before you — not even a slight trace of anger do I have;
half the moonlit night has passed due to the deceptive skill of your husband, O [daughter of] the Lord of <s>Vraja</s>!',

children.text: śubhrālaṅkṛtibhir drutaṃ pathi mayā dūraṃ tataḥ prasthite
children.translated_text: 'When I quickly departed far on the path, with bright ornaments,

children.text: sāndrā cāndram arundha bimbam acirād ākasmikī kālikā // RUnm_15.104 //
children.translated_text: a sudden darkness soon swallowed the moon-disc.' // RUnm_15.104 //

children.text: puṣpebhyaḥ spṛhayā vilambitavatīm ālokya mām unmanāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Seeing me lingering out of desire for flowers, the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,

children.text: kaṃsāriḥ sakhi lambitānana-śaśī tūṣṇīṃ nikuñje sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: O friend, with downcast moon-face, stood silently in the bower.',
'When, in anxiety, I cast a handful of flowers at the tip of His foot,

children.text: tasyālīka-ruṣā bhruvaṃ vibhujato'py āvirbabhūva smitam // RUnm_15.105 //
children.translated_text: a smile appeared on Him even as He bent His brow in feigned anger.' // RUnm_15.105 //
'Standing in the courtyard of the pastures, repeatedly casting sidelong glances,
<s>Hari</s>, O friend, stands longing on the threshold-platform!',
'Swallowed by the surge of false <s>māna</s>, why, with eyes fixed on the lattice window,

children.text: svāntam hanta glapayasi bahiḥ prīṇaya prāṇanātham // RUnm_15.106 //
children.translated_text: do you, alas, wither your inner self? Go out and delight the lord of your life!' // RUnm_15.106 //
'I am here gathering flowers at your very word!

children.text: kathaya katham akāṇḍe caṇḍi vācaṃ yamāsi |
children.translated_text: Tell me, why do you suddenly restrain your speech, O wrathful one?',
'It is known — the lotus-stalk is [but] a pretext, O <s>Rādhike</s>! Tell me: with which
dear friend's flower shall I adorn your ear?' // RUnm_15.107 //

children.text: kuñje tuṣṇīm asi nata-śirāḥ kiṃ cirāt tvaṃ murāre
children.translated_text: 'In the bower, You are silent with bowed head — why so long, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>?

children.text: kiṃ vā śyāme tvam api vimukhī mauna-mudrāṃ tanoṣi |
children.translated_text: And why, O dark one, are you too turned away, maintaining the seal of silence?',

children.text: jñātaṃ jñātaṃ smita-vimuṣite kāpi vāmāsti yogyā
children.translated_text: 'Understood, understood! You whose smiles are stolen — some suitable, perverse one exists

children.text: krīḍā-vāde balavati yayā na dvayor eva bhaṅgaḥ // RUnm_15.108 //
children.translated_text: for the contest of play, by whom there is no defeat for either of you!' // RUnm_15.108 //

children.text: kuñja-dvāri niviṣṭayos taraṇijā-tīre dvayor eva nau
children.translated_text: 'At the door of the bower, we two alone were seated on the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>],

children.text: tatrānyonyam apaśyatoḥ sakhi mudhā nirbandhataḥ klāntayoḥ |
children.translated_text: not seeing each other, O friend, wearied by vain obstinacy.',

children.text: haste drāg atha dāḍimī-phalam abhinyaste mayā nistalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'When I swiftly placed a pomegranate fruit in her palm, soundlessly,

children.text: rādhām udbhidura-smitāṃ parihasan phullāṅgam āliṅgiṣam // RUnm_15.109 //
children.translated_text: I embraced <s>Rādhā</s>, whose smile was bursting forth, laughing, with blossoming body.' // RUnm_15.109 //

body.translated_text: The causeless [<s>māna</s>] subsides by itself, through a spontaneous smile and [similar] means. // RUnm_15.110 //

children.translated_text: 'If your anger was so great, O <s>Rādhike</s>,
then why does this cheek heave [with suppressed laughter]?'
With this jest of His, the son of the Lord of cowherds
kissed the beloved whose smile was impossible to conceal. // RUnm_15.111 //

children.text: hetur yas tu śamaṃ yathāyogyaṃ prakalpitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>māna</s> that has a cause is pacified as appropriate by the following means:

<s>sāma</s> (conciliation), <s>bheda</s> (stratagem), <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>dāna</s> (gift), <s>nati</s> (prostration), <s>upekṣā</s> (indifference), and <s>rasāntara</s> (change of rasa). // RUnm_15.112 //

body.translated_text: The signs of the pacification of <s>māna</s> are shedding of tears, smiling, and the like. // RUnm_15.113 //

children.text: priya-vākyasya racanaṃ yat tu tat sāma gīyate // RUnm_15.114 //
children.translated_text: The composition of endearing words is what is called <s>sāma</s>. // RUnm_15.114 //

children.text: jātaṃ sundari tathaym eva pṛthunā rādhe'parādhena me
children.translated_text: 'It has happened, O beautiful one, through this very great offense of mine, O <s>Rādhe</s> —'

children.text: kintu svārasiko mamātra śaraṇaṃ snehas tvadīyo balī |
children.translated_text: 'But my natural, powerful affection for you is my refuge here!'

children.text: ity ākarṇya giraṃ harer natamukhī bāṣpāmbhasāṃ dhārayā
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of <s>Hari</s>, with downcast face, with a stream of tears,
she filled her breasts — like auspicious water-pots at the festive arena of the celebration of love. // RUnm_15.115 //
Now <s>bheda</s> (breaking [the pride]) —
<s>Bheda</s> is said to be twofold: the display of one's own greatness through indirect means,
and the employment of reproach by friends and others. // RUnm_15.116 //
'Your eyes have darting fish, your breasts are pulled up like a tortoise,
this lip of yours, endowed with a resplendent <s>kroñca</s> bird, nourishes delight;'

children.text: madhyo'sau bali-bandhano mukha-rucā rāmās tvayā nirjitā
children.translated_text: 'your waist is bound like <s>Bali</s> [by <s>Vāmana</s>], by the radiance of your face the <s>Rāmās</s> (beautiful women) are conquered —

children.text: labdhā śrī-ghanatādya mānini manasy aṅgīkṛtā kalkitā // RUnm_15.117 //
children.translated_text: today the majesty of <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune) has been attained, O proud one — accept it in your heart, O cunning one!' // RUnm_15.117 //

body.translated_text: There, the display of one's own greatness by indirect means, as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (4.41) —

children.translated_text: Or, since this is a loving speech, this could be an example [preceded] by delight;

children.text: nāyakasya sva-vacasā bhaṅgyāyaṃ bheda īryate // RUnm_15.118 //
children.translated_text: this <s>bheda</s> through the hero's own words is called [bheda] by indirect means. // RUnm_15.118 //

children.text: rūkṣā yan mayi vartase tvam abhitaḥ snigdhe'pi te dūṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 'That you behave harshly toward me, though I am wholly affectionate — the fault

children.text: tatrāste na hi kintu tat kila mamānaucitya-jātaṃ phalam |
children.translated_text: does not lie in that; rather, it is the fruit of my own impropriety,'

children.text: yena svastaruṇīr upekṣya caramām apy āśrayantīr daśāṃ
children.translated_text: 'by which, having neglected my own women who have reached even the last extremity,

children.text: premārtaṃ vraja-yauvataṃ ca sumukhi tvaṃ kevalaṃ sevyase // RUnm_15.119 //
children.translated_text: O fair-faced one, I serve you alone, love-stricken, along with the youth of <s>Vraja</s>.' // RUnm_15.119 //
'O beautiful one, you should not be neglected by this [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] in the slaying of <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>,
[you whose] beloved is bound by the vow of granting fearlessness to all;'

children.text: ity ālībhir alakṣitaṃ murabhidā bhadrāvalī bheditā
children.translated_text: 'thus unnoticed [reproach being conveyed] by her friends, <s>Bhadrāvalī</s>, her pride broken by the enemy of <s>Mura</s>,

children.text: nāsāgre vara-mauktika-śriyam adhād asrasya sā bindunā // RUnm_15.120 //
children.translated_text: placed upon the tip of her nose the beauty of a fine pearl — [formed] by a drop of her tears.' // RUnm_15.120 //

body.translated_text: The employment of reproach by friends and others, for example —

children.text: vyājena bhūṣaṇādīnāṃ pradānaṃ dānam ucyate // RUnm_15.121 //
children.translated_text: The giving of ornaments and the like under a pretext is called <s>dāna</s>. // RUnm_15.121 //

children.text: kāmo nāma suhṛn mamāsti bhavatīm ākarṇya mat-preyasīṃ
children.translated_text: 'I have a friend named <s>Kāma</s> (Cupid); hearing that you are my beloved,

children.text: hāras tena tavārpito'yam urasi prāpnotu saṅgotsavam |
children.translated_text: this necklace has been sent by him — may it attain the festival of union upon your breast!'

children.text: ity unnamya karaṃ muradviṣi vadaty udbhinna-sāndra-smitā
children.translated_text: 'Thus, with hand raised, as the enemy of <s>Mura</s> spoke, <s>Padmā</s>, her broad smile bursting forth,

children.text: padmā māna-vinigrahāt praṇayinā tenodbhaṭaṃ cumbitā // RUnm_15.122 //
children.translated_text: was boldly kissed by that affectionate one as her pride was subdued.' // RUnm_15.122 //

children.text: kevalaṃ dainyam ālambya pādapāto natir matā // RUnm_15.123 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nati</s> is considered to be falling at [her] feet, resorting solely to humility. // RUnm_15.123 //
'When <s>Mukunda</s>, his peacock-feather crest touching the ground, from afar
performs a prostration — beautiful with masses of lovingly devoted ones —'
'making a rain of tears from her two cloud-like eyes,
the beautiful-bodied one proclaimed the destruction of the summer of pride.' // RUnm_15.124 //
Now <s>upekṣā</s> (disregard) —
When the [methods of] conciliation and the like are exhausted, <s>upekṣā</s> would be neglect;

children.text: upekṣā kathyate kaiścit tūṣṇīmbhāvatayā sthitiḥ // RUnm_15.125 //
children.translated_text: some call <s>upekṣā</s> the state of remaining silent. // RUnm_15.125 //

children.text: sūnur vallabha eṣa vallavapates tatrāpi vīrāgraṇī-
children.translated_text: 'This is the son of the lord of the cowherds, moreover the foremost among heroes,
moreover adorned with a form victorious over the entire host of Cupid —'

children.text: sakhyaḥ samprati rūkṣatā pṛthur iyaṃ tenātra na śreyase
children.translated_text: 'O friends, now this great harshness by him is not for [our] benefit;

children.text: dūre paśyata yāti niṣṭhura-manāḥ kā yuktir atrocitā // RUnm_15.126 //
children.translated_text: see — he departs in the distance, hard-hearted! What remedy is appropriate here?' // RUnm_15.126 //
'When her jealous pride could not be quelled even by repeated strategies,
I swiftly adopted the vow of silence;'
'thereupon <s>Padmā</s>, scattering tears, declared:

children.text: pauṣpaṃ rajaḥ patitam atra dṛśor mameti // RUnm_15.127 //
children.translated_text: "It is flower-pollen that has fallen here upon my eyes!"' // RUnm_15.127 //
Alternatively —
Abandoning the method of appeasement and using words suggestive of other meanings

children.text: prasādanaṃ mṛgākṣīṇām upekṣeti smṛtā budhaiḥ // RUnm_15.128 //
children.translated_text: as a means of winning over the doe-eyed ones — the wise remember this as <s>upekṣā</s>. // RUnm_15.128 //

children.text: dhammille nava-mālatī paricitā savye ca śabda-grahe
children.translated_text: 'The familiar fresh <s>mālatī</s> is in your topknot, and in the left [ear] a <s>śabdagraha</s> [echo-catcher flower];

children.text: mallī sundari dakṣiṇe tu katarat puṣpaṃ tava bhrājate |
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, in the right [ear] — which flower shines?'

children.text: āghreyaṃ paricetum ity upahite vyājena nāsā-puṭe
children.translated_text: '"Let me smell it to identify it" — thus, placing his pretext upon [her] nostril-wing,

children.text: gaṇḍodyat-pulakā vihasya hariṇā candrāvalī cumbitā // RUnm_15.129 //
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s>, with horripilation rising on her cheeks, was kissed by <s>Hari</s> with a laugh.' // RUnm_15.129 //
Now <s>rasāntara</s> (introduction of another rasa) —
The introduction of sudden fear and the like is <s>rasāntara</s>;

children.text: yādṛcchikaṃ buddhi-pūrvam iti dvedhā tad ucyate // RUnm_15.130 //
children.translated_text: it is said to be twofold — accidental (<s>yādṛcchika</s>) and deliberate (<s>buddhi-pūrva</s>). // RUnm_15.130 //

children.text: upasthitam akasmād yat tad yādṛcchikam ucyate // RUnm_15.131 //
children.translated_text: That which occurs suddenly and unexpectedly is called accidental. // RUnm_15.131 //

children.text: api gurubhir upāyair adya sāmādibhir yā
children.translated_text: 'She, the doe-eyed one, who would not even slightly break the seal of [her] pride

children.text: lavam api na mṛgākṣī māna-mudrām abhāṅkṣīt |
children.translated_text: even through weighty and best methods of conciliation and the like —'

children.text: harim iha parirebhe sā svayaṃgrāham agre
children.translated_text: 'behold! the auspicious one embraced <s>Hari</s> here, seizing [him] of her own accord,
