frightened by the roars of fresh storm-clouds!' // RUnm_15.132 //
'When the methods of conciliation and the like had risen fruitlessly, alas, O friend,

children.text: sakhīnāṃ cāturye gatavati ca sadyaḥ śithilatām |
children.translated_text: and the cleverness of her friends had also instantly become lax —'
'the bull-demon [<s>Ariṣṭāsura</s>] produced a harsh bellowing, a substitute for the mantra
to cure the fever of <s>Viśākhā</s>'s anger, with a terrifying cry!' // RUnm_15.133 //

children.text: buddhi-pūrvaṃ tu kāntena pratyutpanna-dhiyā kṛtam // RUnm_15.134 //
children.translated_text: The deliberate is that done by the lover through quick-wittedness. // RUnm_15.134 //

children.text: pāṇau pañcamukhena duṣṭa-kṛmiṇā daṣṭo'smi roṣād iti
children.translated_text: '"I have been bitten on the hand in anger by a five-headed wicked worm [snake]!"',

children.text: vyājāt kūṇita-locanaṃ vraja-patau vyābhujya vaktraṃ sthite |
children.translated_text: '— thus, with eyes squeezed shut, the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, twisting his face, stood under a pretext;'

children.text: sadyaḥ projjhita-roṣa-vṛttir asakṛt kiṃ vṛttam ity ākulā
children.translated_text: 'instantly abandoning the course of her anger, repeatedly asking in agitation, "What happened?" —'

children.text: jalpantī smita-bandhur āsyam amunā gāndharvikā cumbitā // RUnm_15.135 //
children.translated_text: 'speaking with a companion-smile on her face, <s>Gāndharvikā</s> [<s>Rādhā</s>] was boldly kissed by him.' // RUnm_15.135 //

body.text:
yathā vā-
nyastaṃ dāma kṛtāgasādya hariṇā dṛṣṭvā puro rādhayā
kṣiptenābhihataḥ sa tena kapaṭī duḥkhīva bhugnānanaḥ |
mīlann eva niṣedivān bhuvi tataḥ sadyas tayā vyagrayā
pāñibhyāṃ dhṛta-kandharaḥ sthita-mukho bimboṣṭham asyāḥ papau
// RUnm_15.136 //
body.translated_text: Or for example — 'Seeing the rope placed before [her] by <s>Hari</s> who had committed an offense, <s>Rādhā</s> struck him with it, thrown [at him]; that pretender, as if in pain, with face bent down, closing his eyes, sat upon the ground; then she, in haste, holding his neck with both hands, standing face-to-face — he drank the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip of hers.' // RUnm_15.136 //

children.translated_text: By the force of place and time alone, and by hearing the flute,

children.text: vināpy upāyaṃ māno'sau līyate vraja-subhruvām // RUnm_15.137 //
children.translated_text: that jealous pride dissolves, even without a [deliberate] method, for the fair-browed women of <s>Vraja</s>. // RUnm_15.137 //
'<s>Candrāvalī</s>, contemplating the blossoming forest of <s>Vṛndā</s> before [her],

children.text: puro vṛndāraṇyaṃ kim api kalayantī kusumitam |
children.translated_text: filled with the sounds of buzzing swarms of bees,

children.text: hariṃ ca smerāsyaṃ priyaka-taru-mūle priyam itaḥ
children.translated_text: and beloved <s>Hari</s> with smiling face at the root of a <s>priyaka</s> tree from this side —

children.text: skhalan-mānā sakhyām adiśata satṛṣṇaṃ dṛśam asau // RUnm_15.138 //
children.translated_text: with her pride slipping, she cast a thirsty glance at her friend.' // RUnm_15.138 //

body.translated_text: There, by the force of place, for example —

children.translated_text: 'In autumn, behold! The moon with its sweet form, with rays of beauty,
bathes the forest on the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>] with nectar;'
'thus, hearing the speech of the messenger-woman at night,

children.text: smita-rucibhir atānīt tatra rādhā prasādam // RUnm_15.139 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> extended her grace there through the radiances of [her] smile.' // RUnm_15.139 //

body.translated_text: By the force of time, for example —

children.translated_text: 'If you do not release your anger,

children.text: na muñca mama devi nātra nirbandhaḥ |
children.translated_text: then do not release it, my goddess — there is no compulsion here!'
'But may that one be victorious —

children.text: sa bhavatu vijayī harer veṇuḥ // RUnm_15.140 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>'s flute, whose mere breath blows away [all] pride!' // RUnm_15.140 //

body.translated_text: By the sound of the flute, for example —

children.translated_text: Or for example —

children.text: mānasyopādhyāyi prasīda sakhi rundhi me śruti-dvandvam |
children.translated_text: 'O teacher of pride, be gracious, friend — close my two ears!

children.text: ayam uccāṭana-mantraṃ siddho veṇur vane paṭhati // RUnm_15.141 //
children.translated_text: This accomplished flute recites the <s>uccāṭana</s> (expulsion) mantra in the forest!' // RUnm_15.141 //

children.text: tāratamyaṃ tu mānasya hetoḥ syāt tāratamyataḥ |
children.translated_text: The gradation of jealous pride results from the gradation of its cause;

children.text: syāl laghur madhyamaś cāsau mahiṣṭhaś cety atas tridhā // RUnm_15.142 //
children.translated_text: thus it is threefold — light, middle, and great. // RUnm_15.142 //

children.text: susādhyaḥ syāl laghur māno yatna-sādhyasya madhyamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Light pride is easily appeased; middle is appeased with effort;

children.text: duḥsādhyaḥ syād upāyena mahiṣṭhaḥ preyasāpy ayam // RUnm_15.143 //
children.translated_text: great pride is difficult to appease even by stratagem, and even by the beloved himself. // RUnm_15.143 //
Their angry epithets for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [include]: '<s>vāma</s>' (perverse one), 'crest-jewel of misbehavior,'
'king of deceivers,' 'great rogue,' 'hard-hearted one,' 'shameless one,' // RUnm_15.144 //
'excessively pampered one,' 'serpent of the <s>gopīs</s>,' 'prowler among love-games,'
'destroyer of cowherd-women's virtue,' 'mocker of virtuous cowherd wives,' // RUnm_15.145 //
'lord of the lustful,' 'mass of darkness,' 'dark-souled thief of garments,'
'highway robber of the forests on the slopes of <s>Govardhana</s>,' and so forth. // RUnm_15.146 //
Even in the proximity of the beloved, from the delirium of love-madness,

children.text: yā viśleṣa-dhiyārtis tat prema-vaicittyam ucyate // RUnm_15.147 //
children.translated_text: the anguish that arises from the thought of separation — that is called <s>prema-vaicittya</s>. // RUnm_15.147 //
'Though the son of the lord of the cowherds appears right before [her], from the torment of separation-fever
born of intense passionate attachment, with mind overpowered, she whirls about wildly;'

children.text: kāntaṃ me sakhi darśayeti daśanair udgūrṇa-śasyāṅkurā
children.translated_text: '"O friend, show me my beloved!" — with teeth [pressed upon] sprouts of grass rising in anguish,

children.text: rādhā hanta tathā vyaceṣṭate yataḥ kṛṣṇo'py abhūd vismitaḥ // RUnm_15.148 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, alas, behaved in such a way that even <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was astonished.' // RUnm_15.148 //

children.text: samajani davād vitrastānāṃ kim ārta-ravo gavāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Was there an alarmed lowing of the cows from a forest fire?

children.text: mayi kim abhavad vaiguṇyaṃ vā niraṅkuśam īkṣitam |
children.translated_text: Or was there some fault in me — was there an unbridled glance [at another]?'

children.text: vyaraci nibhṛtaṃ kiṃ vāhūtiḥ kayācid abhīṣṭayā
children.translated_text: 'Or was there a secret call made by some desired woman?

children.text: yad iha sahasā mām atyākṣīd vane vanajekṣaṇaḥ // RUnm_15.149 //
children.translated_text: That the lotus-eyed one has suddenly abandoned me here in the forest!' // RUnm_15.149 //

children.text: vilāsam anurāgas tu kutracit kam api vrajam |
children.translated_text: <s>Anurāga</s>, however, in its play, sometimes leads somewhere to some kind of course [of madness],

children.text: pārśve santam api preṣṭhaṃ hāritaṃ kurute sphuṭam // RUnm_15.150 //
children.translated_text: clearly making the most beloved one seem lost even though present at one's side. // RUnm_15.150 //
This has been clearly described by <s>Vopadeva</s> in the <s>Muktāphala</s>,

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ muktā-phale caitad vopadevena varṇitam // RUnm_15.151 //
children.translated_text: excellently illustrating the song-play of the chief queen. // RUnm_15.151 //
The separation of a previously united young couple

children.text: vyavadhānaṃ tu yat prājñaiḥ sa pravāsa itīryate // RUnm_15.152 //
children.translated_text: through being in another country and the like — the wise call that <s>pravāsa</s>. // RUnm_15.152 //
The <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) arising from that is called <s>pravāsa</s>;
all the transitory emotions suited to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, excluding joy, pride, intoxication, and shame, are described [therein]. // RUnm_15.153 //
All the <s>vyabhicāri</s> [bhāvas] suited to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> [occur] in <s>pravāsa</s>;

children.text: sa dvidhā buddhi-pūrvaḥ syāt tathiavābuddhi-pūrvakaḥ // RUnm_15.154 //
children.translated_text: it is twofold — deliberate (<s>buddhi-pūrva</s>) and not deliberate. // RUnm_15.154 //
Here, the deliberate —
Going to a distant place in accordance with a task is the deliberate [<s>pravāsa</s>];
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s task is said to be the delighting of his own devotees and the like. // RUnm_15.155 //

body.text: kiñcid dūre sudūre ca gamanād apy ayaṃ dvidhā // RUnm_15.156 //
body.translated_text: This is further twofold, from going somewhat far or very far. // RUnm_15.156 //

children.translated_text: 'Fixing her gaze upon the avenue of <s>surabhī</s> cows,
knowing the rasa through the practice of the two syllables "<s>Kṛṣ-ṇa</s>,"'
'placing her ears in the service of the flute's sound,

children.text: cittaṃ mukhe tava nayaty ahar adya rādhā // RUnm_15.157 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> today passes the day with her mind upon your face.' // RUnm_15.157 //

children.text: bhāvī bhavaṃś ca bhūtaś ca tirvidhaḥ sa tu kīrtyate // RUnm_15.158 //
children.translated_text: That is described as threefold — future, present, and past. // RUnm_15.158 //

children.text: eṣa kṣattā vrajanarapateḥ ājñayā gokule asmin
children.translated_text: 'This attendant of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, O child, at dawn
in this <s>Gokula</s>, by [the king's] command, spreads the announcement for departing to the city;'

children.text: duṣṭam bhūyaḥ sphurati ca balādīkṣaṇaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ me
children.translated_text: 'and again my wicked right eye throbs forcefully —

children.text: tena svāntaṃ sphuṭati caṭulam hanta bhāvyaṃ na jāne // RUnm_15.159 //
children.translated_text: by that my agitated heart is splitting — alas, I know not what is to come!' // RUnm_15.159 //

body.translated_text: There, the future [<s>pravāsa</s>], as in the <s>Uddhavasandeśa</s> (67) —

children.translated_text: 'When the sun's orb has swiftly set forth from the eastern summit,
the joyful son of <s>Gāndinī</s> [<s>Akrūra</s>] recites the journey-hymn upon the chariot;'

children.text: tāvat tūrṇaṃ sphuṭa khura-puṭaiḥ kṣauṇi-pṛṣṭaṃ khananto
children.translated_text: 'then swiftly, with loud hoof-beats cleaving the earth's surface —

children.text: yāvan nāmī hṛdaya bhavato ghoṭakāḥ sphoṭakā syuḥ // RUnm_15.160 //
children.translated_text: O heart, may his horses, as far as [your] name carries, become blisters [i.e., cause unbearable pain]!' // RUnm_15.160 //

children.text: kāmaṃ dūre sahacari varīvarti yat kaṃsavairī
children.translated_text: 'Let it be that the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> remains far away, O companion —

children.text: na idam lokottaramapi vipaddurdinaṃ me dunoti |
children.translated_text: even this otherworldly, calamitous rainy day does not torment me;'

children.text: āśākīlo hṛdi kila vṛtaḥ prāṇarodhī tu yo me
children.translated_text: 'but that which is the stake of hope fixed in my heart, which obstructs my very breath —
that indeed extends the torment like the fierce fire of <s>vaḍavā</s> (submarine fire).' // RUnm_15.161 //
Here, by the illustrious lion of the <s>Yadus</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] and by his beloveds,

children.text: preṣaṇaṃ kriyate premṇā sandeśasya parasparam // RUnm_15.162 //
children.translated_text: messages are lovingly sent to each other. // RUnm_15.162 //
'It must be endured somehow, dear friend, by forcibly sealing [your] eyes,
the intense burning, the unrestrained advancing chariot of the vanquished Cupid;'

children.text: dvitraireva priyasakhi dinaiḥ sevyatāṃ devi śavye
children.translated_text: 'in just two or three days, O goddess, may the left [side] be served —
I shall come to the splendid display of your love-coquetted eyebrow-pair!' // RUnm_15.163 //
'The bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> [<s>Yamunā</s>], the evening breezes, the lovely moonbeams —'

children.text: santāpaṃ na harantu nāma nitarāṃ kurvanti kasmāt punaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'they do not remove [her] suffering; rather, they intensify it all the more — but why?'
'When <s>Hari</s>, hearing in his inner chambers the message: "Thus say the women of <s>Vraja</s>",'
'sighs that shatter the pride of his beloveds' good fortune issue forth victoriously!' // RUnm_15.164 //
Now the involuntary [separation] (<s>abuddhi-pūrva</s>) —
That which arises from subjugation to another's will is called involuntary;
such subjugation, whether divine or non-divine, and so on, is of many kinds. // RUnm_15.165 //
'With a mind occupied by a hundred desires, I brought you here persistently —'
'the circle of <s>Vṛndā</s>'s forest is filled with the fragrances of the full autumn full-moon night;'
'but O beautiful one, now, by the sudden rise of <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>'s deception,'

children.text: daivenādya virodhinā katham itas tvaṃ hanta dūrīkṛtā // RUnm_15.166 //
children.translated_text: 'alas, how have you been taken far away from here by adverse fate?' // RUnm_15.166 //
Here, anxiety (<s>cintā</s>), sleeplessness (<s>jāgara</s>), agitation (<s>udvega</s>), emaciation (<s>tānava</s>), soiled appearance (<s>malināṅgatā</s>),

children.text: pralāpo vyādhir unmādo moho mṛtyur daśā daśa // RUnm_15.167 //
children.translated_text: delirious speech (<s>pralāpa</s>), illness (<s>vyādhi</s>), madness (<s>unmāda</s>), bewilderment (<s>moha</s>), and death (<s>mṛtyu</s>) — these are the ten stages. // RUnm_15.167 //
When He who intoxicates the hearts of the <s>gopīs</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, departed from the house of <s>Nanda</s>,
finding <s>Gāndinī</s>'s son [<s>Akrūra</s>], [and went] to <s>Madhupurī</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>),
then <s>Rādhā</s>, separated [from Him], was immersed in the river of anxiety,
in the unfathomable waters of affliction, through familiarity with dense whirling [of grief]. // RUnm_15.168 //

body.translated_text: Among these, anxiety (<s>cintā</s>) — as in the <s>Haṃsadūta</s> (2) —

children.translated_text: Now sleeplessness (<s>jāgara</s>), as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (322) —

children.text: yāḥ paśyanti priyaṃ svapne dhanyāstāḥ sakhi yoṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Blessed are those women who see their beloved in a dream, O friend;

children.text: asmākaṃ tu gate kṛṣṇe gatā nidrāpi vairiṇī // RUnm_15.169 //
children.translated_text: but for us, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has gone, even the hostile sleep has departed! // RUnm_15.169 //

children.text: mano me hā kaṣṭaṃ jvalati kimahaṃ hanta karavai
children.translated_text: 'Alas, my mind burns with anguish — what shall I do?'

children.text: na pāraṃ nāvāraṃ kimapi kalayāmy asya jaladheḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I can find neither the farther shore nor the nearer shore of this ocean;'

children.text: iyaṃ vande mūrdhnā sapadi tamupāyaṃ kathaya māṃ
children.translated_text: 'I bow my head to it at once — tell me the means!'
'by which I may touch even a momentary particle of steadfastness!' // RUnm_15.170 //
With the lotus of her face transformed, her interior clouded,
her <s>cakravāka</s>-like breasts withered from perpetual absence of nourishment, O lord of the <s>Yadus</s> —
<s>Rādhā</s>, drying up day after day from the fever of Your absence,
displays the culmination of emaciation like a canal in the summer heat. // RUnm_15.171 //
With the beauty of her face like a lotus shattered by a mass of frost,
with lips like a <s>bandhujīva</s> flower scorched by a harsh wind,
with eyes like blue lotuses burnt by the autumn sun, O destroyer of <s>Agha</s> —
<s>Viśākhā</s> was made to wilt by the calamity of Your absence! // RUnm_15.172 //

body.text:
atha pralāpaḥ, yathā lalita-mādhave (3.25)-
kva nanda-kula-candramāḥ kva śikhi-candrakālaṅkṛtiḥ

children.translated_text: 'Where is the deep sound of the flute? Where is the radiance like <s>Indranīla</s> (sapphire)?'
'Where is the dancer of the <s>rāsa</s> dance's rapture? Where, O friend, is the life-saving medicine?'

children.text: nidhir mama suhṛttamaḥ kva bata hanta hā dhig-vidhim // RUnm_15.173 //
children.translated_text: 'Where is my treasure, my dearest friend? Alas, alas! Curse this fate!' // RUnm_15.173 //

body.translated_text:
Now delirious speech (<s>pralāpa</s>), as in the <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (3.25) —
'Where is the moon of <s>Nanda</s>'s family? Where is the one adorned with the peacock's moon-crest?'

body.text:
atha vyādhiḥ, yathā tatraiva (3.28)
uttāpī puṭa-pākato æpi garala-grāmād api kṣobhaṇo

children.text: dambholer api duḥsahaḥ kaṭur alaṃ hṛn-magna-śūlyād api
children.translated_text: more unbearable than a thunderbolt, sharp enough — more than a spike piercing the heart,

children.text: tīvraḥ prauḍha-visūcikāni-cayato æpy uccair mamāyaṃ balī
children.translated_text: more intense than even a severe attack of cholera, exceedingly powerful —

children.text: marmāṇy adya bhinatti gokula-pater viśleṣa-janmā jvaraḥ // RUnm_15.174 //
children.translated_text: this fever born of separation from the lord of <s>Gokula</s> rends my vital organs today!' // RUnm_15.174 //

body.translated_text:
Now illness (<s>vyādhi</s>), as in the same [<s>Lalita-mādhava</s>] (3.28) —
'More scorching than furnace-fire, more convulsive than a host of poisons,

children.translated_text: She wanders within the house, laughing without reason,
she tells tales of You to the sentient and the insentient;

children.text: lutḥati ca bhuvi rādhā kampitāṅgī murāre
children.translated_text: and <s>Rādhā</s> rolls on the ground, her body trembling, O enemy of <s>Mura</s>,
her mind bewildered, erupting with the anguish of terrible separation! // RUnm_15.175 //
Today she produces sudden bursts of laughter, perspiring,
she utters shrieks — overcome with wonder — unexpectedly with longing,
she lets forth wailing with a thick, gurgling roar — all unpredictable —

children.text: rādhā mādhava-viprayoga-rabhasād anyeva tīvrād abhūt // RUnm_15.176 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, from the violence of separation from <s>Mādhava</s>, has become altogether someone else! // RUnm_15.176 //
'It checks the ocean of wretchedness, it removes the insult of heavy anxiety,
it destroys madness, it forcefully blocks the wave of tears —'
'now, O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, for this lotus-eyed one, only this alone'
'renders service — the companion of the swoon born of Your separation!' // RUnm_15.177 //
'O connoisseur of the <s>rāsa</s> dance-sport, by whom formerly upon my friend'

children.text: purā baddhā yena praṇayalaharī hanta gahanā |
children.translated_text: 'an ever-new, deep wave of love was established — alas!'

children.text: sa cen muktāpekṣastvamapi dhig imāṃ tulaśakalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'if He is now indifferent — then fie upon this thin piece of balance,'
'this [breath] which, placed at the nose of this [friend], still moves even today!' // RUnm_15.178 //

children.text: pravāsa-vipralambhe'smin daśās tās tā harer api |
children.translated_text: In this separation through sojourn (<s>pravāsa-vipralambha</s>), those ten stages belong also to <s>Hari</s>;
here, as illustration for that, a single example is stated. // RUnm_15.179 //
In the jeweled pleasure-palace, on a bed rivaling the softness of milk-foam,
delightful with yak-tail fans from wish-fulfilling trees — the daughters of kings [He] does not desire;
rather, the lord of <s>Dvārakā</s>, meditating upon the art of love-play with <s>Rādhikā</s>

children.text: paryaṅkopari rādhikā-rati-kalāṃ dhyāyan muhuḥ klāmyati // RUnm_15.180 //
children.translated_text: upon the rock-slab couch within the valley of <s>Vraja</s>'s mountain, languishes repeatedly. // RUnm_15.180 //
Due to the variety of the stated divisions of <s>prema</s>, the stages too

children.text: vividhāḥ syur ihety etā bhūma-bhītyā na kīrtitāḥ // RUnm_15.181 //
children.translated_text: are various here — but they have not been enumerated, from fear of prolixity. // RUnm_15.181 //
However, these stages, as <s>anubhāvas</s> of the divisions of <s>prema</s>,

children.text: sādhāraṇyaḥ samastānāṃ prāyaśaḥ sambhavanty api // RUnm_15.182 //
children.translated_text: being common to all [types], generally can occur [in any]. // RUnm_15.182 //
But in this very context, the extraordinary forms of the <s>adhirūḍha</s> [<s>mahā-bhāva</s>]
that has reached the state of <s>mohana</s> — those have been stated previously in that context. // RUnm_15.183 //
Some call the supreme separation by the name <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion);

children.text: sa pravāsa-viśeṣatvān naivātra pṛthag īritaḥ // RUnm_15.184 //
children.translated_text: since it is [merely] a special case of <s>pravāsa</s> (sojourn-separation), it has not been stated separately here. // RUnm_15.184 //

body.translated_text:
Thus end the divisions of separation (<s>vipralambha</s>).
Now the state of union and separation (<s>saṃyoga-viyoga-sthiti</s>) —

children.translated_text: Following the [eternal] manifestation of <s>Hari</s>'s particular <s>līlā</s> (divine play),
the state of separation of the beautiful-browed women of the cowherds' settlement has been described. // RUnm_15.185 //
Since <s>Hari</s>, who sports in <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> always with the <s>rāsa</s> and other pastimes,

children.text: hariṇā vraja-devīnāṃ viraho'sti na karhicit // RUnm_15.186 //
children.translated_text: there is never any separation for the queens of <s>Vraja</s>. // RUnm_15.186 //
'Where the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> plays in the company of cows, cowherds, and <s>gopīs</s>.' // RUnm_15.187 //

body.translated_text: And so [it is stated] in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pātāla-khaṇḍa</s>, in the Greatness of <s>Mathurā</s> —
Thus ends the state of union and separation.

children.translated_text: The <s>bhāva</s> which, through the favorable enjoyment of seeing, embracing, and the like,

children.text: yūnor ullāsam ārohan bhāvaḥ sambhoga ucyate // RUnm_15.188 //
children.translated_text: ascends to exultation in the two youths, is called <s>sambhoga</s> (union). // RUnm_15.188 //

body.text: manīṣibhir ayaṃ mukho gauṇaś ceti dvidhoditaḥ // RUnm_15.189 //
body.translated_text: This is declared twofold by the wise: primary (<s>mukhya</s>) and secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>). // RUnm_15.189 //

children.text: mukhyo jāgrad-avasthāyāṃ sambhogaḥ sa caturvidhaḥ // RUnm_15.190 //
children.translated_text: The primary <s>sambhoga</s> occurs in the waking state and is fourfold. // RUnm_15.190 //
Arising respectively from <s>pūrva-rāga</s> (first love), from <s>māna</s> (jealous anger),

and from the two types of <s>pravāsa</s> (sojourn) — the learned know them as <s>saṃkṣipta</s> (contracted), <s>saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed), <s>sampanna</s> (fulfilled), and <s>samṛddhimān</s> (abundant). // RUnm_15.191 //
Among these, <s>saṃkṣipta</s> (contracted) —
Where the two youths, through timidity, modesty, and the like,

children.text: upacārān niṣevete sa saṃkṣipta itīritaḥ // RUnm_15.192 //
children.translated_text: enjoy contracted [restrained] displays of affection — that is called <s>saṃkṣipta</s>. // RUnm_15.192 //
Among these, performed by the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>), as in the <s>Saptaśatī</s> —
[In Prākrit:] <s>līlāhituliaselo rakkha-u vo rāhiātthaṇapphaṃse</s> /
<s>hariṇo paḍhama-samāgama-sajjhasabebellio hattho</s> // RUnm_15.193 //
[In Sanskrit:] 'May the hand of <s>Hari</s>, trembling with timidity at the first meeting
upon touching <s>Rādhikā</s>'s breast — that hand which playfully lifted the mountain [<s>Govardhana</s>] — protect you!'
At their first union, <s>Rādhā</s> covered her face with a cloth when kissed,
she curled her body-creeper when embraced,
and spoke indistinctly during talk of love-play —
yet even so she gave delight to <s>Madhusūdana</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]! // RUnm_15.194 //
Now <s>saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed) —
Where the displays of affection are mixed with memories of deception and the like,

children.text: upacārāḥ sa saṅkīrṇaḥ kiñcit taptekṣu-peśalaḥ // RUnm_15.195 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>saṅkīrṇa</s> — somewhat like the sweetness of heated sugarcane. // RUnm_15.195 //
The nectars of enviously-tinted speech, those jealous,
delightful glances of feigned displeasure,
the love-sports of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> with beaming faces, with
<s>Rādhikā</s> — they are victorious! // RUnm_15.196 //
Her face slightly lowered reveals a dawn of not-quite-grace;
her glance with curved bank slowly betrays a remaining streak of jealousy;

children.text: rādhāyāḥ sakhi sūcayaty aviśadā vāg apy asūyākalāṃ
children.translated_text: O friend, even <s>Rādhā</s>'s unclear speech hints at the art of envy,

children.text: mānantaṃ bruvatī tathāpi madhurā kṛṣṇaṃ dhinoty ākṛtiḥ // RUnm_15.197 //
children.translated_text: and yet her form, though declaring the end of wounded pride, is nonetheless sweet and enchants <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! // RUnm_15.197 //
Now <s>sampanna</s> (fulfilled) —

children.text: pravāsāt saṅgate kānte bhogaḥ sampanna īritaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the beloved has returned from sojourn, the enjoyment is called <s>sampanna</s>;

children.text: dvidhā syād āgatiḥ prādurbhāvaś ceti sa saṅgamaḥ // RUnm_15.198 //
children.translated_text: that meeting is twofold: through arrival (<s>āgati</s>) and through [divine] manifestation (<s>prādurbhāva</s>). // RUnm_15.198 //
Arrival (<s>āgati</s>) is [His] coming by means of ordinary worldly activity. // RUnm_15.199 //
'Do not cast slow glances at the threshold from within the house, fearing the elders;'
'you are exhausted, having spent the whole day in separation — alas!'
'Behold — smiling, the stealer of the hearts of cowherd women approaches, O gentle one —'
'the enchanting <s>Mukunda</s>, with garlands of <s>guñjā</s> berries, his fragrance licked by bees!' // RUnm_15.200 //
Now manifestation (<s>prādurbhāva</s>) —
When <s>Hari</s> suddenly appears before His beloved ones

children.text: āvirbhavaty akasmād yat prādurbhāvaḥ sa ucyate // RUnm_15.201 //
children.translated_text: who are overwhelmed by the agitation of love — that is called <s>prādurbhāva</s> (manifestation). // RUnm_15.201 //
As in the illustrious Tenth [Canto] (10.32.2) —
<s>Śauri</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] appeared before them, with a smiling lotus-face,
wearing a yellow garment, garlanded — <s>Manmatha</s>'s own <s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid's Cupid) in person! // RUnm_15.202 //

children.text: ayi svapno dūre viramatu samakṣaṃ śṛṇu haṭhā-
children.translated_text: 'Alas! Let dreams be far away! Listen directly! Do not be'
'distrustful through the delusion of mental illusion here, O friend!'
'Your friend, having reached the forest of <s>Govardhana</s>, out of playful curiosity,'
'has suddenly again displayed the skill of love's quarrel!' // RUnm_15.203 //
This <s>sambhoga</s>, born of the state called <s>rūḍha</s> [<s>mahā-bhāva</s>], arising from separation,
is considered the ultimate culmination for those filled with overflowing bliss. // RUnm_15.204 //
The anguish of separation is doubled when there is the manifestation born of the flute's melody;
in [such] manifestation, the festival of all desired happiness occurs. // RUnm_15.205 //
Now <s>samṛddhimān</s> (abundant) —
When two youths, difficult to behold, separated through subjugation to fate,

children.text: upabhogātireko yaḥ kīrtyate sa samṛddhimān // RUnm_15.206 //
children.translated_text: [meet and] there is a superabundance of enjoyment — that is celebrated as <s>samṛddhimān</s>. // RUnm_15.206 //

children.text: dagdhaṃ hanta dadhānayā vapur idaṃ yasyāvalokāśayā
children.translated_text: 'Alas, she whose very form was burnt by the desire of whose glance,

children.text: soḍhā marma-vipāṭane paṭur iyaṃ pīḍātivṛṣṭir mayā |
children.translated_text: this downpour of pain, skilled at tearing vital organs, was endured by me;'
'devoted to the vow of a love-tryst in a cave-dwelling on the bank of <s>Kālindī</s> —'

children.text: so'yaṃ jīvita-bandhur indu-vadane bhūyaḥ samāliṅgitaḥ // RUnm_15.207 //
children.translated_text: 'this friend of my life, O moon-faced one, has been embraced again!' // RUnm_15.207 //

children.text: tavātra parimṛgyatā kim api lakṣma sākṣād iyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'What distinguishing mark of yours was being sought here? This herself —'
'you whom I have brought near — you are the <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) of all worlds!'
'Just as one who runs about the world for the wealth of a handful of chickpeas,'

children.text: janena patitā puraḥ kanaka-vṛṣṭir āsādyate // RUnm_15.208 //
children.translated_text: 'finds a rain of gold fallen before them!' // RUnm_15.208 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the discernment of the maturation of the sweet <s>rasa</s> (<s>madhura-rasa</s>).

children.translated_text: The twofold nature of these [unions] as hidden (<s>channa</s>) and open (<s>prakāśa</s>) —

children.text: iṣṭāpy atra na hi proktā nātyullāsakarī yataḥ // RUnm_15.209 //
children.translated_text: though desired [as a topic], is not stated here, since it does not produce much exultation. // RUnm_15.209 //
Now the secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) —
The special attainment of <s>Hari</s> in a dream is called secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>);
dreams here are declared twofold: ordinary (<s>sāmānya</s>) and special (<s>viśeṣa</s>). // RUnm_15.210 //

children.text: sāmānyaḥ sa tu yaḥ pūrvaṃ kathito vyabhicāriṣu |
children.translated_text: The ordinary is that which was previously described among the transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārins</s>);

children.text: viśeṣaḥ khalu jāgaryā nirviśeṣao mahādbhutaḥ // RUnm_15.211 //
children.translated_text: the special one is truly indistinguishable from waking and supremely wondrous. // RUnm_15.211 //

body.text: bhāvautkaṇṭhye-mayo hy eṣa caturdhā pūrvavan mataḥ // RUnm_15.212 //
body.translated_text: This [special dream] is composed of <s>bhāva</s> and <s>autkaṇṭhya</s> (eagerness), and is fourfold as before. // RUnm_15.212 //

children.translated_text: Sporting in the forest on the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>],
radiant with a splendor that mocks the sweetness of a row of fresh rain-clouds —
the crest-jewel among the clever, some mighty new youth

children.text: mama svapne ko'pi priya-sakhi balīyān nava-yuvā // RUnm_15.213 //
children.translated_text: kisses my face daily in a dream, O dear friend! // RUnm_15.213 //

body.translated_text: Among these, the condensed [type] in a dream, for example —

children.text: sakhi kruddhā mā bhūr laghur api na doṣaḥ sumukhi me
children.translated_text: 'O friend, do not be angry! Not even a slight fault is mine, O fair-faced one!

children.text: na mānāgni-jvālām aśamayam ahaṃ tām asamaye |
children.translated_text: I did not extinguish that flame of jealous anger at the wrong time!

children.text: sa dhūrtas te svapne rasa-vṛṣṭiṃ mayi tathā
children.translated_text: That rogue poured such a shower of rasa upon me in your dream

children.text: yato vistīrṇāpi svayam iyam ayāsīd upaśamam // RUnm_15.214 //
children.translated_text: that even this [anger], though vast, subsided of its own accord!' // RUnm_15.214 //

body.translated_text: Now the mixed [type] in a dream, for example —

children.translated_text: 'If that crest-jewel of the hard-hearted has departed, abandoning me,

children.text: paryātu svacchandaṃ mama samayadharmaḥ kila gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: let him roam freely — my vow of constancy shall indeed be my course!

children.text: idaṃ soḍhuṃ kā vā prabhavati yataḥ svapnakapaṭā-
children.translated_text: But who can endure this — that by the deception of a dream

children.text: dihāyāto vṛndāvanabhuvi kalān māṃ ramayati // RUnm_15.215 //
children.translated_text: he comes here to the land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and artfully delights me!' // RUnm_15.215 //

body.translated_text: Now the fulfilled [type] in a dream, as in the <s>Haṃsadūta</s> (105) —

children.text: cirād adya svapne mama vividha-yatnād upagate
children.translated_text: 'After a long time, O friend, when <s>Govinda</s>, [obtained] in a dream through various efforts,
today attained the abode-of-an-instant in my eyes —

children.text: gṛhītvā hā hanta tvaritam atha tasminn api rathaṃ
children.translated_text: alas, alas! Having then quickly seized a chariot in that very [dream],

children.text: kathaṃ pratyāsannaḥ sa khalu puruṣo rāja-puruṣaḥ // RUnm_15.216 //
children.translated_text: how is it that the king's officer came so near!' // RUnm_15.216 //

body.translated_text: Now the prosperous [type] in a dream, as in the <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (7.11) —

children.text: tulya-svarūpa evāyaṃ prodyan yūnor dvayor api |
children.translated_text: This [dream experience] is of equal nature, arising in both youths [hero and heroine];

children.text: ūṣā-niruddhayor yadvat kvacit svapno'py abādhitaḥ // RUnm_15.217 //
children.translated_text: just as with <s>Ūṣā</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s>, when both are confined, the dream too is unimpeded. // RUnm_15.217 //
For this very reason, in the most wondrous dreams of the perfected ones (<s>siddha</s>),

children.text: prāptāni maṇḍanādīni dṛśyante jāgare'pi ca // RUnm_15.218 //
children.translated_text: ornaments and the like obtained [in dreams] are seen also in the waking state. // RUnm_15.218 //
For those who have transcended even the fourth state (<s>turīya</s>)
and have attained that fifth state, which is pervaded by <s>prema</s> (divine love) —
that type of dream which is an expansion of the <s>rajas</s> mode
is simply impossible for the beloveds of <s>Hari</s>. // RUnm_15.219 //

children.text: ity eṣa hari-bhāvasya vilāsaḥ ko'pi peśala |
children.translated_text: Thus, this is some exquisite play of <s>Hari</s>'s emotion,

children.text: citra-svapnam ivātanvan kṛṣṇaḥ saṅgamayaty alam // RUnm_15.220 //
children.translated_text: which, extending like a wondrous dream, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> abundantly brings into union. // RUnm_15.220 //
Now, among these [aspects of union], those exquisitely beautiful distinguishing features are examined

children.text: ye'nubhāva-daśām asyāḥ prāpnuvanti rateḥ sphuṭam // RUnm_15.221 //
children.translated_text: which clearly attain the condition of <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent expressions) of this love (<s>rati</s>). // RUnm_15.221 //

children.text: te tu sandarśanaṃ jalpaḥ sparśanaṃ vartma-rodhanam |
children.translated_text: These are: mutual beholding (<s>sandarśana</s>), conversation (<s>jalpa</s>), touching (<s>sparśana</s>), blocking the path (<s>vartma-rodhana</s>),
the <s>rāsa</s> dance, <s>Vṛndāvana</s> play, water sports in the <s>Yamunā</s> and elsewhere, // RUnm_15.222 //
boat-sport (<s>nau-khelā</s>), playful theft (<s>līlā-caurya</s>), tollgate encounters (<s>ghaṭṭa</s>), concealment in bowers and the like,
drinking honey-wine (<s>madhu-pāna</s>), wearing bridal attire (<s>vadhū-veśa</s>), feigning sleep (<s>kapaṭa-suptatā</s>), // RUnm_15.223 //
dice-games (<s>dyūta-krīḍā</s>), cloth-pulling (<s>paṭākṛṣṭi</s>), kissing and embracing, nail-marking,
drinking the nectar of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips, sexual union (<s>samprayoga</s>), and so on — thus they are considered. // RUnm_15.224 //
'Inner fear from the presence of the restless-eyed one's elders appears at once;

children.text: kula-sthitir alaṃ tu me manasi tāvad unmīlati |
children.translated_text: decorum of family propriety indeed unfolds in my mind at once —
but only so long as this lotus-face with its blooming cheeks, flashing

children.text: na yāvad aparokṣatām idam apaiti vaktrāmbujam // RUnm_15.225 //
children.translated_text: with swinging <s>makara</s> (crocodile-shaped) earrings, does not come before my direct sight!' // RUnm_15.225 //

body.translated_text: Among these, mutual beholding (<s>sandarśana</s>), as in the <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (2.26) —

children.text: jalpaḥ parasparaṃ goṣṭhī vitathoktiś ca kathyate // RUnm_15.226 //
children.translated_text: Conversation is said to be of two kinds: mutual discussion (<s>goṣṭhī</s>) and teasing banter (<s>vitathokti</s>). // RUnm_15.226 //
Here, mutual discussion (<s>goṣṭhī</s>), as in the <s>Dānakelikaumudī</s> (42-43) —
'How can the king of serpents be fit to assault women of the mongoose clan?

children.text: yad etā daśanair eṣa daśan nāpnoti maṅgalam // RUnm_15.227 //
children.translated_text: For by biting these [women] with his teeth, he gains no auspiciousness!' // RUnm_15.227 //
'Her brow-lines shining with the beauty of the not-yet-full king of stars [crescent moon], having obtained a fresh glory of radiance in herself,
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with eyes sparkling along the path of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s [dark] glance — adorned by <s>Viśākhā</s>,
displaying the expertise of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid) with the luster of her sidelong glance —

children.text: tvaṃ rādhe śiva-mūrtir ity urasi māṃ bhogīndram aṅgīkuru // RUnm_15.228 //
children.translated_text: you, O <s>Rādhā</s>, are the embodiment of <s>Śiva</s> (auspiciousness) — accept me, the king of serpents, upon your breast!' // RUnm_15.228 //

children.text: asminn adrau kati na hi mayā hanta hārādi-vittaṃ
children.translated_text: 'On this mountain, have I not, alas, many times made doe-eyed women
take Jain initiation, seizing their necklaces and other wealth, time after time!
Those whose faces were concealed by the piteous cries, made poor by the offering of leaves,
were quickly taken in from afar by their mature creeper-friends!' // RUnm_15.229 //

body.translated_text: Teasing banter (<s>vitathokti</s>), as in the same work (44) —

children.text: na kuru śapatham asya sparśato dūṣitoccair
children.translated_text: 'Do not take an oath! You are not at all ruined by his touch —
by the arm-serpent of the king of serpents!
O dissembler, see — your body, trembling incomparably,

children.text: kapaṭini paritas te paśya romāñcitāsti // RUnm_15.230 //
children.translated_text: exuding perspiration, is bristling with goosebumps all around!' // RUnm_15.230 //
'Surrounded by the horn, with its dark luster of prominent rocks,
swinging his cane, shining with a belt [made of] interwoven bamboo sticks —
having surpassed this towering mountain, how can you from here

children.text: tvayā gantuṃ śakyā taraṇi-duhitus tīra-saraṇī // RUnm_15.231 //
children.translated_text: go ahead on the path along the bank of the daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>]?' // RUnm_15.231 //

body.translated_text: Now blocking the path (<s>vartma-rodhana</s>), as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (6.19) —

children.translated_text: '<s>Hari</s>, in the form of a fresh rain-cloud, between each pair of brides,
with his arms shining on their shoulders — wonderfully, though one, he whirls about!

children.text: vadhūś ca taḍid-ujjvalā prati-harid vayaṃ madhyataḥ
children.translated_text: And each bride, brilliant as lightning, with a <s>Hari</s> on each side,
her lotus-hands held by her companions — see, she dances at the <s>rāsa</s> festival!' // RUnm_15.232 //
'The land-lotus, stained [with dust], praises your footstep with songs;
the row of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers bows down with the devotion of her teeth;
the <s>bimba</s>-fruit garland hangs, worshipping your lip —

children.text: vilasati tava vaśyā paśya vṛndāṭavīyam // RUnm_15.233 //
children.translated_text: see, this <s>Vṛndāvana</s> forest sports, submissive to you!' // RUnm_15.233 //
'In the water-battle, sprinkled by <s>Rādhā</s> with dense streams,

children.text: mālyaṃ bhaṅgam avāpa vīra tilako yātaḥ kilādṛśyatām |
children.translated_text: your garland was broken, O hero, your forehead-mark disappeared!

children.text: vaktrendau pratimā-cchalena śaraṇaṃ labdhaḥ sakhīṃ kaustubhas
children.translated_text: The <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem], finding refuge on her friend's face-moon under the pretext of a reflection —

children.text: tan mā bhūś cakito vimukta-cikuraṃ nārdaty asau tvad-vidham // RUnm_15.234 //
children.translated_text: so be not alarmed, the loose-haired one does not cry out at one like you!' // RUnm_15.234 //

body.translated_text: Water sports in the <s>Yamunā</s>, for example —

children.translated_text: 'In water-sport, with restless hands,
covering and uncovering <s>Rādhikā</s>'s face again and again —
may <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, curious about the separation and union
of the <s>cakravāka</s> couple [the sun-moon reflections], protect the world!' // RUnm_15.235 //
'The daughter of the Sun [<s>Yamunā</s>] is released by the mass of waves,

children.text: navyā ca naur iti vacas tava tathyam eva |
children.translated_text: and the boat is new — your words are indeed true!
But my excessive source of apprehension is precisely this:',

children.text: tvaṃ cañcalo yad iha mādhava nāviko'si // RUnm_15.236 //
children.translated_text: 'that you, O <s>Mādhava</s>, are the fickle boatman here!' // RUnm_15.236 //
Playful theft is the taking of the flute, garments, flowers, and so on. // RUnm_15.237 //

children.text: nīcair nyāsād atha caraṇayor nūpura mūkayantī
children.translated_text: 'Silencing her anklets by carefully lowering [her feet] to the ground,
repeatedly seizing and pushing up her bangles and bracelets on her arm-tips,
constantly casting timid, watchful glances from her eyes,

children.text: smitvā smitvā harati muralīm aṅkato mādhavasya // RUnm_15.238 //
children.translated_text: smiling and smiling again, [she] steals the <s>muralī</s> from the lap of <s>Mādhava</s>!' // RUnm_15.238 //

body.translated_text: Now stealing the flute (<s>vaṃśī-caurya</s>), as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (253) —

children.text: chadāvali-vṛtaiva naḥ sapadi kācid ekā vrajaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Let just one of us, covered by a [single] strip of leaves, quickly enter <s>Vraja</s>
and bring here old women, fierce in their deeds!

children.text: ayaṃ guṇa-nidhis taror upari tābhir abhyarcyatām
children.translated_text: Let him who sits atop the tree, that treasury of virtues, be duly worshipped by them —
he, the splitter of the garments of the host of maidens observing the vow of <s>Umā</s>!' // RUnm_15.239 //

children.text: ayi jñātaṃ jñātaṃ harasi hariṇākṣi pratidinaṃ
children.translated_text: 'O, I know, I know! You, O doe-eyed one, are the one who daily

children.text: tvam eva pracchannā mama sumanasāṃ mañjarim itaḥ |
children.translated_text: steals my flower-clusters from here in secret!

children.text: cirād diṣṭyā cauri tvam iha vidhṛtādya svayam ato
children.translated_text: At last, by good fortune, O thief, you have been caught here today by yourself!

children.text: guhākārām ārāt praviśa vasatiṃ prauḍhibhir alam // RUnm_15.240 //
children.translated_text: Now enter this cave-dwelling nearby with all due boldness!' // RUnm_15.240 //
'Disrespecting the supreme lord of the tollgate and engaging in dispute itself,
you who refuse to pay the toll —

children.text: manye vidhitsatha tad atra gires taṭeṣu
children.translated_text: I think you intend thereby to wage battle here
on the slopes of this mountain, in these strongholds, on these difficult terrains!' // RUnm_15.241 //

body.translated_text: Now tollgate encounters (<s>ghaṭṭa</s>), as in the <s>Dānakelikaumudī</s> (64) —

children.translated_text: 'I suspect that today, the moon-faced one, with a desire for intimate sport

children.text: kuñje vañjula-śākhinaḥ śaśimukhī līnā varīvarti sā |
children.translated_text: in the inner recesses, lies hidden in the bower of the <s>vañjula</s> [<s>aśoka</s>] tree's branches;

children.text: no ced eṣa tad-aṅghri-saṅgama-vinābhāvād akāle kathaṃ
children.translated_text: for otherwise, how would it, out of season, without the contact of her feet,
become a worthy recipient of the hymn of the bee-host invited by the fragrance of flowers?' // RUnm_15.242 //

body.translated_text: Now concealment in bowers and the like (<s>kuñjādi-līnatā</s>), as in the <s>Vidagdhamādhava</s> (6.25) —

children.translated_text: 'The innocent one, seeing the risen face-moon of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>
sweetly [reflected] in the honey-cup —
directed her gaze there to drink [that reflection],

children.text: na tu vadanaṃ muhur arthitāpi tena // RUnm_15.243 //
children.translated_text: but would not [drink from] the cup, though repeatedly entreated by him!' // RUnm_15.243 //

children.text: keyaṃ śyāmā sphurati sarale gopakanyā kimarthaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Who is this dark girl who appears before me, a simple cowherd-maiden? For what purpose

children.text: prāptā sakhyaṃ tava mṛgayate nirmitāsau vayasyā |
children.translated_text: has she come? She seeks your friendship — she is a manufactured companion!',

children.text: āliṅgāmūṃ muhuriti tathā kurvatī māṃ viditvā
children.translated_text: 'Embrace her repeatedly!' — doing so [to me], and then recognizing me [as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],

children.text: nārīveśam hriyamupayayau māninī yatra rādhā // RUnm_15.244 //
children.translated_text: the proud <s>Rādhā</s>, where she was, attained in woman's disguise — went away overcome with modesty! // RUnm_15.244 //

body.translated_text: Now wearing bridal attire (<s>vadhū-veśa-dhṛti</s>), as in the <s>Uddhava-sandeśa</s> (64) —

children.translated_text: 'His gentle, spreading, soft smile, gradually being restrained bit by bit,
the irrepressible rising of body-hair, flowing forth from the bursting of <s>prema</s> —
we adore the feigned sleep of the Lord, whose eyes are playfully closed,
[assumed] in order to hear the charming mutual whispered conversation of the women of <s>Vraja</s> about [his] pastimes!' // RUnm_15.245 //

children.text: jitvā dyūta-paṇaṃ daśaty aghahare gaṇḍaṃ mudā dakṣiṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having won the dice-wager, the slayer of <s>Agha</s> joyfully bites her right cheek;

children.text: sā vāmaṃ ca daśeti tatra rabhasād akṣaṃ kṣipanty abhyadhāt |
children.translated_text: she bites [his] left in return — thereupon, casting the die impetuously, she declared:',

children.text: ājñāṃ sundari te yatheti hariṇā vāme ca daṣṭe tataḥ
children.translated_text: '"As you command, O beautiful one!" — and when <s>Hari</s> bit her left [cheek] too, then',

children.text: saṃrambhād iva sā bhujā-latikayā kaṇṭhe babandha priyam // RUnm_15.246 //
children.translated_text: 'she, as if in a flurry of anger, bound her beloved around the neck with the creeper of her arm!' // RUnm_15.246 //
'Blessed is that gem [<s>Kaustubha</s>], which in the dense mass of darkness in the bower,

children.text: smitvā smitvā mayi kuca-paṭīṃ kṛṣṭavaty unmadena |
children.translated_text: when [<s>Rādhā</s>], smiling again and again, pulled [his] breast-cloth with the madness [of love] —',
'though deeply hidden in form, it, the knower of his face's intent,

children.text: niṣṭhīvan yaḥ kiraṇa-laharīṃ hrepayāmāsa rādhām // RUnm_15.247 //
children.translated_text: spitting out a wave of rays, put <s>Rādhā</s> to shame!' // RUnm_15.247 //
'The enemy of the demons, from the face-moon of the one with playfully feigned frowning brows,
swiftly shaking [her face] on all sides,
kissed the lotus-eyed one's [lips]
like a bee [kissing] a lotus trembling in the wind!' // RUnm_15.248 //
'Embraced by one of the color of fresh jaggery,
he, of flashing cloud-radiance, by her, in intoxication —
<s>Hari</s> stole the auspicious beauties of the <s>tamāla</s> tree
entwined by a golden creeper!' // RUnm_15.249 //

children.text: na kucāv imau gatijitā tayā hṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: 'These are not [her] breasts, O friend — she has forcefully seized
from the elephant a pair of frontal globes, gait-proud!
The wound here — the tamer of elephants has just bestowed it
with the supreme goad of <s>Kāma</s> (Love), at that very instant!' // RUnm_15.250 //
'O elephant-waisted beauty, do not cover your face,
which is a moon-orb, with your hand!
Let the bee of the <s>nīpa</s> grove, O beautiful one,
drink at the arena of your lip!' // RUnm_15.251 //

body.translated_text: Now drinking the nectar of the <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips, for example —

children.translated_text: 'Her mind excited by the tight pressing of the circle of his arms, through extravagant wildness,',
'from his persistence in drinking the nectar of her lips, her mouth full of hissing sounds,',
'the expert of the festival of <s>Kandarpa</s>, her bower-interior overrun —',

children.text: sārdhaṃ rādhikayā harer nidhuvana-krīḍā-vidhir vardhate // RUnm_15.252 //
children.translated_text: 'together with <s>Rādhikā</s>, <s>Hari</s>'s amorous love-play intensifies!' // RUnm_15.252 //
The connoisseurs know that the delight which comes from the mutual playful display of the clever ones

children.text: na tathā samprayogeṇa syād evaṃ rasikā viduḥ // RUnm_15.253 //
children.translated_text: is not the same as that which comes from sexual union alone. // RUnm_15.253 //
'In embracing, [he uses] force; in scratching with nail-tips, [there is] marking;'
forcibly biting the lip, binding with her pair of arms,
tearing the silk garment, striking with a blue lotus —

children.text: ratād api sukhaṃ harer adhikam ādadhe rādhayā // RUnm_15.254 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Rādhā</s> doing these, <s>Hari</s> derived even greater pleasure than from lovemaking itself. // RUnm_15.254 //
The enchanting play of the eyebrows through the art of sportive glancing steeped in humor,
the pulling of the upper garment, the coquettish blow with the ear-lotus —
this play of the foremost teacher of love among the sophisticated women of <s>Vraja</s>, the <s>Gāndharvikā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>),

children.text: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ suratotsavād api navāsvādaṃ vitene sukham // RUnm_15.255 //
children.translated_text: bestowed happiness of unprecedented relish, even more abundantly than the festival of lovemaking. // RUnm_15.255 //
With the obstacle of horripilation-sprouts, with the screen of tightly closing eyelids,
with playfully feigned gazes, with the drinking of lip-nectar, with the sport of conversation,
and with the attainment of bliss even in the battle of the arts of <s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid) —

children.text: udbhūtaḥ sa tayor babhūva suratārambhaḥ priyambhāvukaḥ // RUnm_15.256 //
children.translated_text: that commencement of lovemaking between the two arose, overflowing with affection. // RUnm_15.256 //
For example —
'O joy of <s>Gokula</s>, O <s>Govinda</s>, O moon of the dynasty of the lord of the cowherd settlement!
O lord of my life, O supreme crest-ornament, O crown-jewel among the gallant ones!
O moon of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O prince of the cowherd youths, O captivator of the heart!' —

children.text: ity ādyā vraja-devīnāṃ preyasī praṇayoktayaḥ // RUnm_15.258 //
children.translated_text: such are the beloved, affectionate utterances of the divine ladies of <s>Vraja</s>. // RUnm_15.257–258 //
Due to its incomparability, boundlessness, and unfathomable depth,

children.text: spṛṣṭaḥ paraṃ taṭasthena rasābdhir madhuro mayā ||o||
children.translated_text: this sweet ocean of <s>rasa</s> has been touched by me only from the shore. ||o||
May this <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>, born from the ocean of the deep, great <s>Ghoṣa</s> [cowherd settlement],
attain the fitness of service in the vicinity of Your <s>makara</s>-shaped earrings, O Lord! ||o||

body.translated_text:
Thus [ends the description of] the varieties of union (<s>sambhoga-bhedāḥ</s>).
Thus ends the chapter on the varieties of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (<s>Śṛṅgāra-bheda-prakaraṇam</s>) in the illustrious <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>.

Thus is completed the treatise named the illustrious <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>,
composed by the venerable <s>Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī Prabhupāda</s>.
